educationalGoal: The aim of this course is to help you develop the skills necessary for you to make the transition to a KIT student. After completing this course, you will be familiar with KIT’s academic support systems and be able to utilize them for self-management, which will provide motivation to engage in learning activities in KIT actively and get on a path to a meaningful and successful career.
advice: 1. Presidential lecture: Comprehending the meaning and significance of “KIT IDEALS” and the “Student Pledge” to raise awareness and consciousness as a KIT student. 2. “Weekly report”: Making good use of KIT’s academic support system to practice self-management. 3. “Newspaper portfolio”: Raising interest in social issues. 4. Counseling center lecture: Discovering our character strengths for career management. 5. Academic writing exercise: Improving writing skills by writing essays. 6. Group discussions and presentations: Improving discussion and presentation skills. 7. Academic planning: Comprehending KIT’s educational programs (Humanities and Social Sciences Program, English Language Program, Mathematics and Science Program, Practical Engineering Program, and other specialized programs) and systems. 8. Interview with the academic advisor about living and learning conditions. *The submission date for each assignments must be strictly observed. *Access the “Student Portal”, “e-syllabus”, and other systems frequently to get the latest information.
requiredKnowledge: 1. Willpower to understand and observe “KIT IDEALS.” 2. Willpower to understand and observe the “Student Pledge.” 3. Willpower to acquire KIT human skills. 4. Motivation and willpower to study and learn by yourself.

activityGoals.body: Be able to improve self-management skills and establish a learning attitude through a weekly report.
Be able to increase your interest in social issues and career design through news reports.
Be able to organize the contents of special lectures accurately and express your opinions in academic writing.
Be able to learn the basic techniques of academic writing and create sentences according to the rules.
Be able to compare and summarize opinions in group discussions, and express them in speech and writing.
Be able to clarify future learning goals and plan for the second semester.

title: 修学基礎B
subtitle: Basic Style for Study B
courseType:

Humanities and Social Sciences
keywords: Academic support system 2.Career management 3.Academic writing 4.Self-reflection 5.Academic adviser
educationalGoal: The aim of this course is to improve further the skills learned in Basic Style for Study A (and other courses) from the first semester in KIT. After completing this course, you will be able to develop critical and logical thinking skills that enable you to put yourself into a social context and see yourself from the perspective of a third person, which is necessary to continue on the path to a meaningful and successful career.
advice: 1. “Weekly report”: Making good use of KIT’s academic support system to practice self-management. 2. “Newspaper portfolio”: Raising interest in social issues in terms of career management. 3. Special lecture on career management: Considering career management in the context of career development. 4. Group discussion and presentation: Becoming familiar with specialized courses for better career development. 5. Academic planning: Comprehending KIT’s educational curriculum and system in detail (such as prerequisites for course registration, graduation requirements, etc.) in terms of career management. 6. Research paper: Improving academic writing skills (including critical and logical thinking skills) by writing a research paper. 7. Self-reflection: Group discussion and interview with the academic adviser to review the first year. *The submission date for each assignments must be strictly observed. *Access the “Student Portal”, “e-syllabus”, and other systems frequently to get the latest information *When submitting research papers and/or assignments, strictly adhere to the designated forms and instructions.
requiredKnowledge: 1. Willpower to understand and observe “KIT IDEALS.” 2. Willpower to understand and observe the “Student pledge.” 3. Willpower to acquire KIT human skills. 4. Motivation to develop language competence (in your native language). 5. Motivation to develop academic writing skills.

activityGoals.body: Be able to express your achievements and goals through weekly report and self-evaluation of achievement report.
Be able to organize the contents of special lectures and express your opinions in academic writing.
Be able to find out problems in group discussions and express your opinions in speech and writing.
Be able to express your opinions of a social issue in academic writing (a research paper).
Be able to clarify in writing the academic planning of your course curriculum and future prospects in life.
Be able to develop and implement the skills necessary for students.

title: 技術者と持続可能社会
subtitle: Engineer and Sustainable Society
courseType:
Humanities and Social Sciences Program
Liberal Arts and Sciences Courses
Ethics for Engineers
keywords: Market, Customer 2.Company, Engineer 3.Quality, Cost, Delivery, Safety 4.Innovation 5.Career design
educationalGoal: Students are interested in social trends and learn to understand market trends and customer needs. Students then understand the activities of companies in society and the role of engineers in preparing for their success as engineers. Students will also learn about the social expectations and quality, cost, delivery and safety that engineers need. Students can understand that innovation is important for the realization of a sustainable society and connect it with their career design.
advice: The students considered the future career direction in the "Basic Style for Study" in the first year. Based on this, in this course students will learn the following items needed to do a good job at the company. (1) Understand the trends of sustainable society such as SDGs, the role of companies, and the responsibilities and rewards of engineers working there. (2) Learn basic management knowledge and matters related to the work of engineers, such as R & D and production processes. (3) Understand that there are a wide variety of industries in society, and engineers are active in various occupations in a wide range of fields. (4) Deepen understanding of the work of engineers by exchanging opinions on items investigated by themselves through group discussions and presentations. (5) Learn examples of innovation in order to play an active role in a developing society.
books: Textbooks:Engineer and Sustainable Society Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: ・ Understanding the "Basic Style for Study" learned in the first year and the introduced subjects of each department ・ Basic knowledge about the structure and movement of Japanese society ・ Basic knowledge about the relationship between Japan and the world

activityGoals.body: Being interested in sustainable society, market and customer trends, and being able to report.
Understand the roles of companies and engineers that contribute to society.
Understand Quality, Cost, Delivery, and Safety, and be able to investigate and analyze the company.
Be able to understand your life plan and be able to present your own opinions at group discussions.
Be able to understand how to become an engineer who contributes to society.

keywords: Market, Customer 2.Company, Engineer 3.Quality, Cost, Delivery, Safety 4.Innovation 5.Career design

keywords: Japanese 2.Differences in values 3.Japanese national character 4.Japanese mythology 5.Japan founding myth
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) Learn about the life of the founders of Japan and how to live and think. (2) Understand the characteristics and national character of Japan. advice: This course will teach the Japanese way of life and thinking by covering the following: 1. Japanese way of life and thinking 2. Japanese national character 3. Japanese mythology 4. books: Textbooks: Reference books:The Story of Japan, Vols. I-III (Seisei kikaku) Reserved books:None

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the Japanese way of life and thinking using appropriate Japanese term.
Be able to explain the Japanese national character using appropriate Japanese term.
Be able to read about the characteristics of Japanese myths and explain them using appropriate Japanese term.

title: 科学技術者倫理
subtitle: Science and Engineering Ethics
courseType:
Humanities and Social Sciences Program
Liberal Arts and Sciences Courses
Human and Social Sciences
keywords: Values sharing 2.Professional ethics and codes of ethics 3.Engineers in globalization 4.Ethical decision making 5.Science and technology (S&T) in society
educationalGoal: In this course, students will learn ethics is a creative practice to design our conduct by balancing values, not by only observing rules. We will examine social and environmental influences and the role of S&T to comprehend ethical and social responsibilities as a professional engineer (including scientists) in a globalizing society. Upon completing this course, students will be able to improve their ethical decision-making skills for carrying out duties as a professional engineer.
advice: 1. Overview of this course, linkage between courses, and institutional objectives 2. Why science and engineering ethics (SEE) is necessary 3. What is SEE? Why should engineers have special responsibilities? 4. In what circumstances are engineers required to make ethical decisions? 5. What values should be emphasized by engineers? Professions and codes of ethics 6. How to act properly as an engineer: seven-step guide to ethical decision-making 7. Engineers in institutional contexts: SEE and business ethics 8. Actual case study 9. Ethical decision-making practice using the case method 10. SEE and the role of engineers in the international community 11. Engineers in the twenty-first century 12. Ethical issues in specific fields - Be interested in news related to S&T to develop an analytical attitude in terms of ethics. -Study independently when you encounter unfamiliar terms. -With the realization that you are a moral agent in the context of S&T, participate in ethical discussions in class as if you were the person involved in the issues, not a third party or a critic.
requiredKnowledge: - Review what you have learned from "Japanology (Japan and Japanese)" and "Engineers and Society." - Prepare for in-class group discussions based on your past experiences to ensure that they are constructive. - Read newspapers closely to be up-to-date with current political, economic, and cultural trends, as well as trends in S&T as a would-be professional engineer.

activityGoals.body: Explain interactions between society (including the economy) and S&T using examples.
Comprehend and explain responsibilities and core values (safety, etc.) as a professional engineer.
Have knowledge of codes of conduct; explain institutional (corporate) activities to promote ethical conduct.
Analyze and consider ethical dilemmas in connection with past experiences and gathered facts.
Not only comprehend the Sseven-step Guide to Ethical Decision Making, but also apply it to actual cases.
Comprehend the LOs of this course and KIT; evaluate your achievements from the perspective of a future engineer.

keywords: Business and Ethics 2.Corporate Social Responsibility 3.Work Style Reform 4.Environment and Economic Practice 5.Globalization and Ethics
educationalGoal: This course aims at acquisition of knowledge about business ethics and skills to solve problems which an engineer in a corporation could encounter. This course also aims at development of presentation skills. This training serves to foster the skills for using statistics and decision-making to ethical problems.
advice: This course consists of three part. First, ethical theories(class#2 to #4). Second, case studies(#5 to #10) and presentation seminar(#11 to #14). Classes are composed as follows: #1: Introduction #2 to #4: Ethical Theories(Normative Ethics, Egoism, Utilitarianism, Deontology, Theory of Justice, Stakeholder and Stockholder Theory and Corporate Social Responsibility) #5 to #10: Case studies(Food Fraud, Manipulative Advertisement, 'Black Enterprise', Suicide from Overwork, 'Work Style Reform', Dismantling of Oil Excavator, Biofuel and Destruction of Rainforest, Fairtrade and AI and Employment). #11 to #14: Presentation Seminar on recent topic about business ethics. #15: Self-Evaluation. Mini tests(class #1-#10) and report(about 3000 letters in Japanese) are required. Be careful for articles about business ethics on newspapers and the Internet. Preparations for the lecture is also required.
books: Ethics of Business, Mitsuhiro Umezu, Maruzen, 2002.
requiredKnowledge: Be aware of ethical problems concerning business and economy. Be sensitive about economy and practice of corporation through media and the Internet.

Be able to analyze ethical problems of business and find the solutions.

keywords: History of electromagnetism 2.Innovation 3.Social values 4.Culture and ethics 5.Social system
educationalGoal: In modern society, it is necessary to consider the essential relationships between science, technology, and social values by coordinating values (risk communication) and creating new values (innovation) among various stakeholders. This course focuses on the relationships between development of scientific knowledge and technology, the thoughts and behaviors of people, and history of relationships between social systems.
advice: Class summary: 1. Understand the problems of analyzing society with the theme of electricity. 2. Explain the historical development of electrical theory and technology. 3. Analyze various aspects of dependence on electrical technology in daily life, culture, and communication. 4. Analyze various aspects of the relationship between electrical technology and politics and economy. 5. Explain analytical methods to consider the above topics, hold group discussions, and write a research paper. Learning advice: A. For the topics of each lecture, pay attention to how your thoughts and behaviors are influenced by electrical technology in your daily life, and consider the social values of people in the past who had no such knowledge and technology. B. Try to identify and understand local issues and history from the perspective of electrical technology. C. Each assignment is prepared to help you write a research paper, in addition to preparing and reviewing each lecture. D. It takes substantial time to write a research paper. Prepare according to the lecture schedule. E. Research papers are also aimed at mastering university-level writing skills. Pay attention to the format.
requiredKnowledge: High school-level knowledge of electromagnetism is not required, but you should review knowledge from junior high school. Consult encyclopedias, dictionaries, reference books, and the Internet for unknown technical terms and personal names. Review the precautions learned in the basics of study when writing a research paper.

activityGoals.body: Be able to analyze social and cultural dependence on electrical technology in your daily life.
Be able to analyze electrical innovations from political, economic, and cultural perspectives.
Be able to discuss your own opinions logically and empirically based on historical research.
Be able to write a research paper in an academic format.
Be able to self-evaluate the relationship between this course and the college’s educational goals.

title: 科学技術と社会
subtitle: Science Technology and Society
courseType:

keywords: science, technology and society 2.media technology and social change 3.communication theory 4.contents production and literacy 5.community cooperation
educationalGoal: The course focuses on the linkage between communication technology and society. It deals with the science and technology. It aims to improve basic academic skills and organically connect them with specialized fields based on the Academic Foundation Programs. Students will acquire innovative knowledge on the diffusion of science and technology to equip with active information transmission processes. It also develops literacy skills through group discussions and individual content creation, which can be applied to later studies in specialized fields.
advice: This class aims to the relationship between science and technology and society, overlapping with various contemporary issues by following points; (1) To understand the evolution and development of media technology and social changes; (2) To expand knowledge by relating the evolution and development of media technology and social changes that people have been consciously and unconsciously involved in their daily lives; (3) To analyze the information and communication environment of a globalized society theoretically;(4) To understand and consider the relationship between communication theory and technology and society through class and group discussions; (5) To understand media theory and acquire literacy skills by creating content to experience the relationship between science and technology and society as an individual; and (6) To learn the relationship between science, technology, and society in the context of regional cooperation and reevaluate it concerning oneself * The class also focuses on the latest science and technology in the Hokuriku area. Students should be aware that science and technology are not generated in one aspect of time based on their daily social experiences but are innovations that extend the continuity of history.
books: [reference books] Communication Models - For the Study of Mass Communication [Rountledge] メディア用語基本辞典(Encyclopedia of Media & Communication Studies) [Sekai Shiso-sha] 社会は情報化の夢を見る(Society dreams of Informatization - John von Neumann's Dream related to the Desire of Modernity) [Kawade Shobo Shinsha]
requiredKnowledge: This course aims to enable students to deal with issues from a more diverse perspective and develop the ability to think independently about the state and position of Japan (as a people) by tracking science and technology and changes in the international community. Therefore, in addition to science and technology, students should pay attention to daily news from media channels that they have access to and be interested in the relationship between Japan and other countries in the international society and issues that need to be resolved internationally.

activityGoals.body: to be able to think about STS from one's point of view as liberal arts knowledge
to understand and explain how science and technology have developed in the context of human history
to understand and discuss the case of digitalization that has revolutionized broadcasting
to experience the characteristics of electronic media by creating digital voice content with narration
to write a research paper on STS based on academic literature, including English written articles
to be able to think about the nature of regional cooperation by self-assessing the STS learning related to SDGs

advice: Students will learn knowledge and procedures for health promotion through measurement and diagnosis in health and physical fitness, the development of safe and effective individual exercise prescription/training programs, lifestyle-related diseases, and health care procedures. requiredKnowledge: Taking an interest in various types of news and information about health and physical fitness. Preparing for physical activities and understanding safety management in sports activities.

lessons.content: 1. Guidance about annual courses of life-long sports classes 2. Guidance about this class 3. Explanation about the importance of health promotion throughout one's own life and the relationships with the contents of this class.

lessons.assignments: Review: Students should read handouts carefully. Assignment: Fill out a health assessment sheet on daily life habits.

lessons.content: 1. Physical fitness tests (physique, body composition, blood pressure, muscular strength, power, flexibility, etc.)
lessons.operation: Warm-up exercises will be done under a leader. Physical fitness tests will be conducted in cooperation with a few group members.
lessons.assignments: Assignment: Fill out the results of the physical fitness test and a health assessment sheet on daily life habits.

lessons.content: 1. Muscular strength test
lessons.operation: Warm-up exercises will be done under a leader. Students will understand how to use the training room and various training machines. Muscular strength tests will be conducted in cooperation with a few group members.
lessons.assignments: Assignment: Fill out the results of the muscular strength test and a health assessment sheet on daily life habits.

lessons.content: 1. Endurance test (20-m shuttle run)
lessons.operation: Warm-up exercises will be done under a leader. A 20-m shuttle run test will be done in cooperation with paired members.
lessons.assignments: Assignment: Fill out the results of the endurance test and a health assessment sheet on daily life habits.

lessons.content: 1. Assessment and analysis of one's own physical fitness characteristics
lessons.operation: This class will be conducted in the lecture hall. Students will summarize their own physical fitness test results, develop a profile of their own physical fitness characteristics, explain how to use the “health and fitness carte” system, and conduct a self-assessment test for mental health.
lessons.assignments: Assignment: Enter your own measurements data into the “health and fitness care” system, and develop a profile of your own physical fitness ( the date of submission follows the teacher's instruction). Fill out a health assessment sheet on daily life habits.

lessons.content: 1. Concepts and protocols of exercise prescription (development of training programs) 2. Review of attendance and learning approach in the previous classes.
lessons.operation: This class will be conducted in the lecture hall. Students will be explained the concepts and procedures of exercise prescription (training programs). Students will develop a personal training program based on the results of a physical fitness test. Attendance and learning approach in the previous classes will be reviewed.
lessons.assignments: Assignment: Develop “Report 2 ” related to exercise prescription (the date of submission follows the teacher's instruction). Fill out a health assessment sheet on daily life habits.

lessons.content: 1.About various health-related problems or familiar issues of sports
lessons.operation: This class will be conducted in the lecture hall. Students will be explained about various health-related problems or familiar issues of sports and discuss about them in a group.
lessons.assignments: Assignment: Develop reports based on group discussion. Fill out a health assessment sheet on daily life habits.

lessons.content: 1. Muscular strength training using strength-training machines; practice personal muscular strength training under an appropriate load for individuals.
lessons.operation: Warm-up exercises will be done under a leader. Students will learn muscular strength training methods with machines. Students will implement muscular strength training based on their own exercise prescription developed in the previous classes.
lessons.assignments: Assignment: Develop “Report 2 ” related to exercise prescription (the date of submission follows the teacher's instruction). Fill out a health assessment sheet on daily life habits.

lessons.content: 1.About the relationship between exercise and mental health.
lessons.operation: This class will be conducted in the lecture hall. Students will be explained about the relationship between exercise and mental health. Students will learn the necessity and importance of exercise for mental health.
lessons.assignments: Assignment: Fill out a health assessment sheet on daily life habits.

lessons.content: 1. Endurance training 2. Maximal and target heart rate 3. Rating of perceived exertion (RPE) scale Understand the appropriate exercise intensity based on heart rate, and the interrelationship between running pace, heart rate, and RPE score.
lessons.operation: Warm-up exercises will be done under a leader. Students will understand the relationship between running pace, heart rate, and RPE through monitoring heart rate during a 20-min paced run.
lessons.assignments: Assignment: Develop “Report 3 ” related to endurance raining (the date of submission follows the teacher's instruction). Fill out a health assessment sheet on daily life habits.

lessons.content: 1. Health promotion in daily life based on health, obesity, and lifestyle-related diseases.
lessons.operation: This class will be conducted in the lecture hall. Students will be explained the concept of lifestyle-related disease. Students will learn the necessity and importance of health promotion and its procedures.
lessons.assignments: Review: Important information about lifestyle-related diseases based on handouts. Assignments: Fill out a health assessment sheet on daily life habits.

lessons.content: 1. Shape-up training 2. Measurement of calorie consumption during various exercises Learn the various shape-up training methods. Understand the relationship between physical activities and calorie consumption.
lessons.operation: Warm-up exercises will be done under a leader. Students will understand the relationship between exercise volume and calorie consumption through various shape-up exercises.
lessons.assignments: Assignment: Develop “Report 3 ” related to shape-up training and calorie consumption (the date of submission follows the teacher's instruction). Fill out a health assessment sheet on daily life habits.

lessons.content: 1. Risk of drug dependence 2. A written test will be conducted.
lessons.operation: Students will consider various health-related problems including drug dependence and their coping behavior throughout group discussion. A written test will be conducted.
lessons.assignments: Assignment: Fill out a health assessment sheet on daily life habits.

lessons.content: 1. Core (trunk of the body) training Experience ball exercises and core training, and learn various training techniques that can be done at home.
lessons.operation: Warm-up exercises will be done under a leader. Students will engage in calisthenics or balance ball exercises.
lessons.assignments: Assignment: Fill out a health assessment sheet on daily life habits.

lessons.content: 1. Summarize the class contents. 2. Review of attendance, submission of reports, and grades. 3. Guidance about the “Academic Exercise in Lifelong Sports” course in the next term.
lessons.operation: This class will be conducted in the lecture hall. Attendance, submission of reports, and grades will be reviewed. The concept of the “Academic Exercise in Lifelong Sports” course in the next term will be explained.
lessons.assignments: Review: What was learned in class. Read the instructions for the “Academic Exercise in Lifelong Sports” course thoroughly, and keep until the beginning of the next term.

title: ビジネスコミュニケーション1
subtitle: Business Communication 1
courseType:
English Language Program
English Language Courses
keywords: Business English 2.Speaking and Listening 3.Reading and Writing 4.Presentation 5.Digital Literacy
educationalGoal: In this course, students will learn English that is used in business situations by setting the course in a (role-play) company. Students will learn vocabulary and phrases by completing business tasks and be expected to use them effectively. By participating in group activities, in addition to the four skills of speaking, listening, reading, and writing, students will learn the skills necessary for completing business situations through activities such as presentations, discussions, and role plays.
advice: 1. In order to learn English that is used in business situations, the majority of class will be conducted through group work. When completing projects, it will be necessary to work together with the other members of the group. 2. Group work includes activities such as presentations and discussions. English will be used for these activities. 3. While doing group work, each student must actively participate and contribute to complete the activities. - Students must try their best to use only English during class. - Students must actively participate in group activities. - Students must bring a Japanese-English dictionary to every class.
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of basic English grammar is necessary.

activityGoals.body: Learn vocabulary and phrases used in the workplace and use them appropriately in business settings.
Learn how to do business tasks such as product development, product proposals, and presentations.
Understand the differences between Japanese and foreign business cultures and appropriately apply them.
Learn the foundations of digital literacy and appropriately apply them.

Students will learn vocabulary and phrases by completing business tasks and be expected to use them effectively. By participating in group activities, in addition to the four skills of speaking, listening, reading, and writing, students will learn the skills necessary for completing business situations through activities such as presentations, discussions, interviews, and role plays.
    授業の概要および学習上の助言   1. In order to learn English that is used in business situations, the majority of class will be conducted through group work. When completing projects, it will be necessary to work together with the other members of the group. 2. Group work includes activities such as presentations and discussions. English will be used for these activities. 3. While doing group work, each student must actively participate and contribute to complete the activities. - Students must try their best to use only English during class. - Students must actively participate in group activities. - Students must bring a Japanese-English dictionary to every class.

title: アカデミックリーディング1

courseType:
English Language Program
English Language Courses
keywords: Intensive Reading 2.Vocabulary 3.Listening 4.Speaking 5.Watching TED talks
educationalGoal: There are 3 course objectives 1. Be able to read and understand passages in the textbook at an appropriate speed. 2. Be able to understand, read, and pronounce the vocabulary in the textbook. 3. Acquire the habit of watching TED talks and practice listening and reading as well as learn about current topics.
advice: Reading is a core component of listening, speaking, and writing skills. The objective of this course is to improve all 4 skills through reading passages at an appropriate speed to understand the content. The following topics will be covered: Unit 5: Finding Wonders. Unit 6: Reef Encounters. Unit 7: Dollars and Scents. Unit 8: Great Explorers. Extra readings will be distributed in class. Active learning in English class includes presentations, Q&A sessions, pair-work, group work, and worksheets. Preview: Read the story, check the content, pronunciation, vocabulary, and answer all of the questions in the textbook. In class: Ask questions and solve any problems you have encountered during the preview. Review: Check the content and pronunciation of the words in the story and memorize the vocabulary. Use office hours to ask extra questions. Make watching TED talks a habit. Make study plans throughout the semester.
requiredKnowledge: Students must have a basic knowledge of grammar and vocabulary. There will be daily quizzes. Quizzes will be collected after students check the answers and scores, so each student must keep a record of their progress.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the topic of the story in each unit.
Be able to understand the structure of paragraphs and stories.
Be able to read, listen, pronounce, and write the words in the story in each unit.
Be able to find specific information about each story using various reading skills at an appropriate speed.
Be able to understand the story and exchange opinions with other students.
Have the habit of watching TED talks.

educationalGoal: In this course, students will acquire basic English writing skills. Students will be able to: (1) Compose grammatically correct English sentences. books: Textbook: Trio Writing 1 (Oxford) Reference books: none Reserved books: none
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of basic English grammar and basic computer skills are required.

title: STEMイングリッシュ
subtitle: STEM English
courseType:
English Language Program
English Language Courses
keywords: Speaking/ Listening 2.Reading/ Writing 3.STEM 4.CLIL 5.Collaborative Competence
educationalGoal: In this course, students will acquire four skills (reading, writing, speaking, and listening) using English in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM). The aim is to acquire the ability to find and solve problems in STEM fields. Find out more about the issues covered and gain the ability to communicate your opinions and ideas in English through discussions and presentations.
advice: In this course, students will gain content knowledge and apply what they have learned to solve a range of different STEM related problems. An outline of the activities is as follows. 1. Science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) centered course 2. Content language integrated learning (CLIL) approach 3. Learn about and apply the scientific method to a range of topics 4. Plan and conduct investigations 5. Collect and analyze data from experiments 6. Report the findings from a range of STEM investigations Be sure to check e-syllabus before each class. Use English videos and related articles for teaching materials. The preparation / review includes activities other than those performed in class, such as interview activities.
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of basic English grammar is required.

activityGoals.body: Can describe STEM issues and research methods in English.
Can analyze the issues in English.
Explain collected data and analysis results in English using graphs and diagrams.
Understand your role during activities and work on issues in teams.
Effectively report the results of activities using presentation software and present solutions.

title: イングリッシュセミナー
subtitle: English Seminar
courseType:
English Language Program
English Language Courses
keywords: Speaking/ Listening 2.Reading/ Writing 3.PBL 4.Collaboration Competence 5.Cooperating with community
educationalGoal: This course aims to develop the skills to identify and solve problems in the local society. Students will conduct research on the chosen topic/issue and express their ideas through group work and discussions.
advice: The class will be conducted through the following steps: 1. Design Thinking Workshop 2. Ethnographic studies (Interview or photo study) 3. Needs identification 4. Ideation (Generate ideas, develop concept, and select design concept) 5. Prototype construction 6. Proposal of solution and acquisition of user feedback 7. Improvement of prototype based on feedback 8. Presentation of solution It is necessary to check the e-syllabus site before each class for homework materials and to listen to the audio files. Homework includes activities such as interviewing non-Japanese people as well.
requiredKnowledge: Students started English studies at KIT from Topics 5 or passed an intermediate-level course with a grade of A or higher.

activityGoals.body: Be able to conduct interviews (on campus or outside the campus) and collect information in English.
Be able to analyze the data and find problems in English
Be able to find solutions to problems in English.
Be able to understand their role in a group and work collaboratively.
Be able to present their results in English.

educationalGoal: This class is for students who started from English Topics 5 (intermediate class) or for students who want to further improve their TOIEC scores for job hunting or going to graduate school. Students will learn the test taking techniques nessesary to improve each part of the TOEIC test. Students will learn skills for listening, grammar, and reading comprehention.
advice: Students will have to attend every class from Monday to Friday. They must have the motivation to give all their time and effort to improve their TOEIC scores during the 3 intensive weeks of study. Students will have to take the pre- and post-course IP tests. Students are strongly encouraged to take the official TOEIC test right after finishing this course. This class is dedicated to improving the TOEIC scores by learning test-taking strategies for listening, grammar, and reading comprehension. This class does not focus on communicative skills or grammar. Students must improve those skills on their own during this course. Active learning includes presentations, Q & A, pair work, and group work.

subtitle: Japanese for Science and Technology 2
courseType:

English Language Courses
keywords: Japanese Language 2.English Language 3.PBL 4.Collaborating with community
educationalGoal: This course aims to develop the skills to identify and solve problems in the local society. Students will conduct research on a chosen topic/issue and express their ideas through collaboration and discussion.
advice: The class will be conducted through the following steps: 1. Design Thinking Workshop 2. Ethnographic studies (Interview or photo study) 3. Needs identification 4. Ideation (Generate ideas, develop concept, and select design concept) 5. Prototype construction 6. Proposal of solution and acquisition of user feedback 7. Improvement of prototype based on feedback 8. Presentation of solution Students will receive homework materials from the instructor via email before each class. Homework includes activities such as a field study as well. Class will be held every week and will be conducted either in-person, on /Zoom or via on-demand lessons.
requiredKnowledge: Advanced Japanese and English language language proficiency

activityGoals.body: Be able to conduct interviews (on campus or outside the campus) and collect information in Japanese and English
Be able to analyze the data and find problems in Japanese and English
Be able to find solutions to problems in Japanese and English
Be able to present their results in Japanese and English

title: 線形代数Ⅰ
subtitle: Linear Algebra I
courseType:
Mathematics and Science Program
Mathematics and Science Courses
keywords: Vectors and Scalars 2.Dot product, Cross product 3.Operations of Matrices 4.Row Reduction 5.Linear Maps
educationalGoal: Students will learn: (1) vector operations. (2) matrix operations. (3) solving linear systems using “row reduction.” (4) representing linear transformations of a plane or a space.
advice: This is a basic course in linear algebra. We will cover the following topics: 1. Vectors 1.1 Vectors and their operations 1.2 Dot products and cross products of vectors 1.3 The equation of a plane or a line 2. Matrices and linear maps 2.1 Matrices and their operations 2.2 Linear systems and row reduction 2.3 Linear maps and linear transformation Classes include exercises and quizzes; a final examination will be given at the end of the semester. Daily preparation and review are important. Students are required to complete the designated tasks. Students should prepare reports and study research topics in a planned manner, and strictly avoid plagiarism. Students are expected to utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center or the office hours of the teacher.
books: Textbook: Linear Algebra I (KIT Math and Science Academic Foundations Programs) Reference book: A First Course in Linear Algebra (Open Textbook Library)[Lyryx]
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of mathematics, especially trigonometric functions.

activityGoals.body: Understand the concept of vectors and be able to properly perform vector operations.
Understand the concept of matrices and be able to properly perform matrix operations.
Be able to find solutions to linear systems by using row reduction.
Understand the concept of a linear transforms and be able to represent them in matrix form.
Understand the meanings of fundamental english words for mathematics.
Understand the contents of the course and be able to complete the required tasks by the announced deadlines.

subtitle: Math and Science for Environmental Engineering and Architecture
courseType:

keywords: Exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions 2.Calculus 3.Statistics 4.Excel 5.Community cooperation
educationalGoal: Students will (1) acquire the necessary mathematical knowledge of functions, calculus, and statistics for structural, soil, and fluid mechanics, materials, surveying, and environmental engineering. (2) understand the importance of fundamental mathematics for solving problems in architecture and civil engineering. (3) apply mathematical knowledge to various problems.
advice: This is a course on the fundamental mathematics used in structural mechanics, soil mechanics, fluid mechanics, materials technology, surveying, and environmental engineering. Students will apply the learned mathematics to analyze various phenomena related to architecture and environmental civil engineering. Students are expected to (1) deepen their mathematical understanding of exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions, and tackle real problems requiring the application of this knowledge. (2) deepen their mathematical understanding of differentiation and integration, and tackle real problems requiring the application of this knowledge. (3) understand basic operations and graph drawings and data analysis by using Excel. (4) learn statistical data processing methods and analyze data generated in experiments. (5) utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center and the teachers of the architecture and the civil engineering. This course should make it possible for students to apply their knowledge of fundamental mathematics to solve architecture and environmental civil engineering problems.

Ability to understand the meanings of fundamental English words for mathematics and architecture etc.

keywords: n-base, numeral system 2.Floating point number 3.Sets and logic 4.Logical circuit 5.Organizing data and basic statistics
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn how to express n-base and floating point numbers (IEEE754). (2) apply the concept of sets to logical algebra and learn the basics of how to represent logic in a computer. Learn how to configure logic circuits to implement logic in a computer. (3) learn basic probabilities, conditional probabilities, and Bayes' theorem. Learn basic data organization and statistics using Excel.
advice: This is a basic course in mathematics, logic, and statistics. We will cover the following topics: 1. n-base: binary system, octal system, hexadecimal system. 2. Representation of numbers in computers: Floating point number (IEEE754). 3. Sets and Logic: basic set theory, propositional logic, truth table, logical circuit. 4. Basic probabilities: Permutations and combinations, probabilities, conditional probabilities and Bayes' theorem. 5: A data analysis method using statistics: Frequency distribution table, histogram, correlation diagram, mean/variance, covariance/correlation coefficient. Students are expected to understand above materials. Students are expected to process data using Excel (computer spreadsheet software). Students are expected to complete the exercises on their own without consulting/copying others. Students are expected to utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center or the office hours of the teacher.

keywords: Data science 2.Random variables & probability distributions 3.Statistical processing 4.Statistical processing by R or Python 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: In modern society, a large amount of data can be easily collected due to the development of information technology. An academic field that statistically analyzes and evaluates a large amount of data is called data science. In this course, we will conduct practical exercises and understand the mathematical meaning of statistical analysis of numerical data, which is a basic method of data science. Also, learn statistical processing methods and expression techniques using computer software such as R and Python.
advice: This is a basic course in statistics. We will cover the following topics: 1. Data science. 2. Mathematical meaning of probability . 3. Probability distributions. 4. Data analysis methods using statistics. Students are expected to understand that measurement data in an experiment have variation and that this variation is a variable associated with a stochastic phenomenon. Students are expected to understand the normal distribution as a common probability distribution function. Students are expected to learn statistics in data analysis, including correlation and regression analysis. Students are expected to analyze data using Excel (computer spreadsheet software). Students are expected to complete the exercises on their own and not copy/consult with others.
requiredKnowledge: Mathematics skills learned in Mathematics for Information Science. Basic computer skills.

title: 情報数理B
subtitle: Mathematics for Information Science B
courseType:
Mathematics and Science Program
Mathematics and Science Courses
keywords: Multivariate analysis 2.Prediction model 3.Multiple regression analysis 4.Principal component analysis
educationalGoal: In evaluation problems related to humanities and social sciences, many properties must be often handled simultaneously and comprehensively, and multivariate analysis methods can often provide effective solutions. In this course, students will learn the concepts of and ways of using multivariate analysis via Excel functions. The primary goal is to give them the opportunity to master the method of prediction analysis and learn how to summarize multivariate data. Another goal is to ensure they are capable of using these methods in future learning activities.
advice: The course focuses on the following items: 1. Features and summary of multivariate analysis (prediction and data summarization) 2. The concept and use method of multiple regression analysis 3. The concept and use method of principal component analysis 4. How to use Excel functions Students are expected to review the basic knowledge of linear algebra. In addition, they should learn the contents of descriptive statistics in “Statistics for Information”. It is also desirable to understand the contents of hypothesis testing.
requiredKnowledge: Review linear algebra (i.e., matrices and vectors). Students must be sure to master the lecture contents by reviewing because each item is closely related to previous lessons. Bring a laptop PC (unless otherwise noted) because the lessons will always include practice sessions using Excel.

activityGoals.body: Be able to use multivariate analysis in future learning activities such as Project Design III.
Be able to distinguish the prediction model concept from the data summarization concept.
Be able to understand the basic concepts and application methods of multiple regression analysis.
Be able to understand the basic concepts and application methods of principal component analysis.

title: アドバンスト情報数理A
subtitle: Advanced Mathematics for Information Science A
courseType:
Mathematics and Science Program
Mathematics and Science Courses
keywords: Partial Derivative 2.Chain Rule 3.Second Derivative Test 4.Double Integral 5.Change of Variables
educationalGoal: Problems in nature are often expressed as two-variable functions or multivariable functions. In this course, students will learn how to: (1) derive partial derivatives. (2) find the extreme values of two-variable functions. (3) calculate a double integral using the iterated integral approach. (4) calculate a double integral using the change of variables approach.
advice: This is an advanced course following single-variable calculus and includes: 1. Multivariable functions, their limits and continuity, and partial derivatives. 2. Tangent plane and total differential for a multivariable function. 3. The chain rule in several variables. 4. Higher order partial derivatives and Taylor expansion of two-variable functions. 5. Maxima and minima of two-variable functions. 6. Iterated integration and reversing the order of integration. 7. Change of variables in a double integral. Students are required to actively participate in class and to engage in the review and preview in every class. Students are required to work on exercises after class and are expected to understand the contents of each class. Students are required to explain carefully and logically the solution procedure in their homework and report. Students should actively use the teachers' office hours and the Math. and Science Education Research Center.
books: Textbook: Advanced Mathematics A (Partial Derivative & Double Integral) [Kanazawa Institute of Technology]
requiredKnowledge: Preliminary knowledge must include an understanding of the basic mathematical concepts studied in the first year; for example, the basics of single-variable calculus and the inner and outer products of vectors learned in linear algebra.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the concepts of multivariable functions and the calculation of partial derivatives.
Be able to find partial derivatives by applying the chain rule.
Be able to find the extreme values of two-variable functions.
Be able to understand the concept of multiple integration and perform it by iterated integration.
Be able to find the value of a double integral by variable transformation, especially polar transformation.
Attend every class, make a strong effort to understand the course contents and English mathematical expressions.

keywords: Error and accuracy 2.Data handling 3.Random variable & Probability distribution 4.Statistical processing 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: Students will learn: (1) how to analyze and evaluate data obtained from experimental surveys using statistical methods. (2) the mathematical meaning of the analyzed and evaluated data. (3) how to use Excel to perform statistical processing and create graphs of statistical results.(Class management and a special lecture will be given in cooperation with local residents and companies.)
advice: This is a basic course in statistics. We will cover the following topics: 1. Error and accuracy of measured results. 2. Normal distribution. 3. Basics of descriptive statistics and their mathematical concepts. 4. Data analysis methods using statistics. Students are expected to understand that the measurement data in an experiment have variation and that this variation is a variable associated with a stochastic phenomenon. Students are expected to understand the normal distribution as a common probability distribution function. Students are expected to learn statistics in data analysis, including correlation and regression analysis. Students are expected to analyze data using Excel (computer spreadsheet software). Students are expected to complete the exercises on their own and not copy/consult with others. Students are expected to utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center or the office hours of the teacher

title: 基礎化学
subtitle: Fundamental Chemistry
courseType:
Mathematics and Science Program
Mathematics and Science Courses
term:
2021年度
 1st year 2nd semester
2nd year 1st semester

keywords: Electron Configuration 2.Chemical Bond 3.Chemical Reaction 4.Ideal Gas Law 5.Chemical Equilibrium
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn the chemical foundations necessary for science and engineering. (2) learn how to apply attitude and chemistry knowledge to science and engineering. (3) establish a style of study using a preview and review approach. (4) develop an autonomous and consecutive self-directed study ability.
advice: This is a course in chemical foundations. We will cover the following: 1. Atomic Structure, Electron Configuration, Periodic Table, Ionization Energy, and Electron Affinity. 2. Chemical Bond, Hybrid Orbital, Electronegativity, and Polarity of Molecules. 3. Calculation of Unknown Molecular Weights Using the “Ideal Gas Law” from Given Conditions. 4. Expressions for Various Concentrations of Solutions, Molarity, and Molar Fractions. 5. Expressions for Reaction Rate and the Temperature Dependence of Reaction Rate. 6. Chemical Equilibrium, Ionization Equilibrium of Electrolyte Solution, and Calculation of pH. 7. Reaction of Acid and Base, Oxidation-reduction Reaction, and Organic Compounds. (1) The class will follow the order of the contents in the textbook according to this syllabus. (2) Students are expected to do the homework, previews, and reviews for every class. (3) Students are expected to ask the teacher questions and use the Math. and Science Education Research Center. (4) Students are expected not to be late, as the accumulation of learning is important. (5) Students are expected to approach exams and quizzes with sufficient preparation. (6) Some details of the course may be changed as the course progresses.
books: Textbooks:John Kenkel, “Basic Chemistry Concepts and Exercises”, CRC Press Reference books:John Mcmarry, “Organic Chemistry”, Brooks/Cole Pub Co Peter Atkins, De Paula, Julio, James Keeler, “Atkins' Physical Chemistry”, Oxford Univ Pr Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge: (1) High school chemistry is not a prerequisite. However, students will need to work hard in the course and make sufficient effort to master the topics. (2) Students are expected to read the textbook, complete the homework, and engage in the previews and reviews. (3) Students are expected to solve simple computational problems without using a calculator.

activityGoals.body: Understand the periodic law of elements and explain basic orbital properties.
Explain basic chemical bonds, the mechanism of hybrid orbitals, and electronegativity.
Calculate an unknown molecular weight and amount of substance using the ideal gas law.
Understand the concentration of solutions and chemical equilibrium, explain it, and calculate pH.
Understand and explain the mechanism of oxidation-reduction reaction, etc.
Attendance at every class and acquisition of English explanations and consecutive self-directed study ability.

    授業の概要および学習上の助言   This is a course in chemical foundations. We will cover the following: 1. Atomic Structure, Electron Configuration, Periodic Table, Ionization Energy, and Electron Affinity. 2. Chemical Bond, Hybrid Orbital, Electronegativity, and Polarity of Molecules. 3. Calculation of Unknown Molecular Weights Using the “Ideal Gas Law” from Given Conditions. 4. Expressions for Various Concentrations of Solutions, Molarity, and Molar Fractions. 5. Expressions for Reaction Rate and the Temperature Dependence of Reaction Rate. 6. Chemical Equilibrium, Ionization Equilibrium of Electrolyte Solution, and Calculation of pH. 7. Reaction of Acid and Base, Oxidation-reduction Reaction, and Organic Compounds. (1) The class will follow the order of the contents in the textbook according to this syllabus. (2) Students are expected to do the homework, previews, and reviews for every class. (3) Students are expected to ask the teacher questions and use the Math. and Science Education Research Center. (4) Students are expected not to be late, as the accumulation of learning is important. (5) Students are expected to approach exams and quizzes with sufficient preparation. (6) Some details of the course may be changed as the course progresses.

keywords: Newton's Laws 2.Work 3.Mechanical Energy 4.Rotational Motion 5.Motion of Rigid Body
educationalGoal: Student will learn: (1) how to calculate position, velocity, and acceleration of motion. (2) the concept of Newton's laws of motion. (3) the concept of force, work, energy, and conservation of energy. (4) how to calculate physical quantities in rotational motion. (5) the basis of oscillatory motion.
advice: This is a basic course in classical mechanics in physics. The laws of physics, based on mechanics and physics, are applicable to other sciences and technologies. Therefore, it is very important to acquire knowledge of mechanics. We will cover the following topics: 1. Dimension and units. 2. Motion in one dimension. 3. Motion in two dimensions. 4. Newton's laws of motion. 5. Energy of a system. 6. Conservation of energy. 7. Rotational motion. 8. Oscillatory motion. Students are required to have a knowledge of vectors, differentiation, and integration. Students will learn a number of formulas related to the laws of physics. Students will not only be expected to memorize the formulas but also be required to understand the meaning of these formulas.
books: Textbooks:Serway Basic Physics (mechanics) [Tokyo Kagaku Dougin] Reference books:5th Edition Physics Basics [Gakujutsu Tosho Shuppan-sha Co., Ltd.] Reserved books:Principles of Physics: A Calculus-Based Text, Hybrid (with WebAssign Printed Access Code) 5th Edition [Brooks/Cole Pub]
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of mechanics such as speed, acceleration, and force. Knowledge of mathematics such as vectors, trigonometric ratios, differential methods, integral methods, and the ability to calculate accurately.

activityGoals.body: Basic knowledge of mechanics such as speed, acceleration, and force.
Ability to evaluate the motion of an object by deriving and solving Newton's equations of motion.
Ability to calculate potential energy using integral calculus and a knowledge of work and energy.
Ability to evaluate the rolling motion of a rigid object by deriving and solving relevant equations.
Ability to understand basic physics vocabulary and phrases.
Ability to understand the content of the lesson by completing the homework and paticipating in group activities.

keywords: Structure of the cell 2.control of gene expression 3.continuity of life 4.evolution/diversity 5.life-science technology
educationalGoal: During the long evolutionary history of life on Earth, organisms have been modified in many different ways. The human organism is included in this process. The driving force of evolution is diversity. In this course, we will learn about life, the environment and relationships among organisms.
advice: The 21st century has been called the Century of Life Science. Biology is a complex study in a new frame, whether taught by liberal arts faculty or by physical science faculty. We will develop the power to think about the subject rather than place an overemphasis on detailed content knowledge. Elements of the class will include: (1) Structure and functions of life (2) The continuity of life (3) Response and regulation in organisms (4) Organisms and their environment (5) Life-science technology and society Classes will be conducted using various methods: lectures, seminars, video viewing or a combination of these.

educationalGoal: Students will (1) acquire basic knowledge of probability. (2) learn probability calculations using Bayes' theorem. requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of basic calculus.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the concept of probability and calculate probability using the laws probability.
Be able to calculate mean and variance for random variables.
Be able to analyze data by calculating the necessary statistics from data.
Be able to estimate and test population mean, variance, and population ratio using a sample distribution.
Understand the meanings of fundamental english words for statistics.
Be able to understand the contents of each class, work on assigned tasks, and attend every class.

title: アドバンスト数理B
subtitle: Advanced Mathematics B
courseType:
Mathematics and Science Program
Mathematics and Science Courses
keywords: 1st order ODEs and properties of their solutions 2.2nd order homogeneous linear ODEs 3.2nd order inhomogeneous linear ODEs 4.Simultaneous systems of linear ODEs 5.Mathematical models for phenomena and analyses of their solutions
educationalGoal: Various issues in engineering, science and social science are often described by differential equations. Students will learn how to solve 1st order ordinary differential equations (ODEs), 2nd order constant-coefficient linear ODEs and systems of simultaneous linear ODEs, and will understand (1) how to construct mathematical models of phenomena, (2) concrete solution method and (3) how to analyze solution properties and characteristics. The students will join computing project using MATLAB, and will gain experience to apply ODEs to real various problems.
advice: In the class, the students will learn differential equations (ODEs): (1) 1st order ODEs, (2) 2nd order constant-coefficient linear ODEs (homogeneous and inhomogeneous ODEs), and (3) systems of 1st order simultaneous linear ODEs. The students will learn the following analytical methods: (I) How to express physical and social phenomena with ODEs (construction of mathematical models). (II) How to solve specific types of ODEs. (III) Analytical methods in which students will analyze obtained solutions and acquire information pertinent to the activities of engineers such as the pattern and the speed of changes in various phenomena. After the student learn the main themes of ODEs, the students will apply the above knowledge (I), (II), and (III) to computing projects by using formula manipulation system, and submit a report of their results. In the class, the students will use MATLAB in the following activities: 1) Visualizing the solutions for ODEs. 2) Setting and evaluating the parameters of ODEs. 3) Modeling physical phenomena and deriving and analyzing their solutions. Therefore, the students should install MATLAB on individual notebook computer, and should master basic usage of MATLAB beforehand.
books: Textbooks:Advanced Engineering Mathematics 1: Ordinary Differential Equation (8th Edition) [Baifukan] Reference books:None Reserved books:Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 10th Edition [John Wiley & Sons, Inc.]
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of differential and integral calculations, basic differential equations, and linear algebra in the subjects: Integrated Math and Science for Engineering I & II, Linear Algebra I & II. Basic computer skills for computing projects.

activityGoals.body: Be able to construct 1st order ODEs for various phenomena and obtain the solutions.
Be able to construct 2nd order linear ODEs for various phenomena and obtain the solutions.
Be able to construct simultaneous systems of 1st order ODEs for various phenomena and obtain the solutions.
Be able to analyze solutions obtained from ODEs and evaluate the pattern and speed of changes in phenomena.
Be able to understand the meanings of fundamental english words for mathematics.
Be able to understand the class contents by completing the homework and attending every class.

title: プロジェクトデザイン入門(実験)(機械工学科)
subtitle: Design Project / Introduction (Mechanical Engineering)
courseType:
Practical Engineering Education Program
Practical Engineering Education Courses
keywords: Verification process 2.Verification process 3.Basic skills 4.Data handling skills 5.PBL for science and technology
educationalGoal: -To gain the basic skills needed in processes from finding problems to solutions. -To understand phenomena, objectives, and events quantitatively and qualitatively. -To be able to find characteristics and laws of phenomena, objectives, and events. -To be able to deliver the above information to a third person intelligibly. -To gain various basic skills to proceed smoothly with verification activities. -To be able to have a picture of technology fields and engineers of discipline.
advice: ・In this course, students learn the basic skills required for inspection and problem-solving in order to achieve the above learning objectives. ・This course focuses on the distinctive experiments of the department of mechanical engineering. ・Students learn the basic skills of data handling required to collect, organize, analyze, hypothesize, visualize, and report data. ・Students learn the basic skills of project-based learning for engineering including the process for problem discovery skills, problem-solving skills and inspection skills. ・In the guidance, students understand how to proceed with class, precautions, and how to use classrooms and laboratories. In addition, students will learn awareness and actions for the safety experiments by attending a safety seminar. ・Students learn how to communicate to visualize their thoughts or the contents of their reports. ・Students learn about experimental equipment and units, and learn how to evaluate experimental results. ・Students work on different experimental themes every week. ・Students collect a wide range of knowledge and information necessary to organize the results of the experiments, and make a report based on the information. ・Students present the experimental results using posters or PowerPoint.
requiredKnowledge: We advise students to become engineers who think and act on their own initiative. Students should actively ask questions about things that they don't understand, but should have their own thoughts in advance. For the collection of information, students will collect information for the purpose of the experiment by utilizing library centers, etc. It is necessary to master how to use a personal computer and a network printer.

educationalGoal: -To gain the basic skills needed in processes from finding problems to solutions. -To understand phenomena, objectives, and events quantitatively and qualitatively. -To be able to find characteristics and laws of phenomena, objectives, and events. -To be able to deliver the above information to a third person intelligibly. -To gain various basic skills to proceed smoothly with verification activities. -To be able to have a picture of technology fields and engineers of discipline.
advice: In this course, students will learn the basic skills required for the validation process and problem-solving process in order to achieve the above-mentioned learning and education goals. In addition, this course focuses on the characteristic experiments of the department.One is to learn the basics of “data handling skills” required to collect, organize, analyze, hypothesis test, visualize, and report data. The following six project themes will be dealt with, focusing on "Direct Current". (1) Ohm's Law, (2) Power Supplies, (3) Electric Flux Lines & Equipotential Lines, (4) Resistors in Series & in Parallel, (5) Kirchhoff's Laws & Superposition Theorem, (6) Joule's Law In order to secure the necessary experiment time, the class will be conducted on the premise of preparation. Always be aware of “safety” during the experiment. In each project, the first week is centered on the acquisition of knowledge and skills necessary for the experiment, and the second week is to tackle the missions using the knowledge and techniques acquired by the team in the first week.
books: Design Project / Introduction of 2021 (Experiment) (Electrical and Electronic Engineering), Kanazawa Institute of Technology
requiredKnowledge: Each project covers the basic laws and phenomena handled in classes such as "Electric Circuit I" and "Electromagnetics I / II". Challenge the experiment with awareness of the "connection" with these subjects. When collecting information, it is good to use information that suits the purpose of the experiment, such as a Library Center or the Internet. In addition, since reports and posters are created on a personal computer, it is necessary to quickly learn how to use the personal computer and how to use the campus printer.

Students learn "data handling skills" and "science and technology PBL" through experiments on basic laws related to electrical and electronic engineering.In “Data Handling Skills”, students acquire and establish knowledge essential for planning, designing, executing, and operating various projects, and learn how to use various measuring instruments. “Science and Engineering PBL (Project Based Learning)” cultivates problem discovery and resolution skills through project issues. The following six project themes will be dealt with, focusing on "Direct Current". (1) Ohm's Law, (2) Power Supplies, (3) Electric Flux Lines & Equipotential Lines, (4) Resistors in Series & in Parallel, (5) Kirchhoff's Laws & Superposition Theorem, (6) Joule's Law In order to secure the necessary experiment time, the class will be conducted on the premise of preparation. Always be aware of “safety” during the experiment. In each project, the first week is centered on the acquisition of knowledge and skills necessary for the experiment, and the second week is to tackle the missions using the knowledge and techniques acquired by the team in the first week.

subtitle: Design Project / Introduction (Architecture)
courseType:
Practical Engineering Education Program
Practical Engineering Education Courses
keywords: Verification process 2.Problem-solving process 3.Basic skills 4.Data handling skills 5.PBL for science and technology
educationalGoal: To gain the basic skills needed in processes from finding problems to solutions. -To understand phenomena, objectives, and events quantitatively and qualitatively. -To be able to find characteristics and laws of phenomena, objectives, and events. -To be able to deliver the above information to a third person intelligibly. -To gain various basic skills to proceed smoothly with verification activities. -To be able to have a picture of technology fields and engineers of discipline.
advice: In this course, to achieve the above educational goals, the students will learn basic skills required for verification and problem-solving processes. This course will deal with characteristic things of corresponding department. One is that the students will learn basics of “data-handling skills” needed for collection → organization → analysis→ hypothesis → visualization → report. One is that the students will learn basic skills of “PBL for science and technology” including basic elements of processes from problem-finding to solution and verification activities. By the experiment of the field of building structure, students perform the strength examination of the paper structure which students made by a team. Students put the structure which students made between the fulcrums of 40cm in a structure object similar to a bridge, and loading does a weight at the center. Students compete with weight before a structure collapsing for durability time. Students make the structure from the design characteristics of the shape and a structural mechanics-like viewpoint using paper material. Students make an insulation material of 15cm *15cm at thickness 3cm every team and, by the experiment of the field of building environment, measure the insulation performance. The insulation performance measures a heat flux level or surface temperature and calculates it using the data. The material to use for an insulation material concentrates an idea every team and devises composition of the material.

    授業の概要および学習上の助言   In this course, to achieve the above educational goals, the students will learn basic skills required for verification and problem-solving processes. This course will deal with characteristic things of corresponding department. One is that the students will learn basics of “data-handling skills” needed for collection → organization → analysis→ hypothesis → visualization → report. One is that the students will learn basic skills of “PBL for science and technology” including basic elements of processes from problem-finding to solution and verification activities. By the experiment of the field of building structure, students perform the strength examination of the paper structure which students made by a team. Students put the structure which students made between the fulcrums of 40cm in a structure object similar to a bridge, and loading does a weight at the center. Students compete with weight before a structure collapsing for durability time. Students make the structure from the design characteristics of the shape and a structural mechanics-like viewpoint using paper material. Students make an insulation material of 15cm *15cm at thickness 3cm every team and, by the experiment of the field of building environment, measure the insulation performance. The insulation performance measures a heat flux level or surface temperature and calculates it using the data. The material to use for an insulation material concentrates an idea every team and devises composition of the material.

keywords: Verification process 2.Problem-solving process 3.Basic skills 4.Data handling skills 5.PBL for science and technology
educationalGoal: -To gain the basic skills needed in processes from finding problems to solutions. -To understand phenomena, objectives, and events quantitatively and qualitatively. -To be able to find characteristics and laws of phenomena, objectives, and events. -To be able to deliver the above information to a third person intelligibly. -To gain various basic skills to proceed smoothly with verification activities. -To be able to have a picture of technology fields and engineers of discipline.
advice: In this course, to achieve the above educational goals, the students will learn the basic skills required for verification and problem-solving processes. This course will deal with characteristic things of the corresponding department. One is that the students will learn the basic "data-handling skills" needed for data collection → organization → analysis→ hypothesis testing → visualization → reporting. subtitle: Design Project II
courseType:
Practical Engineering Education Program
Practical Engineering Education Courses
keywords: Problem solving skills 2.Logical thinking 3.Project-Based Learning 4.On-the-Job Training (OJT) 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: You will be able to gain experience, knowledge, and skills to: Perform activities based on logical thinking; Perform activities to solve an open-ended problem; Gather and utilize individual knowledge to solve problems; and Explore and creatively discover new problems.
advice: - Project teams will work to gather new and previously gained knowledge, information, and experience towards solving real world problems of others. - The Main Theme will be presented by the instructor in class. - Through the project design activities, students are expected to be able to perform ‘activities based on logical thinking’, and their activities focus on: (a) Understanding required resources (information and experience), and making and evaluating decisions made logically based on data, facts, and truth; (b) Realizing characteristics of problems involved in human activities and needs of accumulating learning experiences of different fields of study; (c) Realizing the importance of finding Project Themes in a suited area defined by abilities; (d) Paying attention on problems and situations existing in the real world; (e) Ways to proceed activities (works) in a team (organization), and ways to find roles as a team member as simulation of OJT; (f) Ways to interact with others of different social positions; and (g) Realizing individual abilities by using basic knowledge through problem-solving process.
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge and experience learned and gained prior to the beginning of the course.

activityGoals.body: To be able to make and evaluate the decision made logically based on data, facts, and truth.
To be able to understand and gain resources (information and experience, etc.) required for project activities.
To be able to find a Project Theme appropriate for needs, abilities, and compensations from the Main Theme.
To be able to realize existing problems and develop awareness of problem-finding in the real world.
To be able to proceed effective project activities efficiently as a team (organization).
To be able to self-evaluate abilities objectively.

title: プロジェクトデザイン実践(実験)(機械)
subtitle: Design Project / Implementing and Operating (Mechanical Engineering)
courseType:
Practical Engineering Education Program
Practical Engineering Education Courses
keywords: Verification process 2.Effectiveness/Acceptability 3.Data handling skills 4.Credibility 5.PBL for science and technology
educationalGoal: -To gain skills to verify hypotheses or solution concept with logical approaches. -To understand phenomena, objects and events quantitatively with high credibility. -To reliably find characteristics and laws of phenomena, objects, events. -To deliver the above information to a third person intelligibly. -To gain basic skills to credibly and smoothly conduct verification activities. -To have an image of the technology fields and engineers in the discipline.
advice: -Learn how to proceed with the hypothesis testing process. Learn the process of verifying the effectiveness/acceptability of methods aimed at solving problems. -Learn "data processing skills" necessary for data collection, organization, analysis, hypothesis, visualization, and reporting. -Students will learn "skills to advance the verification process" and "basic skills of verification activities" from hypothesis planning to verification. -The Department of Mechanical Engineering has the theme of "heat sink," which is a heat dissipation mechanism for engines, etc., as the basis of thermal engineering. -Performance has been verified with experimental tests and evidence-based prototypes. -Based on this validation, you will learn data collection skills, validation process progress skills, and validation factor solution proposals. [Activity report] Regardless of the effectiveness of the solution proposal, the results of the project activities are compiled into a project report and presented in a poster session or verbally.
requiredKnowledge: Comprehensive experience in "investigation of information", "how to put out ideas", "experimental methods", and "problem discovery / problem solving / team activity / logical verification activity" acquired in Project Design Introduction I/II. In order to make use of these, it is necessary to review these items. At the same time, students must pay attention to the utilization and improvement of learning CAD skills in mechanical drawing. This course uses Yumekobo machine tools, so be sure to obtain a license.

activityGoals.body: To be able to proceed with activities from finding problems to solutions.
To be able to understand phenomena, objectives, and events quantitatively and qualitatively.
To be able to find characteristics, features, and laws of phenomena, objects, and events.
To be able to deliver acquired information to a third person intelligibly.
To be able to utilize various basic skills needed to proceed smoothly with verification activities.
To be able to have a picture of the technology fields and engineers in the discipline.
