courseType:
Practical Engineering Education Program
Practical Engineering Education Courses
keywords: Verification process 2.Effectiveness / Acceptability 3.Data handling skills 4.Credibility 5.PBL for science and technology
educationalGoal: -To gain skills to verify hypotheses or solution concept with logical approaches. -To understand phenomena, objects and events quantitatively with high credibility. -To reliably find characteristics and laws of phenomena, objects, events. -To deliver the above information to a third person intelligibly. -To gain basic skills to credibly and smoothly conduct verification activities. -To have an image of the technology fields and engineers in the discipline.
advice: The Department of Robotics will set up competitions that are arranged for the Robotics Department with the theme of the ET Robot Contest. Its purpose is to develop embedded engineers. Firstly, students will learn analysis and design methods based on modeling. Secondly, students will develop and verify robots based on the learning results so far. At the same time, this course will build a motivation for specialized fundamental subjects. [Verification of the solution proposal] Students will acquire the knowledge and skills necessary to verify the effectiveness of the solution proposal and create verification models, devices, programs, etc., while devising them by themselves. They will try the validation process and check its validity. [Solution Proposal Redesign] Based on the results of evaluating the effectiveness of the solution, students will examine how to deal with new issues. They will discuss ideas for improvement, and think about revisions. Students will repeat the revision and evaluation, and proceed with the design of the revised solution. Students will repeat the review and summarize the results as a final design. [Activity report] Regardless of whether or not the solution proposals are valid, the results of the project activities are compiled into a project report. Students will present their results at the poster session.
requiredKnowledge: Beginner-level knowledge of C language

educationalGoal: Students will:(1) learn a skill of inspection process of a hypothesis or the solution to the problem concept,(2) understand a phenomenon, an object, a phenomenon quantitatively and qualitatively,(3) tell information to a third party clearly,(4) learn various skills required for pushing forward inspection activity smoothly,(5) imagine a technical area and an engineer image to learn in architecture.
advice: Students learn how to lead processes to inspect a hypothesis or learn how to lead processes to inspect effectiveness / acceptance characteristics of the specific part among the characteristics of a concept aiming at a solution to the problem or the concept.In part students learn "a building design skill" to need data in collection → rearranging → analysis → hypothesis → visualization → report. In part "a structure design skill" to lead to the inspection, "an environmental design skill" and "an element skill of the inspection activity" are learned by the drafting of the hypothesis.(1) Building design skill:Students announce the design of a house that an individual designed in a group and narrow it down to one basic design plan based on exchange of opinions. Students make the 1/20 model of the house.(2) Structure design skill:Based on basic design plan, students examine construction and how to structure and the method of construction. Students examine examination and the transformation of the material of the Class basic axis and perform the loading experiment with the model.(3) Environmental design skill:Based on basic design plan, students perform the examination of the environmental characteristic (insulation characteristics, sound, illumination, air conditioning, ventilation) while using analysis tools.(4) Inspection activity skill: Students summarize result provided by a series of design activity in a project report and announce the team by a poster session and plan communalization of the knowledge in the whole class.
requiredKnowledge: It is desirable to have the experience that worked on design of a house in individuals as a design problem. It is desirable to learn the basics of how to write building plan. It is desirable to review the common rule including how to write dimensions, a building term and the drawing symbol that the design is a team and will wrestle.

keywords: Windows 2.Document creation 3.Spreadsheet 4.Presentation material creation 5.Data handling
educationalGoal: -To understand the structure of personal computers (PCs) and their capabilities and possibilities. -To gain the basic abilities to utilize a personal computer as a student and as a member of society, including education, research, and technical development.
advice: In this course, you will learn the following basic knowledge to use your personal computer (laptop computer) for study and student life. 1. Basic PC operation: Learn basic operations such as Windows operation and software installation. 2. Network operation: Learn how to set up connection to on-campus and off-campus networks, how to view on-campus and off-campus web pages, how to use the on-campus web systems, knowledge and information about network security and anti-virus software, manners when using networks. 3. Office software operation: Learn basic skills in document creation / spreadsheet / presentation material creation. 4. Data handling skills: Learn data handling skills using spreadsheet software.
requiredKnowledge: No prior knowledge or skills are assumed. The exercises will use your own laptop computer. Be sure to bring your laptop computer, power adapter, and network cable (LAN cable) with your course.

activityGoals.body: To be able to understand the basic knowledge of personal computers and usage of laptop computers.
To be able to understand the basic knowledge of Windows and use Windows and applications that run on Windows.
To be able to understand how to install the software and make your PC available for use at our university.
To be able to understand the mechanism of virus infection and protect your computer from computer viruses.
To be able to set up a network settings and use the campus network.
To be able to operate Office software and make effective use of data.

title: 機械系製図Ⅰ
subtitle: Mechanical Drawing I
keywords: Orthographic projection method and drafting 2.Handwritten drafting and CAD 3.Sketch drawing of parts 4.Basics of design and drafting 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn the principles of orthographic projection, which is the basis of mechanical drawing. (2) learn the ability to accurately create 2D&3D drawings according to the third angle projection method. (3) practice 2D-CAD&3D-CAD and handwritten drafting to create and edit drawings efficiently.
advice: Mechanical drawings are the most important basic means of communication for mechanical engineers to accurately convey their ideas. Machine drawing information includes not only the shape and dimensions of parts, but also the "dimensional accuracy", "shape accuracy", and "position/posture accuracy" required for each functional form that makes up the part to perform its functions. This course is the first of the design and drafting education courses offered during a three-year period. It teaches the orthographic projection method, which is the basis of mechanical drafting, and the creation of 2D mechanical drawings. We will cover the following topics: 1. Guidance on how to conduct lessons 2. Orthographic projection and 2D&3D drafting, and basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings 3. Hand-drawn mechanical part sketches and complex shape drawing exercises 4. CAD installation, its functions, and drawing creation procedures 5. Size tolerance and fit 6. The role of CAE in manufacturing
books: Textbooks: New JIS mechanical drawing (5th edition) , Morita Kita Publishing (in Japanese) JIS mechanical drawing operation method using Solid Edge ,Kanazawa Institute of Technology (in Japanese) Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Lectures are “stacked” learning (work on new subjects is based on the knowledge and abilities acquired in the previous week's class). Therefore, students should review the material in the weekly lectures thoroughly and fully understand it by the next lecture. Reference materials and assignment diagrams used in the class will be distributed using the electronic syllabus of this course. A network printer can be used.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the principles of orthographic projection and express the shape of machine parts.
Be able to understand the basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings and draw drawings.
Be able to draw front, top, and side views of machine parts.
Be able to sketch mechanical parts accurately and create hand-drawn mechanical drawings based on these sketches.
Be able to create machine drawings using 2D-CAD & 3D-CAD figure creation and figure editing functions.
Be able to summarize of the role of CAE in manufacturing by obtaining information related to design and CAD.

(5) Understand the size tolerances and surface roughness of machine parts and accurately indicate them in drawings.(6) Gain an understanding of the relationship between design and CAD/CAE, and explain this to a third party by giving a specific example.

(6) Gain an understanding of the relationship between design and CAD/CAE, and explain this to a third party in an easy-to-understand manner.

    授業科目の学習・教育目標   キーワード 学習・教育目標     1.Orthographic projection method and drafting 2.Handwritten drafting and CAD 3.Sketch drawing of parts 4.Basics of design and drafting 5.Regional cooperation  Students will: (1) learn the principles of orthographic projection, which is the basis of mechanical drawing. (2) learn the ability to accurately create 2D&3D drawings according to the third angle projection method. (3) practice 2D-CAD&3D-CAD and handwritten drafting to create and edit drawings efficiently.
    授業の概要および学習上の助言   Mechanical drawings are the most important basic means of communication for mechanical engineers to accurately convey their ideas. Machine drawing information includes not only the shape and dimensions of parts, but also the "dimensional accuracy", "shape accuracy", and "position/posture accuracy" required for each functional form that makes up the part to perform its functions. This course is the first of the design and drafting education courses offered during a three-year period. It teaches the orthographic projection method, which is the basis of mechanical drafting, and the creation of 2D mechanical drawings. We will cover the following topics: 1. Guidance on how to conduct lessons 2. Orthographic projection and 2D&3D drafting, and basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings 3. Hand-drawn mechanical part sketches and complex shape drawing exercises 4. CAD installation, its functions, and drawing creation procedures 5. Size tolerance and fit 6. The role of CAE in manufacturing
    教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック   Textbooks: New JIS mechanical drawing (5th edition) , Morita Kita Publishing (in Japanese) JIS mechanical drawing operation method using Solid Edge ,Kanazawa Institute of Technology (in Japanese) Reference books: None Reserved books: None
    履修に必要な予備知識や技能   Lectures are “stacked” learning (work on new subjects is based on the knowledge and abilities acquired in the previous week's class). Therefore, students should review the material in the weekly lectures thoroughly and fully understand it by the next lecture. Reference materials and assignment diagrams used in the class will be distributed using the electronic syllabus of this course. A network printer can be used.

title: 機械系製図Ⅱ
subtitle: Mechanical Drawing II
keywords: JIS standards and mechanical drawings 2.Mechanical design 3.Manufacturing methods and accuracy/tolerance 4.CAD 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: Machine drafting represents a machine with the shape and features imagined by the designer in a drawing that conforms to standards, and at the same time has the role of transmitting the design to a third party through the drawing. In this course, you will learn how to design parts based on the accepted standards of mechanical drafting. You will also learn how to specify tolerances, and how to translate the three-dimensional shape of parts to two-dimensional drawings.
advice: In this lecture, you will learn the JIS standards that are the basis of mechanical drafting and you will learn drafting methods related to accuracy and tolerance through a combination of lectures and exercises. In each class there will be a lecture during the first half and exercises during the second half, but the drafting of the assignments that are given does not end with the exercise time during the lecture. Review is necessary. As a prerequisite, you must know the handwritten drawing preparation procedure taught in "Mechanical Drawing I". It is necessary to thoroughly review the basic operation methods of CAD from “Mechanical drawing I” before taking this lecture. The contents handled in this lecture are as follows. ・ Outline of JIS standards for drawing creation and CAD operation methods specialized for mechanical drawing ・ Relationship between dimensional tolerance and geometric tolerance ・ Surface roughness ・ Dimension filling method ・ Bolts and nuts ・ Keys and keyways ・ Cross sections ・ Gear basics and design machine elements such as bearings ・ Drawing mechanical parts and assembly drawings with gear pumps and flanged fixed shaft joints In addition, it is necessary to be able to fully understand the design at the actual manufacturing site.  Copying in drafting drawings is against the ethics of engineers, and credits for this subject are revoked when it is found.

title: 材料力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Strength of Materials I
keywords: Stress, Strain 2.Tension, Compression 3.Bending moment of beam 4.Regional collaboration
educationalGoal: Investigating the strength of materials can clarify the forces that act on various parts of bridges, steel towers, cars, planes, energy equipment, living tissues and cells, etc., and the deformations they cause. The results can be used for safety design. It is therefore a foundational subject in mechanical engineering. In this course, students will gain a thorough understanding of the investigation of the strength of materials through lectures and practice.
advice: This is a basic strength of materials course. We will cover the following topics: 1. Stress and strain 6. Statically indeterminate problems 2. Hooke’s law 7. Thermal stress and stress concentration 3. Mechanical properties of materials 8. Thin-walled cylinders subjected to internal pressure 4. Allowable stress and safety factors 9. Beams and their support conditions 5. Tension and compression problems 10. Shearing forces and bending moments of beams In this course, it is important to do many practice exercises, but the study of the strength of materials is extremely difficult to understand just by memorizing formulas and patterns. To solve a problem, one should start with an understanding of the basic formulas needed, and then set the appropriate boundary conditions for the problem. In addition, it is necessary to be able to concretely imagine the actual forces, moments, and deformations using schematic diagrams. Furthermore, students should work on issues related to local companies, and deepen their understanding of the relationship between the strength of materials and society/technology.
books: Textbooks: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials, 2nd edition, Kyoritsu Shuppan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese) Reference books: Basic Strength of Materials, Morikita Publishing Co. Ltd. (in Japanese) Reserved books: Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: Gaining understanding by working through many different problems is the best way to learn strength of materials. As a prerequisite, it is necessary to fully understand "Industrial Mechanics I". In addition, students will be expected to move on to "Strength of Materials II" and "Strength of Materials III", which will be offered subsequently, as they are applications of this course.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the concept of normal stress, shear stress, normal strain, shear strain, and Hooke's law.
Be able to explain the deformation and fracture behavior of materials by drawing stress-strain characteristics.
Be able to explain the relationship between material properties, reference strength, and the allowable stress.
Be able to explain the frame work, thermal stress, thin-walled cylinders and stress concentration.
Be able to explain the shearing force and bending moment generated in a beam by drawing SFDs and BMDs.
Be able to explain the relationship between strength of materials and society/technology.

title: 材料科学Ⅰ
subtitle: Materials Science I
keywords: Iron and steel materials 2.Non-ferrous materials 3.Polymer material 4.Microstructure control 5.Material evaluation test
educationalGoal: In this course, we will give an overview of the industrial materials and learn the basics of the relationship between structure and physical and chemical properties, as well as methods for evaluating the characteristics of materials.
advice: The outline of the class is as follows: Classification of machine materials and characteristics of metals, plastics, and ceramics Structure of materials Basics of crystallography Theoretical strength and crystallographic dislocations in materials, resolved shear stress, and dislocation and deformation of a single crystal Plastic deformation of materials Materials evaluation, tensile test, stress versus strain curves, and hardness test Phase transition of metals
requiredKnowledge: Understand the basics of trigonometric functions, exponential functions, logarithmic functions, and vectors. Memorize the elemental symbols, such as those for carbon, magnesium, aluminum, titanium, iron, and copper, related to materials science. Regarding material structure, it is desirable to have knowledge of high school chemistry.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain basic characteristics of metals, plastics, and ceramics.
Be able to explain types, features, and examples of atomic bonds.
Be able to explain the basics of crystallography (especially Bravais lattice and Miller index).
Be able to explain the difference between elastic and plastic deformation based on materials science.
Be able to explain basics of materials evaluation.
Be able to explain the relationship between equilibrium phase diagram and phase formation.

achievementLevels.ideal: 1: Explain the relationship between typical practical materials and specific applications. 2 & 3: Explain the crystal structure and physical and chemical characteristics of typical pure materials. 4: Explain the phenomena caused by elastic or plastic deformation (for example, slip and twinning deformation) using a crystallographic viewpoint. 5: Propose an appropriate material evaluation test method. 6: Explain phase rate and microstructure at a particular point.
achievementLevels.standard: 1: Explain the characteristics used to measure practical materials and their physical properties (such as Young’s modulus and melting point). 2: Explain the bond types in pure substances and their characteristics. 3: Illustrate crystal planes and directions. 4: Explain the deformation process of mild steel using the stress versus strain curve. 5: Explain material evaluation test methods (for example, tensile test and hardness test) and data processing.

title: 材料力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Strength of Materials II
keywords: Stress in beams 2.Deflection of beams 3.Torsion 4.Combined stress 5.Regional collaboration
educationalGoal: The strength of materials can clarify the forces and deformations on various parts of bridges, steel towers, cars, planes, energy equipment, and living tissues and cells. Those results can be used to improve designs for safety. Therefore, it is an important subject that forms the basis of mechanical engineering. In this course, students will learn about bending stress in a beam, deflection of a beam, torsion, and combined stress based on the content learned in "Strength of Materials I".
advice: This is a basic course on the strength of materials. We will cover the following topics: 1. Bending stress in a beam 6. Torsion of shaft with non-circular cross section 2. Deflection of a beam 7. Stress on oblique section in the rod subjected to uniaxial tension 3. Shearing stress in a beam 8. Principal stress and principal shearing stress 4. Torsion of shaft with circular cross section 9. Mohr's stress circle 5. Power transmission shaft 10. Combined stress problem All of these topics are based on stress, strain, Hook's law, a beam and its supporting condition, and shearing force and bending moment of a beam, which were learned in "Strength of Materials I". Therefore, while reviewing the content of "Strength of Materials I" topic by topic, it is essential to make an effort to develop a bottom-up understanding by carefully considering the topics' relationship with the content of "Strength of Materials II". It is important to do many exercises and review the answers, but the study of strength of materials is extremely difficult to understand by just remembering formulas and patterns. For all problems, start by understanding the basic formula and continue the attitude of answering the problem by setting appropriate boundary conditions for it. Furthermore, students should work on issues related to local companies, and deepen their understanding of the relationship between the strength of materials, society, and technology.
books: Textbooks: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials, 2nd edition, Kyoritsu Shuppan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese) Reference books: Strength of Materials, Basic, Morikita Publishing Co. Ltd. (in Japanese) Reserved books: None specified
requiredKnowledge: Students should have a good understanding of balance of force, stress, and strain, Hook's law, support condition of a beam, and shearing force and bending moment of a beam learned in "Strength of Materials I". In addition, it is necessary to fully understand differential and integral calculation methods.

activityGoals.body: Be able to determine the stress and deflection that occur in a beam and to perform safety design.
Be able to determine torsional stress.
Be able to determine the diameter of a transmission shaft.
Be able to determine the stress in the oblique cross section of a bar subjected to uniaxial tension.
Be able to explain the principal stress and principal shearing stress, and to draw a Mohr's stress circle.
Be able to explain the relationship between strength of materials, society, and technology.

title: 流体力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Fluid Mechanics I
keywords: Characteristics of fluid 2.Pressure 3.Equations of fluid flow 4.Momentum theorem 5.Contribution to local community
educationalGoal: This course teaches a basic of fluid mechanics. Contents of this course plays an important role in design processes of fluidic systems. The contents include a basic characteristic of fluid flow, Bernoulli's theorem, equation of continuity and momentum theorem. Furthermore, the students learn examples of an application of the contents to actual design of fluidic systems through exercises.
advice: This course mainly teaches an introduction of fluid mechanics. Especially, a flow of ideal fluid, which is inviscid and incompressible fluid, is discussed. Furthermore, a part of flow mechanisms of real fluid is additionally explained. The contents and keywords of this course are as follows: 1. Characteristics of fluid and flow phenomena: Difference of solid, liquid and gas, Dimension and Unit, Density, Viscosity, Compressibility and sound velocity, Steam pressure, Surface tension 2. Hydrostatics: Definition of pressure, Hydrostatic pressure, Manometer, Total hydrostatic force, Buoyancy force, Hydraulic pressure drive system 3. Basic equations of flow: Condition of flow, Representation method of fluid flow, Flow velocity, Flow rate and acceleration, Derivation of basic equations of flow 4. Bernoulli's theorem and equation of continuity: Derivation of equation of continuity, Application of equation of continuity, Derivation of Bernoulli's equation, Application of Bernoulli's equation 5. Momentum theorem: Momentum theorem, Application, Equation of angular momentum
requiredKnowledge: The students must take a note in the class. The preparation and the review of the contents of the class must be done. Every class includes exercises and mini-examinations (quizzes). An attitude of willing action and learning is strongly required to the students.

activityGoals.body: Fluid characteristics such as compressibility and viscosity can be explained.
Relationship between fluid depth and pressure can be expressed and total hydrostatic force can be calculated.
Basic equations of fluid flow can be derived for easy examples.
Basic fluid flow can be calculated using the equation of continuity and Bernoulli's equation.
Momentum theorem can be applied to calculation of an actual fluid force.
Relationship between the course content and the local communities can be understood and discussed together.

subtitle: Dynamics of Machines I
keywords: Motion of rigid body 2.Impact 3.Work and energy 4.Friction 5.Vibration
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn the kinematics of rigid bodies when forces and moments of force act on them. (2) learn the concepts of momentum, work, and energy. (3) learn about machines in which friction is utilized. (4) learn the basis of vibration.
advice: This is a basic course on the dynamics of machines. We will cover the following topics: 1. Kinematics of rigid bodies 2. Dynamics of impact 3. Work and energy 4. Dynamics of friction 5. Dynamics of simple machines and mechanics 6. Vibration Students will also learn about advanced issues not found in the textbooks such as three-dimensional motion if time permits. Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms and formulas. Each student is expected to solve the exercises by him- or herself. Students should pay attention to the teacher's instructions in the class, because the schedule of quizzes, tests, and reports may change as the class progresses. Students should not be absent from class, as they may miss handouts.
books: Textbooks: (in Japanese) Reference books: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics [Wiley] Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Acquisition of Industrial Mechanics I and II. Enough skill in mathematics (especially differential/integral and vector inner/outcome calculations). Basic knowledge of mechanics (kinematics and moment of force). How to use a calculator.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the meaning of terms and to use SI units correctly.
Be able to explain the kinetics of rigid bodies.
Be able to explain changes in the motion of rigid bodies when they impact each other.
Be able to describe the energy of rigid bodies in motion.
Be able to analyze the motion of simple machines
Be able to describe vibration in mathematical terms.

title: 流れ学Ⅱ
subtitle: Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics II
keywords: Laminar flow and transition 2.Turbulent flow 3.Viscous fluid 4.Friction, vortex and lift 5.Contribution to local community
educationalGoal: In this course, students will first understand the characteristics of viscous fluid and learn about flow in a pipe and flow around an object in the fluid. Then, students will learn about the mechanisms of drag and lift generation. With an emphasis on viscous fluid dynamics, which is the basis of actual fluid motion, students will focus on grasping the engineering and physical meanings while solving exercises on fluid flow concepts.
advice: This is a basic course in fluid mechanics. We will cover the following topics: 1. Outline of fluid dynamics 2. Outline of viscous fluid flow, laminar flow, transition, turbulent flow, and boundary layer 3. Analysis of viscous fluid flow, laminar flow in a circular pipe, and turbulent flow in a circular pipe 4. Flow in pipes, Bernoulli’s equation considering loss, friction loss of pipe flow, losses of pipes, problems of piping systems 5. Force acting on a body, momentum theorem and drag, force, pressure resistance and frictional resistance acting on boundary layer and flat plate, flow and drag around cylinders and spheres, vortices, drag of objects with various shapes, fluid forces related to vortexes, and related vibration and safety design 6. Vortex and circulation, lift, and flow around a wing 7. Comprehensive problems: Report discussion and study meetings on specific issues (including regional contributions) in fluid dynamics. Express your understanding, ideas, and questions.
requiredKnowledge: Complete Industrial Mechanics I and II. Have knowledge of basic hydrostatics learned in Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics I.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the mechanism of fluid losses and estimate them.
Be able to understand and calculate fluid forces, such as drag and lift.
Be able to set up a physical model for fluid-related phenomena and derive its basic equations.
Be able to apply basic equations to approximate an approach that closely conforms to natural fluid behavior.
Be able to understand the fluid engineering aspects of various fluid phenomena that can contribute to the commun
Be able to actively discuss issues and outcomes.

achievementLevels.ideal: Understand that fluid phenomena are governed by the basic equation of mechanics, and the induction of the basic equation of viscosity-related fluid phenomena, especially flow in pipes, can be completely realized. Explain completely the mechanism of fluid-related loss and calculate the flow in the pipe. Explain completely and calculate concretely the mechanisms of resistance and lift. Actively participate in questions and answers and also in essential discussions.
achievementLevels.standard: Understand that fluid phenomena are governed by the basic equation of dynamics. Describe and develop the method of induction of viscous fluid phenomena, in particular the basic formula of flow in a pipe. Explain simply the mechanism of fluid loss and calculate basic pipe flow. Explain and calculate concretely the definition of resistance and lift, as applied to, for example, wings. Participate actively in questions and answers.

title: 機械力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Dynamics of Machines II
keywords: Non-damping vibration 2.Application of non-damping vibration 3.Damping vibration and forced vibration 4.Multi-freedom vibration 5.Collaboration
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) Learn the basics of vibration problems that occur in machines. (2) Learn how to apply vibration analysis to mechanical designs. (3) Learn how to make a dynamic model of vibration phenomena consisting of multi-freedom vibration, and use it for analysis.
advice: This is a basic and applied course in mechanical dynamics. We will cover the following topics: 1. Non-damping vibration (keywords: linear vibration, torsional vibration, pendulum vibration) 2. Viscous damping phenomenon (keywords: damping ratio, viscous damping coefficient) 3. Forced vibration (keywords: forced vibration by external force, forced vibration by displacement) 4. Application to various vibration problems (keywords: critical speed, vibration measurement) 5. Application to multi-freedom vibration (keyword: dynamic absorber) Students are required to actively participate in class. Students are expected to check for various messages and materials in class. Students should not be absent from class, as they may not receive the handouts.
books: Introduction to vibration engineering, Powersha, (2001) (in Japanese).
requiredKnowledge: Complete Industrial Mechanics I and II, and Dynamics of Mechanics I. Have sufficient skill in mathematics (especially differential/integral and vector inner/outcome calculations) Have basic knowledge of mechanics (kinematics and moment of force). Know how to use a calculator.

activityGoals.body: Be able to express an appropriate model for mechanical vibration.
Be able to formulate a motion equation based on the expressed vibration model.
Be able to analyze a vibration motion equation.
Be able to apply to various vibration problems consisting of multi-freedom vibration.

title: 機械加工学
subtitle: Machining Engineering
keywords: Cutting 2.Cutting mechanism 3.Tool material 4.Life cycle-oriented manufacturing 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: (1) Learn the basic theory of removal machining. (2) Learn methods to measure cutting force and cutting edge temperature. (3) Learn the types of tool damage and their causes. (4) Learn how to manufacture cutting tools using powder metallurgy and surface coating techniques. (5) Learn how to select cutting tool materials and cutting conditions.
advice: This class will cover the following topics: 1. Classification of processing methods 2. Chip formation mechanism (Classification and formation mechanism of chips, Built-up edge, Generation conditions, and Methods to prevent built-up edge) 3. Cutting theory (Theoretical calculation of cutting force and Theoretical calculation of cutting temperature) 4. Measurement of cutting specifications (Cutting force, Cutting temperature, Chip thickness, and Contact length between chip and rake face) 5. Cutting tool wear and wear factors 6. Cutting tool material (Type and Classification) 7. Powder metallurgy technology and coating technology 8. Finished surface quality and control 9. Machinability of difficult-to-cut materials Students should be aware of the teacher’s instructions in the class, because the schedules of quizzes, tests, and reports may change as the class progresses.
requiredKnowledge: Students are expected to watch the machining videos that supplement the lecture content. In addition, it is important to have the experiences of touring machining facilities and attending a machine industry fair.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the basics of cutting theory.
Be able to understand the measurement methods for cutting specifications.
Be able to understand the form and factors of tool damage.
Be able to understand the types of cutting tool materials and their effective use.
Be able to understand the types of difficult-to-cut materials and their machinability.
Be able to select optimum cutting conditions and machine tools.

Students should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class, because the schedules of quizzes, tests, and reports may change as the class progresses. Students should not be absent from class, as they may not receive the handouts. Detailed schedules and content of the course are explained in the first class.

title: 機械設計演習
subtitle: Machine Design Project
keywords: JIS standards and mechanical drawings 2.Mechanical design, strength and reliability design 3.Manufacturing method and accuracy/tolerance 4.3-axis 2-stage helical reducer 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: Students will learn about machine design and manufacturing processes and create design plans and drawings that meet the required specifications. In this course, students will create a design for strength and reliability that follows the engineering drawing, a manufacturing design that considers the manufacturing method and cost, and a draft that represents the mechanical mechanism and overall configuration.
advice: The main mechanism studied in this course is a three-axis two-stage helical gear reducer, and we will use it to acquire the ability to systematically design machines through comprehensive exercises on design accuracy, strength, and reliability of design. Basically, lectures and exercises are held weekly. However, the design and drafting of assigned tasks will not be completed in the practice time during the lecture, so preparation and review as homework will be necessary. In addition, students will use the basics of Solid Edge that were taught in “Mechanical Drawing I” and “Mechanical Drawing II” that they attended before taking this course. It is assumed that you have mastered the operating and reference methods of the JIS drawing textbook, so please check this material carefully before taking this course. The topics covered in this course are as follows: (1) Mechanical design and design process improvement; (2) Design problems, design concepts, and basic design; (3) Design problem strength, reliability of design, and detailed design; (4) Mechanical design problem drawing; (5 ) Inspection of mechanical design problem drawings; and (6) Self-inspection and third-party evaluation of mechanical design problems.
books: Textbooks: New JIS mechanical drawing (5th edition) , Morita Kita Publishing (in Japanese) Mechanical Drawing -operation method using Solid Edge- ,Kanazawa Institute of Technology (in Japanese) Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: This course is intended as a design and drafting course in the Department of Mechanical Engineering in accordance with mechanical principles, Mechanical Drawing I, Mechanical Drawing II, and Mechanical Element Design. Therefore, to participate in this course, the design and CAD drawing abilities acquired in these courses are required. Before attending this course, it is recommended that you review the content acquired in previous courses. Persistent effort is necessary.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the implementation of mechanical design, and use drawings to explain design images.
Be able to carry out design calculations, such as basic design and detailed design of components.
Be able to model a mechanism design and calculate its strength using a computer.
Be able to create machine designs that consider manufacturing methods, according to the machine drafting rules.
Be able to conceive new design solutions by integrating specialized fields of mechanical engineering.
Be able to learn the latest technology from local engineers, and organize and discuss assignments.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Understand the substance and shape of the design according to the instructions and prepare an easy-to-read assembly drawing by applying it to your own design conditions. (2) Summarize the flow of design calculations in detail using a computer. (3) Understand design modeling and strength calculations according to the instructions. (4) Perform drafting while fully avoiding shapes that cannot be manufactured or are difficult to form. (5) In designing according to the instructions, it is possible to derive a design solution. (6) Understand the design and problem-solving techniques presented by local engineers.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Understand the content and shape of the design according to the instructions.(2) Summarize the flow of design calculations with a chart using a computer and perform design calculations according to the issues. (3) Understand design modeling and strength calculations according to the instructions.. (4) Perform drafting while avoiding shapes that cannot be manufactured or are difficult to form. (5) In designing according to instructions, derive design solutions.(6) Understand the design and problem-solving techniques presented by local engineers.

lessons.content: Guidance: ・ Review the outline of this course. ・ Understand the course objectives, goals, and levels required to achieve them ・ Review design problems and specifications. ・ Understand the learning goals, outlines, and behavioral goals of the course using the distributed learning support plan. In particular, understand which part of the faculty's educational goals this course is responsible for and the specific measure of achievement level. Outline of 3-stage 2-axis helical gear reducer: ・ Review the outline and features of the 3-stage 2-axis helical gear reducer. ・ Attend lecture on the content of the textbook and observe points to be noted. Outline of design and exercise: ・ Review the design outline based on the distributed materials and the textbook.
lessons.operation: Lecture and Q&A Note: In this column, “design” indicates the design of the helical reduction gear, “exercise” indicates the machine design exercise, and “design method” indicates the machine design method. Design: pp. 1-6 Exercise: pp. 1-7
lessons.assignments: Preparation: ・ Make sure that Solid Edge is ready for use. ・ Understand the relationship between the educational goals of the department and this subject. ・ Examine the functional performance of the helical reducer. Review: ・ Reconfirm the content and objectives of this course, reconfirm your design specifications as explained, and start design calculations.

lessons.content: Practice using actual 3-axis 2-stage gear reducer: ・ Understand the main elements, such as fittings, bearings, and drafting angle, through disassembly and assembly of the gear reducer as a product, sketches, and measurements of main dimensions. In addition, understand that each part is made according to JIS standards, and confirm the method used to reference JIS standards.
lessons.operation: Practice Q&A Disassembly and measurement of helical reducer Understand functions and performance through assembly. Design: pp. 56-72 Exercise: pp. 8-9 and 85-100
lessons.assignments: Preparation: ・ Investigate and understand gear reducers. ・ Investigate reducer components. Review: ・ Draft drawings according to basic design policy. ・ Review what you learned in machine element design. ・ Check the design items for each element to understand the causal relationship. ・ Perform design calculations.

lessons.content: Outline of 3-axis 2-stage helical gear reducer: ・ Attend lecture on the content of the textbook and receive instructions on how to proceed with the design calculation and note important points in the design calculation. Explanation of mechanism, layout, and plan: ・ Before proceeding with the design work, review the meaning of each drawing and receive instructions necessary for design calculations. Perform design calculations.
lessons.operation: Lecture and Q&A Exercise Design calculation necessary for basic design Explain mechanism, layout and plan Design: pp. 9-25 Exercise: pp. 9-17
lessons.assignments: Preparation: ・ Understand the process of design work. ・ Check the basic design items. ・ Perform the design calculations. Review: ・ Review the content of the lecture, review the design calculations, and complete the design calculations. ・ Complete the reduction gear design calculation (performance and outline calculation).

lessons.content: Strength and selection of machine element parts (such as keys): ・ Review how to calculate the strength of mechanical elements, such as keys, required for the design and how to select them. Perform design calculations.
lessons.operation: Lecture and Q&A Exercise Explain the detailed design of the entire gear reducer Design: pp. 27-52 Exercise: pp. 18-30
lessons.assignments: Preparation: ・ Investigate the strength calculation method for each component ・ Implement a design calculation document. Review: ・ Deepen your understanding of material strength and mechanical strength. ・ Review the lecture content, review the design calculation sheet, and complete the design calculation sheet and plan.

lessons.content: Review of precautions when creating assembly drawings: ・ Explain the points to be noted when creating assembly drawings (such as corner radii R and corner chamfers C). ・ Describe functional design defects that tend to occur in assembly drawings. Create assembly drawings: ・ Start to create assembly drawings based on the design calculations. In addition, understand that the creation of assembly drawings requires review of design calculation documents and feedback. Submit design calculation sheets and plan drawings.
lessons.operation: Lecture and Q&A Exercise Explain the relationship between design calculations (performance and strength requirements) and drawing requirements for manufacturing Design: pp. 74-78 Exercise: pp. 37-58
lessons.assignments: Preparation: ・ Understand the relationship between design calculation and drawing (drafting rules) ・ Complete the design calculation sheet and plan, and prepare printed materials. Review: ・ Creation of assembly drawing based on mechanism drawing, layout drawing, and plan drawing of design calculations. ・ Check the relationship between requirements based on drafting rules and requirements based on design calculations. ・ Start creating assembly drawings.

lessons.content: Description of assembly drawing checklist: ・ Review the content of the assembly drawing checklist and deepen your recognition of points to be noted. Create assembly drawings. Check the consistency of the design calculation sheet and assembly drawing: ・ Check the design calculation sheet and assembly drawing check points, and participate in free-form discussions of the design solution features and ingenious points. Creation of design calculation sheet and assembly drawing: ・ Completion of design calculation sheet and assembly drawing. (Students can earn bonus points for submission of design calculation sheet and assembly drawing.)
lessons.operation: Lecture and Q&A Exercise Understand the relationship between design calculation requirements and drawing requirements Review design points for design calculation and drafting drawings Design: pp. 80-116 Exercise: pp. 59-64 and 75-84
lessons.assignments: Preparation: ・ Confirm rules for interfaces between components. ・ Organize the relation between design policy and design solution for each design solution. ・ Create assembly drawings. Review: ・ Consistency check for each component according to the assembly drawing. ・ Organization of design outline for discussion. ・ Complete assembly drawing and make the design calculation sheet and assembly drawing consistent. ・ Create assembly drawing.

lessons.content: Creating design calculation sheet and assembly drawing-Free-form discussion on design calculation and assembly drawing (part 1): ・ Free-form discussions on the features and ingenuity of each design and assembly drawing among groups with the same design specifications. ・Conduct problem discovery and examination of solutions through group discussions with other students. ・Summarize the results of the study in a report. Listen to problem-solving methods from local engineers to understand design and drafting techniques and deepen discussions.
lessons.operation: Questions and exercises (interim review): Active learning on design calculation and assembly drawings based on design policy Exercise: pp. 75-84
lessons.assignments: Preparation: ・ Prepare for free-form discussions, create design calculation sheets and assembly drawings, and review printed materials. Review: ・ Summarize the knowledge gained from the free-form discussion in a report, and transfer the calculation and drawing corrections to the assembly drawing.

lessons.content: Submission of design calculation sheet, assembly drawing, and report: ・ Submit design calculation sheets and assembly drawings. ・ Submit a report that summarizes the knowledge gained from the free-form discussion and the corrections based on it. Manufacturing method of machine parts and required accuracy: ・ Explain the outline of the manufacturing method of machine parts, and explain each manufacturing method and the processing accuracy required for it. Create part drawings: ・ Start creating parts drawings.
lessons.operation: Lecture and Q&A Exercise Detailed design instructions based on assembly drawings Design: pp. 56-72 Design method: pp. 1-18
lessons.assignments: Preparation: ・ Summarize the knowledge gained from the free-form discussion in a report, complete the design calculations and assembly drawings, and prepare them for submission. ・ Investigate the accuracy of machining and organize the relationship with requirements. Review: ・ Confirm design elements of each component and organize design items. ・ Start creating parts drawings.

lessons.content: Precautions for creating parts drawings: ・ Review the errors that are likely to occur in a parts drawing. In particular, the relationship between geometrical tolerances and dimensional tolerances will be explained again in depth. Create a parts drawing.
lessons.operation: Lecture and Q&A Exercise Explanation of consistency when each component is assembled Design method: pp. 36-59
lessons.assignments: Preparation: ・ Review geometric tolerances and dimensional tolerances, and organize the relationships between them. ・ In particular, investigate the relationship between rotating shafts, bearings, and seals. ・ Create parts drawings. Review: ・ Understand the drafting methods for each tolerance specification in a machine drawing. ・ Create parts drawings.

lessons.content: Return and explanation of design calculation sheet and assembly drawing: ・ Review the assembly drawing and understand any errors to deepen your understanding. Reconfirm drafting rules: ・ Recheck the drafting rules, such as dimensional tolerances, surface roughness, geometric tolerances, and thread representation. Review and correct design calculations and assembly drawings, and transfer these corrections to parts drawings.
lessons.operation: Lecture and Q&A Exercise Reconfirmation of element function and performance and drafting rules for each part and explanation of points during application
lessons.assignments: Preparation: ・ Review the lessons learned in mechanical drawing and machine element design. ・ Create parts drawings. Review: ・ Implement design revisions based on the strength calculation for each part and determine the applicable specifications for parts. ・ Make various revisions of design calculations and assembly drawings, and make them reflect the creation of parts drawings.

lessons.content: Description of parts diagram checklist: ・ Review the content of the parts drawing checklist and deepen your recognition of points to be noted. Exercise for final design solution.
lessons.operation: Lecture and Q&A Exercise Explanation of review exercise of design exercise (design work) following the outline of the detailed design (part diagram) Exercise: pp. 65-74
lessons.assignments: Preparation: ・ Complete strength calculations and the interface design for each part. ・ Recheck the design calculations. Review: ・ Review the design using checkpoints. ・ Complete the design calculation and drawing creation.

lessons.content: Executing design calculations, assembly drawings, and parts drawings-Free discussion on assembly drawings and parts drawings (part 2): ・ Free-form discussion on the features and ingenuity of each design, assembly, and part drawing among groups with the same design specifications, and conduct problem discovery and examination of solutions with other students. ・Summarize the results of the study in a report. Discuss design solutions and design drawings with local engineers and update your design solutions accordingly.
lessons.operation: Questions and exercises Active learning on design solutions
lessons.assignments: Preparation: ・ Outline the final design solution for participation in the free-form discussion and prepare printed materials. Review: ・ Summarize the knowledge and corrections obtained in the free-form discussion, create a report, and incorporate all corrections into the the design calculation sheet, assembly drawing, and parts drawings to complete the final design solution.

lessons.content: Final confirmation and submission of final design solution and report: ・ Final confirmation of the final design solution is performed, and it is confirmed again whether there are any problems in productivity and functionality. ・ Submit the final design solution. Note that if even one of the specified items is insufficient, it will not be evaluated as the final design solution. ・ Submit a report that summarizes the findings and items corrected after the free-form discussion. Implementation of results (practical test): ・ Practical tests will be conducted to measure your mastery of mechanical design, drafting, and CAD operations acquired so far.
lessons.assignments: Preparation: ・ Prepare the final design solution. ・ Prepare for results announcement (practical test).

lessons.content: Explanation and review of results announcement (practical test): ・ Confirmation and review of CAD drafting skills ・ Review of basic items related to design and drafting Performance confirmation test: ・A written test will be given to measure and confirm your level of achievement so far.
lessons.assignments: Preparation: ・ Prepare for the final achievement test

lessons.content: Explanation and review of achievement confirmation test. Self-check: ・ Review topics having insufficient understanding, as indicated by the results of the achievement confirmation test; deepen your understanding. ・ Organize knowledge and ideas obtained from local engineers into a report.
lessons.assignments: Review: ・ Understand the issues of the results announcement (practical exam) and achievement confirmation test, and confirm the achievement goal of this course. ・ Recognize your knowledge and abilities, including knowledge gaps, and restudy course materials as necessary. ・ Note that retests and resubmissions are not allowed.

title: 材料科学Ⅱ
subtitle: Materials Science II
keywords: Iron and steel materials 2.Non-ferrous materials 3.Equilibrium phase diagram 4.Microstructure control 5.Phase transformation
educationalGoal: To design and manufacture machines and structures that exhibit superior performance, it is necessary to select materials based on an understanding of the characteristics of the elements of which they are composed. In addition, the microstructures and properties of materials change after heat treatment and processing. In this course, students learn how to modify materials by heat treatment and processing.
advice: The outline of the class is as follows: Fe-C phase diagram and normal microstructures Heat treatment and microstructure of steel Work hardening, recovery, and re-crystallization Solid solution strengthening, precipitation strengthening, and crystal grain refinement strengthening
requiredKnowledge: It is strongly recommended that students take this course after reviewing and fully understanding the contents of Materials Science I.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the relationship between an Fe-C phase diagram and normal microstructures.
Be able to explain basic heat-treatment methods for steel.
Be able to explain basic heat-treatment methods for aluminum alloys.
Be able to explain microstructures obtained by plastic deformation, and recovery and re-crystallization

achievementLevels.ideal: 1: Explain the formation process of normal microstructures in carbon steels using an Fe-C phase diagram. 2: Propose heat-treatment conditions of steels using the Fe-C phase diagram, continuous cooling transformation (CCT) curve, and time-temperature transformation (TTT) curve. 3: Explain the relationship between mechanical properties and phase transformation and/or precipitation caused by heat treatment. 4: Explain the recovery and re-crystallization process for work-hardened materials.
achievementLevels.standard: 1: Explain the relation between carbon content in carbon steels and normal microstructures. 2 and 3: Explain basic technical terms of heat treatment, for example, quenching, tempering, annealing, normalizing, solid-solution treatment, and aging. 4: Explain the relationship between work-hardening and lattice defects.

lessons.content: Lecture: Course introduction Self-check: Review incomplete knowledge from Materials Science I. Develop future learning plans.
lessons.assignments: Understand the course objectives. Review Materials Science I.

lessons.content: Lecture: Learn the characteristic points (e.g., melting point, transformation point, eutectic point, and eutectoid point) expressed as an Fe-C phase diagram and the formation process of a normal microstructure.
lessons.assignments: Review how to use a phase diagram.

lessons.content: Lecture: Learn the basics of heat treatment for carbon steel and phase transformation of carbon steel.
lessons.assignments: Review crystal structures of alpha, gamma, and delta phases in Fe-C phase diagram

lessons.content: Quiz 1: Check your level of understanding of classes 1-3. Lecture: Understand the relationship between mechanical properties and microstructure obtained by heat treatment.
lessons.assignments: Review the content of classes 1-3 to prepare for Quiz 1.

lessons.content: Self-reflection class: Review Quiz 1 and its answers. As needed, review previous lectures to answer questions and reinforce knowledge. Lecture: Learn the TTT curve (also called the S curve) and CCT curve.
lessons.assignments: Review classes 1-4 to answer your questions.

lessons.content: Lecture: Further learn the TTT curve and CCT curve.
lessons.assignments: Review technical terms of heat treatment using JIS G0201.

lessons.content: Lecture: Learn tempering and temper brittleness of steels. Learn the Charpy pendulum impact test to evaluate temper brittleness.
lessons.assignments: Study JIS Z2242, “Method for Charpy pendulum impact test of metallic materials.”

lessons.content: Quiz 2: Check the level of understanding of lectures from classes 4-7. Lecture: Understand the outline of microstructure control and material strengthening.
lessons.assignments: Review classes 4-7.

lessons.content: Self-reflection class: Review Quiz 2 and its answer. As needed, review previous lectures to answer questions and reinforce knowledge. Lecture: Learn microstructure control with plastic working and heat treatment. Understand the mechanisms of microstructure control with work hardening, recovery, and re-crystallization.
lessons.assignments: Review classes 1-8. Review technical terms of microstructure control.

lessons.content: Lecture: Learn solid solution strengthening and precipitation strengthening. Understand characteristics of aluminum alloys subjected to these strengthening techniques.
lessons.assignments: Research relation between strengthening mechanisms and dislocations after the class.

lessons.content: Lecture: Crystal grain refinement strengthening.
lessons.assignments: Research relation between strengthening mechanisms and crystal grain refinement after the class.

lessons.content: Quiz 3: Check your level of understanding of lectures from classes 8-12. Integrated learning: Discuss the functions of materials in mechanical engineering.
lessons.assignments: Review classes 8-12.

lessons.content: Self-reflection class: Review the answers of Quiz 3. As needed, review previous lectures to answer questions and reinforce knowledge. Integrated learning: To deepen your understanding of this course, a Q&A session is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Review your notes, the textbook, and other materials before the class.

lessons.content: Integrated learning: Review the content of all classes. Exam: Evaluate the degree of your achievement for the entire course.
lessons.assignments: Review the content of all classes.

lessons.content: Self-reflection class: Review the exam and its answers. As needed, review previous lectures to answer questions and reinforce knowledge. Self-check: Self-check of the quiz, exam, and report. Consider the future learning plan.
lessons.operation: Review the exam Study exam answers and request explanations as needed Review comments on the graded report
lessons.assignments: Create and submit a report.

achievementLevels.ideal: 1: Explain the formation process of normal microstructures in carbon steels using an Fe-C phase diagram. 2: Propose heat-treatment conditions of steels using the Fe-C phase diagram, continuous cooling transformation (CCT) curve, and time-temperature transformation (TTT) curve. 3: Explain the relationship between mechanical properties and phase transformation and/or precipitation caused by heat treatment. 4: Explain the recovery and re-crystallization process for work-hardened materials.

lessons.content: Lecture: Course introduction Self-check: Review incomplete knowledge from Materials Science I. Develop future learning plans.
lessons.assignments: Understand the course objectives. Review Materials Science I.

lessons.content: Lecture: Learn the characteristic points (e.g., melting point, transformation point, eutectic point, and eutectoid point) expressed as an Fe-C phase diagram and the formation process of a normal microstructure.
lessons.assignments: Review how to use a phase diagram.

lessons.content: Lecture: Learn the basics of heat treatment for carbon steel and phase transformation of carbon steel.
lessons.assignments: Review crystal structures of alpha, gamma, and delta phases in Fe-C phase diagram

lessons.content: Quiz 1: Check your level of understanding of classes 1-3. Lecture: Understand the relationship between mechanical properties and microstructure obtained by heat treatment.
lessons.assignments: Review the content of classes 1-3 to prepare for Quiz 1.

lessons.content: Self-reflection class: Review Quiz 1 and its answers. As needed, review previous lectures to answer questions and reinforce knowledge. Lecture: Learn the TTT curve (also called the S curve) and CCT curve.
lessons.assignments: Review classes 1-4 to answer your questions.

lessons.content: Lecture: Further learn the TTT curve and CCT curve.
lessons.assignments: Review technical terms of heat treatment using JIS G0201.

lessons.content: Lecture: Learn tempering and temper brittleness of steels. Learn the Charpy pendulum impact test to evaluate temper brittleness.
lessons.assignments: Study JIS Z2242, “Method for Charpy pendulum impact test of metallic materials.”

lessons.content: Quiz 2: Check the level of understanding of lectures from classes 4-7. Lecture: Understand the outline of microstructure control and material strengthening.
lessons.assignments: Review classes 4-7.

lessons.content: Self-reflection class: Review Quiz 2 and its answer. As needed, review previous lectures to answer questions and reinforce knowledge. Lecture: Learn microstructure control with plastic working and heat treatment. Understand the mechanisms of microstructure control with work hardening, recovery, and re-crystallization.
lessons.assignments: Review classes 1-8. Review technical terms of microstructure control.

lessons.content: Lecture: Learn solid solution strengthening and precipitation strengthening. Understand characteristics of aluminum alloys subjected to these strengthening techniques.
lessons.assignments: Research relation between strengthening mechanisms and dislocations after the class.

lessons.content: Lecture: Crystal grain refinement strengthening.
lessons.assignments: Research relation between strengthening mechanisms and crystal grain refinement after the class.

lessons.content: Quiz 3: Check your level of understanding of lectures from classes 8-12. Integrated learning: Discuss the functions of materials in mechanical engineering.
lessons.assignments: Review classes 8-12.

lessons.content: Self-reflection class: Review the answers of Quiz 3. As needed, review previous lectures to answer questions and reinforce knowledge. Integrated learning: To deepen your understanding of this course, a Q&A session is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Review your notes, the textbook, and other materials before the class.

lessons.content: Integrated learning: Review the content of all classes. Exam: Evaluate the degree of your achievement for the entire course.
lessons.assignments: Review the content of all classes.

lessons.content: Self-reflection class: Review the exam and its answers. As needed, review previous lectures to answer questions and reinforce knowledge. Self-check: Self-check of the quiz, exam, and report. Consider the future learning plan.
lessons.operation: Review the exam Study exam answers and request explanations as needed Review comments on the graded report
lessons.assignments: Create and submit a report.

title: 計測・制御工学
subtitle: Instrumental and control Engineering
keywords: Sensors 2.Uncertainty 3.Transfer function 4.Transient response 5.Regional collaboration
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) Learn the basics of measurement (2) Learn the functions and roles of sensors (3) Learn the transfer functions of control systems (4) Learn the transient response method (5) Learn the basics of control system analysis based on the frequency response that is the basis of feedback control
advice: This is a basic course in instrumental and control engineering. We will cover the following topics: 1. Systems and their control 2. Basics of measurement 3. Specification of sensors 4. Standards and uncertainty 5. Types of sensors 6. Laplace transform 7. Transfer function 8. Block diagram 9. Board diagram 10. Stability of control system 11. Design of control system Students are expected to understand the concept of measurement. Students are expected to understand the meaning of the analysis method for control systems. Students are expected to determine the stability of a control system.
books: Textbooks: (in Japanese) Reference books: Reserved books:
requiredKnowledge: Complete of “Mathematics for Mechanical Engineers.”

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain how to select the signal that should be measured.
Be able to explain the traceability of measurement.
Be able to describe the results of measurement and their uncertainty.
Be able to describe an analysis model for a control system using the transfer function.
Be able to analyze the transient response and the frequency response for a control system.
Be able to identify regional issues.

title: マイクロ・ナノ加工
subtitle: Micro-Nano Processing
keywords: Micro- and nanotechnology 2.MEMS and superfine machining 3.Lapping, polishing, and CMP 4.Surface modification 5.Regional collaboration
educationalGoal: Currently, technologies for realizing ultrafine parts and mechanisms are required for manufacturing, and these technologies are applied to pressure sensors, the heads of inkjet printers, MEMS such as gyroscopes, manufacture of Si-IC and LED substrates, and micro-machines. In addition, processing methods include not only top-down types that refine existing elements but bottom-up types that build up atoms according to the purpose. In this course, students will learn the basics of processing methods to obtain such ultrafine parts and mechanisms.
advice: We will cover various leading-edge processes that can fabricate micro- to nanoscale parts. The outline of this class is shown below: 1. Relationship between the processing method and scale concepts expressed as micro, meso, and nano 2. Outline of surface modification methods 3. Outline of MEMS 4. Planarization processing of Si wafers 5. Planarization processing using chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) methods 6. Latest top-down micro-processing methods 7. Micro-processing using lasers 8. Summary To deepen your understanding of the content of this course, exercise questions will be presented and explained appropriately. Students will need to bring a scientific calculator to class. In addition, special classes will be held for outside lecturers as needed.
requiredKnowledge: Fully understand related subjects as integrated research and development. Possess fundamental knowledge of elemental technology learned in processing-related subjects

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the concept of dimensions expressed at the micro-, meso-, and nanoscales.
Be able to explain the principles and features of surface modification methods (PVD, CVD, etc.).
Be able to explain the characteristics and principles of ultraprecision polishing.
Be able to explain the processing principles and application examples of the latest micro-processing technology.

Explain surface modification methods and the functional thin film that they realize. 3. Explain the positioning and principles of ultraprecision polishing, the polishing conditions, and the method for selecting auxiliary materials consumed during its application. 4. Explain the latest processing methods and application examples that realize ultrafine dimensions.
achievementLevels.standard: 1. Explain the concept of dimensions expressed at the micro-, meso-, and nanoscales. 2. Explain the principles of typical surface modification methods. 3. Explain the positioning and principles of ultraprecision polishing, and the method for selecting materials consumed during its application. 4. Explain the principles of the latest processing methods to realize shapes with extremely small dimensions.

lessons.assignments: Study textbook Chapter 5, pp. 204-224.

educationalGoal: Students will: (1) Learn the concept of heat transfer. (2) Learn basic conductive heat transfer. (3) Learn basic convective heat transfer. (4) Learn the basis of heat transfer with phase change. (5) Learn the basis of radiative heat transfer.
advice: This is a basic course in heat transfer. We will cover the following topics: 1. Heat transfer 2. Conductive heat transfer 3. Convective heat transfer 4. Heat transfer with phase change 5. title: 先端材料
subtitle: Advanced Materials
keywords: Corrosion and Protection 2.Fracture mechanics 3.Alloyed steel and non-ferrous materials 4.Non-metallic materials and Composite materials 5.Material seliction
educationalGoal: In the design and manufacture of machines and structures, it is necessary to select appropriate materials based on an understanding of their properties. Based on the basic knowledge of the structure and properties of materials acquired in Materials Science I and II, we will learn about corrosion and fracture mechanisms, which are defects of materials, and understand the structure and properties of nonferrous metals, resins, ceramics, and composite materials. Furthermore, we will discuss some cases of material selection and it helps deeper understanding of materials.
advice: The following items are studied. -Corrosion and corrosion protection techniques -Fracture mechanics -Stainless steel and alloy steel -Aluminum and aluminum alloys -Copper and copper alloys -Plastics -Ceramics -Composite materials Some case studies of material selection are discussed in order to understand materials knowledge deeper.
requiredKnowledge: This lecture requires the understanding of Materials Science I and Materials Science II. Students should understand the relationship between microstructure and material properties of materials in Materials Science 1,and also understand the relationship between microstructure formation and properties of steel in Materials Science 2.Knowledge of thermodynamics is also required to understand phenomena and mechanisms. Students should review the equations between thermodynamic state functions U, H, G and F and state variables V, P, T and S.

achievementLevels.ideal: 1) Abilities to understand the basic principle of corrosion and typical corrosion forms, and corrosion protection methods. 2) Abilities to be able to explain the failure mechanism of materials. 3) Abilities to understand the characteristics of advanced steel materials such as alloyed steel and high tensile strength steels. 4)Abilities to be able to explain the relationship between the structure and properties of non-ferrous metals, ceramics, resins and composite materials. 5)Abilities to be able to select appropriate materials using the knowledge acquired in this course.
achievementLevels.standard: 1) Abilities to understand that corrosion progresses by the anode reaction and cathode reaction and to explain the principle of cathodic protection. 2) Abilities to be able to explain the meaning of the plane strain fracture toughness value (KIC). 3)Abilities to be able to explain the characteristics of advanced materials such as alloy steel and high strength steel. 4) Abilities to be able to explain the characteristics of typical aluminum and copper alloys, ceramics, resins and composite materials. 5) Abilities to be able to point out the hazards of materials in the environment in which they are used.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the educational objectives and achievements of this course. To understand the role of materials in the field of engineering. To explain the lecture policy of this course. To review the contents of Materials Science 1 and Materials Science 2.
lessons.assignments: To review the contents of Materials Science I and Materials Science II using the textbook and handouts. Understand the educational objectives of this course.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the principle of corrosion which include anodic reaction and cathodic reaction, and polarization phenomenon. To understand the effects of pH and electric potential on corrosion reactions.
lessons.assignments: Students should review the oxidizing and reducing reactions involving the transfer of electrons studied in high school.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the characteristics and principles of uniform attack and galvanic corrosion, which are typical forms of corrosion. To understand the hazardous material conditions depending on the environment.
lessons.assignments: To observe the corrosion forms everyday metal products such as cars, coins, and cookware.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the characteristics and principles of typical forms of corrosion (pitting and crevice corrosion, intergranular corrosion, stress corrosion cracking). To understand the hazardous material conditions depending on surrounding environments.
lessons.assignments: To explain the corrosion mechanisms of everyday metal products such as cars, coins, and cookware.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the fracture mechanisms originating from micro-cracks.
lessons.assignments: To explain the methods of corrosion protection for everyday metal products.

lessons.content: [Quiz 1] To check the students' understanding of the contents of lecture 1 to lecture 5. [Lecture] To understand the properties of advanced steel materials such as alloy steels and high strength steels in terms of their structure.
lessons.assignments: To review of the contents of lectures 1 to lecture 5. To review the strengthening mechanisms of metals such as dislocation strengthening, solid solution strengthening, and precipitation strengthening.

lessons.content: [Review and Self-reflection] Quiz 1 is explained and questions are asked to clear up the contents of the lectures. [Lecture] To understand the different types of copper alloys and their structure and properties.
lessons.assignments: To review the relationship between the microstructure formed from the eutectoid system state diagram and the properties of the obtained material.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the types of Cu alloys and their structures, and properties
lessons.assignments: To review the precipitation strengthening by aging and the sliding deformation mechanism by transition.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the types of Al alloys and magnesium alloys, their structures, and properties.
lessons.assignments: To review the three types of chemical bonds and their characteristics.

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the types of ceramics and their structures and properties.
lessons.assignments: To review of basic crystal structures such as fcc and bcc and their characteristics

lessons.content: [Lecture] To understand the types of composite materials and their structure and characteristics.
lessons.assignments: A report will be assigned

lessons.content: [Quiz 2] To check the students' understanding of the contents of lecture 6 to lecture 11. [Overall lecture] Discussions on examples of material selection deepen confirmation of obtained knowledge and understanding of materials.
lessons.assignments: To review of the contents of lectures 6 to lecture 11.

lessons.content: [Review and Self-reflection] Quiz 2 is explained and questions are asked to clear up the contents of the lectures. [Overall lecture] Discussions on examples of material selection deepen confirmation of obtained knowledge and understanding of materials.
lessons.operation: Commentary on Quiz 1 Lecture Q&A Case study
lessons.assignments: To think about the reasons for the selection of everyday metal product.

lessons.content: [Final examination] To check the students' understanding of the contents of lecture 1 to lecture 13.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(山部昌研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Yamabe Masashi)
keywords: Engineering design 2.Design and manufacturing 3.Materials and processing 4.Energy and mechanics 5.Regional collaboration
educationalGoal: (1) Acquire the ability to identify and solve problems to research and develop high-quality products using the basic knowledge learned in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. (2) Learn what technologies or new mechanisms are needed so for that purpose. (3) Learn about the importance of collaboration with society (particularly local communities).
advice: This is the final comprehensive course in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. To realize the educational objectives of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, this course focuses on the following goals: Students will acquire the ability to model phenomena accurately and analyze the models. Students will acquire the ability and the engineering sense to evaluate solutions using the obtained results. In practice, students should reconfirm their project theme, which was determined in Preparatory Seminar, with the supervisors of the individual laboratories. (The theme should be revised if necessary.) Students are expected to pursue identification and solution of problems in accordance with the engineering process. In this laboratory, the molding process phenomena in plastics and other materials are clarified by experiments or numerical analysis. In addition, numerical analysis models are constructed using this knowledge, and a molding process simulation technology is established. Furthermore, the mechanism of molding fault phenomena is clarified by a simulation of the molding process to realize high-quality manufacturing.
requiredKnowledge: It is desirable to obtain a license for machining at the KIT Dream works (Yumekobo). General knowledge of mechanical engineering, such as material dynamics, mechanical dynamics, fluid dynamics, material science, and heat transfer, is necessary for carrying out our research. Especially, plastic processing is the main research area, and it is necessary to have sufficient knowledge about this processes for discussion of the research.

Be able to compile the results correctly into an article and discuss the content through presentations.
Be able to act independently to solve the issues presented separately.
