    授業科目の学習・教育目標   キーワード 学習・教育目標     1.Composite materials 2.Biomaterials 3.Biomechanics 4.Computational mechanics 5.Regional collaboration  Students will:(1) Acquire the ability to identify and solve problems to research, develop, design, and manufacture socially useful and high-quality products using the basic knowledge learned in the Department of Mechanical Engineering, (2) Learn what technologies or new mechanisms are needed for that purpose, and (3) Learn about the importance of collaboration with society (particularly local communities).
    授業の概要および学習上の助言   This is the final comprehensive course in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. To realize the educational objectives of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, this course focuses on the following goals: Students will acquire the ability to model phenomena accurately and analyze the models. Students will acquire the ability and the engineering sense to evaluate solutions based on the obtained results. In practice, students should reconfirm their project theme, which was determined in Preparatory Seminar, with the supervisors of the individual laboratories. (The theme should be revised as necessary.) Students are expected to pursue the identification and solution of problems in accordance with the engineering process. This laboratory focuses on the advanced composite materials. In addition, we also investigate approaches to apply conventional advanced technologies and knowledge to composite materials for other fields, such as the global environment, regenerative medicine, cellular biomechanics, tissue engineering, and biomimetics. The new results obtained by these trials provide feedback to many fields, such as mechanical and aeronautical engineering. Thus, we aim to cultivate flexible and comprehensive thinking abilities regardless of the academic field.

keywords: Engineering design 2.Design and manufacturing 3.Materials and processing 4.Energy and mechanics 5.Regional collaboration
educationalGoal: (1) Acquire the ability to identify and solve problems to research and develop high-quality products using the basic knowledge learned in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. advice: This is the final comprehensive course in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. To realize the educational objectives of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, this course focuses on the following goals: Students will acquire the ability to model phenomena accurately and analyze the models. Students will acquire the ability and the engineering sense to evaluate solutions using the obtained results. In practice, students should reconfirm their project theme, which was determined in Preparatory Seminar, with the supervisors of the individual laboratories. (The theme should be revised if necessary.) Students are expected to pursue identification and solution of problems in accordance with the engineering process. In this laboratory, the molding process phenomena in plastics and other materials are clarified by experiments or numerical analysis. In addition, numerical analysis models are constructed using this knowledge, and a molding process simulation technology is established. Furthermore, the mechanism of molding fault phenomena is clarified by a simulation of the molding process to realize high-quality manufacturing.

Especially, plastic processing is the main research area, and it is necessary to have sufficient knowledge about this processes for discussion of the research.

title: 機械系製図Ⅰ
subtitle: Mechanical Drawing I
keywords: Orthographic projection method and drafting 2.Handwritten drafting and CAD 3.Sketch drawing of parts 4.Basics of design and drafting 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn the principles of orthographic projection, which is the basis of mechanical drawing. (2) learn the ability to accurately create 2D&3D drawings according to the third angle projection method. (3) practice 2D-CAD&3D-CAD and handwritten drafting to create and edit drawings efficiently.
advice: Mechanical drawings are the most important basic means of communication for mechanical engineers to accurately convey their ideas. Machine drawing information includes not only the shape and dimensions of parts, but also the "dimensional accuracy", "shape accuracy", and "position/posture accuracy" required for each functional form that makes up the part to perform its functions. This course is the first of the design and drafting education courses offered during a three-year period. It teaches the orthographic projection method, which is the basis of mechanical drafting, and the creation of 2D mechanical drawings. We will cover the following topics: 1. Guidance on how to conduct lessons 2. Orthographic projection and 2D&3D drafting, and basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings 3. Hand-drawn mechanical part sketches and complex shape drawing exercises 4. CAD installation, its functions, and drawing creation procedures 5. Size tolerance and fit 6. The role of CAE in manufacturing
books: Textbooks: New JIS mechanical drawing (5th edition) , Morita Kita Publishing (in Japanese) JIS mechanical drawing operation method using Solid Edge ,Kanazawa Institute of Technology (in Japanese) Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Lectures are “stacked” learning (work on new subjects is based on the knowledge and abilities acquired in the previous week's class). Therefore, students should review the material in the weekly lectures thoroughly and fully understand it by the next lecture. Reference materials and assignment diagrams used in the class will be distributed using the electronic syllabus of this course. A network printer can be used.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the principles of orthographic projection and express the shape of machine parts.
Be able to understand the basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings and draw drawings.
Be able to draw front, top, and side views of machine parts.
Be able to sketch mechanical parts accurately and create hand-drawn mechanical drawings based on these sketches.
Be able to create machine drawings using 2D-CAD & 3D-CAD figure creation and figure editing functions.

(5) Understand the size tolerances and surface roughness of machine parts and accurately indicate them in drawings.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Understand the trigonometry and basic drawing rules used to create mechanical drawings. (2) Accurately understand the basic line types used in machine drawings and their roles. (3) Select a necessary projection by analyzing the shape characteristics of a part and determine a main projection.(4) Sketch mechanical parts and make hand-drawn 2D mechanical drawings based on these sketches. (5) Understand the size tolerances of machine parts, the size tolerances of surface roughness products, and the surface roughness, and indicate them in drawings.

    授業の概要および学習上の助言   Mechanical drawings are the most important basic means of communication for mechanical engineers to accurately convey their ideas. Machine drawing information includes not only the shape and dimensions of parts, but also the "dimensional accuracy", "shape accuracy", and "position/posture accuracy" required for each functional form that makes up the part to perform its functions. This course is the first of the design and drafting education courses offered during a three-year period. It teaches the orthographic projection method, which is the basis of mechanical drafting, and the creation of 2D mechanical drawings. We will cover the following topics: 1. Guidance on how to conduct lessons 2. Orthographic projection and 2D&3D drafting, and basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings 3. Hand-drawn mechanical part sketches and complex shape drawing exercises 4. CAD installation, its functions, and drawing creation procedures 5. Size tolerance and fit 6. The role of CAE in manufacturing

title: 機械系製図Ⅱ
subtitle: Mechanical Drawing II
keywords: JIS standards and mechanical drawings 2.Mechanical design 3.Manufacturing methods and accuracy/tolerance 4.CAD 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: Machine drafting represents a machine with the shape and features imagined by the designer in a drawing that conforms to standards, and at the same time has the role of transmitting the design to a third party through the drawing. In this course, you will learn how to design parts based on the accepted standards of mechanical drafting. You will also learn how to specify tolerances, and how to translate the three-dimensional shape of parts to two-dimensional drawings.
advice: In this lecture, you will learn the JIS standards that are the basis of mechanical drafting and you will learn drafting methods related to accuracy and tolerance through a combination of lectures and exercises. In each class there will be a lecture during the first half and exercises during the second half, but the drafting of the assignments that are given does not end with the exercise time during the lecture. Review is necessary. As a prerequisite, you must know the handwritten drawing preparation procedure taught in "Mechanical Drawing I". It is necessary to thoroughly review the basic operation methods of CAD from “Mechanical drawing I” before taking this lecture. The contents handled in this lecture are as follows. ・ Outline of JIS standards for drawing creation and CAD operation methods specialized for mechanical drawing ・ Relationship between dimensional tolerance and geometric tolerance ・ Surface roughness ・ Dimension filling method ・ Bolts and nuts ・ Keys and keyways ・ Cross sections ・ Gear basics and design machine elements such as bearings ・ Drawing mechanical parts and assembly drawings with gear pumps and flanged fixed shaft joints In addition, it is necessary to be able to fully understand the design at the actual manufacturing site.  Copying in drafting drawings is against the ethics of engineers, and credits for this subject are revoked when it is found.
books: Textbooks:New JIS mechanical drawing(5th edition),Moritika Publishing(in Japanese) JIS mechanical drawing operation method using Solid Edge,Kanazawa Institute of Technology(in Japanese) Reference books:None Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge: (1) You can draw on the CAD software drawing creation screen. Your ability should be at a level where it is easy to create a model of the text “Mechanical Drawing”. Basically, items that should have been learned in Mechanical Drawing I (functions written in the text, drawing methods) are not taught in this course. (2) 3D (3D objects) can be modeled using 3D drafting, the 3rd angle method (2D drafting) and using two-dimensional drafting (plan view, front view, side view). (3) You have mastered the method of downloading materials and uploading reports using the student portal.

Be able to indicate the machine design, tolerance, and accuracy for the manufacturing method of machine parts.
Be able to prepare and explain the results of preparation and review as works at the specified time.
Be able to explain the design process and role at the manufacturing site.

    担当教員名
 AKASAKA Takeshi
    授業科目の学習・教育目標   キーワード 学習・教育目標     1.JIS standards and mechanical drawings 2.Mechanical design 3.Manufacturing methods and accuracy/tolerance 4.CAD 5.Regional cooperation  Machine drafting represents a machine with the shape and features imagined by the designer in a drawing that conforms to standards, and at the same time has the role of transmitting the design to a third party through the drawing. In this course, you will learn how to design parts based on the accepted standards of mechanical drafting. You will also learn how to specify tolerances, and how to translate the three-dimensional shape of parts to two-dimensional drawings.
    授業の概要および学習上の助言   In this lecture, you will learn the JIS standards that are the basis of mechanical drafting and you will learn drafting methods related to accuracy and tolerance through a combination of lectures and exercises. In each class there will be a lecture during the first half and exercises during the second half, but the drafting of the assignments that are given does not end with the exercise time during the lecture. Review is necessary. As a prerequisite, you must know the handwritten drawing preparation procedure taught in "Mechanical Drawing I". It is necessary to thoroughly review the basic operation methods of CAD from “Mechanical drawing I” before taking this lecture. The contents handled in this lecture are as follows. ・ Outline of JIS standards for drawing creation and CAD operation methods specialized for mechanical drawing ・ Relationship between dimensional tolerance and geometric tolerance ・ Surface roughness ・ Dimension filling method ・ Bolts and nuts ・ Keys and keyways ・ Cross sections ・ Gear basics and design machine elements such as bearings ・ Drawing mechanical parts and assembly drawings with gear pumps and flanged fixed shaft joints In addition, it is necessary to be able to fully understand the design at the actual manufacturing site.  Copying in drafting drawings is against the ethics of engineers, and credits for this subject are revoked when it is found.
    教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック   Textbooks:New JIS mechanical drawing(5th edition),Moritika Publishing(in Japanese) JIS mechanical drawing operation method using Solid Edge,Kanazawa Institute of Technology(in Japanese) Reference books:None Reserved books:None
    履修に必要な予備知識や技能   (1) You can draw on the CAD software drawing creation screen. Your ability should be at a level where it is easy to create a model of the text “Mechanical Drawing”. Basically, items that should have been learned in Mechanical Drawing I (functions written in the text, drawing methods) are not taught in this course. (2) 3D (3D objects) can be modeled using 3D drafting, the 3rd angle method (2D drafting) and using two-dimensional drafting (plan view, front view, side view). (3) You have mastered the method of downloading materials and uploading reports using the student portal.

title: 工業力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Engineering Mechanics II
keywords: Laws of Motion 2.Inertia Force 3.Equations of Motion 4.Moments of Inertia 5.Rectilinear and Angular Motions of Rigid Bodies
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn the kinematics of particles and rigid bodies under forces and moments (2) learn the basic concepts of Newton's laws of motion (3) learn the basic concepts of inertial forces and moments of inertia (4) learn the plane motion of rigid bodies (5) learn the basis of angular motion of rigid bodies and torques (6) research the application to real structures in their localities
advice: This is a basic course of dynamics of machines. The following subjects will be covered: 1. Rectilinear motion of a particle (horizontal motion) and the concepts of position, velocity and acceleration 2. Motion of a freely falling body (vertical motion),curvilinear motion of a particle,and motion of projectile 3. Rotational motion of a particle, tangential and normal components of acceleration, and relative motion of two particles 4. The basis of Newtonian Mechanics, Newton's Laws of Motion, and Equation of Motion 5. Inertia force, D’Alembert's Principle, rotational motion of a particle, and centrifugal force 6. Rotational motion of a rigid body and the moments of inertia of masses 7. Theorems of the moment of inertia; Parallel-axis Theorem, and Vertical-axis Theorem of the moment of inertia 8. Moments of inertia of common geometric shapes such as slender rod, thin rectangular plate, rectangular prism, thin disk, circular cylinder, and sphere 9. Rolling motion of a rigid body, combination of momentum and angular momentum, Equation of angular motion Students will be expected to understand the meaning of technical terms and formulas. Students will be expected to solve the exercises by themselves. title: 材料力学
subtitle: Strength of Materials
keywords: Stress, Strain 2.Tension, Compression 3.Beams 4.Regional collaboration
educationalGoal: Strength of Materials clarify the forces and deformations of various parts of bridges, towers, cars, planes, energy equipment, etc. These results can be used for design safety. It is an important subject that forms the basis of mechanical engineering. In this course, students should gain a thorough understanding of the basics of the strength of materials through lectures and practice. Also, students research the application of strength of materials to real structures in their localities.
advice: Students must thoroughly learn the following as the necessary basic knowledge for engineers at any stage of their career. It is important to work through many exercise answers, but the study of strength of materials is extremely difficult to understand by just memorizing formulas and patterns. For all problems, students will start from an understanding of the basic formula and solve the problem by setting appropriate boundary conditions for the problem. 1. Stress and strain, 2. Hooke’s law, 3. Mechanical properties of materials, 4. Allowable stress and safety factors, 5. Frame structure, 6. Thermal stress, 7. Stress concentration, 8. Thin-walled cylinder subjected to internal pressure, 9. Beams and their supporting conditions, 10. Shearing force and bending moment of a beam, 11. Stress on beams, 12. Deflection of beams Furthermore, students should understand the real applications of structure by applying strength of materials in their locality.
books: Textbooks: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials, 2nd edition, Kyoritsu Shuppan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese) Reference books: Unspecified Reserved books: Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: As a prerequisite, it is necessary to fully understand the course Industrial Mechanics I. Students need to fully understand the content of this course as the basis of the courses Mechanics of Aircraft Structure and Design of Aircraft Structure in later semesters.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain concept of normal stress, shear stress, normal strain, shear strain and Hooke's law.

title: 振動工学
subtitle: Vibration Engineering
keywords: Initial excitation 2.Harmonic excitation 3.Nonperiodic excitation 4.Natural frequency 5.Resonance
educationalGoal: Structural vibration behavior should be well investigated in the process of aircraft structural design. For example, to design a wing structure, it is necessary to clarify its vibration behaviors such as its response to a gust load and its bending-torsional flutter property. In this course, students will learn the basics of vibration engineering necessary to treat practical problems on structural vibration in aircrafts.
advice: In order to understand the nature of structural vibration, students will learn how to express the motions of various vibration systems in mathematical equations, how to solve the equations, and how to examine the meanings of the obtained solutions. Students are required not only to study actively during the class but also to work hard on exams and assignments. In this course, we will cover the following materials: 1. Basic knowledge of vibration in mechanical systems Types of vibration, Harmonic vibration, Synthesis of vibration 2. Response of single degree of freedom systems to initial excitation Undamped or damped systems, viscous damping, coulomb damping 3. Response of single degree of freedom systems to harmonic excitation Response to harmonic force or harmonic displacement excitation, Vibration isolation 4. Response of single degree of freedom systems to nonperiodic excitation Impulse response, Inditial response
books: Required materials will be specified in the first lesson.
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of Industrial Mechanics and Mechanical Mechanics. Basic knowledge of industrial mechanics, including equilibrium (balance) of forces and the equation of motion for an accelerated object.

activityGoals.body: Be able to create an analysis model for the structural vibration
Be able to derive equations of motion based on the analysis model and solve them
Be able to explain the resonance phenomenon
Be able to explain the effect of the damping on responses to both initial excitation and harmonic excitation
Be able to analyze the simple vibration problems and capture the nature of the phenomenon

    授業の概要および学習上の助言   This is a fundamental fluid dynamics and aerodynamics course. Students will learn fluid properties, fluid statics, inviscid flow, and incompressible flow. We will cover the following materials: 1. Fluid properties and flow phenomena: units and dimensions, fluid properties, fluid statics 2. Forces and moments on a body: pressure, hydrostatic pressure, manometer, buoyancy 3. Fluid and body dynamics: fundamentals of fluids, momentum equation, continuity equation, Euler equation, Navier-Stokes equation 4. Laws of similarity: flow similarity, dimensionless numbers (Reynolds, Mach numbers) 5. Momentum conservation: momentum equation Students should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class, because the schedules of quizzes, tests and reports may change as the class progresses. Students are expected to solve the exercises by themselves to understand the course. Students are also expected to review their notebooks for better understanding. Students are expected to actively participate in the presentation and discussion.

title: 航空制御工学
subtitle: Aircraft Control Engineering
keywords: Laplace transform 2.Transfer function and block diagram 3.Frequency response and transient response 4.Stability margin 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: As represented by FBW aircraft, flight control is an essential technology for modern aircraft. In Aircraft Control Engineering, students will learn control technology and learn the basics of flight control law design/analysis.
advice: Students will begin by learning the Laplace transform, transfer functions, block diagrams, etc., which are indispensable for control technology. Next, students will learn pole/zero placement, frequency response, and transient response, which are indispensable for understanding control characteristics. Finally, students will learn about actual flight control systems through examples.
requiredKnowledge: Acquisition of Dynamics of Flight Sufficient skill in mathematics and physics

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the contrast between time domain motion and Laplace transform domain characteristics.
Be able to express a dynamic system by Laplace transform and transfer function and explain pole & zeros.
Be able to find the transient response from the transfer function and explain the relation between pole & zeros.
Be able to draw board diagrams and vector trajectories and also determine whether the system is stable or not.
Be able to determine the transfer function with feedback and draw outlines of the root locus

title: 航空流体力学A
subtitle: Aerodynamics A
keywords: Governing equation 2.Potential flow 3.Conformal transformation 4.Airfoil and wing planform
educationalGoal: Fluid dynamics is one of the major subjects in the machine and aeronautical fields. Students will learn the method of theoretical analysis of fluids using the governing equation. The goal of this subject is to understand the aerodynamic characteristics of the wings of aircraft, and to learn how to analyze the fluid around objects in irrotational ideal flow.
advice: We will learn the two-dimensional flow of incompressible, inviscid and irrotational fluids, and how to apply the theory to airplane wings. We will cover the following materials: 1. Aerodynamic characteristics of two-dimensional wings 7. Aerodynamic characteristics of three-dimensional wings Students must take and review notes because not everything is in the textbook.
books: Introduction to aerodynamics, Maruzen publishing, in Japanese
requiredKnowledge: Acquisition of fluid mechanics. Sufficient skill in mathematics (especially differential and integral calculations).

Be able to explain the mechanism of wing lift generation.

Be able to explain the aerodynamic characteristics of a three-dimensional wing.

title: 航空構造設計
subtitle: Aircraft Structure Design
keywords: Design load 2.Static strength 3.Fatigue strength 4.Composite materials
educationalGoal: Students will learn: (1) Features of aircraft structures (2) Basic concepts of aircraft structural design under static loads (3) Basic concepts of aircraft structural design under fatigue loads (4) Mechanics of composite laminates
advice: On the basis of knowledge learned in subjects such as Industrial Mechanics, Mechanics of Materials, and Mechanics of Aircraft Structure, student will learn the basic concepts of aircraft structural design. We will cover the following materials: (1) Design load of aircraft (limit load, ultimate load, load factor, V-n diagram) (2) Basic concepts of structural design methods under static loads (Strength ratio, Margin of safety) (3) Basic concepts of structural design methods under fatigue loads (Safe life design, Damage tolerance design) (4) Mechanics of composite materials (Mechanics of composite lamina and composite laminate) Students should thoroughly review what they have learned in Mechanics of Materials and Mechanics of Aircraft Structure before taking this course.
books: Required materials will be specified in the first lesson.
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of Industrial Mechanics, Mechanics of Materials, and Mechanics of Aircraft Structure

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the meanings of 'limit load' and 'ultimate load'
Be able to evaluate the static strength of aircraft structure using strength ratio or margin of safety
Regarding the fatigue strength of aircraft structures, be able to explain the concept of damage tolerance design
Be able to calculate the stiffness matrix of composite laminates and explain the mechanical behavior

keywords: Numerical simulation 2.Structural analysis 3.Aerodynamic analysis 4.Finite element method 5.Local collaboration
educationalGoal: With the rapid development of computers, numerical simulations for structural analysis and aerodynamic analysis are essential in the aircraft design process. In this practical training course, students will learn how to properly use numerical simulation for structural mechanics and fluid dynamics in the aircraft design process. Students will also learn how to utilize numerical simulation to solve actual engineering problems that occur in their local community.
advice: In this course, students will learn numerical analysis through the use of numerical analysis software. We will cover the following materials: 1 Introduction to numerical simulation 2 Structural analysis Geometrical modeling, Finite element modeling, Load and constraint conditions, Execution of analysis, Evaluation of results, Comparison with theoretical result 3 Aerodynamic analysis Geometry modelling, Meshing, Computational method, Initial and boundary conditions, Execution of analysis, Evaluation of results, Comparison with experimental results Lectures on structural analysis and aerodynamic analysis will be given separately in the first half and the second half of semester. The order of the two lectures may change. A fixed schedule will be announced in the first lecture of the semester.
books: Required materials will be specified in the first lesson.
requiredKnowledge: It is recommended that students have already taken the following courses: Mechanics of Materials, Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics, 3D-CAD, Aerodynamics for Aircraft A, Applied Mathematics, and Computer Engineering. In structural analysis, we will use the textbook specified above. In aerodynamic analysis, the textbook will be handed out during the class.

title: 航空システム専門実験・演習A
subtitle: Aeronautics Major Lab/Exercises A
keywords: Planning 2.Performing 3.Summarizing 4.Presentation 5.Aeronautical engineering
educationalGoal: Students will: (1)learn the method and theory of a selected basic subject, and perform experiment and practice on selected subject. (2)acquire deeper understanding and ability to apply engineering subjects. (3)learn how to write the experimental method in an experiment report. (4)learn how to create presentations on experiments and their results.
advice: Students will carry out the following experiments in Exercise A. Details on the experiments can be confirmed in the textbook. ① Molding and evaluation of CFRPs (carbon fiber reinforced plastics) ② Strength evaluation of the thin sheet structure with stiffeners (Semi-monocoque structure) ③ Vibration properties evaluation of the structural element Students attending the lecture will be divided into three groups (A, B, and C). Group A will carry out experiment ① for five weeks and then theme ② for the next five weeks and finally theme ③ for another five weeks. Group B will follow the order of ②→③→① and group C the order of ③→①→②. In addition, class details are distributed at the time of the start of each experiment theme.
books: Aeronautics Major Experiments and Exercises A
requiredKnowledge: Student should read the textbook before an experiment and understand what kind of experiment they will be carrying out. In addition, students should make a lesson report before a class as preparation, if necessary for that class.

activityGoals.body: Be able to plan an experiment and carry it out independently based on knowledge learned.
Be able to carry out tests safely based on an understanding of the principle of an experiment and the measuremen
Be able to arrange test data using computers and explain the key and problem appropriately.
Be able to reliably interpret the results of an experiment and evaluate the validity of the test data.
Be able to explain the obtained test data reasonably by comparing it with an analytical solution.
Be able to summarize the experimental results in a report, submit it before a deadline, and explain them.

achievementLevels.ideal: ① Students understand the basics of carbon fiber reinforced plastics (CFRPs) and design CFRPs laminated plates. Students understand the details of the experiments and carry out molding of laminated plates, cutting of specimens, and bending tests, and also carry out recording, analysis and consideration of test results. ② Students properly conduct tests of three characteristic buckling types for semi-monocoque structures b evaluate the validity of obtained data by comparing it with theoretical or numerical analysis results. ③ Students properly conduct vibration experiments and evaluate the validity of obtained data by comparing it with theoretical or numerical analysis results.
achievementLevels.standard: ① Students understand features of the mechanical properties of carbon fiber reinforced plastics (CFRPs). Students understand experiments and carry out molding of laminated plates, cutting of specimens, and bending tests, and also carry out recording and analysis of test results. Students prepare reports and presentations as scheduled. ② Students conduct the buckling experiments and give a general explanation of the buckling phenomena in a presentation. ③ Students conduct vibration experiments and give a general explanation of the vibration phenomena in a presentation.

lessons.content: Students understand the learning objectives, outline, and target abilities of this course based on the distributed syllabus. In particular, students understand which role this course assumes within the learning objectives of the department of aeronautics and a rough concrete level of achievement. ①Guidance on outline and manner of operation of molding and evaluation of CFRPs (carbon fiber reinforced plastics). Students research design of laminated CFRPs using a prepreg sheet with given properties. Students start to prepare lamination.
lessons.assignments: Students understand the relationship between the learning objectives of the department of aeronautics and this course. ①Students research the application, molding method and strength properties of CFRPs, and hand in the research report the following week.

lessons.content: Students laminate prepreg sheets based on a defined design in the first week and make laminated plates by hot press molding.
lessons.assignments: Students research evaluation method of strength properties of CFRPs based on the JIS standards given in the first week.

lessons.content: Students cut out specimens from the molded plates by diamond-cutter and measure the dimensions. Students understand the handling of the universal testing machine. Teaching assistants conduct bending tests and obtain load-deflection curve.
lessons.assignments: Student research strength properties and the calculation method of the strength of the molded plates by load-deflection curve.

lessons.content: Students evaluate the bending properties of the molded plates from the experimental results in the third week, and examine these results and compare them with designed values. Students begin preparation of report and presentation.
lessons.assignments: Students prepare result report, PowerPoint material and presentation.

lessons.content: Students hand in result report and deliver presentation and discussion. Students need to research literature before presentation for proper question and answer. Students self-check the content of the experiments, reports, presentation and attendance.
lessons.assignments: Students rehearse group presentation and prepare presentation by researching literature for question and answer.

lessons.content: Strength evaluation of Semi-monocoque structure Orientation: It is explained that the aircraftstructure consists of thin sheet metal; therefore, buckling strength becomes a problem for structural design. The experimental method and general background of the buckling experiment,including the calculation method of the buckling load, are explained. In addition, actual examples of aircraft structures, T-3 and OH-6D, are shown as the teaching materials.
lessons.operation: Lecture and meeting Confirmation of experimental procedure and task allocation in the experiments.
lessons.assignments: Students should review the three types of buckling typical for semi-monocoque structures from a textbook of structural mechanics. Students should also read p. 5 of the textbook and understand the purpose of the experiment.

lessons.content: Snap buckling test Students can understand the typical failure mode of shell structures though a comparison between a theoretical and experimental buckling load obtained from the snap buckling tests using an aluminum can they prepare. Self-check of lecture content and current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Students review failure behavior of the shell structure and predict the expected failure load and the buckling mode through the textbook pp. 6 to 7.

lessons.content: Shear buckling test Students observe the shear buckling process, such as the shear buckling wrinkle and load resistant capability, under a tension field through the shear buckling test. Students learn the shear load resistant capability of the shear load members of the aircraft, including spar-webs and rib-webs through a comparison between the experimental value and the expected failure load. Self-check of lecture content and current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Students should learn tension field theory and predict the expected buckling load and the buckling mode. Students should also read pp. 7 to 10 of the textbook and understand the calculation method of the shear buckling load of the test specimen.

lessons.content: Compression buckling test A thin sheet has little load-resistant capability after compression buckling. However, reinforcement with thin stiffeners shows an enhanced load-resistant capability even in a post-buckling situation. Students observe the above state by experiment. At the same time, students also confirm by sight the situation of the structure which caused compression buckling. In addition, students estimate the effective width based on the experimental results and also understand the grounds of the enhancement of strength for the stiffened panel. Self-check of lecture content and current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Students learn the theory of the compression buckling and predict the expected buckling load and the buckling mode. Students read pp. 10 to 12 of the textbook and understand the calculation method of the local buckling load of the test specimen.

lessons.content: Oral presentation and report submission Students perform an oral presentation on three kinds of buckling experiments. Using experimental data and a comparison between test results and the theoretical predicted value, students investigate the load resistance capability of the stiffened panels. In the oral presentation, students can appropriately cope with various questions by having researched the reference documents. Self-check of current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Students should perform preparations for their oral presentation and the submitted report. Students should understand the style of the submitted report by reading pp. 13 to 14 of the textbook and also prepare for questions in the oral presentation by reviewing the related documents for the concept of stiffened panels.

lessons.content: Vibration properties evaluation of structural element Vibration test (1) Experiment on single DOF mass-spring vibration system Theoretical analysis of single DOF vibration system
lessons.assignments: Read textbook pp. 21-25.

achievementLevels.ideal: ① Students understand the basics of carbon fiber reinforced plastics (CFRPs) and design CFRPs laminated plates. Students understand the details of the experiments and carry out molding of laminated plates, cutting of specimens, and bending tests, and also carry out recording, analysis and consideration of test results. ② Students properly conduct tests of three characteristic buckling types for semi-monocoque structures b evaluate the validity of obtained data by comparing it with theoretical or numerical analysis results. ③ Students properly conduct vibration experiments and evaluate the validity of obtained data by comparing it with theoretical or numerical analysis results.
achievementLevels.standard: ① Students understand features of the mechanical properties of carbon fiber reinforced plastics (CFRPs). Students understand experiments and carry out molding of laminated plates, cutting of specimens, and bending tests, and also carry out recording and analysis of test results. Students prepare reports and presentations as scheduled. ② Students conduct the buckling experiments and give a general explanation of the buckling phenomena in a presentation. ③ Students conduct vibration experiments and give a general explanation of the vibration phenomena in a presentation.

lessons.content: Students understand the learning objectives, outline, and target abilities of this course based on the distributed syllabus. In particular, students understand which role this course assumes within the learning objectives of the department of aeronautics and a rough concrete level of achievement. ①Guidance on outline and manner of operation of molding and evaluation of CFRPs (carbon fiber reinforced plastics). Students research design of laminated CFRPs using a prepreg sheet with given properties. Students start to prepare lamination.
lessons.assignments: Students understand the relationship between the learning objectives of the department of aeronautics and this course. ①Students research the application, molding method and strength properties of CFRPs, and hand in the research report the following week.

lessons.content: Students laminate prepreg sheets based on a defined design in the first week and make laminated plates by hot press molding.
lessons.assignments: Students research evaluation method of strength properties of CFRPs based on the JIS standards given in the first week.

lessons.content: Students cut out specimens from the molded plates by diamond-cutter and measure the dimensions. Students understand the handling of the universal testing machine. Teaching assistants conduct bending tests and obtain load-deflection curve.
lessons.assignments: Student research strength properties and the calculation method of the strength of the molded plates by load-deflection curve.

lessons.content: Students evaluate the bending properties of the molded plates from the experimental results in the third week, and examine these results and compare them with designed values. Students begin preparation of report and presentation.
lessons.assignments: Students prepare result report, PowerPoint material and presentation.

lessons.content: Students hand in result report and deliver presentation and discussion. Students need to research literature before presentation for proper question and answer. Students self-check the content of the experiments, reports, presentation and attendance.
lessons.assignments: Students rehearse group presentation and prepare presentation by researching literature for question and answer.

lessons.content: Strength evaluation of Semi-monocoque structure Orientation: It is explained that the aircraftstructure consists of thin sheet metal; therefore, buckling strength becomes a problem for structural design. The experimental method and general background of the buckling experiment,including the calculation method of the buckling load, are explained. In addition, actual examples of aircraft structures, T-3 and OH-6D, are shown as the teaching materials.
lessons.operation: Lecture and meeting Confirmation of experimental procedure and task allocation in the experiments.
lessons.assignments: Students should review the three types of buckling typical for semi-monocoque structures from a textbook of structural mechanics. Students should also read p. 5 of the textbook and understand the purpose of the experiment.

lessons.content: Snap buckling test Students can understand the typical failure mode of shell structures though a comparison between a theoretical and experimental buckling load obtained from the snap buckling tests using an aluminum can they prepare. Self-check of lecture content and current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Students review failure behavior of the shell structure and predict the expected failure load and the buckling mode through the textbook pp. 6 to 7.

lessons.content: Shear buckling test Students observe the shear buckling process, such as the shear buckling wrinkle and load resistant capability, under a tension field through the shear buckling test. Students learn the shear load resistant capability of the shear load members of the aircraft, including spar-webs and rib-webs through a comparison between the experimental value and the expected failure load. Self-check of lecture content and current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Students should learn tension field theory and predict the expected buckling load and the buckling mode. Students should also read pp. 7 to 10 of the textbook and understand the calculation method of the shear buckling load of the test specimen.

lessons.content: Compression buckling test A thin sheet has little load-resistant capability after compression buckling. However, reinforcement with thin stiffeners shows an enhanced load-resistant capability even in a post-buckling situation. Students observe the above state by experiment. At the same time, students also confirm by sight the situation of the structure which caused compression buckling. In addition, students estimate the effective width based on the experimental results and also understand the grounds of the enhancement of strength for the stiffened panel. Self-check of lecture content and current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Students learn the theory of the compression buckling and predict the expected buckling load and the buckling mode. Students read pp. 10 to 12 of the textbook and understand the calculation method of the local buckling load of the test specimen.

lessons.content: Oral presentation and report submission Students perform an oral presentation on three kinds of buckling experiments. Using experimental data and a comparison between test results and the theoretical predicted value, students investigate the load resistance capability of the stiffened panels. In the oral presentation, students can appropriately cope with various questions by having researched the reference documents. Self-check of current progress is conducted.
lessons.assignments: Students should perform preparations for their oral presentation and the submitted report. Students should understand the style of the submitted report by reading pp. 13 to 14 of the textbook and also prepare for questions in the oral presentation by reviewing the related documents for the concept of stiffened panels.

lessons.content: Vibration properties evaluation of structural element Vibration test (1) Experiment on single DOF mass-spring vibration system Theoretical analysis of single DOF vibration system
lessons.assignments: Read textbook pp. 21-25.

title: 信頼性工学
subtitle: Reliability Engineering
keywords: Statistical data 2.Quantity for reliability 3.Reliability of structures 4.Reliability of systems
educationalGoal: To minimize the risk of aircraft accidents, it is important to eliminate defects in electronic control systems or structural systems. In this course students will learn: (1) the basic mathematics used in reliability engineering, (2) the concept of structural reliability design, (3) reliability analysis and reliability design methods for aircraft equipment systems
advice: After learning the basic mathematics used in reliability engineering (basics of probability and statistics), students will learn the concept of structural reliability design of aircraft. Students will also learn about reliability analysis and reliability design methods for aircraft equipment systems. In this course, we will cover the following materials: 1. Reliability and reliability engineering 2. The basic The basic mathematics used in reliability engineering 3. Statistical analysis of reliability data 4. Reliability for structural systems 5. Reliability for electronic control systems
books: Required materials will be specified in the first lesson.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of probability and statistics Basic knowledge of calculus, including differentiation and integration

title: 熱力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Thermodynamics I
keywords: Temperature and heat 2.Thermal equilibrium 3.Mixed gas 4.Ideal gas 5.The first law of thermodynamics
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) Learn basic knowledge of the irreversibility in the nature world (2) Learn how to convert energy and obtain work from heat (3) Acquire design skills for energy conversion in mechanical engineering
advice: This is a basic course in thermodynamics. We will cover the following topics: 1. Definitions of heat, temperature and systems 2. Thermal equilibrium and the zeroth law of thermodynamics 3. Thermal properties of mixed gases 4. Equation of state of ideal gases 5. The first law of thermodynamics Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms and formulas. Students are expected to solve exercises independently. Students should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class, because the schedules of quizzes, tests, and reports may change as the class progresses. Students should not be absent from class, as they may not receive the handouts. Detailed schedules and content of the course are explained in the first class.
books: Textbook : Koguchi et al., Thermodynamics (in Japanese), Asakura shoten. Reference book : Arai, Furuhata, English-Japanese Bilingual Textbook Series, Thermodynamics, Morikita. Reserved books : N/A
requiredKnowledge: Have sufficient skill in mathematics (especially differential and integral calculations). Know how to use a calculator.

Be able to explain Mixed gas and apply it to problems

title: 流れ学Ⅰ
subtitle: Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics I
keywords: Fluid properties 2.Fluid statics 3.Basic fluid mechanics 4.Bernoulli equation 5.Local collaboration
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn the fundamentals of fluid dynamics and aerodynamics (2) learn the fluid properties of air because aircraft fly in the air (3) learn the measurement principles of fluid devices (4) learn fundamental equations and their application
advice: This is a fundamental fluid dynamics and aerodynamics course. Students will learn fluid properties, fluid statics, inviscid flow, and incompressible flow. We will cover the following materials: 1. Fluid properties and flow phenomena: units and dimensions, fluid properties, fluid statics 2. Forces and moments on a body: pressure, hydrostatic pressure, manometer, buoyancy 3. Fluid and body dynamics: fundamentals of fluids, continuity equation, Bernoulli equation 4. Laws of similarity: flow similarity, dimensionless numbers (Reynolds, Mach numbers) Students should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class, because the schedules of quizzes, tests and reports may change as the class progresses. Students are expected to solve the exercises by themselves to understand the course. Students are also expected to review their notebooks for better understanding. Students are expected to actively participate in the presentation and discussion.
requiredKnowledge: Acquisition of Industrial Mechanics I and II. Sufficient skill in mathematics and physics (dynamics)

activityGoals.body: Be able to express fluid properties, particularly density, viscosity, pressure etc.
Be able to calculate forces and moments acting on a body due to pressure
Be able to explain Mach and Reynolds numbers
Be able to calculate fundamental fluid computation using continuum and Bernoulli equations
Be able to compute forces acting on a body using momentum conservation

title: 飛行力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Dynamics of Flight I
keywords: Equation of motion 2.Flying qualities 3.Flight control 4.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: The “dynamics of flight” is the foundation of aeronautical engineering. In this course, students will learn what kind of forces act on an aircraft in flight and learn about the balance and dynamics characteristics for stable flight.
advice: Students will begin by learning basic mathematical knowledge and axis definitions, and learn about the six-degrees-of-freedom equation of motion. Next, students will learn to analyze qualities of flight after learning linearization of the equation of motion. In addition to learning design standards, students will deepen their understanding of qualities of flight by learning the basics of flight control.
requiredKnowledge: Acquisition of Dynamics of Machines Sufficient skill in mathematics and physics

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the principles of flight and its characteristics.
Be able to understand the effects on flight motion of changes in the aerodynamic derivative acting on the aircra

title: 流れ学Ⅱ
subtitle: Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics II
keywords: Fluid properties 2.Fluid basics 3.Momentum equation 4.Equation of fluid motion 5.Local collaboration
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn the fundamentals of fluid dynamics and aerodynamics (2) learn the fluid properties of air because aircraft fly in the air (3) learn the measurement principles of fluid devices (4) learn fundamental equations and their application (5) learn the flow around an object
advice: This is a fundamental fluid dynamics and aerodynamics course. Students will learn fluid properties, fluid statics, inviscid flow, and incompressible flow. We will cover the following materials: 1. Equation of fluid motion: fluid basics, continuity equation, Bernoulli equation, Euler equation, Navier-Stokes equation 2. Forces and moments on a body: lift and drag 3. Fluid and body dynamics: fundamentals of fluids, momentum equation, continuity equation, Euler equation, Navier-Stokes equation 4. Laws of similarity: flow similarity, dimensionless numbers (Reynolds, Mach numbers) 5. Momentum conservation: momentum equation Students should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class, because the schedules of quizzes, tests and reports may change as the class progresses. Students are expected to solve the exercises by themselves to understand the course. Students are also expected to review their notebooks for better understanding. Students are expected to actively participate in the presentation and discussion.
requiredKnowledge: Acquisition of Fluid Mechanics I. Sufficient skill in mathematics and physics (dynamics)

activityGoals.body: Be able to calculate fundamental fluid computation using continuum and Bernoulli equations
Be able to compute forces acting on a body using momentum conservation
Be able to understand and explain the basics of equation of fluid motion and continuity
Be able to derive the fundamental fluid equations
Be able to explain the flows around a body

keywords: Aeronautics 2.Aircraft design 3.Problem finding 4.Career building 5.Regional alliance
educationalGoal: Students will: (1)propose a problem for Design Project III. (2)study a procedure to solve the problem. (3)master the design, production, production technology. (4)develop the basic abilities needed for design and production in order to suggest feasible ideas. (5)learn the importance of cooperation with society.
advice: Students will: (1) clarify the knowledge and skills necessary to accomplish a project carried out in Design Project III and confirm their ability to perform these. (2) clarify the knowledge and skills you need to augment your existing knowledge and skills, and apply them to learning new skills. (3) clarify the aim and the action plan of the Design Project III project as the class proceeds. (4) clarify the Design Project III proposal and evaluate these learning results, and confirm the degree of acquisition. (5) receive the following instructions from their lab teacher: -rules and the administration methods in the laboratory -usage of the apparatuses -other conventions of lab use. Note: The description above are the current plan; the details will be distributed at the time of the first class of the specialized seminar.
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge and skills to take this course are presented in the first lecture of each laboratory. Students cannot take Design Project III if the unit of specialized seminar (this subject) is not obtained.

activityGoals.body: Students have a clear image of the aim and the action plan of their Design Project III.
Students can explain the theme of their Design Project III.
Students acquire the knowledge and skills to independently accomplish their Design Project III.
Students come to understand laboratory conventions through experience.
Students understand the safety management guidelines to perform experiments and studies safely.
Students survey future courses and decide the direction of their study.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(廣瀬康夫研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Hirose Yasuo)
keywords: Aeronautics 2.Aircraft conceptual design, Aircraft planning 3.Advanced structural concept 4.Damage tolerance 5.Regional alliance
educationalGoal: The basic ability to design, fabricate and propose feasible ideas on transportation machines by applying aeronautical engineering theory will be obtained. In addition, students feed a viewpoint to evaluate the application effect of the new technologies such as innovative structure concepts by an interest loss and gain of the transportation machines such as aircraft.
advice: Course Description and Expectations for Students The department of aeronautics aims to develop engineers who can support the development of transportation machines such as aircraft using their knowledge of aeronautics, machine design, and production technology of transportation machines. Design Project III is the subject of the collected studies in the final stage of the curriculum. The targets of this subject are the following: -to develop the abilities of design and analysis through the designing of actual transport machines such as aircraft, applying theories of mainly aeronautics, and evaluating actual phenomena relating to the transportation machines such as aircraft. -to develop the ability to estimate the obtained results from the aeronautical engineering viewpoint. -to carry out research on the problem in order to fabricate integral structures to realize the full potential capabilities of composite materials. A detailed project theme is decided through discussion with the teacher. Students will discover their own problems and solve them. Students must also understand the targets of this subject, and an overview of the content of the course and the objectives based on the syllabus. In particular, students must understand which part of the learning objectives of this department this subject carries and a detailed level of the achievement.
requiredKnowledge: Because Design Project III is based on lectures, experiments, and practice of quarters 1-6 in the department of aeronautics, students must review them appropriately as needed.

activityGoals.body: Be able to establish a project theme and put it into action based on an engineering design process.
Be able to finalize the result students obtained as documents and conduct the presentation with related discussi
Be able to perform design, drafting, manufacturing (production) and simulation.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(小栗和幸研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Oguri Kazuyuki)
keywords: Aeronautics 2.Engineering design 3.Integrated engineering 4.Engineering analysis 5.Regional alliance
educationalGoal: On the basis of the design and fabrication technology of the basics of aeronautical engineering learned so far, the basic ability to design, fabricate and propose feasible ideas on transportation machines by applying aeronautical engineering theory will be obtained. At the same time, students will learn the importance of cooperation with society (community in particular) to advance their ideas.
advice: Design Project III is the subject of the collected studies in the final stage of the curriculum. Examples of research subjects at Oguri Lab include the following. -Surface treatment of composite materials Modification and analysis of surfaces by atmospheric pressure and plasma, and fine particle shot blast to otain better adhesion of bond and paint. -Surface treatment of metallic materials Modification and analysis of surface by fine particle shot peening to obtain better fatigue and anti-corrosion properties. -Surface treatment of aircraft materials Various surface microfabrications and analysis to obtain electromagnetic shielding and stealth properties. A detailed project theme is determined through discussion. Students will discover their own problems and solve them. Students will also understand the targets of this subject, the overview of the course and the objectives. In particular, students will understand which part of the learning objectives of this department this subject carries and a detailed level of their achievement.
requiredKnowledge: Because Design Project III is based on the lectures, experiments, and practice of quarters 1 to 6 in the department of aeronautics, students should review them appropriately as needed. In particular, a review of Materials for Aircraft Structure and Strength of Materials is needed.

activityGoals.body: Be able to establish a project theme and put it into action based on an engineering design process.
Be able to finalize the results students obtained as documents and conduct a presentation with discussion.
Be able to perform design, drafting, manufacturing (production) and simulation.

advice: Specific project themes will be determined through discussion, and problems will be discovered and resolved according to these discussions. Themes can be broadly classified as follows. (2) Demonstration and evaluation by proposing new aircraft such as small drones (3) Research on the aerodynamic characteristics of flying creatures in nature and examination of applied technology

Design Project III is the subject of the collected studies in the final stage of the curriculum. The targets of this subject are the following: -to develop the abilities of design and analysis through the designing of actual transport machines such as aircraft, applying theories of mainly aeronautics, and evaluating actual phenomena relating to the transportation machines such as aircraft. -to develop the ability to estimate the obtained results from the aeronautical engineering viewpoint. A detailed project theme is decided through discussion with the teacher. Students will discover their own problems and solve them. The examples of the themes are described as follows: (1) Research and development on computational fluid dynamics for fluid machines. (2) Fundamental research on multidisciplinary analysis and design methods on topics such as aerodynamic noise and fluid/heat conduction. (3) Research and application of design optimization methods for fluid machines. Students must also understand the targets of this subject, and an overview of the content of the course and the objectives based on the syllabus. In particular, students must understand which part of the learning objectives of this subject carries and a detailed level of the achievement.

title: 機械系製図Ⅰ
subtitle: Mechanical Drawing I
keywords: Orthographic projection method and drafting 2.Handwritten drafting and CAD 3.Sketch drawing of parts 4.Basics of design and drafting 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn the principles of orthographic projection, which is the basis of mechanical drawing. (2) learn the ability to accurately create 2D&3D drawings according to the third angle projection method. (3) practice 2D-CAD&3D-CAD and handwritten drafting to create and edit drawings efficiently.
advice: Mechanical drawings are the most important basic means of communication for mechanical engineers to accurately convey their ideas. Machine drawing information includes not only the shape and dimensions of parts, but also the "dimensional accuracy", "shape accuracy", and "position/posture accuracy" required for each functional form that makes up the part to perform its functions. This course is the first of the design and drafting education courses offered during a three-year period. It teaches the orthographic projection method, which is the basis of mechanical drafting, and the creation of 2D mechanical drawings. We will cover the following topics: 1. Guidance on how to conduct lessons 2. Orthographic projection and 2D&3D drafting, and basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings 3. Hand-drawn mechanical part sketches and complex shape drawing exercises 4. CAD installation, its functions, and drawing creation procedures 5. Size tolerance and fit 6. The role of CAE in manufacturing
books: Textbooks: New JIS mechanical drawing (5th edition) , Morita Kita Publishing (in Japanese) JIS mechanical drawing operation method using Solid Edge ,Kanazawa Institute of Technology (in Japanese) Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Lectures are “stacked” learning (work on new subjects is based on the knowledge and abilities acquired in the previous week's class). Therefore, students should review the material in the weekly lectures thoroughly and fully understand it by the next lecture. Reference materials and assignment diagrams used in the class will be distributed using the electronic syllabus of this course. A network printer can be used.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the principles of orthographic projection and express the shape of machine parts.
Be able to understand the basic drafting rules for mechanical drawings and draw drawings.
Be able to draw front, top, and side views of machine parts.
Be able to sketch mechanical parts accurately and create hand-drawn mechanical drawings based on these sketches.
Be able to create machine drawings using 2D-CAD & 3D-CAD figure creation and figure editing functions.
Be able to summarize of the role of CAE in manufacturing by obtaining information related to design and CAD.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Accurately understand the third trigonometric method and basic drafting rules used for machine drafting.(2) Accurately understand the basic line types used in machine drawings and their roles.(3) Select the necessary projections by analyzing the geometric features of parts and determine the main projections appropriately.(4) Sketch machine parts accurately, and create hand-drawings based on the sketches. (5) Understand the size tolerances and surface roughness of machine parts and accurately indicate them in drawings.(6) Gain an understanding of the relationship between design and CAD/CAE, and explain this to a third party by giving a specific example.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Understand the trigonometry and basic drawing rules used to create mechanical drawings. (2) Accurately understand the basic line types used in machine drawings and their roles. (3) Select a necessary projection by analyzing the shape characteristics of a part and determine a main projection.(4) Sketch mechanical parts and make hand-drawn 2D mechanical drawings based on these sketches. (5) Understand the size tolerances of machine parts, the size tolerances of surface roughness products, and the surface roughness, and indicate them in drawings. (6) Gain an understanding of the relationship between design and CAD/CAE, and explain this to a third party in an easy-to-understand manner.

educationalGoal: Understand basic concepts in mechanics (e.g., force, moment of force, center of gravity, and inertial force). Acquire the ability to perform mechanical analysis, such as finding where force is exerted against a machine or machine part and what kind of force it is.
advice: Mechanics is the basis of mechanical subjects, and the basis of mechanical design and dynamic motion analysis of robots. Dynamics includes analytical mechanics, vibration, material dynamics, fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, statistical mechanics, and quantum mechanics. This is an introductory course for specialized robotics subjects, and it provides a foundation in mechanics and dynamics. This course covers the following basic topics: 1. Power 2. Synthesis and decomposition of force 3. Moment of force 4. Equilibrium of force 5. Center of gravity 6. Movement and force
books: Textbook: Basic Mechanics of Machines [Corona Publishing] Reference book: Thinking mechanics [Academic book publisher]
requiredKnowledge: Many exercise problems require familiarity with the mathematics and physics used in basic engineering. Acquire the content of this class, which is essential for understanding specialized subjects in the following year.

activityGoals.body: Appropriately express the force acting on an object and represent its magnitude in SI units.
Understand the concept of force and combined multiple forces, and find any directional component of a force.
Understand the concept of force moments and calculate force moments.
Derive the equilibrium equation of forces and calculate them.
Understand the concept of the center of gravity (or centroid) and find the center of gravity.
Understand the relationship between motion and force and calculate inertial force.

title: 機械系製図Ⅱ
subtitle: Mechanical Drawing II
keywords: JIS standards and mechanical drawings 2.Mechanical design 3.Manufacturing methods and accuracy/tolerance 4.CAD 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: Machine drafting represents a machine with the shape and features imagined by the designer in a drawing that conforms to standards, and at the same time has the role of transmitting the design to a third party through the drawing. In this course, you will learn how to design parts based on the accepted standards of mechanical drafting. You will also learn how to specify tolerances, and how to translate the three-dimensional shape of parts to two-dimensional drawings.
advice: In this lecture, you will learn the JIS standards that are the basis of mechanical drafting and you will learn drafting methods related to accuracy and tolerance through a combination of lectures and exercises. In each class there will be a lecture during the first half and exercises during the second half, but the drafting of the assignments that are given does not end with the exercise time during the lecture. Review is necessary. As a prerequisite, you must know the handwritten drawing preparation procedure taught in "Mechanical Drawing I". It is necessary to thoroughly review the basic operation methods of CAD from “Mechanical drawing I” before taking this lecture. The contents handled in this lecture are as follows. ・ Outline of JIS standards for drawing creation and CAD operation methods specialized for mechanical drawing ・ Relationship between dimensional tolerance and geometric tolerance ・ Surface roughness ・ Dimension filling method ・ Bolts and nuts ・ Keys and keyways ・ Cross sections ・ Gear basics and design machine elements such as bearings ・ Drawing mechanical parts and assembly drawings with gear pumps and flanged fixed shaft joints In addition, it is necessary to be able to fully understand the design at the actual manufacturing site.  Copying in drafting drawings is against the ethics of engineers, and credits for this subject are revoked when it is found.
books: Textbooks:New JIS mechanical drawing(5th edition),Moritika Publishing(in Japanese) JIS mechanical drawing operation method using Solid Edge,Kanazawa Institute of Technology(in Japanese) Reference books:None Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge: (1) You can draw on the CAD software drawing creation screen. Your ability should be at a level where it is easy to create a model of the text “Mechanical Drawing”. Basically, items that should have been learned in Mechanical Drawing I (functions written in the text, drawing methods) are not taught in this course. (2) 3D (3D objects) can be modeled using 3D drafting, the 3rd angle method (2D drafting) and using two-dimensional drafting (plan view, front view, side view). (3) You have mastered the method of downloading materials and uploading reports using the student portal.

activityGoals.body: Be able to transmit a design using mechanical drawing.
Be able to draw a two-dimensional mechanical drawing from a bird's-eye view or a photograph of the machine parts
Be able to imagine the shape of a part drawn from a two-dimensional mechanical drawing created by a third party.
Be able to indicate the machine design, tolerance, and accuracy for the manufacturing method of machine parts.
Be able to prepare and explain the results of preparation and review as works at the specified time.
Be able to explain the design process and role at the manufacturing site.
