lessons.content: Guidance ・ Explain the outline of this course. ・ Understand the objectives, goals and required achievement levels of this course. ・ Understand the learning objectives, outlines, and behavioral goals of subjects based on the learning support plan to be distributed. In particular, understand which part of the department's educational goals this course is responsible for, and the specific measure of achievement level. ・ Introduce the student portal system and download the KIT drafting template file. Drawing screen and KIT drawing ・ For CAD software, Mechanical Drawing I used exercises on the drawing screen, but in Mechanical Drawing II, a drawing is created in the drawing format of KIT, and necessary information is described, laid out, and printed. Drafting exercise -Check the various functions of the CAD software to be used. ・ Exercise A: Within the operation range acquired in Mechanical Drawing I, any three-dimensional object can be represented as a plan view, a front view, and a side view, and printed using the KIT drawing. ・ Exercise B: On the basis of several triangulation drawings, each person can imagine a three-dimensional view (bird's-eye view) and draw it by hand.
lessons.operation: Lectures, questions, and exercises “Drawing” shown in the lesson details indicates Mechanical Drawing, and “JIS” indicates New JIS Machine Drawing. Drawing: Chapters 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 JIS: pp. 1-6
lessons.assignments: [Preparation] Make CAD software usable. Understand the relationship between the department's educational goals and this subject. ・ Review of drafting method from Mechanical Drawing I [Review] Review the content and objectives of this lecture. In addition to reviewing the contents of the lecture, the exercises in Exercise A and Exercise B should be completed. ・ Review of plane display method of objects by 3rd angle method

lessons.content: Review dimensional tolerances, fits, and surface roughnesses learned in Mechanical Drawing I. Review contents ・ Dimensional tolerance, fit ・ Standard dimensions, dimensional tolerance, etc. ・ Functional dimensions, non-functional dimensions, reference dimensions ・ Explanation of IT tolerance and how to read a dimensional tolerance table ・ Learn about surface roughness in specific mechanical drawings based on the outline explanation of Mechanical Drawing I. ・ Explain how to measure surface roughness. ・ Learn about the relationship between machine manufacturing and processing methods and surface roughness. Dimensional tolerance indication method in CAD software ・ Review the dimensional tolerance indication method in New JIS Machine Drafting. ・ Review how to put dimensional tolerances in CAD software. Surface roughness indication method with CAD software ・ Learn how to indicate surface roughness on JIS machine drawings. ・ Learn how to insert surface roughness with CAD software. Drafting exercise ・ Create a drawing of the gear pumps ② and ④ and fill in the dimensions and tolerances. ・ Download the drawing of the gear pump ③ and⑧ from the student portal and add dimensional tolerances to it. "Check back" ・ Confirm how to interpret 3D figures based on specific issues
lessons.operation: Lectures, questions, and exercises Explain the stipulation of dimensions in mechanical drawing, and understand the concepts of tolerance and fit. Drafting: Chapter 6 JIS: pp. 39-44 Lectures, questions, and exercises Surface finishing in the case of machining will be explained, and the relationship between the method of defining the surface roughness and the processing method will be understood. Drafting: Chapter 7 JIS: pp. 44-47
lessons.assignments: (Preparation) Prepare the lecture theme. ・ Investigating accuracy requirements in mechanical drawings ・ Review of dimensional tolerances and fit regulations Review of learning contents of Mechanical Drawing I ・ Investigation of how to express surface properties [Review] Review the content of the lecture and complete the assignment. ・ Learn how to define dimensional tolerances and the relationship between JIS rules from fit relationships ・ Understand the meaning of surface roughness regulations and learn how to request them

lessons.content: Summary of dimensional tolerance, fit, and surface roughness -Review various diameter dimensioning methods and various dimensioning methods (series, parallel, progression, coordinates). -The surface roughness entry method is compared with a method based on the old JIS standard and a method based on the current JIS standard. ・ Explain how to create drawings that are easy for third parties to see. Drafting exercise ・ Create a drawing of the gear pump ⑤ and enter the dimensions and tolerances. "Check back"
lessons.operation: Lectures, questions, and exercises We will explain the dimension specifications that define the dimensions of machine equipment, the fitting regulations that take assembly into account, and the surface roughness instructions that define the finished surface, and help you understand the relationship between the processing method and the geometry of machine parts. JIS: pp. 1-47
lessons.assignments: Preparation] Prepare a lecture theme. Review of learning contents of Mechanical Drawing I ・ Investigation of JIS surface roughness regulations [Review] Review the content of the lecture and complete the assignment. ・ Learn how to draft surface roughness

lessons.content: Bolts and nuts ・ Outline explanation on bolts and nuts. ・ Bolt and nut drawing method and bolt hole drawing method explained Drafting exercise ・ Prepare drawings of bolts and nuts and show dimensional tolerances and surface roughnesses. Note that the size of bolts and nuts to be changed will vary depending on the student. "Check back" ・ Confirm how to interpret drafting drawings based on issues
lessons.operation: Lectures, questions, and exercises Explain about bolts and nuts, which are representative parts of screws, which are fastening elements of machines, and understand how to select and request parts based on JIS standards when designing machines. Drafting: Chapter 8 JIS: pp. 26-27, 68, 114-115
lessons.assignments: [Preparation] Prepare a lecture theme. ・ Investigate the relationship between bolt/ nut function/performance items and design items [Review] Review the content of the lecture and complete the assignment. ・ Acquisition of drafting method for standard parts such as standardized bolts and nuts

lessons.content: Bolts and nuts (continued) -Explain the types of bolts and nuts, selection methods, usage methods, and strength calculations. -Explain one guideline for the design method of bolt mounting points (mounting seats, etc.). "Check back" ・ Confirm how to interpret drafting drawings based on issues
lessons.operation: Lectures, questions, and exercises Explain how to specify standards for standard parts such as bolts and nuts and understand design requirements. Drafting: Chapter 8 JIS: pp. 68, 114-115
lessons.assignments: [Preparation] Prepare a lecture theme. ・ Investigation of relationship between standard parts such as bolts and nuts and JIS standards [Review] Review the content of the lecture and complete the assignment. ・ Deepen understanding of the relationship between parts drawings such as bolts and assembly drawings.

lessons.content: Overall review, interim review ・ Review the outline of dimensional tolerance, surface roughness and instruction method, bolt selection method and instruction method. ・ Interim review "Check back" ・ Confirm how to interpret drafting drawings based on issues 1st exam ・ Confirm the basics of machine drafting explained so far and the level of mastery of CAD operation.
lessons.operation: Lectures, questions, and exercises Examination (practical examination) (interim review) Confirm the acquisition of drafting techniques and JIS standard application methods.
lessons.assignments: [Preparation] Prepare the lecture content. ・ Check the level of understanding up to chapters 1-8 and improve CAD operation skills [Review] Review the content of the lecture. ・ Review any shortage

lessons.content: Key and key groove ・ We will give an overview of the role of keys and keyways. ・ Explain the key designation (size), keyway dimension indication method, and dimensional tolerance selection method along with practice. Comprehensive learning ・ Cooperate with local communities to explain design / manufacturing methods of local manufacturing engineers and understand on-site design processes. Drafting exercise ・ Create a drawing of the gear pump (4) and enter the dimensions and tolerances.
lessons.operation: Lectures, questions and exercises Explain the specifications of keys and key grooves, which are fastening elements related to the assembly of machine parts, from mechanical strength and external dimensions (active learning) JIS: pp. 19-20,110-113
lessons.assignments: [Preparation] Prepare a lecture theme. ・ Investigate parts fastening, especially to understand key and key groove structure [Review] Review the lecture and complete the assignment. ・ Understand the strength design method for key fastening

lessons.content: Geometric tolerance ・ Learn about geometric tolerances in specific mechanical drawings based on the outline explanation of Mechanical Drawing I. -Explain the necessity and method of indicating concentricity, squareness, parallelism, etc. -Explain the relationship between dimensional tolerances and geometrical tolerances. Geometry tolerance indication method and drafting exercise in CAD software -Explain how to specify geometric tolerances in JIS machine drafting. -Explain how to add geometric tolerance in CAD software. ・ Add the geometric tolerance to the drawing of the gear pump ②. ・ Create a drawing of the gear pump ①⑥.
lessons.operation: Lectures, questions, and exercises Explain geometric tolerances, which are the shape specifications for each component considering manufacturing and assembly, and allow them to understand machining techniques and assembly procedures. Drafting: Chapters 7 and 8 JIS: pp. 48-51
lessons.assignments: [Preparation] Prepare a lecture theme. Review of learning contents of Mechanical Drawing I ・ Investigate the geometric tolerance guidelines for parts shape [Review] Review the content of the lecture and complete the assignment. ・ Understand how to display geometric tolerance indications

lessons.content: Cross section - Explain the need for a cross-sectional view. ・ Explain how to represent cross-sectional views. Other ・ Description of key, geometric tolerance, dimensional tolerance, etc., using flange-type fixed shaft coupling Master the procedure. Drafting exercise ・ Draw a flange-type fixed shaft joint. "Check back" ・ Confirm how to interpret drafting drawings based on issues
lessons.operation: Lectures, questions, and exercises Cross-sectional view display regulations, which are illustration methods in mechanical drafting, will be explained to improve drafting skills. Drafting: Chapter 8 JIS: pp. 8-10, 79, 147-149
lessons.assignments: [Preparation] Prepare a lecture theme. ・ Understand cross-section display method [Review] Review the content of the lecture and complete the assignment. ・ Learn how to specify the section. ・ Obtain easy-to-read layout guidelines for parts drawing.

lessons.content: How to draw dimensions in consideration of the reference plane -Explain how to draw dimensions (how to make reference planes, how to draw dimensions that are easy to see). Gear basics 1 ・ Overview of the basics of gears. - Explain the basic calculation method, such as the number of teeth, and the relationship between the module and the reference circle (pitch circle) diameter. - Re-explain how to indicate dimensional tolerances and geometrical tolerances using gear drawing. Drafting exercise ・Draw the gear. ・Give the number of teeth, modules, tooth width, etc. for each student, and create a simple gear design and draw it. "Check back" ・ Confirm how to interpret drafting drawings based on issues
lessons.operation: Lectures, questions, and exercises Explain the relationship between machining methods to be considered from design to drawing and drawing method Understand the basic mechanism of gears JIS: pp. 28-31, 76
lessons.assignments: [Preparation] Prepare a lecture theme. ・ Understand the functional performance of gears [Review] Review the content of the lecture and complete the assignment. ・ Understand gear drafting and geometric mechanisms

lessons.content: Gear basics ② ・ Expression method for meshing of gears, outline explanation and calculation for "reduction gear" which is a typical machine using gears Bearings and oil seals ・ Outline and type of bearings and oil seals that are important machine elements for comprehensive force learning ・ Investigate and examine selection methods. Drafting exercise ・ Draw a gear pump assembly drawing. "Check back" ・ Confirm how to interpret drafting drawings based on issues
lessons.operation: Lectures, questions, and exercises Practice gear design specifications for your requirements (Active learning) JIS: pp. 37-38, 152-153
lessons.assignments: [Preparation] Prepare a lecture theme. ・ Understand the reducer as a mechanical mechanism [Review] Review the content of the lecture and complete the assignment. Report the results of the investigation and examination ・ Understand the interface requirements for ensuring the functional performance of the assembled machine

lessons.content: Overall review, general exercises (Last review (1)) ・ Review the geometrical tolerances, outline of cross-section display and indication methods, key and keyway selection and indication methods, and drawing of gears. ・ Review items to be confirmed regarding CAD skills "Check back" ・ Confirm how to interpret drafting drawings based on issues
lessons.operation: Lectures, questions, and exercises Explain the relationship between design requirements, design specifications, and drawings, and understand the flow of machine design and the meaning of each drawing. Discuss the pump design of each specification based on gear pump assembly drawings. At the same time, check the design process.

subtitle: Engineering Mechanics II
keywords: Equation of motion 2.Moment of inertia 3.Laws of conservation of momentum and angular momentum 4.Collision and impulse 5.Rigid body motion
educationalGoal: Continue improving your understanding of Newton's equation of motion as the basis for dynamics, such as the movement of a mass system and rigid body caused by external force or torque. title: ロボット材料力学
subtitle: Mechanics of Materials
keywords: Stress, strain 2.Shearing force, bending moment 3.Beam deflection
educationalGoal: Understand how force application to and deformation of a material is important as a basis of the structural design of machines and robots. Learn step-by-step stress and strain and the deformation of stressed objects, truss structures, and beams by lecture and exercises. Represent the inner stress caused by external forces as a mathematical model useful for design.
advice: 1. Students will use mathematical tools (matrix, vector, and differential equations) and physical tools (units, force, and moment). In this course, these tools are reviewed and supplemented. Students are expected to review mathematics and physics. 2. Students are expected to work hard on exercises during the class and review them afterward. Students are expected to complete all exercises. 3. Questions should not be left unsolved. Review of basic mathematics and physics is recommended.

educationalGoal: (1) Review complex numbers for frequency response. (2) Learn Laplace transforms for solving linear differential equations. (3) Acquire the capability to formulate transfer functions and block diagrams.
advice: This is a basic course in control engineering. We will mainly cover the following topics: 1. Calculation using complex numbers and Laplace transforms. 2. requiredKnowledge: Completion of Engineering Mechanics I/II and Electric Circuit I/II. Basic knowledge of differential calculus.

Use basic Laplace transforms.
Solve linear differential equations with inverse Laplace transforms.
Obtain transfer functions from differential equations.
Obtain transfer functions from block diagrams.

title: ロボティクス数理・演習Ⅱ
subtitle: Mathematical Fundamentals of Robotics II
keywords: Mathematical basics
educationalGoal: Acquire the mathematical knowledge necessary to learn robotics. Further improve your basic academic ability by participating in lectures and exercises related to the content of other classes offered during the same semester.
advice: In “Mathematical Fundamentals of Robotics”, two subjects are designated from the required subjects offered in the same semester as active learning consisting of comprehensive exercises. This course, which can be taken as an elective, is intended to promote your learning skills and to deepen your understanding of the required courses. In Mathematical Fundamentals of Robotics II, the exercises for Dynamics of Machine Systems I and Introduction to Control Engineering/Control Engineering I are carried out every other week. Depending on the level of understanding of students in the course, the content of the lecture and the learning objectives are reviewed, together with the taking of quizzes and completion of exercises. Summarizing and reviewing the lessons learned in the latter two courses is a preparation and review task for this course.
requiredKnowledge: Review and understand the content of Dynamics of Machine Systems I and Introduction to Control Engineering/Control Engineering I.

activityGoals.body: Reinforce and apply the basic knowledge learned in Dynamics of Machine Systems I
Reinforce and apply the basic knowledge learned in Introduction to Control Engineering/Control Engineering I
Learn and practice independent learning habits

title: ロボット応用力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Dynamics of Machine Systems II
keywords: Solving equation of motion 2.Free and forced vibration 3.Natural angular frequency 4.Damping ratio, damped natural frequency 5.Resonance phenomenon
educationalGoal: Acquire basic knowledge about machinery vibration problems. Understand the basics of vibration and apply it to machine design. Model and analyze basic vibration phenomena.
advice: In recent years, high speed and high precision have been achieved to improve productivity, but vibrations generated in various machines cause problems. In this course, it is necessary to understand how to derive and solve the equations for expressing the motion of various vibration models. Therefore, students must not only understand the lectures but also work on exercises and reports the help them acquire the ability to solve vibration problems. The following topics are covered: 1.Basics of mechanical vibration: equations of motion, simple vibration, harmonic vibration, vectors, and complex representation of vibration 2.Free vibration of a one-degree-of-freedom system without damping 3.Free vibration of a one-degree-of-freedom system with damping 4.Forced vibration of a one-degree-of-freedom system 5.Basics of vibration of a two-degree-of-freedom system
books: Textbook: Basic Vibration Engineering (2nd Edition) [Kyoritsu Shuppan]
requiredKnowledge: Review Robot Basic Mechanics I & II and Robot Applied Dynamics I in addition to mathematics such as trigonometric functions and differential equations.

activityGoals.body: Model vibration phenomena and derive equations of motion.
Solve equations of motion (differential equations).
Understand and explain the characteristics of the free vibration system with and without damping.
Understand and explain the characteristics of the forced vibration system with and without damping.
Understand and explain the characteristics of a two-degree-of-freedom vibration system using eigenvalue analysis

advice: In "Mathematical Fundamentals of Robotics", two subjects are designated from the required subjects offered in the same semester as active learning consisting of comprehensive exercises. title: 信号処理
subtitle: Signal Processing
keywords: Digital signal processing 2.Convolution 3.Z-transform 4.Fourier analysis
educationalGoal: (1) Learn the foundations of signal processing, including analog-to-digital conversion. (2) Understand the basic concepts for digital signals processing, including convolution, Z-transform, sampling theorem, and Fourier analysis. (3) Acquire the ability to evaluate signals transmitted between linear time-invariant (LTI) systems and to extract the features underlying signals.
advice: This is a basic course in signal processing for discrete time signals. We will mainly cover the following topics: 1. Basic concepts of digital signal processing. 2. Expressing LTI systems with linear convolution. 3. Expressing discrete time transfer functions using Z-transform and its frequency domain property. 4. Expressing Fourier series and Fourier transform for continuous and discrete time signals in relation to the sampling theorem. Students are expected to actively participate in class. Students are expected to complete exercises independently. Students are required to be aware of the instructor’s messages in the class and to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class because the course schedule may change depending on the class progress.
books: Hitoshi Kiya, Digital Signal Processing (in Japanese), Ohmsha
requiredKnowledge: Sufficient mathematical calculation skills (especially those covered in Control Engineering I). Basic knowledge of differential and integral calculus.

activityGoals.body: Explain expressions of discrete time signals obtained by sampling various continuous time signals
Express the linear convolution of discrete time signals, Fourier series, and Fourier transform
Express the characteristics of transient responses and frequency responses of discrete LTI systems

    授業科目の学習・教育目標   キーワード 学習・教育目標     1.Kinematics 2.Inverse kinematics 3.Dynamics 4.Inverse dynamics 5.Position and force control  (1) Learn kinematics and inverse kinematics of robot manipulators. (2) Learn dynamics and inverse dynamics of robot manipulators. (3) Learn modeling and control methods for robotic systems.
    授業の概要および学習上の助言   This is a basic course in robot control. It covers the following topics: 1. Mechanism of robotic manipulators and statics and dynamics for robotic systems. 2. Representation of position and orientation of manipulators, and velocity and moment of rigid bodies. 3. Dynamic equations of manipulators. 4. Generation of a desired trajectory and position control method. 5. Force control method, including impedance/hybrid control.
    教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック   We have one textbook. The textbook is written in Japanese.
    履修に必要な予備知識や技能   Sufficient mathematical skills (differential equations, integrals, and linear algebra). Basic knowledge of dynamics and control engineering.

title: ロボットインテリジェンス
subtitle: Robot Intelligence
keywords: Artificial intelligence 2.Machine learning 3.Probability 4.Regression 5.Classification
educationalGoal: Learn the basics of machine learning, which is one of many subfields of artificial intelligence and is applied in various fields including robotics, where it can play an important role especially for treating uncertainty that a robot can encounter in the real world, in order to be able to apply it in developing a robot.
advice: This is a basic course in machine learning, which is one of the many artificial intelligence subfields and is applied in various fields, including robotics, where it can play an important role. We will mainly cover the following chapters of the textbook: Chapter 1, Introduction Chapter 2, Probability Distributions Chapter 3, Linear Models for Regression Chapter 4, Linear Models for Classification Students are expected to actively participate in class. Students are expected to complete exercises independently. Students are required to be aware of the instructor’s messages in the class and to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class because the course schedule may change depending on the class progress.
books: Textbooks: Christopher M. Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, 1st volume, Maruzen Publishing Co., Ltd., 2012 (in Japanese).
requiredKnowledge: Sufficient knowledge in mathematics (especially regarding differential and integral calculus and linear algebra) Completion of Integrated Math and Science for Engineering (Functions and Differentiation), Integrated Math and Science for Engineering (Integration and Differential Equations), and Linear Algebra I and II.

title: 機械加工学
subtitle: Machining Engineering
keywords: Cutting 2.Cutting mechanism 3.Tool material 4.Tool wear 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: (1) Learn the basic theory of removal machining. (2) Learn methods to measure cutting force and cutting edge temperature. (3) Learn the types of tool damage and their causes. (4) Learn how to manufacture cutting tools using powder metallurgy and surface coating techniques. (5) Learn how to select cutting tool materials and cutting conditions.
advice: This class will cover the following topics: 1. Classification of processing methods 2. Chip formation mechanism (Classification and formation mechanism of chips, Built-up edge, Generation conditions, and Methods to prevent built-up edge) 3. Cutting theory (Theoretical calculation of cutting force and Theoretical calculation of cutting temperature) 4. Measurement of cutting specifications (Cutting force, Cutting temperature, Chip thickness, and Contact length between chip and rake face) 5. Cutting tool wear and wear factors 6. Cutting tool material (Type and Classification) 7. Powder metallurgy technology and coating technology 8. Finished surface quality and control 9. Machinability of difficult-to-cut materials Students should be aware of the teacher’s instructions in the class, because the schedules of quizzes, tests, and reports may change as the class progresses.
books: Textbooks:[Jitsuyou sessaku kakouhou],Yoshio Fujimura, Kyouritsu syuppan Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Students are expected to watch the machining videos that supplement the lecture content. In addition, it is important to have the experiences of touring machining facilities and attending a machine industry fair.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the basics of cutting theory.
Be able to understand the measurement methods for cutting specifications.
Be able to understand the form and factors of tool damage.
Be able to understand the types of cutting tool materials and their effective use.
Be able to understand the types of difficult-to-cut materials and their machinability.
Be able to select optimum cutting conditions and machine tools.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) A two-dimensional cutting model and the theoretical mechanism of shearing can be explained using figures. (2) Measurement methods of cutting force and cutting temperature can be explained using detailed figures. (3) The damage classification of cutting tools and its cause can be explained in detail. (4) The method for manufacturing cutting tools with powder metallurgy and surface coating techniques can be explained in detail. (5) The finished surface quality can be explained. (6) The machining conditions, and tool shape for high-efficiency machining can be selected appropriately.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) A two-dimensional cutting model and the theoretical mechanism of shear can be explained. (2) Measuring methods for cutting force and cutting temperature can be explained. (3) The types and causes of cutting tool damage can be explained. (4) Methods for using powder metallurgy and surface coating technology can be described. (5) Surface roughness can be explained. (6) The machining method, machining conditions, and tool shape can be selected.

lessons.content: Conditions that generate a built-up edge and methods to prevent it. Basics of cutting force.

lessons.assignments: Study pp.14-18 of textbook Review about derivation of theoretical formula for cutting force.

lessons.content: Experimental techniques and methods of measuring phenomena during cutting.
lessons.assignments: Study pp.32-39 and pp.50-60 of textbook Review about the measuring method of cutting force and temperature.

lessons.content: Exercises on theoretical calculation based on measured data during cutting force.
lessons.assignments: understand about theoretical formula for cutting force. Review about the calculation method for cutting force.

lessons.content: Tool wear patterns and wear mechanisms.
lessons.assignments: Study pp.61-78 of textbook Review the Tool wear patterns and cutting environment.

lessons.content: Causes of tool damage.
lessons.assignments: Study pp.68-78 of textbook. (Especially about the cause of Tool wear) Review the tool wear patterns and the cause of tool wear.

lessons.content: Material properties required for tool materials. Characteristics of tool materials and their application (high-speed steel, cemented carbide, and coated cemented carbide)
lessons.assignments: Study pp.101-109 of textbook. Review the material properties required for tool and characteristics of tool materials.

lessons.content: Characteristics of tool materials and their application (cermet, ceramics, cubic boron nitrite, and poly-crystalline diamond)
lessons.assignments: Study pp.108-130 of textbook Review the material properties required for tool and characteristics of tool materials.

lessons.content: Definition and classification of hard to cut materials.
lessons.assignments: Study pp.190-195 of textbook Review the classification of hard to cut materials and machining problems.

lessons.content: Learn the characteristics of hard to cut materials and cutting conditions.
lessons.assignments: Study about characteristics of hard to cut materials. Review the machining problems and countermeasures it.

lessons.assignments: Review of classes 1 to 13. self-inspection of final exam.

title: 電気回路Ⅰ
subtitle: Electric Circuit I
keywords: Electric circuit 2.Circuit equation 3.Transient phenomena
educationalGoal: (1) Learn the foundations of electronics. (2) Understand the basic concepts of electric circuits. (3) Acquire the capability to formulate and analyze various phenomena in electric circuits mathematically.
advice: This is a basic course on electric circuits. We will mainly cover the following topics: 1. Basic concepts of electric circuits 2. Expressing relationships between voltages and currents in DC circuits in mathematical formulas and calculating voltage, current, and electric power in such circuits 3. Expressing transient phenomena in electric circuits consisting of DC power supplies, resistors, capacitors, and inductors in differential equations Students are expected to actively participate in class. Students are expected to complete exercises independently. Students are required to be aware of the instructor’s messages in the class and to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class because the course schedule may change depending on the class progress.
books: Textbooks: Masao Saito, Introduction to Electric Circuits and Systems, Corona Publishing Co., Ltd., 2006 (in Japanese).
requiredKnowledge: Sufficient skill in mathematical calculations (especially polynomial and fractional expressions). Basic knowledge of differential calculus.

Mathematically express the relationships among voltage, current, and electric power in DC circuits.
Express transient phenomena in differential equations.

title: 専門ゼミ(ロボティクス学科)
subtitle: Preparatory Seminar for Design Project III (Robotics)
keywords: Robot intelligence 2.Robot mechanics 3.Intelligent control 4.Mechatronics 5.Regional collaboration
educationalGoal: (1)Predict robotics issues that could be encountered in Design Project III. (2)Learn how to use your acquired knowledge and techniques to address these issues. (3)Learn how to comprehensively apply your ability as an engineer. (4)Learn the importance of collaboration with regional society (especially the local community).
advice: Issues to be addressed in Design Project III are presented. Students will understand the knowledge and skills required to carry out their senior project and identify where supplemental knowledge is needed. During the course of this seminar, students will clarify the purpose and action plan for their project, and finally make a project proposal. Note: Details will be provided during the first class.
requiredKnowledge: If you do not earn credit for this course, you cannot take Design Project III.

activityGoals.body: Clarify the purpose and action plan of your design project.
Understand important robotic technologies in each laboratory.
Apply your basic skills to develop a new robotic system during the project.
Decide the theme of the project, and summarize the research proposal.
Understand safety management for conducting experiments and developing the project.
See your future course and decide the direction you should follow.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(出村公成研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Demura Kosei)
keywords: Robot mechanics and mechatronics 2.Robot intelligence 3.Measurement and control 4.Robot programming 5.Regional collaboration
educationalGoal: (1) Acquire the ability to find and solve problems to research, develop, design, and create new robotic systems, using the basic knowledge and skills you learned in other Department of Robotics courses. (2) Learn what technologies are required to solve problems. (3) Learn about the importance of collaboration with society (particularly local communities).
advice: This is the final comprehensive course in the Department of Robotics. It is a two-semester course. For the realization of the educational objectives in the Department of Robotics, this course focuses on the following topics: (1) Students will acquire the ability to create new robotic systems integrated mechanics, measurement and control engineering, electronics, and programming techniques. (2) Students will acquire the ability and the engineering sense to propose optimal solutions through design projects. Students should reconfirm their project theme, which has been determined in a preparatory seminar with the supervisors of the individual laboratories.
requiredKnowledge: Have the skills and knowledge required for carrying out a project at each laboratory. Obtain a license for using machine tools at YUMEKOBO.

activityGoals.body: Advance your project in according to the engineering design process.
Compile the results correctly into a report and discuss the content through presentations.
Act independently to solve the issues presented separately.

subtitle: Mathematical Basics for Engineering
keywords: Engineering and manufacturing 2.Mathematics for EE
educationalGoal: Students will learn about the technology in the fields of machinery, electricity / electronics, and information, which are the three major technologies for manufacturing that support society, as preparation to become “an engineer to consider and act on their own”. Students will have training to develop their mathematical skills that are essential for our fields.
advice: 1.Introduction of research fields Students will learn about the research area in the field of electrical and electronic engineering, and will learn about the research efforts in that area through some specific examples. 2. Development of mathematical skills Students will review and have trainings on the basic mathematical functions (trigonometric function, exponential function, and logarithmic function), vector (vector basics, vector and plane coordinates, vector and space coordinates, scalar product, and vector product), differentiation (differentiation method, derivatives of commonly used functions, and application of differentiation), and integration (indefinite integration, definite integration, and application of integration) , which will be widely needed in their future.
books: A textbook written in Japanese will be used.
requiredKnowledge: This course is an introduction to the field of electrical and electronic engineering. It is important to pay close attention to the technology in which each student is interested. It is also important to review mathematics (functions and graphs, trigonometric functions, exponential functions, vectors, differential methods, integration methods, and etc.) learned in high school for future learning. It is desirable to study areas that were not taken in high school using self-study and learning support systems in our university.

title: 電気回路Ⅰ
subtitle: Electric Circuits I
keywords: DC circuits 2.Ohm's law 3.Kirchhoff's law 4.Sinusoids 5.AC basic circuits, Phasors
educationalGoal: This is a fundamental and important subject in the electrical engineering course. To acquire basic knowledge about electrical circuits and develop the ability to conduct analysis and design of electrical circuits through physical and mathematical considerations. First, a case where a circuit having resistors (R) are connected to DC sources is learned, and then a case where a circuit comprising resistors (R), inductors (L), capacitors (C), and combinations thereof are connected to an AC power supply is learned.
advice: The outline of the subjects is as follows. 1.DC circuits: electric circuits and Ohm's law, Kirchhoff's law, superposition principle, Thevenin's Theorem, power and energy. 2.AC basic circuits: sinusoids, phasors relationships for resistors, inductors, and capacitors. AVIS Video Courseware has been prepared for each item in the above, and will be used actively for preparation and review to deepen understanding. This subject is not only "Electrical Circuit II", "Electrical Circuit III", and "Electrical Circuit IV", but also each specialized subject should be studied keeping in mind that it is a special basic course required. Since the progress is adjusted while checking the level of understanding based on the results of a quiz, etc., changes may occur in the class schedule and the content of study.
requiredKnowledge: In this subject, it is important to solve more problems in order to understand and practice the theory. In addition, since they are made one by one, continuous efforts are required on a daily basis. Therefore, we would like you to take actions such as 1) examining various reference books, 2) asking questions to the lecturer, 3) taking advantage of the Mathematical and Science Education Research Center, so that you can definitely clear what you don't understand.

activityGoals.body: Participants can explain Ohm's and Kirchhoff's law in DC circuits, and calculate it using these laws.
Participants can calculate the maximum power condition in the DC circuit.
Participants can calculate the mean and rms value of sinusoids, and analyze combined circuits of R, L and C.
Participants can analyze circuits by the phasors of complex number, and draw graph in each part of the circuit.

To acquire basic knowledge about electrical circuits and develop the ability to conduct analysis and design of electrical circuits through physical and mathematical considerations. First, a case where a circuit having resistors (R) are connected to DC sources is learned, and then a case where a circuit comprising resistors (R), inductors (L), capacitors (C), and combinations thereof are connected to an AC power supply is learned.
    授業の概要および学習上の助言   The outline of the subjects is as follows. 1.DC circuits: electric circuits and Ohm's law, Kirchhoff's law, superposition principle, Thevenin's Theorem, power and energy. 2.AC basic circuits: sinusoids, phasors relationships for resistors, inductors, and capacitors. AVIS Video Courseware has been prepared for each item in the above, and will be used actively for preparation and review to deepen understanding. This subject is not only "Electrical Circuit II", "Electrical Circuit III", and "Electrical Circuit IV", but also each specialized subject should be studied keeping in mind that it is a special basic course required. Since the progress is adjusted while checking the level of understanding based on the results of a quiz, etc., changes may occur in the class schedule and the content of study.
    教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック
    履修に必要な予備知識や技能   In this subject, it is important to solve more problems in order to understand and practice the theory. In addition, since they are made one by one, continuous efforts are required on a daily basis. Therefore, we would like you to take actions such as 1) examining various reference books, 2) asking questions to the lecturer, 3) taking advantage of the Mathematical and Science Education Research Center, so that you can definitely clear what you don't understand.

keywords: Phasor 2.Complex impedance 3.Complex admittance 4.Resonance, Electric power
educationalGoal: This course, including a review of “Electric Circuits I”, covers resistance (R), inductance (L), capacitance (C), and basic circuits that combine them to slightly more complex AC circuits. In the calculation of AC circuit, it is no exaggeration to say that it is common sense to use a so-called symbolic method using phasors and complex numbers. Here, students learn circuit analysis techniques using symbolic methods. After this course, “Electric Circuits III” will be the basis for learning more advanced and complex analysis methods for electrical circuits.
advice: 1. Phasor of a complex number and symbolic method of AC circuit 2. Series and parallel connection of complex impedance and complex admittance 3. Therefore, do not leave what you do not understand, so be sure to clear 1) check various reference books, 2) ask the teachers, 3) use the Mathematics Education Center. title: 電気磁気学Ⅰ
subtitle: Electromagnetics I
keywords: Charge and coulomb force 2.Electric field and electric potential 3.Capacitance of conductor system 4.Dielectric material 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: “Electromagnetics I” is an important basic subject in the field of electrical, electronic and information communication, and is essential for understanding the specialized subjects to be taken after the second year. “Learning objectives” is to learn basic mathematics necessary to analyze various physical phenomena in “electromagnetics”, to understand the basic laws on charge, electric field, electric potential and capacitance in electrostatic field, to acquire the ability to answer various problems of static electric field.
advice: The class covers the following items. Chapter 1 : Charge and Coulomb force (Phenomenon to charge, charge and properties, conductor and nonconductor, electrostatic induction, Coulomb's law, Coulomb force, Coulomb force and plane coordinates, composition of multiple Coulomb forces in plane coordinates, Coulomb force and space coordinates) Chapter 2 : Electric field and electric potential (electric field, synthetic electric field by multiple electric charges, synthetic electric field by electric charge distributed continuously, electric field lines, small area passing, lines of electric force, potential, potential due to multiple charges, equipotential surface, spatial representation of potential, Gauss's law and its application) Chapter 3 : Capacitance of conductor system (the nature of charged conductor, capacitance, capacitance of various conductor systems, electric imaging method, contact of capacitor, Energy of the capacitor) Chapter 4 : Dielectrics (Dielectric properties, polarization, electric field and electric flux density in dielectric, electric field and electric flux density in two dielectrics, conduction with dielectric energy stored between bodies, force between conductors filled with dielectrics) Chapter 5 : Current (Transfer of charge, ohm's law, resistance and resistor, conductance and conductivity, Joule heat and power, electric field in conductor, current density)
books: Textbook,A.Mikami, M.Masahiko, S.Makino, Y.Fujita, H.Yanagibashi,"Basic electromgnetics Ⅰ", Kanazawa Institute of Technology,(2019)
requiredKnowledge: This class is an introductory subject of "electromagnetics", and it is planned to take "electromagnetics II" and "electromagnetics III". So, the following background knowledge and skills are required. 1. Review the basic mathematics such as functions and graphs, trigonometric functions, vector analysis. 2. In electromagnetics, many new "units" are used. Understand the main units of physical quantities and the configuration of unit systems. 3. Be aware of the definitions and key formulas of technical terms.

activityGoals.body: The nature of charge, the Coulomb law acting between charges can be understood.
Understanding the relationship between electric field and potential formed by charge, and using Gauss's law.
The basic problem of the capacitance of a conductor system, electrostatic energy can be solved.
Understanding the electrical polarization of dielectrics.

    授業科目の学習・教育目標   キーワード 学習・教育目標     1.Charge and coulomb force 2.Electric field and electric potential 3.Capacitance of conductor system 4.Dielectric material 5.Regional cooperation  “Electromagnetics I” is an important basic subject in the field of electrical, electronic and information communication, and is essential for understanding the specialized subjects to be taken after the second year. “Learning objectives” is to learn basic mathematics necessary to analyze various physical phenomena in “electromagnetics”, to understand the basic laws on charge, electric field, electric potential and capacitance in electrostatic field, to acquire the ability to answer various problems of static electric field.
    授業の概要および学習上の助言   The class covers the following items. Chapter 1 : Charge and Coulomb force (Phenomenon to charge, charge and properties, conductor and nonconductor, electrostatic induction, Coulomb's law, Coulomb force, Coulomb force and plane coordinates, composition of multiple Coulomb forces in plane coordinates, Coulomb force and space coordinates) Chapter 2 : Electric field and electric potential (electric field, synthetic electric field by multiple electric charges, synthetic electric field by electric charge distributed continuously, electric field lines, small area passing, lines of electric force, potential, potential due to multiple charges, equipotential surface, spatial representation of potential, Gauss's law and its application) Chapter 3 : Capacitance of conductor system (the nature of charged conductor, capacitance, capacitance of various conductor systems, electric imaging method, contact of capacitor, Energy of the capacitor) Chapter 4 : Dielectrics (Dielectric properties, polarization, electric field and electric flux density in dielectric, electric field and electric flux density in two dielectrics, conduction with dielectric energy stored between bodies, force between conductors filled with dielectrics) Chapter 5 : Current (Transfer of charge, ohm's law, resistance and resistor, conductance and conductivity, Joule heat and power, electric field in conductor, current density)

    履修に必要な予備知識や技能   This class is an introductory subject of "electromagnetics", and it is planned to take "electromagnetics II" and "electromagnetics III". So, the following background knowledge and skills are required. 1. Review the basic mathematics such as functions and graphs, trigonometric functions, vector analysis. 2. In electromagnetics, many new "units" are used. Understand the main units of physical quantities and the configuration of unit systems. 3. Be aware of the definitions and key formulas of technical terms.

title: 電気電子プログラミング演習
subtitle: Programming Practice for Electrical and Electronic Engineers
keywords: Computer 2.Programing 3.C Language 4.Algorithm 5.Electrical and Electronic Engineers
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn the fundamental concepts and methods of programming using C language. (2) learn how to solve problems and transform the solutions into computer programs written in C language. The goal of this course is to provide an introduction not just to C but also to logical thinking. (3) learn some applications of C programming in electrical and electronic engineering.
advice: This course is designed to familiarize students with computer programming, with an emphasis on a widely used language, C. The classes incorporate lecture with hands-on programming exercises. We will cover the following materials: 1. Elementary programming in C 2. Selection statements 3. Repetition statements 4. Arrays 5. Modular programming with functions 6. Pointers 7. Structures 8. File input/output 9. Using C in electrical and electronic engineering applications Students should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class, because the detailed course schedules may change depending on the students' progress in understanding.
books: Textbooks: None Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: You are expected to bring your Windows laptop to class with you to work on programming exercises using Visual Studio. No prior programming knowledge is required. This course and “Computer Engineering for Electrical and Electronic Engineers” are complementary. “Electronic Circuits II” and “Feedback Control” are related to this course.

activityGoals.body: Be able to demonstrate problem-solving skills by developing algorithms to solve problems.
Be able to incorporate the selection and repetition control structures into C programs.
Be able to demonstrate understanding of the use of arrays and structures.
Be able to decompose the solution into modules at the function level.
Be able to demonstrate understanding of the use of pointers.
Be able to implement programs using file input/output.

title: 電子回路Ⅱ
subtitle: Electronic Circuits II
keywords: Boolean function 2.Logic circuits 3.Flip-flops 4.Counter circuits 5.A/D D/A converter
educationalGoal: Electronic circuits is a very important topic. In this subject, Digital Circuits, the objective is to learn the fndamentals of Boolean equations (logic algebra) and logic circuits, and to understand the principles behind how various logic circuits operate.In addition to combined logic circuits such as AND, OR, and NOT gates, the students will learn to understand and explain the operating principles of sequential circuits such as flip-flops and counters as well as more functional circuits such as analog to digital(A/D) and digital to analog (D/A) converters.
advice: We will cover the following materials. 1. Fundamental logic circuits and boolean function AND, OR, NOT, EX-OR 2. Design for combination logical circuit Conversion circuit (NAND, NOR) Simplification using the karnaugh map Logical circuit design Adder Circuit 3. Flip Flop(FF) Circuit Synchronous / asynchronous 4 types of FF RS-FF, JK-FF, T-FF, D-FF 4. Counter Circuit Synchronous/asynchronous type UP/DOWN counter Ripple counter Shift resister 5. A/D and D/A converter circuit Principle and design
requiredKnowledge: All you need to study this subject is to understand the physical electronics and basic electric circuit.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the digital electronics and fundamental logicl circuits.
Be able to design the basic combination logical circuit.
Be able to explain the 4 types for Flip Flop.
Be able to design the synchro and asynchro type digital counter circuit.
Be able to explain the principle opreration for A/D and D/A converter.

keywords: Transient Analysis 2.Circuit Equation 3.Laplace Transform 4.Transient Phenomena 5.Regional Collaboration
educationalGoal: The aim of this course is to help students acquire the necessary knowledge needed to understand the theory to learn in “Feedback Control” course in the 5th term. Students will: (1) solve transient electrical circuits using circuit equations and initial conditions. (2) analyze transient phenomena of more complex circuits by Laplace transform. (3) understand the various transient phenomena that occur in electrical circuits.

title: 電気電子計測
subtitle: Electrical and Electronic Instrumentation
keywords: SI units 2.Pointer type meter 3.Instrumentation apparatus 4.Digital Instrumentation 5.apparatus
educationalGoal: Electrical and electronic measurements are a way of measuring various electrical quantities. In some cases, it is possible to step out of the world of electronics and measure physical quantities such as length, weight, and speed. In this lecture, the students will learn what the units and measurement terms are and how to apply them. Additionally, they will learn the construction and measurement principles behind major electrical and electronic equipment so that they can understand the fundamentals of electric and electronic measurements.
advice: We will cover the following materials (1) Fundamental Instrumentation SI unit, Standard apparatus, measurement terminology (2) Pointer type meter moving coil type, moving iron type, rectifier type, etc. (3) Electrical instrumentation apparatus Electronic galvanometer, Electronic power meter (4) Digital Instrumentation apparatus digital voltmeter (5) Recording Instrument and waveform measurement Pen recorder, oscilloscope (6) Various electrical quantities instrument Voltage, current, resistor, power, frequency, magnetic field, etc.
requiredKnowledge: All you need to study this subject is to understand the basic electric circuits and basic electromagnetics you have already learned.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the measurement terminology and to used SI unit.
Be able to explain the basic block diagram of electrical instrumentation apparatus(mainly analog type)
Be able to explain the basic block diagram of electrical instrumentation apparatus(mainly digital type)
Be able to explain the various measuring apparatus, oscilloscope, impedance bridge, frequency counter.
Be able to choose the variable measuring apparatus in the intended purpose.

educationalGoal: In the field of optoelectronic devices such as electronic devices and lasers, it is essential to understand material properties. In this course, students learn the basics of their material properties. Specifically, we learn the basics of quantum mechanics, band theory, and understand the behavior of electrons in materials where electric and magnetic fields are present. Furthermore, we will understand the electrical, dielectric, magnetic and optical properties of materials from the atomic and molecular level of microscopic perspective.

(4) Debye's dispersion equation can be derived and explained for dielectric dispersion and dielectric loss in a dielectric. (5) The local electric field in the dielectric can be described by the Lorentz electric field and the Clausius-Mosotti equation.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Use the Schrodinger wave equation to explain the electron's wave function, orbit and energy levels. (2) The band theory can be explained from the energy levels of electrons in the crystal. (3) The band theory can be used to explain the difference in electric conduction in conductors, semiconductors, and insulators. (4)Be able to explain the difference between Drude's theory and quantum theory about the movement of electrons in crystals. (5) Various dielectric polarization mechanisms can be described from the relationship between electric dipole moment and dielectric dispersion.

title: 自動制御
subtitle: Feedback Control
keywords: Feedback Control 2.Transfer Function 3.Laplace Conversion & Inversion 4.Transient & Frequency Responses 5.Stability
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn framework of feedback control theory involving "Mathematical Expression","Laplace Conversions","Block Diagrams","Transfer Functions" and furthermore (2) learn characteristics "Transfer Functions","Stability","Transient & Frequency Responses","Steady States".
advice: This is a basic course of Feedback Control. We will cover the following materials: 1. Basic concepts in feedback control: The Laplace inversion & the time functions, System elements and block diagram, Graphical representation by the frequency functions. Representation with elementary blocks. 5. Stability of linear control systems 2. The various elements of a control process: The concept of stability Proportional, integrating, differentiating, and Stability analysis using the Routh-Hurwitz criterion 1st-order-, 2nd-order-, & delay-time lag blocks. (matrices & determinants) 3. Transformation from time (t) to frequency (s) domains: The elementary blocks & the transfer functions, The Laplace transformation & the transfer functions, Examples of electric circuit systems. 4. Transfer characteristics of typical basic blocks: Specifications in the time domain (transient responses), Specifications in the frequency domain (frequency responses)
requiredKnowledge: Acquisition of “Computer Engineering for Electrical Engineers” and “Electrical and Electronic Instrumentation”. Enough skill of mathematics (especially matrix / inverse matrix and determinant calculations). Basic knowledge of mathematics (the Laplace conversion & inversion and so on). How to use a calculator.

Be able to explain the Laplace conversion and inversion.
Be able to explain the transfer functions and represent control systems with the transfer functions & block diag
Be able to perform basic designs of the feedback control systems using the transfer functions.
Be able to explain analytical stability criteria on linear control systems.

title: 電気回路Ⅳ(電子工学)
subtitle: Electric Circuits IV for Electronic Engineering
keywords: Distributed-Constant Circuits 2.Reflection Coefficient 3.Smith Chart 4.Scattering Matrix 5.Impedance Matching
educationalGoal: In the previous study of electric circuits, the physical dimensions of a circuit has been assumed to be small enough. At the higher frequencies, however, the size of the circuit must be taken into account, and voltages and currents behave as waves. In this course, students will learn the theory of distributed-constant circuits, propagation of electric waves along transmission lines. They will also study about the tools and techniques for high-frequency circuit analysis and design.
advice: 1. Voltages and currents on distributed-constant circuits 2. Reflection Coefficient, standing waves, and input impedance looking into a transmission line. 3. Smith chart 4. Impedance matching for a distributed-constant circuit 5. Scattering matrix Students are expected to understand the difference between lumped-constant circuits and distributed-constant circuits, relation between frequency and wavelength, and will learn about the equations for voltages and currents on distributed-constant circuits and their solutions. Students are also expected to learn how to use Smith chart and scattering matrix.
requiredKnowledge: Understanding of Electric Circuits I, II and III, especially theory of alternating voltage and current. Enough skills of circuit analysis using complex numbers.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the difference between lumped-constant circuits and distributed-constant circuits.
Be able to analyze basic lumped-constant circuits.
Be able to use Smith chart.
Be able to design matching circuit.

Contents are following; [A] Fundamental properties of semiconductors 1. Density of states and Distribution function 2. Carrier density of impurity semiconductor 3. Drift current and diffusion current [B] Diodes 4. pn junction diode, its I-V characteristics, C-V characteristics, breakdown phenomena 5. MS(metal-semiconductor) contact and Schottky barrier diode [C] Transistors 6. Bipolar junction transistor, its operation mechanism, characteristics 7. MOS (metal-oxide-semiconductor), its structure and properties 8. MOS-FET (field effective transistor), its structure, operation mechanism, characteristics

title: 電子材料
subtitle: Electronic Material Engineering
keywords: Atomic orbital and electron configuration 2.Ferroelectrics 3.Ferromagnetism 4.Superconductor
educationalGoal: In this lecture, we learn about the material properties of dielectrics and magnetic materials, which are the basic materials in the electronic field along with semiconductors. To understand the polarization phenomenon and dielectric loss of dielectrics and the physical meaning of the magnetism, and also about applications of ferroelectric and ferromagnetic materials to devices. Make it possible to recognize the importance of materials through lectures.
advice: 1. Basics of electronic materials : We learn the basic contents in learning electronic materials, especially the atomic orbital and electron configuration in solids, the bonding between atoms, band structures, and electrical conduction. 2. Dielectric materials and their properties : Learn about polarization, which is a general response phenomenon to the electric field of a solid. After learning the polarization under applying a DC electric field, the complex permittivity is derived under applying an AC electric field, and the dielectric loss. Furthermore, we learn about the properties of ferroelectrics that show strong polarization and their applications. 3. Magnetic materials and their properties : We understand from a microscopic point of view the magnetization phenomena that occur when a substance is placed in a magnetic field, and learn about the basic content of magnetism that determines the magnetic properties of the substance. Learn about the origin and classification of ferromagnetism, and their applications to the field of electrical and electronic engineering. In addition, we will learn about the basics and applications of spintronics that apply electron spin, which has attracted attention in recent years.
requiredKnowledge: The purpose of this lecture is to learn the characteristics and practical applications of the dielectric and magnetic materials that make up the various devices that form the basis of the electrical and electronic engineering field, based on the knowledge learned in the Electronic Engineering and Physical Electronics. You will learn about various materials through this class, but please systematically organize your knowledge.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain atomic orbital and electron configuration, the bonds between atoms, and band structure in sol
Be able to explain properties and applications of dielectrics.
Be able to explain properties and applications of magnetic materials.
Be able to explain properties and applications of superconducting materials.

title: 情報通信ネットワーク
subtitle: Network Technology of Information and Communication
keywords: IoT 2.Communication Protocol 3.Internet 4.Network design 5.Community cooperation
educationalGoal: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) including IoT and related technologies is an indispensable factor in the social infrastructure. Especially, in communication networks, understanding communication protocol and network configurations are important items. This course focuses on these items. Moreover, this course comes in touch with the latest trends and future directions in ICT.
advice: This course is a systems approach of fundamental technologies including "Communication and Network system" and "Transmission of Electronic Information". This course includes the following topics. (1) Overview of communication network focusing on the Internet (2) Communication protocols in each layer of the Internet reference model - Data link layer (Ethernet, Wireless LAN) - Network layer (IPv4, IPv6) - Transport layer (TCP, UDP) (3) Applications on the Internet - e-mail - Web access - File transfer, etc. (4) Basic technologies on performance analysis in networks (5) IoT services and technologies (6) The latest topics in ICT by a guest lecturer

title: 情報伝送工学
subtitle: Transmission of Electronic Information
keywords: Fourier series and Fourier transform 2.Amplitude modulation and Frequency modulation 3.Continuous time system 4.Analog modulation 5.Pulse code modulation and sampling theorem
educationalGoal: This course introduces the basis of information signal and its transmission. For signal analysis in frequency domain, Fourier series/transform are explained. Frequency spectra of radio waves in analog modulations are analyzed. In addition to above, this course introduces the coding method named PCM from analog to digital and sampling theorem that gives the basic restriction for sampling frequency. For each topic, basis and principle are explained with basic formulas.
advice: This course is constructed following chapters: i) Basic topology of telecommunication systems, ii) Signal analysis method, - Fourier series and Fourier transform iii) Continuous time system, - Filters’ behaviors and their analysis - Quadrature modulation iv) Analog modulation and demodulation, - Amplitude modulation and frequency modulation v) Pulse code modulation and sampling theorem. - Pulse amplitude modulation and pulse code modulation - Sampling theorem
requiredKnowledge: Acquisition of Electrical circuits. Enough skill of mathematics (basic functions, integral calculus, complex number) How to use a calculator.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand and calculate Fourie series for basic periodic functions.
Be able to understand and calculate Fourier transform and inverse Fourier transform.
Be able to understand basic properties of filters in time domain and frequency domain.
Be able to understand and explain amplitude modulation.
Be able to understand and explain frequency modulation.
Be able to understand and explain principles of pulse code modulation and the sampling theorem.

title: 音響工学
subtitle: Acoustic Engineering
keywords: Physical phenomenon of sound 2.Physical quantity of sound 3.Audio application 4.Room acoustics 5. Hearing
educationalGoal: In our daily life, all kinds of sounds are surrounded. The sounds are essential to our lives. In this course, mathematically expression of the physical characteristics of sound waves and analysis of phenomena are learned. Also applied techniques of sound and audio, behavior of sounds related to room acoustics and hearing in daily life, and so on are learned.
advice: 1 Physical phenomenon of sound Characteristics of sound wave, vibration of string, vibration of air column 2 Physical quantity of sound Sound velocity, sound intensity, sound pressure level, noise level, distance attenuation, absorption/reflection/refraction/transmission, diffraction 3 Audio application CD player, sound editing, sound processing 4 Room acoustics Basic concept, sound ray method, impulse response, reverberation time, room sound field, acoustic design 5 Hearing Hearing mechanism, sound perception, three elements of sound, pitch perception, direction perception This course are conducted by following the syllabus, but since progress is adjusted while confirming the degree of understanding from the results of students' attitudes in the class, question situations, quizzes, etc., the course schedule and learning contents may be changed. This course is more specialized in the field of acoustic in the "Introduction to Acoustics and Imaging", which has already been offered. It will also lead to the understanding of the "Acoustic and Imaging Systems" and "Optical Information Engineering" which will be offered in the next semester.
requiredKnowledge: This course is related to the contents of "Electric Circuits", "Electronic Circuits" and "Electromagnetics", and please review the basic items you have learned in those courses. title: エネルギーデバイス工学
subtitle: Energy Devices
keywords: Environment / energy 2.Energy conversion device 3.Electrochemical device 4.Photo/ thermoelectric, piezoelectric conversion 5.Power storage technology
educationalGoal: Harmonization with the environment is required to utilize modern electric energy. In this course, students learn the social background of environmental energy. Next, primary batteries, secondary batteries, fuel cells, solar cells, piezoelectric / thermoelectric conversion elements, etc. are taught as important energy conversion devices constituting an electric energy system. The development trend, the situation of practical use, the structure, the operation principle, and the characteristics are learned.
advice: The following topics will be addressed in this lecture. 1. Environmental energy problems and energy conversion applied devices Current status of environmental energy problems / Overview of various energy conversion application devices 2. Fundamentals of electrochemical energy conversion Electrolysis and battery / principle of voltage generation / principle of current generation 3. Operation principle of electrochemical device Primary battery / Secondary battery / Fuel cell / Electric double layer capacitor 4. Fundamentals of photoelectric conversion, thermoelectric conversion, and piezoelectric conversion Principle of photovoltaic generation / Principle of thermoelectric generation / Principle of piezoelectric effect 5. Operating principle of photoelectric conversion, thermoelectric conversion, and piezoelectric conversion device Solar cell / Thermoelectric device / Piezoelectric device 6. Other power storage technologies
requiredKnowledge: This subject covers a wide range of energy conversion & storage technologies resulting from environmental energy problems. Therefore, in addition to knowledge in the fields of chemistry and physics, it is an integrated subject that requires a social perspective on the environment. Work to deepen understanding while referring to textbooks in each field as appropriate.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain global environmental energy issues and the role of various energy conversion devices.
Be able to explain an overview of electrochemical energy conversion, which is the basis of batteries
Be able to explain the characteristics of various devices to which electrochemical energy conversion is applied.
Be able to explain the principle of photoelectric, thermoelectric, and piezoelectric conversion and its applicat
Be able to explain the type, operation principle and development status about the power storage technologies.

Other power storage technologies

keywords: Audio and video signals 2.Digital signal processing 3.Machine learning and pattern recognition 4.Virtual reality and augmented reality 5.System integration
educationalGoal: Sound and image are indispensable as information communication media. In this course, especially participants study the information processing technology of audio and video systems which connect human and machine. They learn how to analyze audio and video in a computer and understand the data processing techniques required for machine recognition of audio and video. The goal is to use specific hardware and software to gain an experiential understanding of audio and visual technology.
advice: 1. Capturing and formatting audio and video signals 2. Digital transmission and recording of audio and video signals 3. Digital audio and video analysis 4. Digital audio and video processing 5. Digital audio and video reproduction This course are conducted according to the syllabus. However, check the level of understanding based on the questions in the class and the results of the quizzes and exercises, then adjust the progress accordingly. Mathematical knowledge such as frequency conversion and matrix calculation is required to understand the technology in the lecture. If you have any questions about this type of knowledge, you should consult several reference books and ask to lecturer. In addition, several educational centers: Mathematical and Science Education Research Center and Center for Information Services and Processing can be used for the consultation. Be sure to bring your laptop PC with headphones and network cable during the lecture to practice how to handle sound and video. In addition, prepare the internet connection for acquiring lecture materials and retrieving information.
books: Textbooks: Multimedia System Technology (in Japanese) [Corona publishing] Reference books: Introduction to Sound and Audio (in Japanese) [Corona publishing], Basic Studies of Video Systems -Fundamental Technologies for Digitization and their Applications- (in Japanese) [Corona publishing] Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: This course is based on the contents of "Introduction to Acoustics and Imaging" and "Acoustic Engineering", and requires knowledge of "Programming Practice for Electrical Engineers". title: 電気設計
subtitle: Designing Skills in Electrical Engineering
keywords: Electrical design 2.CAD drafting 3.Standard 4.Specification 5.Electrical equipment
educationalGoal: Many electrical equipment that support the functions of modern society are manufactured through electrical design. The definition of design is that producing the electrical equipment most economically and within the deadline, while determining the specifications to be realized and satisfying the given technical requirements, its size, shape. In this course, you will learn about both the concept of the design method and drawing by CAD through lectures and exercises.
advice: In this course, you will learn the following items in order. 1. Fundamentals of design 2. Structure, principle and basic theory of synchronous machine 3. The nature and content of electrical equipment 4. Basic principles of electrical design 5. Design method of three-phase synchronous generator 6. Design exercise of three-phase synchronous generator 7. CAD drafting basics 8. CAD drafting exercises
requiredKnowledge: "Electrical equipment I, II" should be completed, because the example of design exercise is three-phase synchronous generator. "Electrical drafting" should be completed, because the item of CAD drafting exercised is included.

activityGoals.body: You can explain the objective of design technology.
You can explain the purpose and types of standards for design.
You can explain design flow and understand the basic principles of electrical equipment.
You can understand the design method of synchronous machine and can design following the design method.
You can design simple drawing using CAD drafting.

educationalGoal: This course introduces the laws and regulations required for obtaining qualifications to students taking this course. advice: The outline of this course is shown in below. 1. Introduction: Trends of telecommunication policy, Amendment of Telecommunications Business Act, Summary of telecommunications system etc. 2. keywords: Semiconductor material 2.Thin films 3.Optoelectrodevices 4.Photoelectrochemistry
educationalGoal: Theme : Research on your project theme. Through research activities, learn about the significance of research, the research process, the formulation of research plans, research methods, and presentations. Goal : Obtain new knowledge or create unique results based on conventional research. (Related Program Objectives : (G, K, L, M, N))
advice: In order to cultivate the ability to find problems and issues, and to solve problems, you will actually learn the phenomena through experiments while reviewing basic subjects and acquiring specialized knowledge. Not only the superficial understanding of the phenomenon, but also the sense of understanding the essence of the phenomenon. The research process emphasizes mutual communication and discussion. Make sure you fully understand the nature and handling of chemicals and gases used before the experiment. The progress of the research will be reported in the contents of the weekly report and a seminar that is regularly conducted. The seminar will also introduce related research fields and give lectures. The annual schedule is as follows. Previous semester : To clarify the purpose of the research, make a research plan, conduct a literature survey, etc., and acquire basic knowledge to understand the project. In parallel with this, we will clarify the problems to be studied, show specific solutions, and implement them. The effectiveness of the solution is shown by experimental results and theoretical considerations. At the end of the term, the results will be announced at the interim report meeting, and the research results will be reported in a report. Second semester : Further research and solving remaining problems, summarize the research results in a project report, and present it at the public presentation review meeting. At the end of the period, the project will be handed over to the students of the next year.
requiredKnowledge: Project Design III is a creative activity that attempts a unique approach within a limited amount of time to a goal. For this reason, it is required to study basic knowledge energetically, identify problems and formulate and implement solutions to the problems themselves. It is necessary to have the ability to review the progress so far and to find a better direction through discussions with supervisors, graduate students and classmates. It is necessary to acquire the habit of always recording the contents of activities and learning and making them available later.

Be able to communicate with project members and faculty members to promote the project.
Be able to solve problems and issues in project execution.

Be able to explain the contents of the project, and effectively present the results of activities.

subtitle: Design Project III (Hirama Junji)
keywords: Electrophysiology 2.Electric Circuit 3.Plants and insects 4.Measurement control 5.Magnetic measurement
educationalGoal: Topic: Research based on the specialized knowledge and skills acquired during previous classes. Project themes contribute topics in the following fields; electrical/electronic engineering, agriculture, biology. The results obtained in this research have the potential to greatly contribute to society. Objective: To improve upon specialized technical knowledge and develop exceptional engineers.
advice: This course summarizes the project design process while integrating and reviewing all of the subjects previously studied, from the basics to the specialized and advanced.Students enrolled in one of the subjects listed below will be divided into groups and conduct research activities throughout the school year. A research notebook will be submitted daily, and meetings once a week will be conducted. (1)Development of equipment to physically control insect pests using light (a)This topic focuses on developing a pesticide-free and environmentally friendly insect pest control light source device by utilizing specially fluctuating ultra-bright light-emitting diodes (LED). (b) Measure the light stimulus response (electrophysiology) from the retinal potential of insects (moths and stink bugs). Furthermore, verify the phototaxis of the insects by behavioral observation. (2)Plant bioelectrophysiology (a) Investigate the bioelectrophysiological phenomena of plants by measuring the bioelectric potential response to ambient environmental stimulation conditions. (b) Optimized plant factory environmental control (3) Biomagnetic field measurement application: Using a prototype MRI device, measure various biological information in a non-invasive and none-destructive manner. (4) Development of ultra-low magnetic field measuring equipment: development of the Flux Gate Magnetometer
requiredKnowledge: PDIII combines the various knowledge obtained during the undergraduate period. It is a laboratory class that conducts research activities based on existing research themes. Therefore, the goal is to peruse self-development by working with teachers, senior students and fellow students. In particular, it is important to learn how to apply and use electronic circuits, magnetics, measurement and controls and biology.
