title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(宮田俊弘研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Miyata Toshihiro)
keywords: Display 2.Solar cell 3.Transparent conducting thin film 4.Phosphor 5.Thin film
educationalGoal: To learn the ability to discover the problems and issues necessary for technological development in the electronics field, and the ability to solve and achieve them. The basic knowledge, advanced expertise and engineering sense required for that are acquired through experimentation. Specifically, acquire the research and development ability of materials and devices in the field of optoelectronics, and cultivate the research and development ability of "systems" combining those materials and devices
advice: This subject is the final subject of the design project process, and is regarded as a subject that integrates the items learned in all subjects. Aim to acquire advanced expertise through experiments and studies. 1. Research activities --- Conduct in a research team consisting of (3 to 5 persons) per research theme. The contents of the main research activities of the year are shown in each semester as follows. Previous semester: Review of basic subjects and acquisition of semiconductor materials production and processing basic technology. Then work on developing new materials, devices and systems under specific research themes. Second semester: Following the previous semester, work on developing new materials, devices, and systems under a specific research theme. Then, the results of one year will be put together as research papers and presented to the public. 2. Training for Outcome Reporting --- Provides the following training throughout the year: Training of oral presentations using projectors in front of a large number of people by joint research report of 1.2-3 research groups, training of questions and answers sessions once a week from the previous semester to the middle of the second semester . 4. Conduct discussion training and write research notes daily through meetings on research content within the research group. 5. Work with graduate students to prepare one week's worth of results from the middle of the previous semester.
requiredKnowledge: In Design Project III, we will conduct research activities while manufacturing devices and evaluating their characteristics. Therefore, it is necessary to fully understand the contents of the specialized subjects. In particular, it is important to review and deepen your understanding of what you have learned in electronic physics, semiconductor engineering, electronic device engineering, and electronic application

subtitle: Design Project III (Yamaguchi Atsushi)
keywords: Research 2.Semiconductor Lasers 3.LEDs 4.Optical properties 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: Training will be carried out to grow up engineers in the electrical & electronic fields with problem-finding ability, solution ability, and application ability through educational programs that emphasize basic knowledge and skills in the fields of electrical engineering and electronic engineering, which are highly important in modern society

(1) Evaluation of physical properties of InGaN quantum wells (2) Physical property evaluation of GaN substrate (3) Evaluation of physical properties of oxide semiconductors (ZnO, etc.) (4) Physical property evaluation of InGaAs / InP semiconductors (5) Study of laser beam quality of laser scanners
requiredKnowledge: Review what you have learned in mathematics, semiconductor engineering, and electronic properties. English is also required to read academic papers. Metal processing skills (Yumekobo license) and computer programming skills are also desired.

To analyze and evaluate the research results correctly based on the social needs.
To discuss actively in group and make a presentation on research results effectively
To summarize the research results as project reports..

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(伊東健治研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Ito Kenji)
keywords: Wireless power transfer 2.Rectenna 3.Rectifier 4.Mixer Circuit
educationalGoal: This course is the final destination of design project course. Regarding to the project theme, theoretical, experimental investigations are done for integration of knowledge. Project theme: Microwave semiconductor circuits Activities: Through research activities for each student, a PDCA cycle for research is introduced.
advice: Following PDCA cycle is arranged: i) Assignment of the project theme: Detailed technical theme is established from technical area of microwave semiconductor circuits. ii) Understanding of the background of the assigned project theme: Through investigations for past works, technical issues that will be solved through the activity is clarified. iii) Planning research activities: The planned schedule is reviewed in weekly meetings. Final destination that is “differentiation compared with past works” is defined through discussions. iv) Learnings of EDA tools: Microwave circuit simulator (Keysite ADS), Analog IC design simulator (Cadence Virtuoso), EM simulator (Keysite EM-pro) are trained. v) First design activity: Design procedures is established at first. By using theoretical and simulational approaches, first circuit is designed. vi) First validation activity: With use of PCB etching, the validated circuit is fabricated. vii) Analysis of the first trial: From difference between the design and the validation results, improvement actions are planned. Above activities are reviewed in weekly meetings. Deliverables of the project are implemented as “the project report”. And they are presented in the review conference in Feb.
requiredKnowledge: i) Acquisition of electrical circuits, electronic circuits and EM theory. Enough skill of mathematics (basic functions, integral calculus, complex number) ii) Basic presentation skills and technical writing skill.

Be able to describe the research deliverable as the project report, and to present it in the review conference.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(宮城克徳研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Miyagi Katsunori)
keywords: Environment & Power 2.Power system insulation 3.Power apparatus 4.Impulse discharge 5.Insulating liquid
educationalGoal: Based on electric power distribution facility, this course study mainly from a viewpoint of the integrated evaluation between Materials, Apparatuses and Systems; (a) Sustainable development to the next generation (b) Eco-friendly apparatus supporting a low carbon society (c) High efficiency power energy system
advice: This course is positioned as a subject which integrates the contents studied with all the subjects while it has assumed the last subject with a series of Design Project programs started by the Design Project / Introduction. The purpose of this project is learning advanced technical knowledge while reviewing the basic subjects through experiment and theoretical examinations of these project themes. Research fields and General subjects 1. High-voltage substation facility field - General subject: The investigation of behavior-analysis and life-time in the internal insulation phenomena in the equipment using various biodegradable insulation oils, and the verification for practical applications 2. Power system field - General subject: Influence of the electrical degradation and investigation of the degradation mechanism caused by natural environment in power transmission and distribution systems
requiredKnowledge: This course refers to the references (mainly scientific paper) relevant to research activities. Especially, fundamental English grammar and technical vocabularies are reviewed because English papers increase in number. In the experiment, always accompanied by danger to deal with high-voltage equipment and many medicine. Be sure to follow the professor's directions.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(藤田洋司研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Fujita Yoji)
keywords: Energy storage technology literacy 2.Energy storage device 3.Transient response and energy conversion 4.Reliability and safety evaluation 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: [Subject] Set a theme for using batteries (storage technology literacy). Through this research, understand the social and technical background of power storage technology as an electrical engineer. Learn techniques and presentation techniques. [Goal] To achieve unique results for the project theme to be implemented, based on conventional research. Summarize the results as a graduation thesis.
advice: [Outline of class] Conduct research activities alone or in groups.Have a weekly meeting.Submit weekly reports based on daily communication.The annual schedule is as follows. First semester: Create a research schedule for the first semester according to the project proposal. Learn the basics of research and investigate related literature.Submit weekly reports and learn the process of accelerating and modifying your plan.The results of the semester will be presented in June and August. Second semester: Create weekly reports and activate discussions.We hold briefings in October and December to improve presentation skills.The results will be compiled into a dissertation and presented at the public presentation judging committee. Summarize the handover materials for the next year's students. [Learning advice] Think and act on your own. Work on activities that give you a sense of achievement and solidarity when overcoming difficulties and questions. [Example of project theme] (1) Study on the effect of high voltage pulsed high electric field on batteries (2) Study on the effects of the equalization circuit and method for assembled batteries (3) Cell performance analysis and modeling of lead-acid batteries

requiredKnowledge: Energy storage technology is the engineering of the boundary area. Summarize the handover materials for the next year's students. [Learning advice] Think and act on your own. Work on activities that give you a sense of achievement and solidarity when overcoming difficulties and questions. keywords: Power Semiconductor 2.Power Electronics 3.Circuit Simulation 4.Device analysis and SOA estimation
educationalGoal: (1) Students will learn the power semiconductor and power electronics. (2) Students will learn circuit simulation techniques to analyze the power converter system. advice: Class overview and management Under the advice of the academic advisor, research activities will be conducted on the project theme. Project 1. title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(泉井良夫研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Izui Yoshio)
keywords: Energy management 2.Renewable energy 3.EV utilization 4.Energy share 5.Electric heat cooperation
educationalGoal: Cource objective is establishing the theme for supplying low-carbon safe and reliable power and energy in the local community. Through this objective, you will understand the social and technical background for power and energy technology as an electrical system expert and cultivate an engineering sense such as problem solving and communication ability. In this project being conducted, the results are summarized as a paper.
advice: [Aim and tasks of the projec] This course is the final course in the design project process, including the introduction to design project, and is regarded as a course that integrates the items learned in all design projects. Aim to review basic course and acquire advanecd expertise through experiments and theoretical studies. Project activities will be conducted alone or in groups. You will meet weekly and report the progress in your weekly activity report based on your daily communication. The annual schedule is as follows. (1) The firat half classes: Based on the project proposal, create an assumed project schedule for the research contents of the first half classes. Learn the basics of research and submit weekly activities to accelerate and revise plans quickly. (2) The second half classes: With fhe final report in mind, conduct research activities continuously, prepare weekly reports, and activate discussios. The results are put together in a paper and presented at the public presentation review board. In addtion, you will submit the hand-over materials for students of the next fisical year. [Examples of project theme] (1) Collection and analysis of measurement data of Hakusan-roku campus energy management demonstration system, (2) Modeling and simulation of micro grid system, (3) Autonomous control system with thermo-electrical coordination or DC d-loop control for micro grid system, (4)V2X system for EV utilization for energy management system.
requiredKnowledge: The energy management system is an integareted field of study that deals with all of creation, transmission, storage use of electricity and energy, and from hardware devices such as power generatio, storage, demand, control and mobility. Futhremore, in relation to global environment issues and regional cooperation, Professro in charge hope that you acquire knowledge in a wide range of fields, from elemental technology to system wide technology and even business models.

activityGoals.body: You can define the purpose of research and make a reserach plan
You are able to communicate well with research group members and Professor in order to promote research
You can solve your own problems or issues in research
You can summarize the research results in the final report (project report)
You can explain research contents and present your researech resutls effectively

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(大澤直樹研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Osawa Naoki)
keywords: Non-thermal plasmas 2.Dielectric breakdown 3.Plasma applications 4.Green technology 5.Local cooperation
educationalGoal: The aim of this course is to enhance the development of student's R&D skills on electrical and electronic engineering through the research project on plasma science and high voltage engineering. By the end of the course, students will be able to: 1. find an important problem, 2. create a plan for problem-solving, 3. promote a research project, 4. write a project report, and 5. make a presentation of a research work.
advice: [Projects] (1) fundamental research on non-thermal plasmas and dielectric breakdown phenomena Elucidation of mechanism on atmospheric pressure air diffuse dielectric barrier discharge generation, dielectric breakdown phenomena of solid/gas composite insulation, etc. (2) applications of non-thermal plasmas Ozone generation by non-thermal plasmas, air and water treatment, surface modification of interfacial bonding property of composite materials, plasma catalysis for green technology, bio-applications, etc. [Advice for learning] Close communication with team members or a professor promotes your research project effectively.
books: Textbooks: none Reference books: [1] A. Fridman, "Plasma Chemistry", Cambridge University Press (2008), [2] J. Meichsner, M. Schmidt, R. Schneider, H.-E. Wagner, "Nonthermal Plasma Chemistry and Physics", Chapman and Hall/CRC (2012) Reserved books: none
requiredKnowledge: Fundamental knowledge of electric circuits, electromagnetism, transient phenomena in electric circuits, high-voltage and pulsed-power engineering, and machine tools (drilling, lathe, milling, etc.) are necessary. "High voltage and high current are extremely dangerous. In order to avoid the risk of electric shock, students must follow safety regulations and instructions.

To be able to make the presentation at DP3 final conference.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(池永訓昭研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Ikenaga Noriaki)
keywords: Plasma generation / measurement 2.Ion / radical species 3.Functional thin film / regional collaboration 4.Physical sensor
educationalGoal: Utilize knowledge and skills acquired so far to acquire vacuum technology and thin film fabrication technology. Find new themes such as new functional thin film materials with a view to application from close relations with industry, and focus on developing the ability to plan and execute research to achieve the objectives. In particular, it deals with themes that make full use of plasma. The goal is to acquire comprehensive skills as an engineer.
advice: Students will persevere under the advice of their supervisors about the research themes they are working on, and obtain new knowledge while solving problems. Through research activities (project activities), acquire problem-finding / solving ability, self-development / self-management ability, communication ability, literature research ability, importance of safety inspection, and ethical judgment ability as an engineer. Aiming to actively present research results at academic societies, etc., so that questions and answers can be made accurately among experts. Specific lessons are as follows: 1.Project activities: Divide into 1 or 2 people for each research theme. In the previous semester, we will mainly study basic knowledge and literature on plasma and functional thin films. In the second semester, students will learn basic research skills and communication skills by working on each research theme and at the same time summarizing the research results and reporting on the progress of each research theme. 2.Presentation of research results: In the second semester, oral presentations will be made at various academic societies for each research theme. In addition, regarding themes related to joint research with companies, other universities, and public institutions, we participate in regular meetings and actively participate in discussions to conduct specialized Q & A training. . Eventually, a project design III report will be created and presented at a public presentation.
requiredKnowledge: In order to handle plasma, basic knowledge about the behavior of charged particles ("electromagnetism") must be understood. In addition, since improvements and repairs of the equipment are also required, prior knowledge of “electrical circuits”, “transient phenomena”, and “electrical materials” is also necessary, so it is important to review and deepen your understanding.

activityGoals.body: To be able to acquire basic vacuum technology and design more advanced vacuum equipment
To be able to explain scientific definition of plasma and basic calculations on behavior of charged particles
To be able to understand and apply various technologies using ions and plasma
To be able to acquire thin film fabrication technology using plasma and apply it to various fields
To be able to appropriately communicate your thoughts to third parties through discussions and presentations

title: 進路セミナーⅠ
subtitle: Career Planning Seminar I
keywords: work and life 2.target setting 3.personality discovery 4.self-development
educationalGoal: The main subjects are the following three: 1. Practice in self-analysis and career design 2. Search for self-future direction with making to improve in job consciousness by expert-lecture sessions and factory inspections, etc. 3. Initiate activity with planning in the subjects required for a long period on the written exams of qualification acquisition, general common sense, and SPI, etc.
advice: The class is carried out by a course unit. 1. Advice of career design and self-development 2. Grasp the basic ability level and overcome the weaknesses in electrical and electronic engineering (Integrated practice) 3. Aware of self-characteristics (advantages and disadvantages) and self-appeal 4. Lecture by expert working on -Attendance and whole discussions- 5. Research on companies 6. Research on business and industries related with electric occupations 7. Research on business and industries unrelated with electric occupations 8. For my career design -Integrated practice and whole discussions
requiredKnowledge: It is due to perform the career planning seminar I carried out at the current fiscal year towards job-hunting activities of next year, and to make the preparation and strategy to the severe job-hunting expected. All students need to take a lecture irrespective of a future direction, because it is necessary to make preparations of mental attitude and employment exam for job-hunting activities. Moreover, this study result serves as reference data of the employment placement in next year.

activityGoals.body: The relation between a life design and a career path can be considered deeply for your own self.
Thinking and action required in order to discover a suitable life path for yourself can be performed.
Your life plan and target can be drawn up yourself.
Knowledge, capability, and qualification required to achieve a life path are investigated.

lessons.content: - Guidance on this class - Advice of career design and self-development (lecture and discussion)
lessons.operation: - Distribution of Future employment note - Arrange and submit your idea
lessons.assignments: - For the availability of the qualifications in connection with your career design.

lessons.content: - Efforts towards to conquest of weak points while having grasped the level of basic ability in electrical and electronic engineering (Integrated study).
lessons.operation: - The past employment exam problems are solved, self-weak points are clarified, and efforts towards conquest by each one.
lessons.assignments: - Major subjects etc. are reviewed in order to conquer your weak points.

lessons.content: - Aware of self-characteristics (advantages and disadvantages) and a means of self-appeal
lessons.assignments: - Arrange to aware of self- characteristics, study the effective self-appeal method in advance.

lessons.content: - Lecture by an expert working on (attendance and whole discussions)
lessons.assignments: - Arrange the points to help for your career design.

lessons.operation: - Understand the importance of business information collection for your career design. - While reviewing this lessons so far and grasping self-advantage and weak points, the weak point compensation methods are examined.
lessons.assignments: - Meaning of business information collections is explained and practical demonstration and exercise are performed. - Reviewing this lessons so far and self-weak point compensation methods are submitted.

lessons.content: - Research on business and industries related with electric occupations (lecture and exercise)
lessons.operation: - List up the company groups which got interested in the lecture, and the reasons are summarized.
lessons.assignments: - List ten or more companies where you get interested related with electric occupations. - Narrow down several companies and examine the reasons in advance.

lessons.content: - Lecture and whole discussions to deepen the understanding on "get a job" - Self-Assessments
lessons.operation: - Based on the questions collected in advance, discussions are performed with questioners. - Then, the uneasy feeling and doubt over getting a job are clarified and the understanding is deepened.
lessons.assignments: - Summarizes "question and doubt points through the course" in advance.

title: 情報工学大意
subtitle: Introduction to Information and Computer Science
keywords: Engineering 2.Manufacturing 3.Regional cooperation 4.Information engineering 5.IT infrastructure/Solutions and Services
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn about the connection between engineering and society, as well as the connection between engineering and the local community. (2) learn about the history of those technologies and the technologies of the present and future, and clarify their consciousness in relation to becoming an “engineer who thinks and acts independently”.
advice: This is an introductory course to engineering (Information and Computer Science). We will cover the following materials: 1. Understanding of the College of Engineering: Students are expected to learn and understand the history of the related fields of the College of Engineering, the role and importance of the current and future fields, and the importance of standardization through lectures by teachers and engineers working in society. 2. Understanding of the Department of Information and Computer Science: Students are expected to understand the curriculum in the Department of Information and Computer Science (ICS), the expansion of "areas of study", and their relationship with society. 3. Exercises that foster the ability to think logically about the essence of phenomena and things (scientific skills): Students are expected to understand the role that information engineering has played in society, culture, and history through concrete examples. In order for them to take on such roles, the knowledge and basic skills acquired in the department are important. 4. Introduction of research fields: Students are expected to understand the contents of the "areas of study" in the department of ICS and research efforts in that area. 5. Comprehensive exercises: Students engage in exercises and group activities based on their portfolios and the tasks given in classes to date, and then submit the result as reports to confirm them.
requiredKnowledge: It is important for students to pay close attention to the technologies they are interested in, and then to tackle those subjects proactively and voluntarily so that they can understand the “areas of study” of the department including the past, present, and future prospects of their research fields. They must also formulate learning objectives and learning plans for future specialized subjects, and determine the direction of their success in their future of society.

title: プログラミングⅠ
subtitle: Programming I
keywords: expressions and operations 2.variables and data types 3.collections 4.control flow 5.functions
educationalGoal: The goal of this course is to be able to write and execute basic computer programs in Python. By completing this course, students are expected to obtain skills to setup an appropriate development environment on their PC, write basic Python programs, and execute them.
advice: In Programming I (this course) and the first half of the subsequent course, Programming II, students will learn how to write programs in Python to accomplish certain tasks. This introductory course covers the following topics. (1) How to install software necessary for developing programs in Python and running them. (2) How to edit and save programs written in Python and execute them. (3) How to combine basic building blocks of Python to accomplish certain tasks. For (3), students will have a lot of opportunities to engage in hands-on exercises where they can acquire working knowledge of computer programming.
requiredKnowledge: There is no prerequisite course for Programming I. Students have to bring a PC, an AC adapter, and a network cable to the class because there will be exercises where students are asked to write programs and upload them during class hours for later grading.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain what operations it takes to run a program.
Be able to assign values to various variables and use the print function to display their contents.
Be able to write expressions combining properly named variables and operators and evaluate them.
Be able to define lists and dictionaries and write programs that use them.
Be able to use control flow structures such as conditional statements and loops in writing programs.
Be able to define functions for relatively simple tasks.

advice: In this course, we learn the following topics: 1. Sets and their operations 2. Propositional logic 3. Predicate and quantifier 4. Mathematical induction 5. Relation 6. Equivalence class 7. Be able to classify elements according to the equivalence class.
Be able to perform modulo arithmetic.
Be able to explain isomorphism of groups.
Be able to perform arithmetic operations of polynomials over a field.

educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn basic logic circuits consisting of commonly used circuit components. (2) learn the actions of logical gates and flip-flop. (3) learn the basic design approach of logic circuits.
advice: This is the basic course of computer architecture. We will cover the following materials: 1. Characteristics of logical gates. 2. Truth table for given a logic circuit. 3. Simplification of a logic circuit using a Karnaugh map. 4. Circuit architecture and design methodology of encoders, decoders, data selectors, multiplexers, coincidence circuits, binary adders, flip-flops, shift registers, and counters. 5. Application of local cooperation on logic circuits. Students are required to calculate binary numbers. Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms and characteristics. Students are expected to understand actions of logical circuits using a logic circuit simulator. Students are expected to review each course content.

title: データ構造とアルゴリズム
subtitle: Data Structure and Algorithms
keywords: Data structure 2.Algorithms
educationalGoal: In order to develop good programs, knowledge about data structures and algorithms is necessary. The objectives of this course are the following: 1. Learning fundamental knowledge about data structures and algorithms. 2. Developing data structure and algorithm selection skills suitable for the problems.
advice: A data structure is a form in which data is stored in a computer, and an algorithm is a "procedure used to solve a problem" that abstracts a program. In order to write a good program, a good data structure and a good algorithm are necessary. Since multiple data structures and algorithms can be used to solve a problem, students of this course will learn about time complexity, which is a typical index for comparing them. They will also compare multiple algorithms with varying time complexities in these lessons. The order of the learning contents shown in the lesson schedule is a guideline. Students should follow the instructions of the teacher in charge for additional details. At a minimum, the following contents will be addressed: sort algorithms (basic and advanced techniques, including merge sort and quick sort), basic data structures (array, list, stack, queue, tree, and graph), and search algorithms on graph. Other contents may be added.
books: 「アルゴリズムとデータ構造」(第2版)森北出版株式会社
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge about inequality, polynomial functions, exponential functions, logarithm functions, numerical sequences, and recurrence relation.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand several data structures.
Be able to understand several algorithms.
Be able to judge algorithms from the viewpoint of computational complexity.
Be able to select the best algorithm and best data structure for a given problem.

title: 情報ネットワーク
subtitle: Information Networks
keywords: Computer networks 2.Protocols 3.OSI reference model 4.TCP/IP 5.Internet
educationalGoal: This course introduces the knowledge and theory of TCP/IP protocols supporting the current Internet, and imparts various related communication technologies to students taking this course. Through this, students will gain an understanding of computer networks such as LAN and WAN to acquire basic skills related to network operations.
advice: Students will systematically learn the basic knowledge and theories related to computer networks as shown below. 1. Basic mechanisms of computer networks 2. OSI reference model and TCP/IP 3. Physical layer and datalink layer 4. Network layer and transport layer 5. Routing protocol and application layer
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge and skills (binary number calculation, programming, etc.) related to first-year computer learning are required.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the basic mechanisms of computer networks.
Be able to explain the functions of each layer in the OSI reference model and TCP/IP protocols.
Be able to explain the basic mechanisms of the Internet.
Be able to perform network diagnostics using basic network commands and tools.

Routing protocol and application layer Additionally, students should be able to use appropriate network commands and tools for network maintenance and management.

lessons.assignments: Review of lecture content (history of information network, etc.) and preparation for Chapter 1 (basic network knowledge) of the textbook.

lessons.content: Overview for information & communication network (Part 2): Outline network technologies and usage patterns in recent years and learn about their relationship with this course.
lessons.assignments: Review of lecture contents (current network usage) and preparation for Chapter 2 (basic knowledge of TCP/IP) of the textbook.

lessons.content: Fundamentals of TCP/IP: Learn the basic principles of TCP/IP networks, the mechanisms and roles of layering and encapsulation using the OSI reference model, coexistence of different models within a network, and multiprotocol networks.
lessons.assignments: Review of lecture contents (OSI reference model and TCP/ IP), and preparation for Chapter 3 (Datalink) of the textbook.

lessons.content: Datalink (Part 1): Learn about datalink systems, MAC address, Ethernet, etc.
lessons.assignments: Review and preparation of lecture contents (various datalink systems).

lessons.content: Datalink (Part 2): Learn about wireless communication, PPP, public access network, etc.
lessons.assignments: Review of lecture contents (various datalink systems), and preparation for Chapter 4 (IP protocol) of the textbook.

lessons.content: IP protocol: Learn about IP, IP address (IPv4/IPv6), routing, IP segmentation and reconstruction.
lessons.assignments: Review not only the basic contents of IP and IP address calculation, but also the contents of the lectures learned in the first half.

lessons.content: Midterm Review: Exam or exercises will be conducted to deepen understanding of the content and exercises relating to the lectures that have been given thus far.
lessons.assignments: Preparation for Chapter 5 (Technologies related to IP) of the textbook.

lessons.content: IP related technologies: Learn about DNS, ARP, ICMP, DHCP, NAT, etc.
lessons.assignments: Review of lecture contents (IP-related technologies) and preparation for Chapter 6 (TCP and UDP) of the textbook.

lessons.content: TCP and UDP (Part 1): Learn about TCP, UDP, port number, window control, retransmission control, flow control, and congestion control.
lessons.assignments: Review and preparation for Chapter 6 (TCP and UDP) of the textbook.

lessons.content: TCP and UDP (Part 2): Learn about TCP, UDP, port number, window control, retransmission control, flow control, and congestion control. Additionally, exercises using these protocols will be conducted.
lessons.assignments: Review of Chapter 6 (TCP and UDP) and preparation for Chapter 7 (Routing Protocol) of the textbook.

lessons.content: Routing Protocol: Learn about static routing, dynamic routing, and routing algorithms such as RIP and OSPF.
lessons.assignments: Review of lecture contents (Routing Protocol) and preparation for Chapter 8 (Application Protocol) of the textbook.

lessons.content: Application Protocol: Learn about the server-client communication mechanism using the TCP/IP protocol and actually use various protocols.
lessons.assignments: Review of lecture contents (various protocols in Application layer) and preparation for Chapter 9 (security) and appendix (Physical layer) of the textbook.

lessons.content: Security and Appendix (Physical layer): Learn about the importance of network security in the Internet, its realization technologies and physical layer.
lessons.assignments: Review of lecture content and review for final exam.

educationalGoal: In this course, students will achieve the following three objectives: 1) Learn the basic concepts of software design, especially the concept of object-oriented development. 2) Acquire knowledge on a typical software design description language (UML). 3) Learn software design technology through experience from the design to implementation process.
advice: To develop the software required for an information processing system, it is necessary to analyze the requirements for the system, analyze the system, design the system, conduct system building, software design, software implementation, and system verification, and then perform operational testing. To understand the importance of software design, it is important to experience it during the system development process. In this course, students will experience object-oriented development using UML and the Java language. The following main topics will be covered: 1) Object-oriented overview 2) Object-oriented development procedure 3) Analysis, design, and modeling using ULM 4) Program creation using Java Note: Bring your own laptop computer.

To understand the importance of software design, it is important to experience it during the system development process. In this course, students will experience object-oriented development using UML and the Java language. title: ソフトウェア工学Ⅱ
subtitle: Software Engineering II
keywords: Productivity 2.Reliability 3.Confirmation for Information 4.Methodology of Software Development 5.Project
educationalGoal: Software engineering is a technical system for solving various problems in software development and maintenance. It is said that there are four aspects of software development: three Ps and one M, namely, product, process, project, and management. This course gives students the necessary understanding of various problems in these aspects of software development and shows how to solve them.
advice: The course consists of lecture participation and question-answer report submission (shown as "Quizzes" in the "Evaluation Criteria" column). In addition to the question-answer report, a software-development-company report (shown as “Other” in the "Evaluation Criteria" column) is to be submitted weekly. Each lecture must be attended with awareness of the presented problem. In order to ensure it is presented and understood well, a theme will be given in the second half of the lecture, and students will write and submit a composition (question-answer report) corresponding to the theme by the assigned deadline. Students are required to indicate their level of problem awareness in the composition (approximately 500 characters). A revised version of the software-development-company report will be submitted each week. Although the report title will remain the same, its contents are to be updated weekly. Students will attempt to make gradual improvements to its content and quantity. The primary issue of the report is to explain what kind of technology each company uses in order to become the president of a “virtual” software development company. Students will be required to incorporate the contents learned in class into the contents of their report.
requiredKnowledge: Students should bring a laptop PC to class. The software-development company reports can be created as either a Word or a PDF file and then uploaded to the University portfolio system. Students should compose a Word file during class [question-answer report]. Students should submit their weekly reports by the predetermined deadlines [Software-Developer-Company Report].

activityGoals.body: Be able to make a proposal contributing to reliability guarantees in software development.
Be able to make a proposal contributing to productivity improvements in software development.
Be able to confirm information correctly and show an understanding of the importance of technology.
Be able to understand and apply technology related to the internal structure of software products.
Be able to understand and apply technologies related to software development processes.
Be able to understand and apply technologies related to software development projects.

lessons.content: Think about how software development management should be. Think about what software development organizations and development projects should be. Consider what types of software engineers have and what kind of approach they want.
lessons.assignments: Think about how to manage software in the middle of development, quality control, and project management.

lessons.content: Understand an operating system (OS) and Application Program Interface (API). Understand compiler and linker technologies. Understand control structure and function technology.
lessons.assignments: Understand the basic operating principles of computers. Consider a computer as a “program execution device”. Imagine that both OS and API are programs.

lessons.content: Learn various data structure technologies. Understand the existence of various algorithms. Understand module structure and encapsulation technology.
lessons.assignments: Think about why the technology to regulate the storage area, such as variables, arrays, tree structures, and recursive structures, was created.

lessons.content: Understand the technology of layer structure. Understand the relationship between instances and classes in object orientation. Understand the relationship between object-oriented classes and inheritance.
lessons.assignments: The layer structure is a structure in which modules are divided into hierarchies and given a hierarchical relationship. A structure that can be called from top to bottom, but not vice versa. Think about the benefits.

lessons.content: Consider multiple inheritance techniques and issues. Understand object abstraction, condition abstraction, and behavior abstraction. Consider information hiding and localization techniques.
lessons.assignments: Think about what happens when you have multiple superclasses.

lessons.content: Consider exception handling technology. Understand parallel processing and transaction technology. Think about data independence and database technology.
lessons.assignments: Rules with many exceptions are complex and annoying to both the programmer and the user. Exceptions should be eliminated as much as possible, but exceptions still occur. What should we think about?

lessons.content: Consider design patterns and reusability. Understand a graphical user interface (GUI) and framework technology. Consider the memory leak problem and the storage area technology.
lessons.assignments: A module is a part as a program entity, but a design pattern is a conceptual part. Imagine that there is a pattern in the design.

lessons.content: Follow the history of programming language technology development and think about language and parts collection. Understand how to make secure (safe) programs with antivirus and anti-hacker measures. Consider development technology for embedded software.
lessons.assignments: There are various languages such as C, C++, Java, and C#. Technology improvement and language development are linked. Understand what has changed over time.

lessons.content: The software development process technology is explained. Consider software design technology, implementation technology, review technology, test technology, verification technology, and documentation technology.
lessons.assignments: Consider human factors in software development, the characteristics of knowledge labor, and human resource development. Review of lecture content and review for final exam of achievement confirmation test.

lessons.content: General exercise
The software development project technology is explained. Think about knowledge labor and human resource development. An achievement confirmation test is given.
lessons.operation: Lectures and Final exam of achievement confirmation test
lessons.assignments: Consider human factors in software development, the characteristics of knowledge labor, and human resource development. Review of lecture content and review for final exam of achievement confirmation test.

lessons.content: General exercise
Students learn using external materials such as videos, and consider their future approach to software engineering. Students self-evaluate their achievements.
lessons.assignments: Looking back on what has been learned so far. It will lead to future learning and research.

Students will attempt to make gradual improvements to its content and quantity. subtitle: Digital Communications and Signal Processing
keywords: Discrete time signal and frequency characteristics 2.z-transform and transfer function 3.Sampling theorem 4.Discrete Fourier transform and FFT 5.Modulation/demodulation and multiple access
educationalGoal: Analog signals such as voice, music, images, and video are digitized and processed. Digital signal processing can be implemented as a computer program, which enables flexible and complex processing. In this course, students will learn the basics of digital signal processing by digitizing analog signals such as audio and video. They will also learn the basics of digital communications achieved by digital signal processing.
advice: Students will systematically learn the following basic knowledge and theory about digital signal processing and digital communication: 1. Discrete time signals and systems. 2. Frequency characteristics of discrete-time systems. 3. z-transform and transfer function. 4. Sampling theorem. 5. Discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and fast Fourier transform (FFT). 6. Digital filter design method. 7. Baseband transmission, modulation/demodulation and multiple access.
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of the basics of mathematics such as exponential functions, trigonometric functions, complex numbers, and linear algebra is required. It is desirable that students have knowledge of probability statistics, Fourier transform, and Laplace transform. These are introduced in this course. Numerical calculation software such as Excel are used in the practices.

title: 計算論
subtitle: Theory of Computation
keywords: Turing machine 2.Computability 3.Complexity 4.NP-completeness
educationalGoal: Computers can be used to solve various kinds of problems. Here a question arises; “Can computers solve any problem?” The theory of computability can provide an answer to that question. Some problems take extremely long time to be solved and they are called `intractable problems'. The theory of complexity deals with intractable problems.
advice: In this course, we introduce the Turing machine, a formal model of computation. Students will learn computable and incomputable problems by means of the Turing machine. Some classes on computable problems will be provided and students will learn the relationship between these classes. The primary topics are as follows: 1. Turing machine as algorithm 2. Incomputable problems 3. Complexity class 4. Intractable problems On the whole, the topics are abstract. Therefore, solving problems independently is important for gaining a sufficient level of understanding.
books: オートマトン 言語理論 計算論II[第2版],J.ホップクロフト,R.モトワニ,J.ウルマン著,サイエンス社
requiredKnowledge: It is desirable for students to have taken "Formal language and automata". Prior knowledge of formal language is especially helpful although it is also taught in the course.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the movements of a Turing machine.
Be able to explain the definition of recursively enumerable language.
Be able to explain at least one example belonging to class P.
Be able to explain the difference between class P and class NP.
Be able to explain NP completeness.

title: コンピュータグラフィックス
subtitle: Computer Graphics
keywords: 3D coordinate system 2.3D modeling 3.Rendering 4.Shading 5.Texture mapping
educationalGoal: Computer graphics (CG) is used in various fields such as numerical simulations, the visualization of engineering or scientific phenomena, and contents production for education or entertainment use. In addition, output devices such as GPUs and 3D printers have been developed rapidly in recent years. In this course, students will systematically learn the technologies used in CG today. They will also acquire the skills needed to create CG content through programming using a CG library.
advice: In this course, lectures on basic theories about 3D representation and modeling methods are provided, and programming exercises for implementing the theories learned are conducted. Specifically, students will learn and implement knowledge related to coordinate transformation, 3D modeling, hidden surface removal, shading, rendering, texture mapping, and animation in 3D space. Specific topics include the following: 1. Overview of 3D CG technology 2. 3D coordinate system 3. Coordinate and projective transformation in 3D space 4. 3D CG modeling 5. 3D CG animation 6. Overview of 3D CG rendering 7. Hidden surface removal and shading 8. Texture mapping 9. Radiosity and shadowing 10. Summary and reflection
books: Required Materials will be provided in the class.
requiredKnowledge: 1. Students must have basic mathematical skills such as trigonometric functions, matrices, and vector calculations. 2. Student must be able to program an application using C language. Student should spend one hour preparing for the next class or exercise and spend more one hour for reflection.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain and use coordinate systems in 3D space.
Be able to explain coordinate and projection transformation of 3D CG and use them properly.
Be able to explain the basic methods of 3D modeling and implement them by programming.
Be able to explain hidden surface removal and shading techniques and select effective techniques.
Be able to explain 3D CG animation techniques and program basic animations.

achievementLevels.ideal: Students with ideal achievement will have acquired expert-level knowledge based on the “CG-ARTS CERTIFICATION TEST for CG Engineer”. Specifically, they can explain coordinate systems in 3D space and coordinate transformation. They can also explain basic and advanced 3D modeling. Moreover, they can explain methods of rendering, hidden surface removal, shading, and texture mapping sufficiently, and develop original CG animations using a computer graphics library.
achievementLevels.standard: Students with standard achievement have basic-level knowledge of the “CG-ARTS CERTIFICATION TEST for CG Engineer”. Specifically, they can understand coordinate systems in 3D space and coordinate transformation. They can also explain basic 3D modeling. Moreover, they can explain basic methods of rendering, hidden surface removal, and shading, and develop primitive CG animation using sample programs of computer graphics library.

lessons.content: Learn the overview of 3D computer graphics. In addition, students will install the computer graphics programming environment on their personal notebook PCs.
lessons.assignments: Prepare the programming environment and understand the overview of 3D computer graphics. Prepare 3D coordinate system and geometric transformation system.

lessons.content: Learn 3D coordinate systems such as World, local coordinate systems, and 3D geometric transformations such as Modeling transformation, Viewing transformation, and Projection transformation.
lessons.assignments: Review and understand the 3D coordinate system and perform several transformations by executing the exercises. Prepare basic 3D modeling.

lessons.content: Learn several 3D modeling methods such as Wireframe model, Surface model, Free-form surface, and CSG representation, etc.
lessons.assignments: Review and understand 3D modeling by performing the exercises. Prepare more complex 3D modeling.

lessons.content: Learn complex 3D modeling such as fractal, particle, and voxel representations.
lessons.assignments: Review complex 3D modeling and prepare the non-objective modeling. In addition, continue work on CG animation programming.

lessons.content: Learn non-objective modeling such as lights, background, and sound sources.
lessons.assignments: Review non-objective modeling and prepare computer graphics animation. In addition, continue work on CG animation programming

lessons.content: Learn CG animation methods such as the key frame method, kinematics, motion blur, etc. In addition, learn the hardware such as the GPU and 3D printer.
lessons.assignments: Reflect all learning topics in the first half of this class. Complete the first CG animation programming.

lessons.content: Mid-term reflection: understand all the topics learned in the first half of this class deeply. Take the test to verify comprehension.
lessons.operation: Test or quizzes, exercise, and self-check
lessons.assignments: Prepare the overview of the topics (rendering, shading, texture mapping, etc.) in the last half of this class.

lessons.content: Learn the overview of rendering (photo realistic rendering, non-photo realistic rendering, volume rendering, etc.).
lessons.assignments: Review the basic rendering method through the exercise and prepare to study hidden surface removal.

lessons.content: Learn hidden surface removal methods such as the Z-buffer method and scan line method.
lessons.assignments: Review hidden surface removal method through the exercise and prepare to study shading methods.

lessons.content: Learn shading methods such as Gouraud shading and Phong shading.
lessons.assignments: Review shading methods through the calculating in actual cases and prepare to study texture mapping. In addition, continue work on CG animation programming.

lessons.content: Learn texture mapping methods such as wrap mapping and UV mapping.
lessons.assignments: Review texture mapping methods and prepare to study radiosity method and shadowing. In addition, continue work on CG animation programming.

lessons.content: Learn radiosity method and shadowing.
lessons.assignments: Review radiosity method and shadowing and proceed CG animation programming.

lessons.content: Final reflection: understand all the topics learned in the last half of this class deeply and complete CG animation programming.
lessons.assignments: Review the all learning topics in the last half of this class for the final exam.

lessons.content: Take a test to make sure all learning topics in the last half of this class.
lessons.assignments: Complete CG animation programming, if necessary.

lessons.content: Self-evaluation class: Confirm the level of understanding of computer graphics and discuss future research.
lessons.assignments: Review the topics learned in this class once again, and connect them for future studies and research.

title: 知識情報処理
subtitle: Intelligent Information Processing
keywords: Artificial Intelligence 2.Problem Solving 3.Inference 4.Machine Learning 5.Natural Language Processing
educationalGoal: Intelligent information processing requires knowledge to be represented and stored systematically. Students will: (1) Learn how to represent and use knowledge for problem solving and transform knowledge into a data structure for knowledge representation in computers. (2) Touch briefly on AI programming and deepen their understanding of problem solving, machine learning, natural language processing, etc.
advice: This course is a lecture/practice course that gives an overview of artificial intelligence, which has recently been in the spotlight again. First, students will learn an outline of intelligent information processing. Next, students learn about search algorithms used in computer shogi programs, localization techniques important for robot cars (automated driving vehicles), and machine learning for big data processing. Finally, students learn about natural language processing, image processing, etc. To deepen their understanding of each method, emphasis is placed on tackling the quizzes that are presented throughout the semester. We will cover the following materials: 1. Basics of intelligent information processing. 2. Problem solving (state space model, various search algorithms, and dynamic programming). 3. Probabilistic methods (Bayesian theory, reinforcement learning, and localization). 4. Machine learning (clustering and pattern recognition). 5. Natural language processing.
requiredKnowledge: “Problem solving” requires basic algorithms, “inference” requires probability theory at a high school level, and “machine learning” requires understanding of linear algebra. Additionally, the quizzes include tasks that students are encouraged to solve in their favorite programming language because they take a considerable amount of time if done manually.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand and explain the basic concepts of intelligent information processing.
Be able to understand and explain search algorithms and dynamic programming for problem solving.
Be able to understand and explain localization methods.
Be able to understand and explain how to apply machine learning to those problem and solve them.
Be able to understand and explain the basics of natural language processing and image processing.

advice: In this course, students learn practically how to develop compilers and interpreters through compact examples. subtitle: Information and Computer Science Major Lab/Exercises A
keywords: Microcontroller 2.Input/output control 3.Networking 4.Router, switch 5.Programming
educationalGoal: In this course, students will learn the basic mechanisms of microcontrollers and embedded programming. advice: This course covers the following topics: 1. Embedded programming with C/C ++ and assembly language. 2. Analysis of information transmission path by network capturing 5. Implementation of network capture program using C / C ++ NOTE: A review of Programming I, Programming II, Fundamental Computer Architecture, and Information Networks is required.
requiredKnowledge: Students of this course are expected to have the following: 1. C programming skills. 2. Understanding of the differences between IO mapped register and memory mapped register. 3. Knowledge and skill related to the construction of information networks. 4. Knowledge related to information transmissions using packet capturing tools. 5. Understanding of packet capture implementation techniques.

Be able to explain network hierarchical structures.
Be able to understand Internet traffic using packet capture.
Be able to set a personal IP address on a personal computer.

keywords: Lego Mindstorms 2.Developing embedded system 3.Android programming 4.GUI and APIs 5.Solution proposal

subtitle: Applied Information and Computer Science

educationalGoal: Learn about the application paths to many technology groups that support the information and communications industry, namely information network technology, web service & cloud technology, information security technology, human interface technology, and embedded technology.

educationalGoal: Probability and statistics are two of the basic knowledge of science and technology. keywords: Project Design 3 2.Information infrastructure technology 3.Solution & Service 4.Ethics and crisis management for IT engineers 5.Project Proposal
educationalGoal: Specialized seminars supplement the knowledge and skills that were not necessarily sufficient in past lectures, exercises, and experiments required for the PD3 project, and acquired new knowledge and skills in each activity area. advice: In order to carry out any research / work / assignment in PD3, the faculty presents the learning area program and clarifies the knowledge and skills required to carry out the project in this learning area program. The student confirms his / her ability, clarifies items to be supplemented and items to be newly acquired, and learns and acquires them. In the course of the lesson, teachers clarify PD3 goals and action plans. Students conduct tests on these learning results to confirm their achievement, and prepare a project proposal for PD3. Specifically, in performing PD3, learn the latest technology trends in specialized fields that are closely related to each project, and summarize the technology explanation and your opinion in the form of an essay. After understanding such a common technical foundation, learn the outline of the technology related to PD3 and plan the project. In addition, each project of PD3 Since the use of equipment and applied software differ for each project, the students will actually experience the operation in the laboratory so that they can grasp the goals and action plan of the project as a real feeling. We will announce the project proposal as the final result of this course.
requiredKnowledge: If you do not earn credits for this course, you will not be allowed to take PD3. Two or more unauthorized absences will be rejected. Be sure to read the booklet “Safety Guidelines for Experiments and Research” provided in the laboratory.

subtitle: Design Project III (Nagata Shigemi)
keywords: Concept Setting 2.Problem Solving Method 3.Development Design 4.Implementation 5.Operation
educationalGoal: In this course, based on the concrete knowledge of fundamental technologies, students acquire problem-solving skills related to computer & information engineering. Students are also given opportunities to experience R&D activities related to concrete information technology and systems. Through this process, students cultivate advanced abilities in the areas of problem-setting, production process development, information gathering, communications, problem-solving in regional orientation, and conducting objective evaluations.
advice: In this course, students are required to learn and practice R&D methods in the following areas of activity: 1. Computer & Network System Area: - Fundamental technologies such as signal processing, image processing, numerical processing, etc., based on mathematical structures, logical structures, and the physical structures of information and information systems. - Application systems using these technologies. 2. Information & Software System Area: - Fundamental technologies such as artificial intelligence, deep learning, knowledge processing, agent systems, WWW search, and so on. - Intelligent systems and multimedia search/mining systems using these technologies. 3. Cybermedia Information System Area: - Fundamental technologies such as machine learning, deep learning, pattern recognition and understanding, image processing, video processing, augmented reality, and so on. - Application systems using these technologies.
books: Textbooks: None Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Accumulation of results is extremely important. Students are expected to be sure to conduct self-checks at every milestone, such as progress reports for each semester and interim presentations.

activityGoals.body: Be able to set one-year achievement goals in relation to your chosen research.
Be able to set a specific production approach based on your set research concept.
Be able to use your acquired information engineering expertise to advance your design and analysis efforts.
Be able to cope with various problems that occur during the design and analysis process.
Be able to technically describe what you have accomplished in a convincing manner.

subtitle: Design Project III (Nakano Jun)
keywords: Conceive 2.Design 3.Implementation 4.Creativity
educationalGoal: In this capstone project, students will conduct research activities related to IT systems based on the knowledge and skills related to computer science and technology that they have learned so far. Through these activities, students acquire the abilities needed for identifying a problem, designing the project, and implementing an IT system. Additionally, students will acquire generic abilities related to communicating with others, and evaluating results.
advice: Students will choose either the data science track or the Web services track according to their interest and design and execute the project. - Data science track Students will learn theory and practice about machine learning, distributed and parallel processing, and visualization techniques for processing Big Data. Thereafter, they step onto acquiring necessary skills about natural language processing and image processing, for instance, according to the domain of the project. - Web service track Students will design and implement a Web service that would solve social problems, meet a small group of users' needs, or even lead to a commercial service. The project should involve quick implementation of a minimum viable product and several iterations of improvement cycles based on usability studies.
requiredKnowledge: Major achievements are the results of small and daily achievements. Students are recommended to conduct self-checking every quarter.

Be able to set an appropriate approach or method for the project.
Be able to acquire the IT knowledge and skills needed for proceeding with the project.
Be able to deal with the problems that will occur in the analysis and design process.
Be able to evaluate the result from subjective and objective viewpoints for better understanding.

In this course, students will be exposed to laboratory research covering a wide range of areas including chemistry, physics, and aeronautical engineering. Some of the actual contents of research conducted in this laboratory are as follows. 1. Fireworks design systems, as seen from the viewpoint of particle movement simulations. 2. KIT Guidance systems, as an application of computer graphics, database skill, etc. 3. Research into origami airplanes via data mining. 4. VR systems as real-world simulation systems. 5. High-performance computing.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(向井宏明研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Mukai Hiroaki)
keywords: Concept Setting 2.Problem Solving Method 3.Development Design 4.Implementation 5.Operation
educationalGoal: Based on the concrete knowledge of fundamental technologies, students acquire problem-solving skills related to computer & information engineering. Students are also given opportunities to experience R&D activities related to concrete information technology and systems. Through this process, students cultivate advanced abilities in the areas of problem setting, production process development, information gathering, communications, problem-solving in regional orientation, and making objective evaluations.
advice: Investigate and examine the relationships between the technologies and services of interest. Moreover, the following areas should be addressed. Students learn R&D methods through the development of programs or evaluation models. 1. Information infrastructure design, construction, evaluation and operation In this area, students focus on lifecycles, components, and the development process, tools and methods to solve issues, and so on. 2. Next-generation information infrastructure In this area, students explore content delivery by combining server, database, network, and program technologies, with the goals of creating reliable networks, collaborative work, and industry applications, etc. 3. Improving information system stability/disaster recovery Students will address topics such as redundancy, disaster recovery, non-functional design and so on. 4. Data structure analysis/conversion Students explore data structure analysis, processing, conversion with functions of programming languages such as Python3, Perl6, Elixir, Haskell, Kotlin, and Scala. 5. Application by cooperation among end users Systems that promote end user interaction, relationship extraction, SNS data aggregation, and so on, are examined.
requiredKnowledge: Research guidance policy In this laboratory, seminars by students and faculty members are conducted once a week. Students are expected to set themes, summarize survey analysis results, discover social problems, and conduct annual events such as the writing of academic papers and making conference presentations.

title: 進路セミナーⅠ
subtitle: Career Planning Seminar I
keywords: Career design 2.Self-analysis 3.Occupation and life 4.Self-development 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: The objectives of this course are to assist students in determining their future progress and facilitating their development as professional engineers. There are two main issues: 1. Performing the necessary self-analysis prior to the start of job hunting and grasping themselves well. 2. Making plans for issues that require relatively long periods of preparation and groundwork such as qualification acquisition and practice exams(SPI test).
advice: The outline of this course is as follows: 1. Guidance/Recommendations to career planning. 2. How to write your selling points and exercises. 3. Lecture II: Lecture by specialist from a local company. 7. Lecture III: Lecture by specialist from a local company. 8. Lecture IV: Lecture by specialist from a local company. 9. Lecture V: Lecture by specialist from a local company. 10. Self-inspection and review of correction results for your own paper "MY SALES POINTS". requiredKnowledge: Career Planning Seminar I is to be held this year as a course for job hunting activities, and is intended to encourage students to engage in groundwork and preparations for the current difficult employment front. All students are encouraged to take this course, regardless of their advancement or employment opportunities, as part of their job hunting preparations and in preparation for employment examinations. This learning acquired in this course will provide reference material for use when seeking employment next year.

achievementLevels.ideal: Students can explain the Surveying Act and operation specifications for public surveys. They can explain the geodetic coordinates 2000 accurately, particularly the difference between the world geodetic system and the Japanese geodetic system. Students can handle surveying errors by applying basic mathematical knowledge. They can use the least squares method and process observed values. They can explain the relationship between radians and degrees, and can use Excel to create worksheets. They can also explain the concepts of distance measurement and error, can handle errors, understand and explain the leveling method.
achievementLevels.standard: Students know about the Surveying Act and specifications for public surveys. They can outline the geodetic coordinates 2000. They can also use basic mathematical knowledge and can handle survey errors. Students can explain the relationship between radians and degrees, the concepts of and errors in distance surveys, leveling, and can outline 3S technology.

subtitle: Structural Mechanics I
keywords: Mechanics of rigid bodies 2.Modeling of loads and structures 3.Reaction of structures 4.Cross-sectional forces in beams

title: 測量実習・演習Ⅰ
subtitle: Surveying Practicum / Exercises I
keywords: Distance, Degree, Bearing 2.Error, Precision 3.Total Station 4.Distance survey, Control point survey 5.Declination survey, Leveling survey
educationalGoal: (1) Practice the surveying methods learned in Surveying I and Surveying II (2) Practice distance, control point, leveling and declination surveys and reports. (3) Reports are equivalent to company reports. Students will learn how to create data in required formats. (4) Students who master the topics in Surveying I/II and Surveying Practicum I/II will have the skills necessary for an Assistant Surveyor national license.
advice: Surveying Practicum / Exercises I will be carried out as active learning practice based on “Total Ability” learning in the CLIP learning process. (1) Distance Surveying Students learn the basics of distance surveying including measuring distances by pacing, using steel tape, fabric tape and TS, and will compare the accuracy of each. (2) Total Station (TS) equipment Students learn how to use TS equipment and its internal programs. (3) Angle Surveying Students learn the basics of angle surveying using TS equipment, including how to set control points and conduct declination surveys. (4)Leveling Surveys Students learn how to use auto levels and electrical levels, practice small-scale direct leveling and master profile leveling and rise-fall leveling recording methods. (5)Advice Materials in Moodle are useful for practice and for creating reports. The schedule is subject to change depending on the weather. Reference the e-syllabus for the latest information of class relating Covid-19.
requiredKnowledge: Surveying Practicum / Exercises I builds on the contents of Surveying I and II with practical skills. Students must fully understand lecture content from the Surveying I and II courses. High-level courses, Surveying II, Surveying Practicum / Exercises II, and Spatial Information Engineering are also offered, along with other surveying-related courses such as Environmental Civil Engineering Experiments B and Spatial Information Design Exercises.

subtitle: Surveying Practicum / Exercises II
keywords: Distance, Degree, Bearing 2.Error, Precision 3.Control Point Surveying 4.Digital Photogrammetry,GNSS Survey 5.Regional Cooperation
educationalGoal: (1) Students will practice the surveying methods learned in Surveying I and Surveying II(2) Students will practice control point surveying, digital photogrammetry and GNSS surveying (3) Students will prepare reports that are equivalent professional company reports and will learn how to create data and reports.(4) Students will undertake the Regional Cooperation project considered in Surveying I
advice: Surveying practice will be undertaken as active learning based on “Total Ability” learning in the CLIP learning process. (1) Traverse Surveying (TS may be part of the teaching material for Camellia Kids). Students will gain practical knowledge about traverse surveying as an application of control point surveying learned in Surveying II (2) GNSS surveying (GNSS may be part of the teaching material for Camellia Kids). Students will practice real-time positioning using a network-based RTK method and static positioning using VRS-GPS. (3) Digital Photogrammetry (Digital Photogrammetry may be part of the teaching material for Camellia Kids). Students will learn digital photogrammetry practices using “Image Master Beginners” developed by the JSPRS (Japan Society of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing) and Topcon Ltd. Real time class by Zoom only in the first week. Reference the e-syllabus for the latest information of class relating Covid-19.
requiredKnowledge: In Surveying Practicum II, students strengthen their understanding of the contents learned in Surveying I and II with practical skills. Students must fully understand the content from the classroom lectures in Surveying I and II. Spatial information engineering is offered as a related high-level class and other surveying-related courses include environmental Civil Engineering Experiments B and Spatial Information Design Exercises.

title: 空間情報工学
subtitle: Geoinformatics
keywords: Geoinformatics 2.Remote Sensing 3.GIS 4.3D Mapping 5.Regional Cooperation
educationalGoal: A variety of spatial information is necessary for environmental management of the earth and its regions. Students will acquire basic knowledge on geospatial information engineering, and technology for collecting, accumulating, and analyzing geospatial information.
advice: This class focuses on remote sensing, geographic information systems, and 3D mapping in spatial information engineering. In recent years, environmental problems such as global environmental problems have attracted attention, and it is desirable to grasp changes in the environment. Remote sensing technology is a technology suitable for analyzing satellite data and monitoring the environment over a wide area. A geographic information system is a means of storing, searching, and analyzing geographic information. 3D mapping is used for advanced navigation systems and augmented reality technologies. The lectures match the basic materials that are distributed. We provide a wealth of examples such as remote sensing images and explain them using PowerPoint presentations. In addition, in order to deepen our knowledge, we conduct exercises using computers. For exercises, students use software such as EISEI, Google Earth, Google Map, SKETCHUP, etc. Special lectures will be held by invited representatives from companies that are making use of these technologies.
requiredKnowledge: Students must be familiar with the concepts from Surveying 1 and Surveying 2. During the exercises, students need to bring a laptop computer that can connect to the Internet on campus. Materials and data used in the class will be distributed in the teaching material distribution system. Use of private language in class is strictly prohibited.

Remote sensing technology is a technology suitable for analyzing satellite data and monitoring the environment over a wide area. A geographic information system is a means of storing, searching, and analyzing geographic information. 3D mapping is used for advanced navigation systems and augmented reality technologies. The lectures match the basic materials that are distributed. We provide a wealth of examples such as remote sensing images and explain them using PowerPoint presentations. In addition, in order to deepen our knowledge, we conduct exercises using computers. For exercises, students use software such as EISEI, Google Earth, Google Map, SKETCHUP, etc. Special lectures will be held by invited representatives from companies that are making use of these technologies.

keywords: Seismic design 2.Static lateral force method 3.Dynamic analysis 4.Time history response analysis 5.Finite difference method
educationalGoal: To understand the mechanism of seismic damage in infrastructures. To understand basic theory of seismic design. To understand dynamic analysis by solving the equation of motion. To understand numerical programing of time history response analysis with finite difference method.
advice: In quake prone countries like Japan, specifications of substructures are decided from seismic design in most cases. Students will learn seismic damage and history of seismic design of reinforced concrete columns in this class. Static lateral force method was used in the past. On the other hand, dynamic analysis is now used for seismic design owing to the development of ICTs. Therefore, students will learn present style of seismic design through the programing of time history response analysis.

title: 環境工学Ⅱ
subtitle: Environmental Engineering II
keywords: Wave 2.Coastal current 3.Sand transport 4.Coastal structure 5.Coastal ecosystem
educationalGoal: The coastline of Japan is the fifth in the world, and the conservation of the coastline is an important issue. Waves are an important external force when considering coastal fluid dynamics, ecological environment, and disaster prevention. In this course, students will learn basic knowledge about the nature and deformation of waves.
advice: In this course, students will understand the basic equations describing waves and the characteristics of wave deformation, storm surge and tsunami. In the second half, students will learn about beach currents and sand drift, hydrodynamic forces acting on coastal structures, and coastal ecosystem problems. 1. Basic properties of waves 2. Wave deformation 3. Basic characteristics of wind waves 4. Long period wave 5. Coastal current 6. Sand transport 7. Hydrodynamic forces acting on coastal structures 8. Coastal ecosystem
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of physics and mathematics, and credits for hydraulics I and II are required.

educationalGoal: In this Web design course, students will learn the concepts behind website construction, including information structure and effective navigation, as part of efforts to impart the knowledge necessary for designing easy-to-read and easy-to-use Web pages. In addition, the characteristics of multimedia material, the use of HTML and CSS, as well as techniques for making Web pages using a laptop computer, will be covered.
