subtitle: Technical Seeing and Hearing
keywords: Sensitivity 2.Color and Sound 3.Perception 4.Identification 5.Refilnal cooperation
educationalGoal: In this course, students will: (1) Learn human visual and auditory processing within the context of physiology and psychology. (2) Train to be able to discriminate and identify the value, chroma, and hue of visual stimuli. (3) Train to be able to discriminate between slight differences in the frequency and intensity of auditory stimuli. Additionally, train to be able to identify the frequency and intensity of auditory stimuli quantitatively. (4) Discuss application of the skills obtained for regional cooperation.
advice: This is a basic skills course for “technical seeing and hearing”. We will cover the following materials: 1. Human perception processing for visual and auditory stimuli. 2. Training for discrimination or identification of the value, chroma, and hue of visual stimuli. 3. Training for discriminating between slight difference in frequency and intensity of auditory stimuli. 4. Training for identifying the frequency and intensity of auditory stimuli. The contents of this class are related to “Project for Technical Seeing and Hearing”.
requiredKnowledge: None

Be able to identify the value, chroma, and hue of visual stimuli using Munsell notation.
Be able to discriminate between slight differences in frequency and intensity of auditory stimuli.
Be able to identify the frequency and intensity of auditory stimuli.

title: プログラミング基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Programming
keywords: Syntax of C language 2.Control Statement 3.Numerical calculation 4.Function 5.Debug
educationalGoal: Computer systems are constructions of hardware and software technology. This course focuses on the software side of the combination. Programming is the skill used to create software, and knowledge regarding it also helps users employ software effectively. Since the C language is widely used currently, this course teaches students about software design concepts through the practice of C programming.
advice: In this course, students will learn the software design concepts by programming, debugging, compiling, and running sample programs. The evaluation results of exams and reports will be reported to students, who will then be encouraged and required to use those results to improve their skills. Specifically, students in this course will learn about the following topics: ・Fundamental programming procedures ・Variable and type declarations ・Input, output, and calculation ・Branch and repetition ・Function ・File processing ・Pointer and structure
requiredKnowledge: The installation of a development environment will be covered during the first class and each student must establish the environment before the second class. Students will be expected to write source code during in the class, so advanced keyboard skills are expected.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the programming syntax of C.
Be able to program applications capable of handling numerous numbers, letters, and data.

subtitle: Media Informatics I

advice: Students learn how the medeia information, e.g., characters, sounds, pictures and movies is encoded and preserved in the computers. Analog signal and digital information 4. Creation of basic media works

educationalGoal: In this course, students will: (1) Learn the history of computer graphics (CG). (2) Gain an understanding of geometric transformation. title: 音楽・音響情報処理
subtitle: Acoustical and Musical Processing
keywords: Music synthesizer 2.Fourier synthesis 3.Music sequencer 4.Automatic music performance 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: In this course, students will: (1) Learn the mechanisms for synthesis of sound in a musical synthesizer and automatic performance methods through MATLAB programming. (2) Learn the physical characteristics of sound and methods for the input or output of sound. (3) Consider the impressions of sound created by programming. (4) Discuss application of the contents for regional cooperation.
advice: In this course, the mechanism for Fourier synthesis in a musical synthesizer and method for automatic performance will be examine based on the knowledge imparted in “Media Informatics I”. In a part of the course, students will learn and practice how to create sound or music work via MATLAB programming. Students are expected to review the contents of “Media Informatics I” and other courses related to computer programming.
requiredKnowledge: An understanding of the course “Media Informatics I” is required. Basic computer programming skills are required.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand how sound is represented in a computer.
Be able to understand the relationship between sound timber and Fourier synthesis.
Be able to understand the relationship between temporal characteristics of sound loudness and time envelopes.
Be able to recreate an imagined sound via MATLAB programming.
Be able to present an automatic music performance via MATLAB programming.
Be able to create original sound or music.

educationalGoal: Students learn the animation principle and how to create and express animations based on the principle. advice: In the first half, students create a flip-book animation to understand the principles of animation. Time-lapse images are animated using Movie Maker or Giam. In order to create original, fun, and high quality animations, it is recommended that students watched many animations from the creator's point of view, such as “expression methods”, “screen composition”, and “color and form”.
requiredKnowledge: Freehand drawing skills is required. It is preferable that image processing software (PhotoShop etc.) can be used.

title: 情報ネットワーク
subtitle: Information Networks
keywords: Computer Network 2.Protocol 3.TCP/IP 4.Internetworking
educationalGoal: Firstly, the students will learn the fact that the network connection is based on the internal hierarchical protocols. Then, each layer of the hierarchy will be focused on stepwise. For example, the hardware, media and wireless technology is addressed in the study of the bottom layer. Especially, the concept of TCP/IP and the structure of IP address, which belong to the intermediate layers and are rather familiar to the end-user with web access, will be illustrated in detail.
advice: This course aims to foster student’s knowledge of network structure and fundamental communication procedure. It is important to understand the contents of this course because many kinds of web service, which becomes mainstream of the computer application today, are realized on the basis of the network technology. The abstract of this course is following: 1. Introduction to Computer Network Subjects: Constituent Element of Network, Communication Method and Protocol Hierarchy, etc. 2. Hierarchy of Protocol Subjects: Application / Transport / Internet / Network Access Layer, etc. 3. Local Area Network (LAN) and Wide Area Network (WAN) Subjects: Basic structure of LAN, Internetworking, etc. 4. Actual Operation of Network Subjects: Method of troubleshooting using network diagnostic commands, Security, etc. Although this course mainly adopts classroom lecture, sometimes the learners are required to practice some commands related to network maintenance.
requiredKnowledge: It is preferable for the students to have acquired a credit of the course“Introduction to Server Management” . At the 1st class, the supervisor will give an instruction of the usage of Learning Management System (LMS), which supports the learning of the students. Immediate mastery of LMS operation is required for the students.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the hierarchy of network protocols
Be able to explain the function of network hosts and medium and its physical structure
Be able to explain the structure of IP address and Ethernet frame
Be able to explain the technical terms related to security, LAN operation and maintenance
Be able to explain the network applications such as world wide web or e-mail

title: メディア情報論Ⅲ
subtitle: Media Informatics III
keywords: Cognitive information processing 2.Sensibility and emotional information processing 3.Vision psychology 4.Auditory psychology 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: In this course, students will: (1) Learn human visual and auditory processing within the context of physiology and psychology. (2) Learn cognitive, sensibility, and emotional information processing for media contents. (3) Learn the method for creating affecting contents. (4) Discuss content application for regional cooperation.
advice: In this course. based on the knowledge imparted during “Media Informatics I”, the cognitive, sensibility, and emotional information processing of media contents (pictures, movies, music, etc.) will be examined. As a part of the course, students will learn and practice to simulate the human processing via computer programming. Accordingly, students should review the contents of “Media Informatics I”, “Media Informatics II”, and ther computer programming courses.
requiredKnowledge: An understanding of the contents of “Media Informatics I” and “Media Informatics II” is required. Basic computer programming skills are required.

Be able to understand human sensibility and emotional processing for visual and auditory stimuli.
Be able to understand the method of simulating the above-mentioned processing via computer programming.
Be able to understand the method of engineering design of media contents

educationalGoal: A database is a system that shares, updates, and reuses data between multiple applications, thereby ensuring data consistency. In this course, students learn the fundamental theory of a relational database, database design, Structured Query Language (SQL), which is the language used for database management, and practical database operations using an actual database management system.
advice: There are three essential abilities needed to manage a database: (1) The ability to handle SQL. (2) The ability to ensure data consistency based on the concept of normal form, primary key, and foreign key, etc. (3) The ability to design a database application system using transactions. In this course we mainly focused on (1) and (2), but (3) will be also mentioned in the later classes. Since SQL is used for comprehensive database operations such as design, handling, and/or maintenance, it will be necessary to polish student SQL management skills by providing them with significant amounts of experience. With that point in mind, students will be required to connect with and use our database server and then use it to manipulate their own databases in order to foster skills and knowledge related to the operation and management of a relational database.

title: Webプログラミング
subtitle: Web Programming
keywords: Web Application 2.Script Language 3.Web Server 4.PHP, HTML 5.Regional Corporation
educationalGoal: Websites not only show home pages, but also provide a more useful system by hosting applications on the internet that are associated with databases. In this course, students will master the scripting language that enables web programming to be executed on the server side. In addition, by acquiring technologies related to web production, students will develop an awareness of issues related to regional collaboration and future information dissemination to society.
advice: In this course, students will learn programming for the processes executed on the server side for the purpose of mastering web applications using Apache for the web server and Hypertext Preprocesser 5 (PHP5) for the scripting language. Practice will take place on each student's laptop PC operating in a Windows environment. Specific class topics include the installation and configuration of the PHP development environment, the basics of PHP grammar, PHP built-in functions, PHP programs on the web, and creating applications using classes and objects in PHP. Before joining the class, students are requested to enter textbook program examples, practice using them, and understand the contents of the textbook. Students should note that, because there is insufficient time to explain each legal item and each program in detail, they are expected to read the textbook thoroughly beforehand. In class, lectures will focus extensively on supplementary and advanced textbook explanations.
requiredKnowledge: Students are expected to understand the contents of the following previous courses: Web Design, Information Technology Basic, Fundamentals of Programming, and Programming. The ability to write HTML is essential for this course.

Be able to set up web servers running PHP.

Be able to utilize PHP built-in functions.

title: メディア情報専門実験・演習B
subtitle: Media Informatics Major Lab/Exercises B
keywords: PC Assembly 2.LAN Construction 3.Physical Computing 4.Interactive Design
educationalGoal: This course is separated into following two parts. The “PC Assembly and Network” part aims to foster the knowledge and skills needed to build a personal computer from parts and construct a simple network. In the "Physical Computing" part, students are required to create an original system consisting of I/O devices connected to a microcomputer and learn about practical interaction designing.
advice: “PC Assembly and Network” In this part of the course, the following experiments and exercises will be conducted: assembly of an IBM-PC compatible machine, configuration of BIOS, installation of the operating system, configuration of the device drivers, assembly of the LAN cable, construction and configuration of the Ethernet local network based on switching hubs, construction of a client-server system, and troubleshooting. “Physical Computing” The goal of this part of the course is to realize a human-oriented interaction through experiments designed to create many kinds of interactions using I/O devices connected to a microcomputer. Students are required to participate actively in the class and engage in teamwork. Safety must be observed at all times. Compliance with scheduled actions and careful treatment of the equipment and tools are also required. All items must be restored to their original conditions when the class is over. Copyright infringement related to class work is strictly prohibited. To pass this course, students grade points must exceed 60% for each part. If any point is less than 60%, the student will fail the entire course.
books: Textbooks: None Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Students are expected to have fundamental knowledge about PCs, networks, and programming. Since safety is a top priority, students must follow instructions from supervisors and work carefully during the exercises.

Be able to construct a simple LAN using multiple PCs and hubs.
Be able to give a presentation about your work.
Be able to connect and control a microcomputer and input/output devices.
Be able to create and produce original interaction designs.

title: モバイルアプリケーション
subtitle: Mobile Application
keywords: Smartphone 2.Tablet 3.HTML5/JavaScript 4.iOS/Android 5.Regional contribution
educationalGoal: In this course, students will learn how to develop graphical interactive applications for mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets using HTML5/JavaScript.
advice: In this course, students will develop applications on the client side of the Web using HTML5/JavaScript. As basic knowledge, it is assumed that students have acquired the HTML/CSS webpage creation method that was taught in the first-year “Web Design” class. In this class, students will learn basic application development methods using HTML5/JavaScript through exercises and assignments. As an overall assignment, teams will be formed to address themes related to community contributions. Therefore, students are expected and encouraged to collect information about the region and try to extract relevant issues on a continuing basis.
requiredKnowledge: Students are expected to have basic knowledge of object-oriented languages and HTML/CSS. In addition, students will need to install the Google Chrome browser on their laptop in order to use the features of Google Chrome developer tools.

Be able to utilize basic technologies such as event processing and Canvas drawing.
Be able to design and develop graphical applications that are intended for mobile use.
Be able to design and develop applications using functions specific to mobile devices such as GPS and sensors

title: 画像情報処理
subtitle: Image Processing
keywords: Digital image 2.Geometric transformation 3.Histogram 4.Edge, binarization, line information extraction 5.Regional contribution
educationalGoal: The objective of this course is to ensure students understand the basic methods used to process digital image data using computers. Learning Objectives: 1. Students will understand fundamental image processing techniques. 2. Students will be able to make programs that process real digital images and video image data using programming language.
advice: In this course, students will learn the fundamental digital image processing methods that input, output, and transform digital images. In addition, students will learn to make programs that process real digital images using various fundamental techniques. Lectures and exercises regarding the following items will be given. The outline of the class content is as follows: (1) Basics of image processing History of image processing, light and color, image digitization, image conversion (2) Fundamental real image processing Image data input/output, image data enhancement, geometric transformation, smoothing/sharpening, Binarization (3) Programming method to realize various fundamental image processing methods Students will learn the skills necessary to make application programs through the creation of works aimed at contributing to the community.
books: Textbooks:ディジタル画像処理 改訂第二版[CG-ARTS協会],reference books:none,reserved books:none
requiredKnowledge: It is important to use textbooks for preparation and review. The scope of the exam is based primarily on materials presented in the class, so it is necessary to understand the class contents well. If students study the class contents in advance and ask questions on matters than need clarification in the class, they can proceed more efficiently. In image processing programming exercises, it is important for students to review and acquire the presented lessons well.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand and explain the basics of digital image processing.
Be able to make fundamental programs that process digital image data and video image data.
Be able to understand binary images, gray images, and color images and then display them.
Be able to understand and explain the manipulation of pixel values of image data, calculation between images.
Be able to understand and explain histograms, contour extraction, and edge extraction from image data.

title: メディア数理
subtitle: Media Mathematics
keywords: Mathematics 2.Physics 3.Matrix 4.Game programming 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: In this course, students will learn mathematics, physics, and how to write game programs. More specifically, students will learn the basics of geometry, vector operations, matrix operations, and geometric transformations as mathematics knowledge. Next, they will learn the basic equations of 1D, 2D, and 3D motion, Newton's law of motion. In parallel with learning mathematics and physics, students will also learn how to write programs.
advice: In this course, students will learn about mathematics, physics, and corresponding programs up to their application to game programs. Students will learn to solve exercises autonomously and explain the answers appropriately. In addition, students will acquire practical knowledge about familiar game programs through consideration of applications such as community contributions.
requiredKnowledge: It is desirable for students to have taken basic mathematical courses.

Be able to express 1D, 2D, and 3D movements using mathematical formulas.
Be able to express collision detection mathematically.
Be able to express parabolic motion mathematically.
Be able to understand programs related to geometric expression.
Be able to understand programs related to physical movement.

title: メディア情報学統合演習
subtitle: Media Informatics Integrated Exercises
keywords: Media informatics 2.Human-centered design 3.Research and development methods 4.Environmental conservation 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: The goal of this course is to teach students the abilities needed to solve real-world and regional problems using Media Informatics knowledge and technology. Students are expected to develop the ability to create specialized and advanced systems or contents that consider environmental conservation based on human-centered designs.
advice: In this course, students are given opportunities to comprehensively use the basic knowledge of Media Informatics, including the programming and audiovisual design skills learned in specialized Department of Media Informatics courses, as a means of facilitating communication and knowledge. As part of efforts aimed at learning how to solve real-world and local problems, students will study R&D methods at companies, after which they will be provided with opportunities to create systems or contents aimed at environmental conservation based on human-centered designs. It is thought that, by developing e-learning contents using Media Informatics, IT knowledge, instructional design theory, and Web programming skills, students will acquire practical skills that are useful in the real world and in regional communities.
requiredKnowledge: All knowledge and skills acquired in the first to third years of the Department of Media Informatics are required.

activityGoals.body: Be able to propose problem solving using Media Informatics knowledge and technology.
Be able to create human-centered designs that consider environmental conservation.
Be able to develop advanced systems and contents.
Be able to advance projects in a planned and documented manner.
Be able to use knowledge and skills practically.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(松下裕研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Matsushita Yutaka)
keywords: Problem/solution 2.Video 3.Web site 4.Kansei evaluation 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: This course integrates what has been learned so far. The purpose of this course is to provide students with opportunities to discover problems (e.g., usability, response time) that are involved in the use of digital contents (videos and websites) and to propose solutions. In order to create digital contents useful for people and society, students will not only create digital contents based on the knowledge they have learned so far but will also assess the physiological properties and emotional states of people using the contents.
advice: Our laboratory aims to teach mastery of the techniques used to effectively edit scenes of videos and to design attractive websites. In order to create digital contents that people can easily use and enjoy, the assessment of their physiological properties and emotional states is just as important as the technique used to create the contents. Therefore, aiming to develop a human sensory measurement technology based on data analysis methods and psychological knowledge, students will use their acquired knowledge to create novel digital contents. Learning Tips: Students of this course are expected to take a full year to solve the problems that they have raised. To ensure this work progresses smoothly, it is important that their research themes be set properly. Indeed, if students set a research theme to which they are strongly committed, they will be able to devote their energies to acquiring necessary knowledge and deriving new ideas, even when they experience difficulties. Additionally, although some may feel that bibliographical search and information gathering process are redundant when determining themes, students should be aware that they are extremely helpful for solving related problems.
requiredKnowledge: Students are required to have completed all the prerequisite subjects of the department. Students must be able to generalize what they have learned from the first to third year. Students are expected to have mastered some of the techniques used for creating digital contents or a technique of programming.

Be able to explain contents related to your specialized field.
Be able to deepen insights into "engineer ethics."
Be able apply specialized expertise to the project theme.
Be able to conduct CDIO-based research and development on the set project theme.

lessons.content: In the first half, a preliminary experiment is conducted for the evaluation of a digital content. Students will recreate the content if necessary. Ultimately, each student integrates their research results to create clear documents.
lessons.operation: Each student reports their progress and analysis results. If necessary, the seminar is conducted on analysis methods. Guidance is provided for creating project reports and presentations.
lessons.assignments: Students study analysis methods and endeavor to complete their research project for about nine hours each week.

educationalGoal: This course is for an educational goal of the Dept. of Management Systems to acquire "Information and Communication Technology ability". advice: To create, manage and operate a WWW site, the following 3 abilities are required: (1) The ability to understand the WWW site production process, (a) Planning a WWW site, (b) Design and implement a WWW site, (c) Manage and Operate a WWW site. (2) The ability to understand and apply HTML (Hyper-Text Mark-up Language) and CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) to produce a WWW site, (3) The ability to produce a web site that considers effective expression of information, ease of use, and availability to anyone. Students will acquire abilities 1 and 2 mainly through lectures and exercises in the first half of the course; they will acquire ability 3 in the second half of the course.

keywords: A series of bookkeeping procedures 2.Closing procedure 3.Financial statements 4.Depreciation 5.Accrual basis
educationalGoal: This course corresponds to the “Financial Accounting Ability” learning/education goal of the Faculty of Management Information. The goal is to have students understand the process of creating accounting information that contributes to the decision-making of management and corporate stakeholders, and to understand the content and role of financial statements, which are the means of conveying accounting information.
advice: Companies record and aggregate the status of their activities using bookkeeping and provide accounting information to managers and stakeholders through financial statements. In this course, students will learn the importance of financial statements as a tool for providing accounting information, as well as how to create and use them, after learning the “Bookkeeping cycle”. By working a large number of exercises, students will develop appropriate bookkeeping and financial statement preparation/analysis skills. Students should also be able to develop logical thinking skills that can be used to assess corporate activities based on monetary value.

subtitle: Marketing Basics
keywords: Marketing Research & Strategy 2.Needs, STP, 4P 3.Branding 4.Regional orientation and regional cooperation 5.Co-creation with society
educationalGoal: This course is a basic course for developing "Marketing Ability (K)" in the Department of Management Systems. Through lectures, learn the concepts, theories and methods of marketing activities necessary for business management. Identify their role and effectiveness through information gathering and case analysis. It is also aimed to create the imege of co-op education, co-creation with society such as CDIO practice.
advice: Course description ○ Lectures on various marketing themes are held. This course focuses on the basic concepts of marketing and the relationship between strategies suc as ① marketing research, ③ key points of marketing 4P (product, price, distribution, sales promotion), ② brand formation etc. ○ In class, use PowerPoint and whiteboard together. List important keywords and points and discuss them with deepen understanding of the theory. In addition, we will try to learn effectively by incorporating video and online information. Expectations ○ Ask for your own ideas, not memorization of knowledge. ○ Always keep an eye on the latest markets and make your own thoughts and interpretations of the movement. In that case, why did you think so? should be presented logically. ○ It is very important to actively participate in classes every time. Absence, lateness, and poor attitude are strictly prohibited.
requiredKnowledge: ◎ Specialized education and training objectives of the Department of Management Systems, aiming to develop "IT skills", "Marketing skills", "financial accounting skills", "Accounting skills", and "Database Management skills". ◎ It is desirable to always pay attention to market trends and collect the latest market information. ◎ Preparation work is basically unnecessary, but review work is required.

keywords: Relational Database 2.E-R Diagram 3.Normalization 4.SQL
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) acquire the basic ability to utilize IT. (2) learn the fundamental theory of relational databases. (3) learn how to design a database, use SQL, and operate a database.
advice: To use a database, the following three abilities are required: 1. The ability to use SQL, a language for managing data held in a database. 2. Be able to design a database.

title: 統計学Ⅱ
subtitle: Statistics II
keywords: Multivariate analysis 2.Prediction model 3.Multiple regression analysis 4.Principal component analysis
educationalGoal: In evaluation problems related to humanities and social sciences, many properties must be often handled simultaneously and comprehensively, and multivariate analysis methods can often provide effective solutions. In this course, students will learn the concepts of and ways of using multivariate analysis via Excel functions. The primary goal is to give them the opportunity to master the method of prediction analysis and learn how to summarize multivariate data. Another goal is to ensure they are capable of using these methods in future learning activities.
advice: The course focuses on the following items: 1. Features and summary of multivariate analysis (prediction and data summarization) 2. The concept and use method of multiple regression analysis 3. The concept and use method of principal component analysis 4. How to use Excel functions Students are expected to review the basic knowledge of linear algebra. In addition, they should learn the contents of descriptive statistics in “Statistics for Information”. It is also desirable to understand the contents of hypothesis testing.
requiredKnowledge: Review linear algebra (i.e., matrices and vectors). Students must be sure to master the lecture contents by reviewing because each item is closely related to previous lessons. Bring a laptop PC (unless otherwise noted) because the lessons will always include practice sessions using Excel.

activityGoals.body: Be able to use multivariate analysis in future learning activities such as Project Design III.
Be able to distinguish the prediction model concept from the data summarization concept.
Be able to understand the basic concepts and application methods of multiple regression analysis.
Be able to understand the basic concepts and application methods of principal component analysis.

title: システムモデリング
subtitle: Systems Modeling
keywords: System Design 2.Systems Thinking 3.Conceptual Modeling 4.UML 5.Object Diagram
educationalGoal: Students will learn: (1) how to grasp complex systems correctly. (2) how to describe conceptual models using UML diagrams. (3) how to improve the system using the model.
advice: To grasp complex systems correctly, the following three abilities are required : 1. The ability to view the system in two levels (concept level and implementation level). 2. The ability to view the system from three aspects (static, functional, and dynamic). 3. The ability to visualize the structure and behavior of the system with appropriate expressions. In the first half of the class, students will learn 1 and 2 through lectures and quizzes, and in the second half, they will learn 3 through exercises. In 3, students use PC to draw UML diagrams. As the drawing software, astah* will be used. The installing will be instructed in the class.
books: Textbook : The Introduction to UML Modeling, Nikkei-BP (Japanese book)
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of any model diagram (Not required)

Be able to draw UML diagrams of a simple system.
Be able to design specific requirements and draw the concept model.
Be able to understand system behavior from UML diagrams.
Be able to pick up problems and improve systems.

title: 経営分析
subtitle: Business Analysis
keywords: Corporate database such as EDINET 2.Industry analysis 3.Profitability analysis 4.Safety analysis 5.Cash flow analysis
educationalGoal: This course corresponds to the “Financial Accounting Ability” learning/education goal of the Faculty of Management Information. In order for managers to fulfill their duties in the future, analytical information on management activities is required. In this course, students will acquire the knowledge and skills necessary for management analysis and develop the ability to make comprehensive judgments on the results of management analysis from a multifaceted perspective.
advice: In the first half of the course, students will learn how to collect and organize information centered on the use of EDINET, etc. In the second half, students will practice management analysis using various analytical methods based on information collected and organized for specific companies. Finally, students will prepare and submit a management analysis report and give a presentation on the results of their management analysis. When doing the assigned exercises, it is important that students pay attention to economic news and company information and study in depth their target company and industry.
books: Textbook: Not specified Reference book: Not specified Reserved Book: Not specified
requiredKnowledge: Students will need to thoroughly review what they learned in Basics of Corporate Accounting before taking this course.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand that management analysis information is useful for making decisions.
Be able to collect and organize corporate information through EDINET, HP, and other media.
Be able to understand basic ratio analysis formulas and use them in specific management analysis exercises.
Be able to a conduct business analysis of a given company and clearly present ideas and findings.

keywords: Python 2.Programming 3.Data analysis 4.Machine learning
educationalGoal: This course is a specialized core class to achieve the specialized core “IT utilization ability” goal of the Department of Management Information. Students will learn Python, a general-purpose programming language, so that they can create simple tools for data analysis.
advice: Students will learn the basics and application of Python by completing a number of programming exercises. By actually writing programs, students will produce a tool that will perform data analysis; they will then use the tool on open data. Simply running the program in class is not sufficient; students will need to actually run the program on their own, especially as a means of review.
requiredKnowledge: Students should have a knowledge of general corporate management and information technology by taking other classes. It is assumed that students will have an understanding of Web design, IT system basics, database management, programming basics, and applied programming; these topics should be reviewed as necessary.

title: 経営情報システム
subtitle: Management Information Systems
keywords: Algorithms 2.Search, encryption, digital signature 3.Dynamic programming 4.K neighborhood method 5.Indeterminably
educationalGoal: This course is for an educational goal to acquire "IT basic ability". Students will: (1) acquire the basic algorithmic thinking ability to fuse and utilize management and IT, (2) learn the fundamental algorithms which are useful to solve several problems, (3) acquire the ability to devise solutions for management organizations aim.
advice: There is a need for managers and business promoters who understand IT in these days, so that various management functions and IT application systems should be vital for students who are willing to become modern business persons. Up to now, students have learned web page creation method, IT system basics that enable IT passport acquisition, database construction techniques, hands-on efforts such as dynamic web page creation, and programming with Python. To understand the IT technology used in actual business from a bird's-eye view, it is necessary to solve problems rather than using individual applications. So students should understand algorithms that are methods and means to solve them. The purpose of this class is to learn the outline of more than a dozen types of algorithms and to acquire the ability to solve problems using algorithms. Specifically, learning of the following ten algorithms that students normally use in an invisible form, they will deepen understanding through the proposal of practical solutions. (1) Sort, (2) Recursion, (3) Quick sort, (4) Hash table, (5) Breadth-first search, (6) Dijkstra method, (7) Greedy algorithm, (8) Dynamic programming, (9) k-neighbors, (10) cryptography. One of the purposes of this class is “deeply think about the answer by yourself”, so that students will have a simple assignment at each lecture. In addition, lectures will be held by using Python, students can learn by executing some actual programs.
books: Grokking Algorithms: An illustrated guide for programmers and other curious people, Manning Publications, Manning Publications
requiredKnowledge: It is necessary to have a certain level of knowledge about general corporate management and information technology by taking other subjects: Web design, IT system management, database management, programming basics, applied programming, IT systems and management.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand and explain information technology in general by learning basic knowledge of IT.
Be able to explain necessity and effectiveness of algorithms used in various information systems.
Be able to explain algorithms being important means and subject of corporate strategies.
Be able to devise and design algorithms to solve problems by yourselves.

Students will: (1) acquire the basic algorithmic thinking ability to fuse and utilize management and IT, (2) learn the fundamental algorithms which are useful to solve several problems, (3) acquire the ability to devise solutions for management organizations aim.
    授業の概要および学習上の助言   There is a need for managers and business promoters who understand IT in these days, so that various management functions and IT application systems should be vital for students who are willing to become modern business persons. Up to now, students have learned web page creation method, IT system basics that enable IT passport acquisition, database construction techniques, hands-on efforts such as dynamic web page creation, and programming with Python. To understand the IT technology used in actual business from a bird's-eye view, it is necessary to solve problems rather than using individual applications. So students should understand algorithms that are methods and means to solve them. The purpose of this class is to learn the outline of more than a dozen types of algorithms and to acquire the ability to solve problems using algorithms. Specifically, learning of the following ten algorithms that students normally use in an invisible form, they will deepen understanding through the proposal of practical solutions. (1) Sort, (2) Recursion, (3) Quick sort, (4) Hash table, (5) Breadth-first search, (6) Dijkstra method, (7) Greedy algorithm, (8) Dynamic programming, (9) k-neighbors, (10) cryptography. One of the purposes of this class is “deeply think about the answer by yourself”, so that students will have a simple assignment at each lecture. In addition, lectures will be held by using Python, students can learn by executing some actual programs.

title: 原価管理
subtitle: Cost Accounting and Cost Management
keywords: Job-order costing 2.Manufacturing overhead 3.Standard costing 4.Cost differences analysis 5.ABC costing
educationalGoal: This course corresponds to the “Business Applied Practical Ability” learning and educational goal of the Department of Management Systems. The goal is for students to understand the process of calculating product costs and sales costs in the manufacturing industry in relation to industrial bookkeeping, and to learn cost management concepts and accounting methods while learning how to analyze cost differences that occur in job-order costing and standard costing.
advice: Students will first learn the basics of cost accounting and manufacturing cost statements. They will then learn job-order costing and cost differences analysis, standard costing and cost differences analysis, and ABC (activity-based costing). Finally, students will learn strategic cost management. Through these, students should understand the relationship between the cost determination process and cost management. Since step-by-step learning takes place, students are expected to make a serious effort to keep up.
requiredKnowledge: As the contents learned in finance-related classes will be effectively utilized, students should review the contents learned in these previous courses before attending the class.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the cost elements that compose product cost.
Be able to understand the relationship between cost records and financial statements.
Be able to understand cost summary procedures and account entry in job-order costing.
Understand the allocation procedure for manufacturing overhead and the analysis of allocation differences.
Be able to understand cost summary procedures and cost differences analysis in standard costing.
Be able to understand ABC (activity-based costing.)

title: 経営情報学統合演習
subtitle: Management Systems Integrated Exercises
keywords: Management 2.Data Analysis 3.Communication in English 4.Design Thinking 5.Community-Oriented
educationalGoal: This workshop-style course aims to foster practical skills for general management. Students will apply much of what they have learned from their past three years of study, including analytical methods, marketing skills, and information technology, in simple exercises related to business cases.
advice: This is a course for senior students, providing them an opportunity to brush up on learned skills and prior knowledge by working exercises in workshop style. The small class size enables students to freely discuss issues and easily interact with one another. The detailed contents of the exercises will be decided after a discussion with students in the first class. The tentative course plan includes the following: 1) Reading articles written in English from journals and newspapers in order to explore current topics related to the global situation and various cutting-edge technologies. 2) Working on mini-exercises based on the concept of “design thinking.” 3) Completing data analysis exercises. Especially for element 1), students are strongly encouraged to participate in the “TOEIC(R) Challenge!” program offered by the KIT Essential English Center. Students are expected to actively commit to each and every class.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of management. Basic data analysis skills. Knowledge of basic English grammar and vocabulary. Basic computer skills.

activityGoals.body: Be able to gather information from articles written in English.
Be able to manage a project based on the procedures of design thinking.
Be able to properly conduct analysis procedures for business data.
Be able to develop a management plan in a simple business case.

title: 会計情報とビジネス法規
subtitle: Accounting Information and Business Regulations
keywords: Accounting standards 2.Corporate tax 3.Income tax 4.Corporate law 5.Civil law
educationalGoal: This course corresponds to the “Financial Ability” learning and educational goal of the Department of Management Systems. The goal is for the student to understand important accounting standards to understand what accounting information conveys and to understand the basic part of legal knowledge such as tax system, corporate law, civil law, etc. as peripheral knowledge so that they can understand the contents of securities report, which is a general disclosure document of a company.
advice: This course covers a wide range of subjects such as accounting standards, taxation, and legal knowledge related to corporate law. First of all, since this course will be conducted on the premise that you understand the matters learned in the "Accounting basic", it is necessary to review the "Accounting basic". In addition, new terms and ideas will appear frequently, so enthusiastic class participation and constant efforts are required.
requiredKnowledge: Since this course teaches the theoretical part of accounting, it is necessary to have a solid understanding of what was learned in "Accounting Basic" in order to understand the content of the lesson.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the concept of important accounting standards.

Be able to use your tax knowledge for business and life by understanding the overall mechanism of the tax system
Be able to recognize the importance of legal knowledge in conducting corporate management.
Be able to understand the minimum required legal knowledge about corporate management.

subtitle: Elements of Psychological Data Analysis
keywords: Spreadsheet 2.Data processing 3.Functions 4.Basic statistics 5.Creating figures and tables
educationalGoal: Through practical training using spreadsheet software (Excel) students will: ・ Be able to understand data processing and chart creation. ・ Be able to understand how to use functions. ・ Be able to understand basic statistics.
advice: The data analysis courses of the Department of Psychological Science aim to teach the knowledge and skills necessary to analyze data obtained from psychological experiments. In particular, this course will teach students about data processing using the spreadsheet software Excel. The course is conducted with lectures and practical training. In order to spend as much time as possible on the practical training, students are required to prepare for the class, and they are required to understand the contents through preparation and to confirm their understanding through practical training during the course. If students do not understand the information during class time, they should deal with it as soon as possible by using office hours. This course will focus on the following topics: 1. Spreadsheet software (Excel) basic technology: data processing, creating figures and tables 2. How to use Excel functions 3. Concepts of basic statistics: mean, median, mode, maximum, minimum, variance, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis * Be sure to bring a computer to each class as you will be using the spreadsheet software (Excel)
requiredKnowledge: Students must to bring a personal computer to each class to do the practical training every week. There are many opportunities to use data analysis in psychology, so students should look for solutions with an awareness of the problem.

title: 教育・学校心理学
subtitle: Educational and School Psychology
keywords: Learning Science 2.Learning How to Learn 3.Meta-cognition 4.Collaborative Learning 5.School as a Team
educationalGoal: Through reflection on previous learning and connecting students with the theories covered in the course, students will: - be able to understand the problems that occur in the educational field and the background. - be able to understand psychosocial issues and necessary support in the field. - be able to set their own learning goals, observe learning performance and make self-assessments of their learning.
advice: This course will focus on two areas of educational psychology and school psychology. These two psychologies may have a strong focus on the “theory for teaching” taken by those who aim to be teachers, but the course will also focus on the “theory for learning” from the perspective of learning science. Learning educational psychology will help to refine the way of learning and learning school psychology will help improve the quality of learning in school education where students are currently located. Specifically, the following topics are covered: (1) Learning how to learn: (a) Experiential learning, (b) Self-regulated learning, (c) Expertise (2) Cognition and cognition: (a) Meta-cognition, (b) Adaptive meta-cognition, (c) Critical thinking (3) Collaborative learning:(a) Legitimate peripheral participation (b) the Knowledge-constructive jigsaw method (4) School as a team: (a) Three kinds of psychoeducational services, (b) Four aspects of student support The above contents are learned through knowledge internalization (e.g., lectures) and knowledge externalization (e.g., discussions and presentations). There is an opportunity to consider the course subjects that have been taken so far and those that have been taken in the same semester based on the content of this course. # This course is required for Certified Public Psychologists and Certified Psychologists.

title: アカデミックライティング(再履修クラス)
subtitle: Academic Writing
keywords: How to write a report 2.How to grasp the purpose 3.How to consider 4.logical thinking
educationalGoal: This course takes over from “Basics Style for Study A and B” and aims to develop reporting skills in specialized fields. In the process of discovering and solving problems, it is necessary to have the ability to summarize and share information on your thoughts and claims in reports. In order to acquire this as an “individual” ability, students will learn the procedure for writing reports on themes in line with the specialty of their chosen department. The course will provide an introduction to the writing of reports and papers for specialized subjects.
advice: In order to cultivate the basic abilities of “grasping the purpose”, “organizing information”, “thinking logically”, “reporting in writing”, and “distinguishing between plagiarism and citation”, students learn the procedure for writing reports. Reports will be based on information collected on themes according to the specialty of the department to which the students belong and reference articles will be used to write reports. The goals of the course are to: 1. Understand the concept of papers in psychology. 2. Understand the purpose of the psychological experiments and organizing the results to create a logical description of the considerations. 3. Learn the expressions used and the types of papers and reports in psychology. The course is linked to the contents of the “Practice of Elementary Psychological Experiments” course which will be held in the same semester. Students are required to make use of what they learned in the both courses. The progress of classes will be adjusted as needed according to the level of understanding of students and the progress of assignments. Note: Since this is a one-credit course, there are some weeks when there are no classes. The specific class schedule will be provided in the first class.
books: Writing Manual of the Japanese Psychological Association. Other materials are indicated in the class.
requiredKnowledge: Improve your reading and writing skills in “Basics Style for Study A and B”. Be familiar with the how to use the library center, which is necessary for information collection, and how to use the Internet.

activityGoals.body: Ability to understand the meaning of psychological experiments and describe their purpose clearly.
Ability to describe the results and considerations of psychological experiments logically.
Ability to write reports that follow a standard format in psychology.

title: 心理学統計法
subtitle: Psychological Statistics
keywords: Population and sample 2.Descriptive statistics 3.Statistical tests 4.Power analysis
educationalGoal: Statistical analysis is required for psychological research with high generalizability. The goal of this course is to provide students with the basic knowledge to run statistical tests and to understand the results of the tests precisely.
advice: The class proceeds with lectures on the basic theory of psychological statistics and practical training of statistical analyses that include calculations with real data using Microsoft Excel and R. Students are expected to understand the basics of psychological statistics and learn the method of statistical analysis to avoid misuse of statistical analysis and misinterpretation of the results of analyses. Note that the course flow can be changed according to other closely related courses such as “Practice of Elementary Psychological Experiments.” Note: This course is required for Certified Public Psychologists & Certified Psychologists.
books: 数学が苦手でもわかる心理統計法入門 : 基礎から多変量解析まで[サイエンス社] Sugaku ga nigate demo wakaru shinritoukeihou nyuumon: kiso kara tahenryou kaiseki kade
requiredKnowledge: Students are required to bring their own personal computer with Microsoft Excel, R (RStudio) and other software for statistical analysis.

activityGoals.body: Ability to decide which statistical analyses are appropriate for the data acquired in experiments and surveys.
Ability to run statistical analyses with appropriate methods and to interpret the results in appropriate ways.
Ability to understand the selection, computation, and interpretation of descriptive statistics.
Ability to understand inferential statistics.

title: 心理学基礎実験実習Ⅰ
subtitle: Practice of Elementary Psychological Experiments I
keywords: Psychological experiment 2.Data analysis 3.Report writing 4.Sensasion, Perception, Cognition 5.Social behavior
educationalGoal: The aim of this course is to understand the concept of experimental psychology and to acquire deeper knowledge of experimental methods to obtain accurate results through exercises of elementary psychological experiments. Students will also learn statistical analysis and evaluation of experimental data and basic skill of writing psychological reports.
advice: The class will be roughly divided into three terms with a total of five experiments (the themes of experiments are subject to change). In this class, students participate in the entire process of psychological research using experimental methods, namely conducting experiments (especially experiments on sensation and perception, memory, cognition and social behavior), analyzing the experimental data, and writing paper on the results of experiments. Throughout the semester students will participate in several cycles of research (conducting experiments, analysis, writing reports). It is very important to have practical experience in conducting experiments, to understand psychological phenomena and to analyze the data, and to acquire skill of writing report. Therefore, marks will be deducted for absence and tardiness. Students must bring their own PC to every class. This course is also linked to "Psychological Statistical Methods" and "Psychological Experiments," which are offered at the same semester, so students are expected to gain a deeper understanding of how to conduct experimental research in psychology considering the relationship with the contents of these courses.
books: Writing Manual of the Japanse Psychological Association. Other materials will be indicatd in each topic.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of psychology and experimental methods studied in the “Introduction to Psychology” and “Method of Psychological Research”courses in the previous semesters is required.

Students will also learn statistical analysis and evaluation of experimental data and basic skill of writing psychological reports.
    授業の概要および学習上の助言   The class will be roughly divided into three terms with a total of five experiments (the themes of experiments are subject to change). Throughout the semester students will participate in several cycles of research (conducting experiments, analysis, writing reports). It is very important to have practical experience in conducting experiments, to understand psychological phenomena and to analyze the data, and to acquire skill of writing report. Therefore, marks will be deducted for absence and tardiness. Students must bring their own PC to every class. This course is also linked to "Psychological Statistical Methods" and "Psychological Experiments," which are offered at the same semester, so students are expected to gain a deeper understanding of how to conduct experimental research in psychology considering the relationship with the contents of these courses.

title: 心理学データ解析応用
subtitle: Advanced Psychological Data Analysis
keywords: Data cleaning and handling 2.Statistical analysis 3.R(software) 4.Effect size, 95%CI, power 5.Power analysis
educationalGoal: The goals of this course are: 1) to provide students with the basic knowledge to use software for data analyses in psychological research, and 2) to apply this knowledge to actual data analysis. In addition, we aim to statistically analyze the data obtained from previous psychological research and make socially and academically meaningful claims and proposals. Acquire essential skills for research in Project Design III.
advice: Current psychological study requires researchers to use R software, which enables various statistical analyses from basic analyses (e.g., t-test, ANOVA) to multivariate analyses (e.g., regression analysis, factorial analysis). Students also deepen their understanding of sample size design and power analysis, as well as indicators such as effect sizes and confidence intervals in addition to p-values, and acquire the ability to calculate them. R is so useful that students make use of it in their Project Design III, but it is difficult to learn how to use it. Students should make use of office hours and peer instructions.
requiredKnowledge: Students should make use of their previous knowledge of data analysis during the course. Students are expected to review the knowledge on statistical analysis. Students must bring their own personal computer to every class.

title: 健康・医療心理学
subtitle: Health and Medical Psychology
keywords: Stress 2.Health care activity 3.Health 4.Medical site 5.Prevention
educationalGoal: Students will learn the basic knowledge and skills to provide psychological support in the health care field. Students must learn: 1. Stress process and disease in daily life 2. Psychosocial problems at medical sites 3. Psychological supportive approach for victims of the disaster
advice: The course aims to introduce health and medical care from a psychology point of view. Students will discuss psychological support for people who need to improve their mental/physical health. The course gives students advice to improve people's (and their own) health. Students should understand their own health and stress process with relation to experiences in daily life. Students are expected to read the reference book and other books related to stress and stress management. The course asks students to answer questionnaires about mental health to fully understand their own health. However, these questionnaires are not mandatory. This course is required for Certified Public Psychologists.
books: Textbooks: Health and Medical Psychology, Ishiyaku Publishers, Inc. Reference books: Health and Medical Psychology, Nakanishiya Publishers, Inc. Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Students need to read books related to stress health care and health behaviors (eating, exercise, sleep, smoking, etc.). In addition, students should find health promotion and medical psychological support in their local community, and should consider what kind of psychological support they want to receive. Students are expected to apply the knowledge of and skills in health/medical psychology to people's (and their own) health care.

Ability to describe the role of Certified Public Psychologists at medical sites

title: 学習・言語心理学
subtitle: Psychology of Learning and Language
keywords: Respondent conditioning 2.Operant conditioning 3.Situated cognition 4.Language acquisition 5.Phonetics-syntactics-pragmatics
educationalGoal: In this course, we will study high-level cognitive processes such as language and learning that support human intellectual activities. Beginning with behavioral learning theory, we will explain the model of knowledge acquisition in cognitive psychology. In addition, we will explain the characteristics and acquisition process of language as a tool for communication and thinking. Based on this knowledge, the goal is for students to be able to improve their own daily activities and apply them to the real world.
advice: We use language, learn various things from past experiences, and change our behavior to live a smooth life. Language also distinguishes humans from other animals and plays a vital role in various cognitive activities. In this course, we aim to teach specialized knowledge on learning and language that supports our higher level cognitive activities, based on what was learned in previous courses. Language and learning are associated with various interesting phenomena in our daily lives. I hope the lessons learned in this course will be used to understand the various phenomena experienced in daily life. Classes will be centered on lectures, but exercises will be introduced as needed to aid understanding.
books: Reference books are indicated in each topic.
requiredKnowledge: Fully understand basic information on learning, cognition and language learned from previous courses. Be sure to fully understand the basic operations of a PC, as it may be necessary to perform exercises using a PC.

Ability to understand the theories of respondent conditioning and operant conditioning.
Ability to understand the role of social context in learning and language acquisition.
Ability to understand the characteristics of language acquisition different from learning in general.
Ability to understand the role of language in learning, thinking, and cognition.

title: ヒューマンインタフェース設計学
subtitle: Designing of Human Interface
keywords: Human Interface 2.User Experience (UX) 3.Cognitive Property 4.Human Error 5.Regional Collaboration
educationalGoal: “Human Interface” refers to a system’s interface that humans can actually see and touch. If the interface is not user-friendly and has a lot of functions, we might fail to operate the system and it could cause problems or accidents. This lecture teaches knowledge of cognitive and physiological properties of the user, concepts of user experience (UX), and definitions of human centered design (HCD) in order to make the human interface more user-friendly.
advice: Topics covered in this lecture are as follows: 1. Basics of human interface. 2. UX and HCD process. 3. Cognitive properties and usability design. 4. Feedback and temporal elements in human interface. 5. Human error. Special lectures on designing the interface by product development experts in private enterprises are going to be planned.

requiredKnowledge: UX design is an issue in daily life, and you must be always aware of the usability of products around you. Talking, recording and taking pictures without permission during the lecture are prohibited. Seats are assigned every time.

title: 観察法
subtitle: Observational Method
keywords: Natural Observation 2.Experimental Observation 3.Hypothesis-generating Research 4.Time-sampling vs Event-sampling 5.Regional Collaboration
educationalGoal: The observational method is the most basic scientific research method, which involves looking closely at phenomena, especially human behavior in the case of psychology. The observational method is also used in hypothesis-testing research as well as in exploratory hypothesis-generating research. In this course, students will learn the basic concepts of the observation method, how to plan and conduct observations, and how to analyze the data, with practical exercises.
advice: In this class, the following topics will be studied with practical exercises. 1. Basic characteristics of observation methods 2. Types of observation methods 3. How to perform observation methods 4. Basic analysis methods in observation methods 5. Appropriate interpretation of observation data In the practical training, teams of several students will be formed to experience the flow of each type of observation method, from setting the research objectives, planning and conducting observations (data collection), to analysis and interpretation. Since research using observation methods often focuses on the casual behaviors that people take in their daily lives, we recommend that participants in this class pay attention to people's daily behaviors and their characteristics. The lecture content and schedule are subject to change slightly.
books: Reference books are introduced in the class.
requiredKnowledge: Review the basics of observation methods learned in "Research Methods in Psychology". In addition, it will be helpful to review the knowledge of other research methods learned in previous classes and the methods used to obtain various findings in psychology, in order to understand the characteristics and implementation of the observation method.

activityGoals.body: Ability to understand and to explain the basic features of the observation method.
Ability to understand and to perform the characteristics and implementation of natural observation.
Ability to understand and to perform the characteristics and implementation of experimental observation.
Ability to understand and to perform analysis of observation data based on the time-sampling method.
Ability to understand and to perform analysis of observation data based on the event-sampling method.
Ability to interpret the results of obsabational data analysis appropriately, and to create new hypothesis.

title: 脳情報科学
subtitle: Brain Information Science
keywords: Research method of brain science 2.Attention 3.Memory 4.Emotion 5.Cognition
educationalGoal: Brain is the basis of psychological functions. The rapid development of brain research method allowed the clarification of brain functions in various psychological processing. The goal of this course is to provide students with the basic knowledge of brain functions such as “attention & eye movement”, “long/short term memory”, “Emotion and its control”, “Emotion & brain waves”, “Cognitive control & decision making”, “Social cognition” and “Theory of mind”.
advice: This course proceeds with the combination of lectures, quiz and exams on important topics of brain science such as “attention & eye movement”, “long/short term memory”, “Emotion and its control”, “Emotion & brain waves”, “Cognitive control & decision making”, “Social cognition” and “Theory of mind.” Students are required to learn the contents in the integrated way. The course is consisted of four main topics on which some lectures, quiz and an exam will be provided. 1) the brain research methods (e.g., EEG, fMRI, NIRS) and the brain function of attention and eye movement (3weeks) 2) long/short term memory and working memory (3weeks) 3) information processing on emotion (4 weeks) 4) higher cognition (cognitive control, decision making, social cognition and theory of mind) (3 weeks) Because there are four exams for each topic, students are not evaluated by a final exam but are required to pay much attention to each topic. Note: This course is a part of requirements of Certified Public Psychologist.
requiredKnowledge: Students are required to understand the learning contents of “Cognitive neuroscience”, and “Psychology of information processing”.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand brain function of various psychological processing.
Be able to understand the basis of psychology and brain science.
Be able to explain fundamental factors to construct a system that suits psychological processing.

title: 脳生理データ解析演習
subtitle: Analysis of Brain and Physiological Data
keywords: Eye movement data 2.ECG data 3.EEG data 4.fMRI data 5.MATLAB
educationalGoal: In recent years, there has been an increase in the use of various measuring devices in psychology to conduct physiological and brain measurements. The data obtained from these measurements are characterized by a large number of data, time series, and multiple channels compared to conventional psychological experiment data. In this course, we will focus on four types of brain and physiological measurement data that are often used in psychological research, and aim to learn the basics of analyzing these data.
advice: In this course, students will learn a wide range of analysis methods, from the basics of data processing using the basic functions of MATLAB to how to use software commonly used in actual research situations, mainly through exercises. This is not just a class of listening to lectures, so please be motivated to work hard.
requiredKnowledge: MATLAB will be used, so be sure to have it installed before the class starts.

activityGoals.body: Be able to run the statistical analyses with MATLAB.
Be able to visualize data with MATLAB.
Be able to choose an adequate analyzing tool with data.
Be able to use effectively various analyzing tools implemented in MATLAB.

educationalGoal: Psychological assessment is a multifaceted process of understanding the client's problems and resources and finding appropriate interventions.In this course, you will learn about the following four points.1.Psychological assessment objectives and ethics,2. title: 心理科学専門実験・演習A
subtitle: Psychological Science Major Lab/Exercises A
keywords: Questionnaire method 2.Factor analysis 3.Observation 4.Elderly simulation 5.Nonparametric test
educationalGoal: In the “Questionnaire Method and Survey Practice” component, students will learn a series of processes from questionnaire preparation to surveys and analysis in psychological survey methods. In the “Observation Method and Elderly Simulation” component, students will practice data collection and analysis in observation methods (including statistical analysis using nonparametric tests) through the experience of elderly simulation.
advice: Of the major research methods in psychology, this course will focus on questionnaire methods and observation methods. As a comprehensive task of learning results so far, students will conduct complete a research study using these methods. Students form a team, determine the purpose of the survey and the behavior to be observed, set the survey items and performance tasks, collect and analyze the data, make a presentation for each team, and discuss the research results. In addition, each individual student will write a research paper summarizing the entire study. In the “Questionnaire Method and Survey Practical Training” component, students will learn a series of processes from data collection to analysis, starting with selection of question items, with the aim of acquiring procedures and analysis methods for the questionnaire method. The “Observation Method and Elderly Simulation” component aims to teach the procedure and analysis method of the observation method and to help students understand the method of hypothesis generation type research. The main objective of observation is human behavior in elderly simulation. Students also practice qualitative data analysis methods obtained by observation methods and statistical analysis using nonparametric methods. This course requires students to bring a PC to every class. Strictly refrain from being late, taking unauthorized absences, and having an uncooperative attitude toward team activities.
requiredKnowledge: Fully understand basic information on learning, cognition and language learned from previous courses. Be sure to fully understand the basic operations of a PC, as it may be necessary to perform exercises using a PC.

activityGoals.body: Ability to pick out the question items necessary for the evaluation and creation of a questionnaire
Ability to sum up and analyze the data.
Ability to perform a statistical analysis of the data and consider the results.
Ability to understand a series of procedures in observation methods and collect data.
Ability to understand data analysis in observation methods, and actually analyze the data.
Ability to understand nonparametric methods and actually use them in data analysis.

title: 心理科学専門実験・演習B
subtitle: Psychological Science Major Lab/Exercises B
keywords: Programming 2.Stimulus-Response Relationship 3.Analysis of Variance 4.Measurement of Brain Activity 5.Measurement of Biological Information
educationalGoal: Programming and Psychological Experiment: Students practice writing a program for a psychological experiment using MATLAB and PsychToolBox, run the experiment, and perform analysis of variance with the data obtained in the experiment. Measurement of Brain Activity and Biological Information: Students practice measuring brain activity and biological information with different measurement devices, and analyze the data.
advice: This course is required for Certified Psychologists. In order to reveal the system for processing on Kansei and cognition, it is necessary to measure and analyze not only overt behavioral indices, but also implicit ones like brain and biological activity. In “Programming and Psychological Experiment”, students practice writing a program for a experiment on cognitive psychology using MATLAB and PsychToolBox. In “Measurement of Brain Activity and Biological Information”, students practice experiments to measure brain activity and biological information. Both components include not only experiments, but presentations and writing reports on the experiments. Understanding these methods is important to understand the system for processing on Kansei and cognition, and to prepare for experiments in Design Project III.

In “Measurement of Brain Activity and Biological Information”, students practice experiments to measure brain activity and biological information. Understanding these methods is important to understand the system for processing on Kansei and cognition, and to prepare for experiments in Design Project III.

title: 精神疾患とその治療
subtitle: Psychiatric Disorders and Treatments
keywords: mind, spirit, soul or will 2.brain function 3.psychological treatment
educationalGoal: What are mental activities? We take a look on how they are manifested, how they are caught in our perception. Students are supposed to have fundamental knowledge on brain function, which is the commanding center of mental activities in the body of human being. We are going to look into the meaning and significance of psychiatric treatment. The main psychiatric disorders including their treatment are briefly explained with the things described above. Students are supposed to understand the outline of psychiatry as a basic knowledge of clinical psychologist.
advice: In various clinical settings, one to one consultation, group interviewing with a patients and his or her family, friends an so on, at a medical institution, at a facility, and at home, we are going to think what can be found, what can happen, and what can be done. We are going to examine the case where a client can`t adapt oneself to one`s circumstances, how can we help him or her? What are problems on the course of life time in our modern society? What are they from their birth to the infancy before going to school? During compulsory education? After the education thereafter or during the vocational training? During the work life? Or unfortunately out of work as a NEET? On marriage life? In the middle age when we have responsibility of the family and work? What are problems when children become grown-up, in his or her elder or older age? We are going to think about the cases when we may suffer severe disease in-between, may encounter severe accidents and have handicaps. Or when we may have cancer and unfortunately we may live a few more months, how can we live in the community, and surmount our problems of life. Or if we can`t solve our problems and turn to be pathological, what can our community do? Students are supposed to think themselves about the issues above. There are many possibilities and points of view. The performances by each clinician can be delivered case by case with flexibility along each situation. As still a college student, it is advisable for you to be able to have various ideas on possibilities and points of view to deal with the problems.

    授業科目の学習・教育目標   キーワード 学習・教育目標     1.mind, spirit, soul or will 2.brain function 3.psychological treatment  What are mental activities? We take a look on how they are manifested, how they are caught in our perception. Students are supposed to have fundamental knowledge on brain function, which is the commanding center of mental activities in the body of human being. We are going to look into the meaning and significance of psychiatric treatment. The main psychiatric disorders including their treatment are briefly explained with the things described above. Students are supposed to understand the outline of psychiatry as a basic knowledge of clinical psychologist.
    授業の概要および学習上の助言   In various clinical settings, one to one consultation, group interviewing with a patients and his or her family, friends an so on, at a medical institution, at a facility, and at home, we are going to think what can be found, what can happen, and what can be done. We are going to examine the case where a client can`t adapt oneself to one`s circumstances, how can we help him or her? What are problems on the course of life time in our modern society? What are they from their birth to the infancy before going to school? During compulsory education? After the education thereafter or during the vocational training? During the work life? Or unfortunately out of work as a NEET? On marriage life? In the middle age when we have responsibility of the family and work? What are problems when children become grown-up, in his or her elder or older age? We are going to think about the cases when we may suffer severe disease in-between, may encounter severe accidents and have handicaps. Or when we may have cancer and unfortunately we may live a few more months, how can we live in the community, and surmount our problems of life. Or if we can`t solve our problems and turn to be pathological, what can our community do? Students are supposed to think themselves about the issues above. There are many possibilities and points of view. The performances by each clinician can be delivered case by case with flexibility along each situation. As still a college student, it is advisable for you to be able to have various ideas on possibilities and points of view to deal with the problems.
