title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(神宮英夫研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Jingu Hideo)
keywords: Kansei Engineering 2.Ergonomics 3.Sensory Evaluation 4.Engineering Psychology
educationalGoal: The aim is to propose a service that is reflected the function of the mind and the planning/development of a product that is safe, comfortable, and fun to use. Students work on theme, while making use of psychological knowledge and measurement/evaluation techniques acquired so far.
advice: This course is required for Certified Psychologists. Lectures, practice exercises, and experiment are carried out as needed. Presentations and discussions are held appropriately. At the end of the previous semester, activities are presented in the department presentation time. At the end of the academic year, the one-year results are presented collectively. Students participate in a seminar every week and work on a problem until the following week. In the seminar every week, activity contents of the week are reported. The themes are Kansei engineering, ergonomics, product development, and brand management, etc. Collaborative investigation with professional research workers and the external persons is important. The themes are continuously progressed while adhering to deadlines and schedules and students can learn about business interactions. At the end of the second semester, a presentation is evaluated by research workers and the external persons and students can obtain their guidances.
requiredKnowledge: This course cannot be completed if students are absent from weekly seminars and do not submit reports. Review the specialized subjects you have studied so far and work on Design Project III actively.

Ability to use techniques of measurement/evaluation for the function of the mind.
Ability to explain the process of manufacturing by Kansei engineering.

Ability to obtain behavior guidance for your future career.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(田中吉史研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Tanaka Yoshifumi)
keywords: Cognitive psychology 2.Cognitive science 3.Kansei information processing 4.Aid for learning and thinking 5.Creativity enhancement
educationalGoal: The aim of this course is to be able to plan and develop products/systems that can be used safely, comfortably and enjoyably, and be able to propose services considering human psychological function. Examining phenomena and data from various perspectives, students are expected to be able to discover and organize problems by themselves, and to tackle their own research issues.
advice: We conduct seminars regularly throughout the year, and students report and discuss their own activities and deepen their own research. When reporting in the seminar, please prepare a resume or slide presentation (submit the electronic file of the resume or slides later). Spring semester: Reading prior research papers related to the research theme and discussing with class members, clarifying the overall picture of your research. Specifically, the research purpose, research positioning, and methods for empirical data collection are clarified and a research schedule is established. In addition, preliminary experiments/surveys will be conducted. The results will be reported at the interim presentation at the end of the semester. Fall Semester: Based on the results of preliminary experiments/surveys, modify the plan for the experiments /surveys as necessary, conduct the main experiments/surveys, analyze the results, and deepen the discussion. Students will write a research paper, and give an oral presentation at the end of the year.
books: Reference books and research articles are presented during the course.
requiredKnowledge: ・Prepare a notebook and make a habit of taking notes on the documents. It is not only useful for writing papers later, but it is also very useful for expanding and organizing ideas. ・Review the data collection and statistical analysis methods learned in previous classes. ・To conduct research effectively, familiarize yourself with the specifications of the equipment and teachers in the laboratory.

activityGoals.body: Ability to discuss various problems around us from a psychological point of view.
Ability to choose a research method for the research theme, and conduct experimental design.
Ability to conduct the experiment, and obtain the data to fulfill the purpose.
Ability to interpret the obtained data objectively and write a thesis.
Ability to notice your role in seminar activities, and act in cooperation with other class members.
Ability to draft an action agenda for your future career.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(渡邊伸行研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Watanabe Nobuyuki)
keywords: Cognitive Psychology 2.Communication 3.Face 4.Human Interface 5.Regional Collaboration
educationalGoal: The aim of the Design Project III is to be able to plan and develop products and systems that can be used safely and comfortably, and are enjoyable, and to be able to propose services that consider the psychological function of humans. The fundamental policy is to address one's own research theme by utilizing the knowledge on psychological function, and techniques of scientific measurement and evaluation.
advice: Lectures, practice exercises, and experiments are conducted when needed. Meetings are conveniently held and students report their own studies and engage in discussion. At the end of the former semester, a debriefing session of the department is held and all students must give an oral presentation on the progress of their own studies. At the end of the latter semester, the same debriefing session is held and all students must give an oral presentation on the consequences of their own studies. Students must participate in the meeting held every week, and perform their studies while engaging in the task for their research interests. Students need to not only do their own studies, but also have interest in and discuss the studies conducted by others. The research interests in our laboratory are human communication ( especially nonverbal behavior and its cognition), man-machine communication (human interface), creation and evaluation of regional culture contents that promote communication in different regions, and their peripheral domain. It is preferred that students choose their research theme based on their daily lives. To realize this, students need to make a habit of observing the events or products around their daily lives carefully and think about them. [This course is required for Certified Psychologists.]
books: Textbooks: None Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: This might be the only occasion in your life to experience considering a research theme, designing and conducting an experimental plan, analyzing the obtained data, and writing a thesis. What is required in this laboratory is to actively enjoy investigating or considering your research theme.

activityGoals.body: Ability to discuss various problems around us from a psychological point of view.
Ability to choose a research method on the research theme, and conduct experimental design.
Ability to conduct the experiment, and obtain the data to fulfill the purpose.
Ability to interpret the obtained data objectively and write a thesis.
Ability to notice your role in seminar activities, and cooperate with other class members.
Ability to create an action agenda for your future career.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(田中孝治研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Tanaka Koji)
keywords: Cognitive psychology 2.Cognitive science 3.Education engineering 4.Learning science 5.Knowledge science
educationalGoal: The aim is to be able to design and propose things and Kotozukuri that are conscious of the cognitive functions by fusing psychology and engineering. The basic policy is to make use of the knowledge of the mind works learned so far and the skills of scientific measurement and evaluation to tackle each theme. Students should always be aware of how human cognitive functions are organically linked to knowledge and behavior related to social life, and tackle your own research agenda.
advice: Seminars are held regularly throughout the year, and students will report on and discuss the status of each person's activities and research situation. At the end of the previous semester, a department presentation will be held to summarize the activities of the semester. At the end of the academic year, the results of the research will be compiled and presented. In order to demonstrate superior capabilities in a knowledge-based society, setting appropriate goals for truly unanswered problems and taking action based on beliefs appropriate to those goals and using available evidence (rational thinking) and self-direction to practice them autonomously are important. For maturity of rational thinking skills, we must generalize and learn from experiences of independent activities that deal with problems that are not truly answered. Research activities seem like questions that have no answer. Seminars are conducted as follows: through various proactive, research and laboratory activities, students learn from experience and set the goal of nurturing their ability to continue to grow after graduation. Also, human research hits more walls than you can imagine. For this reason, research activities require resilience (a tough mind). With the goal of fostering resilience, seminars are conducted so that not only successful experiences but also failed experiences can be accumulated. # This course is required for Certified Psychologists.
requiredKnowledge: It is important to be interested in learning support that is based on human cognitive and psychological characteristics and to have some motivation to elucidate these characteristics. Completing the “Educational and School Psychology” course is recommended, but it is not essential.

activityGoals.body: Ability to psychologically explain how the human mind works.
Ability to use a method to measure and evaluate according to the theme.
Ability to explain how to make things and Kotozukuri that are used in the mind.
Ability to practice project activities autonomously using your knowledge and skills.
Ability to practice learning activities that maintain your growth.
Ability to obtain personal principles for future career paths.

title: 建築大意
subtitle: Introduction to Architecture
keywords: Architectural planning 2.Design and history of architecture 3.Exterior space and landscape 4.Building production and profession 5.Building structures and equipment
educationalGoal: Students gain not only an overview of the architectural field but also the expanse of the construction industry. Then they come to understand the importance of planning various elements of architecture that influence the consciousness and actions of people. Furthermore, throughout discussion with construction professionals, students develop their interest in architecture, cultivate a questioning attitude to problems, and acquire an ability to plan for the future.
advice: This course explains not only the relationship between architectural planning and society but also the influence of architectural planning on town development and the landscape. Concretely, we presents students the goals of studying architecture by showing the superior instances of architecture and exterior spaces. Next, we expand the viewpoint of architectural planning to the fields of town development and landscapes. Furthermore, we show students various jobs related to architectural planning, and their awareness of architectural jobs and their morals grow. The subjects of this course are as follows: 1. Fields of architecture: first and eleventh lectures 2. Design and history of architecture and exterior space: second to fifth lectures 3. Areas covered by architectural planning: sixth to tenth lectures 4. Jobs related to architectural planning: twelfth to fifteenth lectures
requiredKnowledge: It is important that students not only learn from the textbook of this course but also read as many books and magazines on architecture as possible. Furthermore, it is more important that students observe architecture and urban space in their daily lives. This attitude is needed for the four years of learning in this college as well as in this course.

title: 日本建築史
subtitle: History of Japanese Architecture
keywords: History of Japanese architecture 2.Shrine architecture 3.Temple architecture 4.Residential building 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: Students learn the history of Japanese architecture from ancient to modern times and understand its architectural design and technical features, space composition, social background, and regionality. They learn about the role and characteristics of architecture and streets.
advice: Students learn about temple architecture, shrine architecture, and residential architecture from ancient to modern Japan. 1. History of residential buildings and cities, townscapes. 2. Ancient temples and shrines. 3. Medieval temples and shrines. 4. Early modern temples and shrines. 5. Modern temples and shrines.
requiredKnowledge: Students must have an interest in Japanese history, art history, archeology, folklore, etc., and try to understand Japanese architecture and architectural culture from a broad perspective.

activityGoals.body: Students understand the history of Japanese architecture and summarize key points.
Students can learn by themselves and write their own considerations.

title: 建築デザイン基礎
subtitle: Basic Representation of Architectural Design
keywords: Three-dimensional thinking and scale sense 2.Visual expression and communication 3.Spatiality;Material,Mechanics,Beauty 4.Humanity;Memory,Experience,Sensitivity 5.Relationship;History,Environment,Regional Cooperation
educationalGoal: In this course, students will learn the basic ideas and framework of activities for proposing architectural designs. To be specific, the purpose is to be able to consider about how to proceed architectural design work including structures and design elements by conceptualizing the 3-d composition of architectural design and expressing it with sketches, models, and CAD models. In addition, it will be basic literacy for "Architectural Design Studio I/II" in the second year.
advice: This lesson is composed of following contents. # 1st week; Orientation: Class outline explanation, assignment explanation # 2-6th week; theme 1 "Small space design inspired by basic solids" Students have to propose a new small space by edit a given basic solid by creating a model and a presentation board. # 7-9th week; theme 2 "Reading and communicating spatial design" Students have to create a presentation board that can convey the essence of a real architectural work to others. # 10-14th week; theme 3: "Spatial design inspired by site and context" Students have to propose a new small space based on observation and analysis of the site by creating a model and a presentation board. # 15th week; Review of outcomes and the entire class
requiredKnowledge: Architectural design consists of absorbent of various knowledge and experience, and integration of them into proposals of architecture and cityscapes. Students should actively collect information of the characteristic architecture, its background, the relationship between the space and people, and try to acquire the habit of connecting them to your own ideas. In addition, always check out expression samples such as sketches, models and words in architectural books and magazines and learn to use them yourself.

activityGoals.body: Students can gather information on characteristic architecture and understand their characteristics.
Students can organize their own thoughts and idea, and summarize them in sketches and words.
Students can create a model expressing their own idea and explain it easily to others.
Students can study their own design idea three-dimensionally using 3D CAD.
Students can create presentation board that can convey design concept and composition to others.

title: 建築構造力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Structural Mechanics for Architecture I
keywords: Structure 2.Beam, truss, and frame 3.Reaction force 4.Stress resultant 5.Stress
educationalGoal: Students learn the mechanical characteristics of statically determinate beams, trusses, and frames, which are basic models of building structures. They understand the balance of forces that work on buildings and learn how to find reaction forces. Students understand the concept of resultant stress and the balance of free bodies, and learn how to determine the distribution of resultant stress in beams and frames. They learn how to find the axial forces in trusses by solving the nodal balance.
advice: 1. Building structures and structural mechanics 2. Equilibrium of force 3. Structure modeling and reaction forces 4. Loads and external forces 5. Mechanical classification of structures 6. Stress and resultant stress 7. Reaction forces and resultant stresses in statically determinate structures 8. Sectional properties 9. Material properties 10. Stress and member design
requiredKnowledge: Students must understand trigonometric functions and elementary mechanics. A scientific calculator is required for testing. Students should review the application of vector operations in Linear Algebra.

activityGoals.body: Building structure and loads/external forces can correspond to the dynamic model.
Students can determine the reaction forces of static structures.
Students can draw diagrams of axial force, shear force, and bending moment of a statically determinate structure
Students can explain the basic cross-sectional and mechanical properties of materials.
Students can determine the stress in a beam.

title: 建築設備総論
subtitle: Introduction of Building Equipment
keywords: Air conditioner and ventilation design 2.Water supply and drainage sanitary installation 3.Building equipment 4.Air current analysis 5.Area cooperation
educationalGoal: It's learned about important air conditioning and building equipment in general of ventilating installation and water supply and drainage sanitary installation by building equipment and the ability which can be applied to an equipment design is learned through a problem and a practice. Air current analysis technology is learned by a practice as air streaming design technique for aerial environmental improvement.
advice: Building equipment in general is explained by the lecture focusing on air conditioning among the building equipment, ventilating installation and water supply and drainage sanitary installation and basic terminology and concept of building equipment in general are understood by a practice. A practice of a way of thinking with a basic equipment design is performed based on those. The damage case and the trial case which have formed by building equipment in general are considered by a lecture and a practice. An analysis of strong winds blowing through the tall buildings by air current analysis technology is performed and a basic skill of analysis technology is learned to know more construction and aerial relation. Architecture and building equipment. Knowledge of an air conditioner and design concept. Knowledge and design concept of water supply and drainage sanitary installation. Site electrical facilities and firefighting equipment. Disaster preventing. Way of thinking of ventilation design and ventilation design. title: 建築構法計画
subtitle: Building System Design
keywords: Structural systems 2.Building elements 3.Design of building elements 4.Building element performance 5.Building production system
educationalGoal: In this course, students develop the knowledge required for planning, constructing, and maintaining buildings while comprehensively considering building materials, structural systems, and equipment. Specifically, they acquire the basic knowledge of building systems to standardize or componentize buildings, and learn new about designs in the environmental age.
advice: This course explains the typical of structural systems and building elements from the viewpoints of required performance and construction work, and shows examples of superior building element design. In the first half of this course, structural systems are explained, outlining all the materials used and the points that need supervision in each type of construction work. In the latter half, finishing layers and substrates are explained with respect to each building element. The contents of this course are as follows. 1. Structural systems: steel construction, reinforced concrete construction, and wooden construction. 2. Building elements: roofs, walls, openings, floors, stairs, and ceilings. 3. Building system design methods: prefabrication, modular coordination, and componentization.
requiredKnowledge: Students don't need any special background, because this course is a first step in learning building production. Students are urged to deepen their understanding of structural systems and building elements by observing many buildings in their daily lives.

activityGoals.body: Students can explain the basics of building materials and building systems.
Students can explain the constituent elements and required performance of basic structural systems that support.
Students can explain the constituent elements and required performance of basic building elements that partition
Students can explain the merits of prefabrication, componentization, and industrialization of buildings.

Based on their understanding of the constituent elements and required performance of basic structural systems as well as basic building elements, students can explain the important points that need supervision in construction work and in building maintenance. lessons.assignments: Review lecture notes to develop understanding.

lessons.assignments: Review lecture notes to develop understanding.

lessons.assignments: Review lecture notes to develop understanding.

lessons.content: Structure systems (4) design of reinforced concrete structure Students learn the important points of designing and supervising reinforced concrete constructions throughout instances of the frame construction and the wall construction.
lessons.assignments: Review lecture notes to develop understanding.

lessons.content: Structure systems (5) materials for wooden structure Students learn the type, standard and jointing of wooden members.
lessons.assignments: Review lecture notes to develop understanding.

lessons.content: Structure systems (6) design of wooden structure Students learn the important points of designing and supervising wooden constructions throughout instances of the Japanese conventional construction and the so-called 2x4 construction. ●Small test and review covering from the fourth lecture to the seventh
lessons.assignments: Review lecture notes to develop understanding.

lessons.content: Structure systems (6) ground leveling and foundations Students learn not only the type of piles and foundations but also the important points of supervising the construction of those.
lessons.assignments: Review lecture notes to develop understanding.

lessons.content: Building elements (1) roofs Students learn not only the waterproofing of pitched roofs and flat roofs but also the superior roof designs.
lessons.assignments: Review lecture notes to develop understanding.

lessons.content: Building elements (2) walls #1 Students learn not only the layers of walls installed into detached houses but also the superior wall designs of those. ●Small test and review covering from the eighth lecture to the ninth
lessons.assignments: Review lecture notes to develop understanding.

lessons.content: Building elements (3) walls #2 Students learn not only the layers of walls installed into office buildings but also the superior wall designs of those.
lessons.assignments: Review lecture notes to develop understanding.

lessons.content: Building elements (4) openings Students learn not only the way of opening and shutting of windows and doors but also the superior designs of the openings.
lessons.assignments: Review lecture notes to develop understanding.

lessons.content: Building elements (5) floors and stairs Students learn the layers of floors, the details of stairs, and the superior designs of stairs. ●Small test and review covering from the tenth lecture to the twelfth
lessons.assignments: Review lecture notes to develop understanding.

lessons.content: Building elements (5) ceilings Students learn not only the structure of ceilings but also the superior designs of ceilings.
lessons.assignments: Review lecture notes to develop understanding.

lessons.content: Methods of building system design Students learn the merits of prefabrication and modular coordination of buildings. ●Small test and review covering from the thirteenth lecture to the fifteenth
lessons.assignments: Review lecture notes to develop understanding.

educationalGoal: In architectural design, it is important to visualize ideas with 3D models and drawings using digital media and to communicate smoothly with others using the data. educationalGoal: Learn basic knowledge about building structures and materials, and develop the ability to show structural plans to plan and design mechanically rational building spaces.
advice: Learn the basics of structural planning to be safe from loads and external forces, and to select structural types, shapes, materials, and member arrangements from the mechanical standpoint that are suitable for the intended use of the building.
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of Introduction of the structure (1st phase) and Structural Mechanics for Architecture Ⅰ (2nd term) and Ⅱ (3rd term) is required.

activityGoals.body: Explain the basic characteristics of structural materials and the features of structural systems.
Explain keywords important in structural planning.
The collapse load using the virtual work method can be calculated.
Explain the characteristics of loads and external forces and damage to buildings due to natural disasters.
Able to present seismic diagnosis and reinforcement of small houses.

title: 建築設備学
subtitle: Building Equipment
keywords: Solar radiation 2.Thermal environment 3.Heating and cooling load 4.Air conditioning system 5.Heat source equipment
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn about human thermal sensation and comfortable ranges of temperature and humidity. (2) learn how to calculate the heating and cooling loads of buildings. (3) learn about various kind of air conditioning systems. (4) learn about heat source equipment such as boilers, refrigerators, and heat pumps.
advice: In this course, after recognizing the quantitative size of the transmission heat loads of buildings through exercises, students learn about the calculation methods for various heat loads, such as direct gains from solar radiation, ventilation, lighting, human bodies, and indoor heat generated by machine and instruments. Next, students learn about air conditioning equipment and the kinds of systems that correspond to different heating and cooling loads. Students will also come to understand the features of the various compositions of heat source equipment used to control energy consumption and carbon dioxide emissions. 1. Passive architectural design 2. Human thermal sensation and indexes 3. Calculation of heating and cooling loads 4. Use of psychrometric charts 5. Air conditioning equipment and systems 6. Heat source equipment and composition 7. Climate of location and building thermal performance 8. Net-zero energy buildings 9. Plumbing system
requiredKnowledge: Students should have taken Introduction to Building Equipment, Architectural Environment I.

activityGoals.body: Students can calculate the heating and cooling loads of buildings.
Students can explain the meaning of terms related to air conditioning equipment, etc.
Students can explain the differences in the kinds of air conditioning and heat source systems.
Students can solve the problems that appear on the Japanese registered architect examination.
Students can give an overview of the Building Energy Efficiency Act.
Students can explain the feature of eco-buildings.

educationalGoal: By learning the concepts and techniques of architectural design and regional planning, using the actual building and cityscape as learning materials, advanced specialization in architectural design, planning and design, architectural structure, construction methods, urban planning and urban design Acquire knowledge. advice: Students will select modern buildings and cities, traditional buildings and cityscapes in Hokuriku, and conduct literature surveys and field surveys. subtitle: Architectural Safety Engineering
keywords: matrix method 2.plastic analysis 3.seismic design 4.vibration theory 5.foundation structure
educationalGoal: Apply the knowledge of building structural mechanics and general building structure to learn basic knowledge of structural design in the following;(1) Matrix method for calculating the stress of a rigid frame, (2) Plastic analysis for calculating the strength of buildings, (3) Vibration theory that treats external disturbances such as earthquakes and winds as dynamic external forces, (4) Seismic isolation and basics of seismic control, (5) Foundation structure.
advice: This course focuses on practical work and applies the knowledge of basic structural fields learned; (1) Stress analysis premised on calculation by computer (matrix method) (2) Plastic analysis that is the basis for constructing a mechanism to safely plasticize a building under an excessive external force (3) History of seismic design and vibration theory as the basis of dynamic design (4) Basics of the foundation structure that safely supports buildings

title: 建築法規
subtitle: Laws and Regulations of Architecture
keywords: The role of the Building Standards Law and the composition 2.Safety of a building (element regulation) 3.The harmony with the area (restrictions for grouping) 4.Architect's obligation 5.Construction related decree
educationalGoal: When a building is made in our country, Building Standards Law is set as the standard of the floor to plan for securement of public welfare while respecting the fundamental human rights set as the Constitution of Japan. The standard which should be considered is set as the environment of the city and the area about an achieved thing, location of the building and the scale, etc. while securing the sanitary society and structure safety about beauty and the function asked from architectural space.
advice: It's explained about a building code decree and it's made only a point about architects law and a builder law and so on related decree mainly. Tuition uses a chart and an illustration much and makes an effort toward simple explanation while advancing it by a text "teaching materials for building law" and referring to statute at large. Further, the knowledge is trained by trying the exercise by which it's for an architect examination question. The item of the syllabus planning is as follows. 1.The role of the building law, 2. The construction of the construction decree and definition of terminology, 3. Calculation method of the area and the height,4. The general structure and lighting 5. Ventilation and sound insulation, 6. Wooden pillar and wall framing,7. The structural strength and structure calculation, 8.Fire resistive building and quasi-fire-proof building, 9.Restriction on interior finish, 10. Refuge facilities and smoke eliminating equipment, 11. Land use regulation of a building by use zones, 12. Relation between a road and a site building, 13. The building coverage and rate of building volume, 14. Restriction of the height, 15. Sun shadow regulation, 16. Fire-proof district and quasi-fire-preventive district, 17. District plans, 18. Procedure about construction, 19. Registered Architect Law, 20. The city planning law
requiredKnowledge: Registered Architect Law was revised in March, 2020. Without also passing through business experience about registered architect of the first class as well as the second-class architect test for which you could take an examination immediately after graduation, this change could take an examination now. A pass also tries a first class registered architect examination question simultaneously with that, and aims at the possible ability in a registered architect of the first class legal test.

title: 建築デザイン総合演習A
subtitle: Architectural Integrated Exercises for Design A
keywords: Functional planning (program) 2.Architectural design 3.Urban design 4.Regional cooperation 5.Presentation
educationalGoal: This course is an exercise course that comprehensively utilizes the basic knowledge of architecture that has been acquired so far. Students will practice safe, beautiful and comfortable architecture and urban space through exercises. Understand the relationship with architectural conditions by developing architectural design II and working on facility design and urban design with more complex contents. Conditions include program, plan, structure, environment, city, etc.
advice: This subject is a design practice subject that develops the contents of architectural design I and II. The class management includes lectures on architectural planning, architectural planning, structure, environment, and urban space in accordance with each design issue, and esquisses on design proposals. title: 建築デザイン総合演習B
subtitle: Architectural Integrated Exercises for Design B
keywords: Architectural design 2.Spatial Composition 3.Functional planning (program) 4.Inner-outer space 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: This class is the final stage of the architectural design exercise. Understand the function and composition of large public buildings or complex urban spaces, and plan and design them. In particular, at the stage just before Project Design Ⅲ, the goal is to develop a variety of conditions and functions, and to develop creative abilities that can be integrated as plans and design proposals.
advice: Assignment is design and planning of buildings and cities with special surrounding environment and complicated required functions. The design issues are roughly divided into three issues (see below). However, in addition to general design drawings, students propose appropriate and attractive expressions using drawings and sentences showing concepts, model photographs, CG, etc. 1) A large-scale building that satisfies the various functions of facilities, such as elementary school buildings and multicultural buildings in central Kanazawa, and that requires attractive architectural spaces. (two assignments). 2) Planning issues for integrated urban design of buildings and external spaces by decoding and re-editing the contexts of cities and towns (two assignments). 3) Renovation of buildings with changing the use of existing public buildings (two assignments). If students choose 1) out of the above 3 tasks, they will divide a course to learn practical design and a course to learn conceptual design. If students select 2), the course will be a city / landscape study. If students select 3), the course will be to learn sustainable architectural design. * The first and second assignments can be freely selected in any course (four) to create works. However, only one course can be selected in each assignment.
requiredKnowledge: This course is based on basic knowledge of architecture in general and the design ability of architectural design I and II, Architectural Integrated Exercises for Design A. Students try to apply the knowledge related to the planning and design of architecture and exterior space learned in various classes to the design work.

activityGoals.body: Students can analyze the characteristics of the urban area, traditional space, natural environment of location.
Students can develop their ability to organize and design various spaces as architecture and urban space.
Students can analyze the characteristics of the local culture and community and reflect them in urban design.
Students can understand and propose about conversion of existing architecture by renovation project.
Students can create and express drawings, models, photographs, and texts as works, and presentate beautifully.

keywords: Air, heat and luminous environment 2.Sound, landscape and psychological environment 3.Environment design and region cooperation 4.Structural planning and design 5.RC structure and steel structure
educationalGoal: Integrated exercises in the structural and environmental fields of architecture are conducted. Students will understand the physical phenomena related to architecture through experiments and exercises as well as specialized environmental measurement techniques and structural design methods. They will acquire the ability to apply such knowledge and techniques in practice. Furthermore, through the process of doing the experiments and exercises, students will be able to discover various problems encountered in actual design.

This exercise will include lectures on conformity to building-related regulations and correct drafting methods. -RC + S structure design Students perform structural design of the above-mentioned buildings designed by students. * Please note that many points are deducted for absences.
books: None Necessary handouts will be distributed by each teacher.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(蜂谷俊雄研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Hachiya Toshio)
keywords: Architectural design 2.Landscape design 3.Design trends 4.Design concept 5.Location and regional cooperation
educationalGoal: (1) Students will see and analyze world famous buildings and read books describing architectural design. In addition, they will consider what good architecture is. (2) Students can analyze the social situation and place surrounding a building, solve its complex conditions, and create a building form and space that satisfies the facility’s program and functionality. (3) Students can explain their efforts in excellent presentations and logically explain the design concept of the work.
advice: Course Description (1) Students will work on planning and design issues for site selection and facility program creation, as well as architectural design issues to be compiled as works. (2) Students will read designated architectural design books, summarize their points, and publish the summaries. (3) During the summer vacation, students will go on a tour to see a city and its architecture. They will investigate and analyze the city and its architecture and summarize the results in a report. (4) If there is a project related to the city or architecture, students will participate in a project activity. (5) Students will express the results of the year with drawings and models, present them in a public place, and receive a review. Expectations for students (1) Students should be interested in architectural design and regional planning, always striving to improve. (2) Students should admire beautiful architecture and their favorite spaces and consider the reasons. (3) Students should analyze works of famous architecture and analyze how they differ from the works they designed. (4) Students should keep thinking about what good architecture is and what design can last through history. (5) Students should actively apply for student architectural design competitions.
books: Textbooks:Not specified. Reference books:Not specified. Reserved books:Not specified.
requiredKnowledge: (1) It is desirable to have mastered "Architectural Integrated Exercises A and B" and further subjects such as "History of Japanese Architecture", " History of Occidental Architecture ", "Methods of Architectural Design", "Theory of Architectural Design". (2) Architectural design is the synthesis of various types of knowledge and technologies, and it is important to learn in a balanced way about other specialized fields such as history, cities, structures, production, and the environment.

Students can comprehensively consider architectural design, and apply it to their own works.
Students can analyze various architectural issues, and present suggestions for improvement through their works.
Students can draw completed images of their work with computer graphics and explain it logically.
Students understand social trends in the field of architecture, and determine their own direction.

(2) Students can analyze the social situation and place surrounding a building, solve its complex conditions, and create a building form and space that satisfies the facility’s program and functionality. (3) During the summer vacation, students will go on a tour to see a city and its architecture. They will investigate and analyze the city and its architecture and summarize the results in a report. (4) If there is a project related to the city or architecture, students will participate in a project activity. (5) Students will express the results of the year with drawings and models, present them in a public place, and receive a review. (2) Students should admire beautiful architecture and their favorite spaces and consider the reasons. (3) Students should analyze works of famous architecture and analyze how they differ from the works they designed. (4) Students should keep thinking about what good architecture is and what design can last through history. (5) Students should actively apply for student architectural design competitions.

subtitle: Design Project III (Takeuchi Shinichi)
keywords: Architectural design 2.Urban and landscape design 3.Integration with structure and environment 4.History reference 5.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: Seeing and analyzing architecture or reading books by architects and researchers, to learn and evaluate what is architecture. requiredKnowledge: It is desirable to have completed Architectural Design Studio I, II, and Architectural Integrated Exercises for Design A, B and to have further studied subjects such as Method of Architectural Design, Theory of Architectural Space, and Architectural Information Design. Select the site of the work and assemble the facility program which is a prerequisite for the design.
Analyzes various problems in modern society and presents improvement plans through works.
Present the completed image of own work with graphics, models, etc., and explain it logically.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(菅野圭祐研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Sugano Keisuke)
keywords: Urban Design 2.Machizukuri 3.Action Research
educationalGoal: The purpose of learning and education is to take various actions to change the region, through being involved in the local life to be studied, organize the responses obtained using qualitative analysis, and cultivate the ability to link to concrete architectural and urban designs. This series of research processes is logically planned, designed, and executed, and the results are compiled into a research paper or design work.
advice: Project Design Ⅲ emphasizes developing students' own knowledge and abilities to plan and execute projects through their own independent actions. For this reason, they will generally work on the following activities, assuming their own interests in cities, regions, and society. 1) Clarification of concerns about cities / regions and society (information collecting and discussion) 2) Systematic understanding of the factors surrounding the problem (information collecting and problem structuring) [Review of existing studies, review of literature / Field survey (case studies of related cases, excellent cases, etc.)] 3) Setting project theme [Theme setting / target area setting / planning of project execution (setting of analysis method)] 4) Project implementation and coordination [Case study and analysis / Visualization and structuring of analysis results, (if necessary) designing / result presentation (mid review committee (December), public presentation review committee)]
requiredKnowledge: ・ Being interested in daily phenomena related to urban space, society and landscape. ・ Visiting to various cities and regions. ・ Having a willingness to go deeper and explore their interests, or continue their efforts.

activityGoals.body: Collecting information in accordance with their own interests and explain the positioning of the problem.
Appropriate research methods can be set and executed according to the purpose of the project theme.
Research and analysis results can be expressed in appropriate way.
A series of processes from problem setting to survey analysis and their results can be logically expressed.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(垂水弘夫研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Tarumi Hiroo)
keywords: Thermal environment 2.Green building 3.Energy conservation 4.Air conditioning system 5.Natural power sources
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn about human thermal environments. (2) learn about energy conservation and green buildings. (3) learn about radiation cooling/heating systems for zero-energy buildings. (4) learn about natural power sources in buildings’ surroundings.
advice: Buildings and residences have entered a time when energy conservation is called for. As well as securing the health and comfort of users or residents, buildings and residences are beginning to make energy themselves, and there is a need to realize net-zero energy conditions. In Project Design III at the Tarumi laboratory, students will be doing research on the use of natural energy power. There are various kinds of natural power sources in buildings’ surroundings, such as sunshine, rain, wind, clouds, green, the ground, and water. The planned subjects of research are as follows: 1. Experimental studies on the ceiling radiation of cooling/heating systems using groundwater. 2. Monitoring of the thermal effect of a heating/cooling trench. 3. Research on the thermal effect of a system that indirectly uses subterranean heat by installing a ventilation duct in a heating/cooling trench. 4. Research using numerical analysis methods to estimate the thermal effect of a heating/cooling trench through subterranean heat transfer. 5. Research on the effect of groundwater application on the summer thermal environment on agricultural greenhouses. 6. Monitoring of subterranean thermal effects in an earth tube residence. 7. Study on net-zero energy buildings and campuses.
requiredKnowledge: Students must have acquired credits for Building Equipment and Environmental Design for Architecture I.

activityGoals.body: Students can review previous research relevant to a project theme.
Students can conceive an experiment, survey, and analysis necessary to move the research forward.
Students can correctly explain actual conditions and phenomena related to the environment & energy consumption.
Students can create and display suitable charts to aid in explanations to third parties.
Students can create an appropriate project report.

title: 進路セミナーⅠ
subtitle: Career Planning Seminar I
keywords: Occupation and life 2.Goal setting 3.Excavation 4.Self-enlightenment
educationalGoal: In addition to measuring the future career and forming a professional view as an engineer, students will set goals and envision advancement/employment plans suitable for themselves, and recognize the voluntary and ambitious actions needed to prepare to achieve those goals.
advice: The course addresses the following two main issues: 1. Investigating occupational awareness through lectures by career teachers and senior students, and through internships, open desks, etc., in students' search for the ideal career path. 2. Planning and beginning to address issues that require a relatively long period of preparation and proactive behavior, such as acquiring qualifications, developing general common sense, and successfully completing the comprehensive aptitude test (SPI).
requiredKnowledge: Career seminars are lectures mainly for job hunting, and are held to prepare students for the employment front. In order to prepare for job hunting and job examinations, all students need to take this course regardless of their advancement or employment. In addition, this learning will be reference material for employment placement in the following year.

subtitle: Physical Chemistry
keywords: Amount of substance 2.Structure of atoms 3.Electron configuration 4.Periodic law 5.Molecular bond
educationalGoal: Three general objectives will be addressed in this course: -Fundamental understandings of the structure of substances. -Ability to solve problems using knowledge gained above-mentioned. -Ability to apply the method of inquiry used by chemists to solve chemical problems
advice: There will be three one-hour examinations during the term and a regularly scheduled final examination. The exercise sheets will be also distributed in the class. All the exams will be closed-notes and closed-book, although the key equations will be provided on the exam sheets. Tutorial classes will be held regularly in the library.
books: Peter Atkins, Elements of Physical Chemistry 7th Edition, Oxford University Press
requiredKnowledge: 1. Fundamentals of physics and mathematics 2. Fundamentals of high-school level chemistry

Understandings of the three phases of matter.

lessons.assignments: Read the relevant part of the textbook beforehand and prepare to be able to answer the exercise problems.

title: 無機化学
subtitle: Inorganic Chemistry
keywords: Electron configuration 2.Atomic orbitals 3.Chemical bonds 4.Crystal structures 5.Acids and bases
educationalGoal: Students will learn the basics of inorganic chemistry, such as atomic structure (electron configuration, atomic orbitals), chemical bonding, and crystal structures, and the technical terms used in inorganic chemistry. In addition, students will learn about chemical properties that can be explained theoretically by examining the electronic structure. Concepts and theories acquired in this course are the minimum necessary for understanding the properties and reactivity of inorganic compounds.
advice: Students will learn essential concepts in modern inorganic chemistry, with the goal of gaining an understanding of the structure and properties of a variety of inorganic compounds without the need for a teacher. 1. Structure of atoms: electron configuration and atomic orbitals, the periodic table and element blocks 2. Chemical bonding and structures: covalent bonding and Lewis structures, ionic bonds, metal bonds, van der Waals bonds, hydrogen bonds; atomic radius and ion radius, lanthanide contraction, Born-Harber cycle, Mardelung constant, metal crystals; ionic crystals (rock salts, cesium chloride types, zinc blende type); ionization energy, electron affinity, electronegativity 3. Reactions: definitions of acid and base (Arrhenius, Brsted-Lowry, Lewis), HSAB
requiredKnowledge: Pay attention to units as you solve calculation problems. Bring a scientific calculator.

activityGoals.body: Describe electron configurations and atomic orbitals for each element on the periodic table.
Explain trends in ionic radius and electronegativity from the periodic table.
Calculate lattice energy using the Born-Harber cycle.
Describe representative crystal structures and their relation to the ionic radius ratio.
Explain the principles of X-ray diffraction and calculate d from θ and reflection index.
Define the different types of acids and bases, including Arrhenius, Bronsted, and Lewis types.

title: 分析化学
subtitle: Analytical Chemistry
keywords: Acid-base titration 2.Gravimetric analysis 3.Chelatometric titration 4.Redox titration
educationalGoal: After completing this course, you will be able to : 1. Perform calculations for molar mass and molarity using titration data. 2. Perform calculations involving molar solubility and solubility product constant. 3. Describe complexation titrations using the Lewis concept of acids and bases. 4. Systematically balance oxidation-reduction reactions
advice: Analytical Chemistry is a foundation course for School of Applied Chemistry, also highly related to Laboratory course on sophomore and junior, and also senior capstone-course (Project Design III). The course is designed to help build a foundation of Analytical Chemistry, Acid-Base titration, Chelatometric titration, and Redox Titration. Through the course, the foundations of this titration method will be described from the view of gravimetric analysis. At the end of the course, you can solve single answer problems using these foundations.

title: 化学反応論
subtitle: Chemistry of Phase and Reaction
keywords: State of Matter 2.Pure Substances and Mixture 3.State Change and Energy 4.Chemical Kinetics 5.Chemical Equilibrium
educationalGoal: After completing this course, you will be able to: 1. Explain the foundations of phase diagrams. 2. Explain the theories of chemical kinetics. 3. Perform calculations using chemical kinetics with the thermodynamic concepts. 4. Recognize the value of chemical kinetics in our daily life
advice: Chemistry of Phase and Reactions is a foundation course for School of Applied Chemistry, also highly related to Laboratory course on sophomore and junior. The course is designed to help build a foundation of Chemical Kinetics, Chemical equilibrium, and Phase diagram. Through the course, these foundations will be described from the view of thermodynamics (e.g. the concept of enthalpy, entropy, and Gibb's free energy). At the end of the course, you can solve single answer problems using these foundations.
books: Textbooks: Peter Atkins and Julio de Paula (2015), Atkins' Physical Chemistry 6th Ed. (In Japanese) Reference Books: Haruaki Tazaki (2000), Thermodynamics (In Japanese) Reserved Books in the Library: not applicable
requiredKnowledge: General knowledge of inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry, physics, and math are required. B008-01 "Chemical Thermodynamics" with a grade of C or better.

activityGoals.body: You will be able to describe three states of matter and phase shift.
You will be able to explain the foundations of phase diagrams.
You will be able to describe the reaction rate in terms of the Arrhenius equation.
You will be able to determine the effect of temperature on rates using the collision model.
You will be able to Perform calculations using chemical kinetics with the thermodynamic concepts.

Effect of dissolution of substances on water quality.

title: 電気化学
subtitle: Electrochemistry
keywords: Electrochemistry 2.Energy and equilibrium 3.Electrolysis 4.Batteries 5.Standard electrode potential
educationalGoal: Electrochemistry deals with chemical phenomena involving electron exchange. Applications are numerous and include batteries, chemical synthesis by electrolysis, chemical sensors, surface treatment, and metal plating. An understanding of the field requires knowledge of standard electrode potential, the Nernst equation, and other information. Students will learn basic concepts, formulas, and applications such as batteries, chemical synthesis by electrolysis, and metal plating.
advice: 1. Basic concept of electrochemical systems (such as how electrolysis proceeds and electrode interface description) 2. Energy and equilibrium (such as standard Gibbs free energy of formation and chemical potential) 3. Standard electrode potential and the Nernst equation 4. Electrolysis current (relation between potential and current and the dynamics of electrode interface) 5. State-of-the-art electrochemistry (electrochemical STM, solid electrolytes, secondary batteries, fuel cells, solar cells)
requiredKnowledge: A knowledge of units is required to solve calculation problems. Bring a scientific calculator.

activityGoals.body: Explain electrolysis in a simple electrochemical system, such as a water and electrolyte solution.
Determine correctly whether a reaction proceeds spontaneously from the changes in Gibbs free energy.
Calculate standard electrode potential and electromotive force using thermodynamic data and the Nernst equation.
Explain energy conversion between chemical energy and electrical energy.

educationalGoal: You will learn absorption spectrophotometry for the determination of ions and substances, IR and NMR for structural analysis of organic compounds, X-ray analysis methods, and thermal analysis methods. You will learn the basic principles of each analytical method and the information provided by each method.

title: アドバンスト環境化学

keywords: Securing of aquatic resources 2.Water clean-up systems 3.Water clean-up materials 4.Methods and apparatus for analyzing water quality 5.Aquatic environment preservation
educationalGoal: You will learn about modern environmental problems based on the chemical knowledge acquired previously in the lectures. The goal of this course is to acquire the ability to understand local environmental problems and work toward solutions by examining methods for securing of aquatic resources, water purification materials, quality of water analyses, and others. You will have a basic understanding of these specialized subjects in environmental chemistry.
advice: 1. Understand how to securing aquatic resources and maintain water quality of the water supply and sewer system. 2. Understand water clean-up systems based on materials chemistry, analytical chemistry, and environmental chemistry. 3. Understand water clean-up materials using inorganic materials, such as zeolites and organic-inorganic hybrid materials. 4. Can use methods and apparatus to analyze water quality and secure water resources. 5. Understand water quality conservation methods and techniques for determining water quality. 6. Understand the utilization of carbon resources and the carbon cycle.
requiredKnowledge: A knowledge of chemistry and biology gained from high school courses is needed to understand the lectures.

title: 地球環境学
subtitle: Environmental Science of Earth
keywords: Biogeochemical cycle 2.Chemical composiiton of the earth's crust 3.Basic chemical equilibria 4.Environmental issues
educationalGoal: The earth can be divided into the atmosphere, the lithosphere, and the hydrosphere, but elements such as carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus circulate among all of these spheres. This course will cover the behavior of substances in the global environment and the chemical reactions related to the behavior of the substances. The goal of this course is to raise awareness of the factors affecting the global environment.
advice: 1. Chemical composition of the earth's crust. 2. The evolution of the earth and changes in the atmosphere. 3. Basics of analytical chemistry. 4. Basics of aquatic environment. 5. Chemical equilibria in environmental water. 6. Environmental problems.
books: (Textbook) An Introduction to Environmental Chemistry, Julian E. Andrews, et al., Wiley-Blackwell, ISBN: 9780632059058
requiredKnowledge: A knowledge of high school level chemistry and biology is required to understand the lectures.

activityGoals.body: Understand the origins of the earth and changes in the global environment.
Understand atmospheric changes of the earth from the beginning to the present.
Describe the greenhouse effect caused by carbon dioxide..
Understand major chemical equilibria in environmental water.
Understand the mecanisms of seasonal variations in the water quality of lakes.
Understand global environmental problems.

title: 環境計測学
subtitle: Environmental Analysis
keywords: Global environment 2.Environmental analyses 3.Environmental issues 4.Water quality measurements
educationalGoal: To fully understand environmental issues, such as pollution, that have multiple effects on the global environment, you will learn about the natural environment (air, water, soil) and the circulation of matter in the environment. In addition, you will be able to explain the role of environmental analysis in environmental issues and understand the principles of environmental measurement technology.
advice: To understand environmental issues, such as pollution, that significantly affect the global environment, an understanding of the natural environment (air, water, soil) and the circulation of substances through it are necessary. In this course, you will learn about the natural environment, material circulation, and environmental issues. You will also learn the principles and application of measurement methods used for environmental analyses, especially water quality measurements.
books: Textbooks: Chikyu no Kagaku to Kankyou (Sankyo Shuppan Publishing) Reference books: Kankyo Kagaku (Shokabou Publishing), Mizu no Bunseki (Kagaku Dojin Publishing), Kankyo Kagaku Gairon (Maruzen Publishing) Reserved books: Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of analytical chemistry is necessary. In addition, knowledge of instrumental analytical chemistry is helpful to understand the principles and applications of environmental analysis methods. Bring a scientific calculator to class.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain material circulation in the natural environment (air, water, soil).
Be able to explain the significance of environmental analysis in relation to environmental issues.
Be able to describe water analysis methods.
Be able to understand the principles and characteristics of dating methods.

lessons.content: Analysis of water (3): Electrochemical analysis
lessons.assignments: Preview: Understand redox potential. Review: The principles and characteristics of electrochemical analysis.

lessons.content: Analysis of water (4): Chromatography
lessons.assignments: Preview: Study chromatography. Review: Various chromatographic methods.

lessons.content: Dating method (1): Radionuclides and decay
lessons.assignments: Preview: Understand the content in chapters 9 to 11. Review: Radionuclides and their decay.

lessons.content: Dating method (2): Dating methods using disintegration of primary natural radionuclides and 14C.
lessons.assignments: Preview: Understand primary natural radionuclides. Review: The carbon-14 dating method.

title: 無機・エネルギー機能化学
subtitle: Functional Chemistry of Inorganic and Energetic Materials
keywords: Glass and ceramics 2.Metals and semiconductors 3.Magnetic materials 4.Optoelectronic and dielectric materials 5.Power electronic materials
educationalGoal: Students will learn: (1) the classification of inorganic materials (ceramics, glasses, and metals). (2) the properties and applications of inorganic materials in the fields of electronics, magnetics, and optics. (3) about crystallography and the electronic structure of inorganic solids. (4) about advanced functional materials and their practical applications.
advice: This is an introductory course for materials science. The course will cover: 1. Substances and materials 2. Functions of inorganic materials 3. Crystal structures of solids 4. Electronic structures of solids 5. Preparation of functional materials 6. Optical and photonic properties of inorganic materials 7. Properties and production processes of glass 8. Dielectric materials, magnetic materials, and ion conducting oxides Students must a scientific calculator or personal computer to every class. Students should check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class.
books: Textbooks: not specified Reference books:"Nyu-mon Mukizairyou", Jiro Shiokawa, Kagaku Doujin (1997). ("Introduction to Inorganic Materials") Reserved books: not specified
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of inorganic chemistry, physical chemistry, and structural chemistry. Refer to the basic concepts in textbooks such as Elements of Physical Chemistry by Atkins and Paula and to the procedure for powder X-ray crystallography in Major Experimental Course B.

activityGoals.body: Be able to describe the crystal structure of typical inorganic materials
Be able to explain the electronic states of metals, semiconductors, and insulators and their electric properties
Be able to explain the functions of inorganic materials
Be able to explain the application of inorganic materials in the energy industry
Be able to describe methods for the production of inorganic materials

title: バイオ・化学基礎実験・演習A(応用化学)(再履修クラス)
subtitle: Basic Experiments and Practice in Bioscience and Chemistry A (Applied Chemistry)
keywords: Analytical chemistry experiments 2.Organic chemistry experiments 3.Environmental chemistry experiments
educationalGoal: Learn the correct clothing/protective equipment suitable for experiments, use experimental tools correctly, and conduct experiments safely. Learn the specific information for the experiments and conduct experiments on your own. Prepare a report describing the experimental method and results and submit it by the deadline. Acquire the ability to conduct experiments by verifying and reporting on material learned in courses and through experiments.
advice: Conduct experiments in analytical chemistry, organic chemistry, and environmental chemistry. The objective of this experimental course is to acquire more knowledge than that learned in lectures and to gain skills in research, experimental methods, and reporting that are necessary to perform activities in Design Project III (4th year). If understanding experiments is difficult, you need to actively gain the understanding through reading, asking questions, and attending office hours, along with sufficient preparation and review of the experimental method and principles. Be sure to attend the guidance given for each experiment to learn about precautions, handling of experimental apparatus, safety training, and other important information. Common to all experiments: Experimental guidance, safety training, examination Analytical chemistry experiments: Volumetric analysis, acid-base titration, pH measurement, and ionization equilibrium Organic Chemistry experiments: Fundamentals of distillation, nucleophilic substitution, esterification, and preparation of polymers Environmental chemistry experiments: Paper chromatography, qualitative analysis of metal ions
books: Textbooks: Baio Kagaku Kiso Jikken/enshu AB (Kanazawa Institute of Technology Publishing) Reference books: Kenkyu no tameno Anzen Shishin (Kanazawa Institute of Technology Publishing) Reserved books: Jikken Deta wo Tadashiku Atsukau tameni (Kagaku Dojin Publishing), Jikken wo Anzen ni Okonau tameni (Kagaku Dojin Publishing), Zoku Jikken wo Anzen ni Okonau tameni (Kagaku Dojin Publishing)
requiredKnowledge: Bring an A4 size experimental notebook, scientific calculator, and ruler. Experiments should be conducted after reviewing the course material, understanding the experimental theory, and preparing the materials for the experiments. If the progress of the experiment is delayed, class time will be extended until the experiment is completed, so keep some time free after the class on experiment days.

activityGoals.body: Wear appropriate clothing, understand the use of the equipment, handle reagents properly, and conduct safely.
Record experimental conditions and results accurately in the experimental notes.
Complete the experimental report using the prescribed format and explain it to others.
Describe observed phenomena and obtained data in experiments, based on principles of physics and chemistry.
Conduct the experiments on your own, according to the instructions.
Understand the fundamental principles of analytical chemistry, organic chemistry, and environmental chemistry.

title: 人体の構造と機能
subtitle: Structure and Function in Physiology
keywords: Cell 2.Tissue and organ 3.Metabolism 4.Structure and function 5.Evolution
educationalGoal: Human Structure and Function majors can explain how the human body works, based on a deep understanding of the relationship between physiology and anatomy. This is the first course designed to provide foundational knowledge of the human body deemed necessary for discipline-specific courses in neuroscience and brain science. This course introduces not only the proximal factors, but also the ultimate factors of the mechanisms of the human body.
advice: This course will provide information that should enable the student to explain: 1. Generic skills and science literacy (logical thinking, critical thinking, knowledge synthesis). 2. Difference between science and religion (originality, falsifiability, plagiarism). 3. Difference between life and stone (purpose of life, purposiveness, ultimate factor). 4. Evolution of life (mutation, fitness, natural selection, selective pressure, polymorphism). 5. Chemical context of life (organic compounds: carbohydrates, fats, proteins and nucleic acids, etc.). 6. Cell structure and function (cell membrane, organelles, movement across membranes, diffusion, osmosis, active transport). 7. Metabolic pathway (catabolic pathway and anabolic pathway, enzyme, cellular respiration, fermentation) 8. Protein structure and function. 9. Synthesis of protein (DNA to RNA: transcription, translation: making protein from RNA template). 10. Intercellular signaling (ion channel, receptor, transporter). 11. Regulation of blood sugar and the mechanism of diabetes. 12. Endocrine system (hormones and target receptors, feedback regulation). 13. Nervous system (neurons, synapses, resting potential, action potential, neurotransmitters). 14. Significance of homeostasis at the cellular, tissue, organ, and organismal levels.
requiredKnowledge: General knowledge of chemistry, physics, and math is required. In order to understand the information presented, the habit of studying the background information is required.

activityGoals.body: Explain human structure and function from an evolutionary perspective.
Explain the structure and function of the human body, its organs, and tissues.
Explain regulation of blood sugar and the mechanism of diabetes.
Explain human functions through signaling at the intracellular and intercellular levels.

title: 細胞の構造と機能
subtitle: Structure and Function of the Cell
keywords: Cell structure 2.Cell function 3.Signal transduction 4.Gene expression 5.Experimental techniques
educationalGoal: Cells are important elements of all living things on Earth. Humans, plants and animals, every living organism, is composed of cells. Naturally, if cells are the structural and functional units of living things, there must be something peculiar about them. What is it about cell structure and function that make them so important?
advice: This course will cultivate understanding of the molecular mechanisms that govern cells, the structural and functional units of living things. The basic cellular processes of organelles and localization, movement, proliferation and signal transduction in cells will be introduced. To cultivate your familiarity of the science behind what we know from modern biology, we will discuss the experimental techniques utilized to study cell structure and function. The lectures are designed to be interactive. In addition to instructor presentations, we will often break into short discussions about current issues and analyze data. Additionally, students will give feedback in questionnaires given in the classroom on the successes and failures of each lecture in order to continually improve the course. This course will work on your skills in scientific writing. We will discuss how to read and interpret primary contents of the textbook, and how to construct precise and concise scientific writing.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of biochemistry, physics and chemistry. High school-level knowledge of biology.

Describe the basic cellular signaling process
Describe basic cellular metabolism
Describe basic cell division
Describe basic cell migration
Describe the application of cell biology in industry

title: 神経科学
subtitle: Neuroscience
keywords: Neuron 2.Synapse 3.Action potential 4.Neurotransmitter 5.Behavior
educationalGoal: This course is intended for Brain Science majors. The goal of this course is to introduce students to the study of neuroscience. Students will learn fundamental information about cellular biology and the electrophysiological properties of neurons, neuroanatomy, psychopharmacology, and how the activity of neurons can yield sensory perception, motor control, and complex behavioral functions such as learning and motivation.
advice: The course will provide information that should enable the student to explain: 1. Neuron structure and function (dendrites, axon, cell body, synapse). 2. Information processing by the nervous system (sensory input, motor output). 3. Formation of resting potential (ion channels, sodium-potassium pump). 4. Modeling of resting potential (equilibrium potential, Nernst equation). 5. Monitoring neural activity (intracellular recording, extracellular recording). 6. Generation of action potential (hyperpolarization, depolarization, voltage-gated ion channel). 7. Conduction of action potential (saltatory conduction). 8. Synaptic transmission (chemical synapse, synaptic vesicle, neurotransmitter, ligand-gated ion channel). 9. Generation of postsynaptic potential (EPSP, IPSP). 10. Neurotransmitters (acetylcholine, biogenic amines, amino acids, neuropeptides). 11. Sensory reception and transduction (sensory receptor, coding of stimulus intensity). 12. Mechanism of human vision (retina, rod, cone, rhodopsin, color vision, visual field). 13. Mechanism of hearing, equilibrium, smell and taste (mechanoreceptor, chemoreceptor). 14. Neuromuscular transmission (skeletal muscle, smooth muscle, cardiac muscle, acetylcholine receptor). 15. Regulation of motor system (motor reflex, locomotion). 16. Evolution of behavior (instinctive behavior, fixed action pattern, releaser, key stimulus).
requiredKnowledge: General knowledge of chemistry, physics, and math are required. In order to understand the information presented, the habit of studying the background information is required.

activityGoals.body: Explain neuron structure and function.
Explain information processing by the nervous system.
Explain the behavior of animals and humans as a function of nerves and brain.
Explain the function of the nervous system from an evolutionary perspective.

title: 微生物学
subtitle: Microbiology
keywords: Microorganisms 2.Types and cell structure 3.Growth and metabolism 4.Genetic engineering 5.Regional cooperation and environmental protection
educationalGoal: Humans have been producing various fermented foods, such as bread, liquor, cheese, yogurt, and miso, using microorganisms since ancient times. In recent years, microorganisms have become widely used in the fields of pharmaceuticals, environmental protection, waste recycling, material production, and energy in addition to food. Students will learn about the microorganisms and their various applications.
advice: It is important to have basic knowledge of microbiology, biochemistry, organic chemistry, molecular biology, gene engineering and protein engineering. 1. Microorganisms: culture and observation 2. Types and cell structure: composition of a typical prokaryotic cell 3. Growth and metabolism: ATP production, nutrition and metabolism 4. Genetic engineering: heredity, repair, mutation, and recombinant microorganisms in biotechnology 5. Function of microorganisms: fermentation, medicine, production of useful substances 6. Environmental protection: current environmental protection and initiatives
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of microbiology, biochemistry, organic chemistry, molecular biology, gene engineering and protein engineering.

activityGoals.body: Ability to explain how to operate laboratory equipment and instruments used to culture microorganisms.
Ability to explain the cell structure, classification, metabolism of a microorganism.
Ability to explain the mutation and transformation of microorganisms.
Ability to explain the effective use of microorganisms, such as environmental protection and energy production.
Ability to explain the relationship between the use of microorganisms and local industries.

subtitle: Sensory Information
keywords: Sense and perception 2.Visual sense 3.Auditory sense 4.Somatosensory sense 5.Gustation and olfactory sense
educationalGoal: When we sense and recognize our environment or target objects, our brain processes a huge amount of information from the sensory system. Students will learn basic functions of various human sensory systems.
advice: We will cover the following topics: 1. Basic characteristics and psychophysical measurement of the sensory system 2. Structure and function of the visual information processing system in the periphery and central nervous system 3. Structure and function of the auditory information processing system in the periphery and central nervous system 4. Overview of the somatosensory and tactile information systems 5. Ability to explain the basics of gustation and olfactory sense.

title: 運動機能論
subtitle: Motor Function
keywords: Motor control 2.Brain 3.Learning 4.Memory 5.Brain disorder
educationalGoal: This course provides an overview of the neuroscience of: (1) motor control (2) learning through motor control of the peripheral and central nervous systems (3) mind, brain, and health, and the intersection of psychology and cognitive neuroscience.
advice: This course provides an overview of the neuroscience of motor control and learning through motor control of the peripheral and central nervous systems, mind, brain, and health, and the intersection of psychology and cognitive neuroscience. Fundamental biological, psychological, social, and environmental factors are introduced with an emphasis on critical functions related to motor control and animal neuroscience of learning, such as sensitive periods, and neuroplasticity. In addition, factors that facilitate and roadblocks that inhibit optimization of learning are explored as we discuss key cognitive constructs (language, attention, memory, executive functions, brain disorders), with special attention on neurocognitive processes and motor control. These studies will be directly applied by each student in future Project Design III activities conducted in an area of each student’s personal interest.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of biochemistry, physics and chemistry is required. High school-level knowledge of biology, and students should have knowledge of basic cell biology, anatomy of human body, and sensory physiology.

activityGoals.body: Describe the basic cellular structures and functions of neurons
Describe the basic signaling process in the brain
Describe the pharmacological approach to brain disorders
Describe the plasticity of brain circuits
Describe motor control in humans
Describe the role of the hippocampus in the short-term memory formation

educationalGoal: Brain science is a comprehensive science in the fields of science including biology and the fields of humanities including psychology. In that sense, this subject has the role of finishing what was learned in the 1st and 2nd grades. We will study neural circuits composed of DNA, proteins, nerve cells, etc., and learn what kind of function our brain exerts and the structure of the brain that is the basis of it. As a result, we will understand the function of a large information processing system called the nervous system, that is, the higher functions of the brain.

subtitle: Medical Engineering
keywords: Examine the inside of the body 2.Examining blood and cells 3.Measure motor function 4.Examine the brain 5.Optical measurement/biosensor
educationalGoal: Engineering plays an extremely important role in the medical field. Medical engineering is the application of engineering principles and design concepts to medicine and is indispensable for medical diagnosis and treatment. This course aims to help students understand how these principles are applied to diagnostic devices and treatment devices that are actually used in the medical field. Students also learn about safety measures for the human body in diagnosis and treatment.
