title: 細胞工学
subtitle: Cell Engineering
keywords: Biotechnology 2.Drugs and medicine 3.Biologics 4.Food production 5.Biofuel
educationalGoal: Biology and technology are harnessed to serve many purposes including: (1) gene therapies, (2) drug therapies, biologics, (3) food production and biofuel development, (4) understanding the breadth of biotechnology and how it can serve as a research tool.
advice: This course is designed to acquaint a non-scientist professional with aspects of science as they apply to the biotechnology industry. Biology and technology are harnessed to serve many purposes including gene therapies, drug therapies, biologics, food production and biofuel development. Grasping the breadth of biotechnology can be confusing to a student. This is because modern-day research not only studies biological problems in a classical sense, but also puts biological principles to work as research tools. Antibodies are an example of a fundamental component of the immune system, yet antibodies are also used as tools by researchers to detect other proteins and are being developed in ways to work like drugs to treat diseases such as cancer. In a wider sense, the inner workings of cells are examined to identify defects in diseases, yet cells are also used to make products like biofuels. This course is specifically designed to give an overview of the biotech industry and to teach the scientific principles that apply to numerous biotechnology sectors.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of biochemistry, physics and chemistry. High school-level knowledge of biology. Students should have learned basic cell biology.

Describe basic cell biology and food production

keywords: Transformation 2.DNA extraction 3.Gel electrophoresis 4.PCR 5.Enzyme
educationalGoal: Students will learn the skills related to experimental operations, instrument handling, instrumental analysis, data analysis, and report preparation in bioscience. Students will acquire the ability to qualitatively and quantitatively evaluate the results obtained from the experiments, and to think logically. Through experiments and exercises practicing theories and methods, students will acquire comprehension and application ability based on a basic foundation.
advice: Students will carry out experiments and exercises based on the topics in bioscience. If components are difficult to understand in experiments and exercises, students will be asked to work on the topic before the next class through research and asking the instructor and other classmates questions. Basics: Experimental guidance, safety training, exam Genetic experiments: DNA Extraction, Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), Restriction enzyme treatment, Transformation, Agarose gel electrophoresis Protein research: Protein quantification assay, SDS-PAGE Enzyme research: Enzyme activity, Optimum pH, Optimum temperature
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of the fundamentals of bioscience, such as molecular cloning and biochemistry.

title: 応用バイオ統合演習
subtitle: Multidisciplinary Practices for Applied Bioscience
keywords: Biotechnology 2.Genetic Engineering 3.Brain Science 4.Food Technology
educationalGoal: The goals are to utilize the knowledges learned in Applied Bioscience and to acquire the abilities necessary to achieve your future activities. In this course, you will understand the principles of fundamental phenomena on scientific considerations, and you can plan your future activities. In addition, you can understand and explain the role of a science and engineering engineer in the area of Applied Biotechnology.
advice: The outlines in this course are the history and the interaction with society the fields of the applied biotechnology and the applied chemistry. Also, you introduce your subject of research and understand in the wide range of research fields through presentation and discussion. In addition, you will study the basic principles in the field of food science and technology, and understand the visions of food industry.
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge and experience learned and gained prior to the beginning of the course.

activityGoals.body: To be able to scientifically think about the significance and the principle fundamental phenomena and concepts.
To be able to understand the role of Applied Biotechnology in society.
To be able to understand the outline of the educational program in the department of the Applied Bioscience.
To be able to explain the role as an engineer of the science and engineering in the applied biology field.
To be able to introduce the future development of the applied biotechnology field based.

title: 専門ゼミ(応用バイオ学科)
subtitle: Preparatory Seminar for Design Project III (Applied Bioscience)
keywords: Design Project III 2.Brain information system 3.Cognition and behavior 4.Bioengineering 5.Gene and protein
educationalGoal: In Design Project III, students will learn the educational goals of the Department of Applied Bioscience. In the Preparatory Seminar for Design Project III, students review safety education and engineering ethics education. Furthermore, students learn how to implement the project activities and learn basic knowledge as engineers in the field of science and engineering.
advice: In this course students prepare for their graduation research to be conducted in Design Project III. Students clarify their research objectives and build an experiment plan in Design Project III. Students also prepare a learning plan to acquire knowledge and skills necessary for carrying out their research. Students analyze the research theme and summarize: 1) Background 2) Problem extraction 3) Objective setting 4) Methods of experiment and analysis 5) Anticipated results Students are required to present of their results in Preparatory Seminar for Design Project III, and submit reports as necessary.
requiredKnowledge: Details of Preparatory Seminar for Design Project III will be explained in the guidance for each laboratory.

activityGoals.body: Ability to provide objectives and a plan in Design Project III.
Ability to explain your research theme in Design Project III.
Ability to learn knowledge and skills autonomously for Design Project III.
Ability to understand engineering ethics and safety guidelines.
Ability to understand research processes in Design Project III.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(辰巳仁史研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Tatsumi Hitoshi)
keywords: Actin 2.Mechanical force sensing 3.Cell migration 4.Single molecule imaging 5.Image analysis
educationalGoal: Dynamic reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton is crucial for a number of cellular processes including cytokinesis, cell motility, and morphogenesis.
advice: Students will attend lectures introducing several research concepts. Dynamic reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton is crucial for a number of cellular processes including cytokinesis, cell motility, and morphogenesis. However, filamentous actin alone is relatively stable, and acceleration of filament disassembly is often required to promote actin cytoskeletal dynamics. ADF/cofilin is one of the major factors to accelerate disassembly of actin filaments by enhancing filament fragmentation and monomer dissociation from the pointed end. However, in vitro studies indicate that ADF/cofilin alone severs actin filaments only weakly and optimally when a cluster of ADF/cofilin molecules bind to an actin filament at low densities. When ADF/cofilin binds to the side of actin filaments at high densities, fragmentation of the filaments is rather infrequent. These biochemical properties suggest that ADF/cofilin alone may not be sufficient to account for rapid turnover of actin filaments observed in live cells. ADF/cofilin is one of the major factors to accelerate disassembly of actin filaments by enhancing filament fragmentation. Tension dependent changes in actin filament fluctuations, and ADF/cofilin molecules bind to an actin filament. It is possible that a mechano-dependent process is involvement in cell re-organization.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of biochemistry, physics and chemistry. High school-level knowledge of biology. Students should have learned basic cell biology.

title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(野村一樹研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III (Nomura Kazuki)
keywords: Food technology (Food engineering) 2.High-pressure technology 3.Food-processing technology 4.Regional cooperation
educationalGoal: The foundation of Food technology (Food engineering) is a chemical-engineering process based on the idea that "more effectively". Predecessors have developed a chemical-engineering process for "safer" and "more efficient" processing of foods. The objectives are to understand the basic principles of food technology and to present novel ideas in this field. Also, the purposes are to learn the ideas of improving the quality, branding, expanding distribution, and local contribution by focusing on the local food products, to plan your future activities.
advice: This laboratory focuses on the local food products and studies the following research themes. 1. Improving the quality and branding of the local food products. ・Development and evaluation of the novel processing and storage technologies. 2. Reducing agricultural damage caused by wild birds and animals. ・Development and evaluation of an effective utilization method of the gibier (meat of the wild birds and animals). 3. Clarification of processing mechanism of the traditional products. ・Analysis of various mechanism, such as fermentation, production, and degradation of each component.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledges of biology, chemistry, physics, statistics, and food and nutrition. Basic experimental techniques acquired in "Basic Experiments and Practice in Bioscience and Chemistry" and "Applied Bioscience Major Lab/Exercises" "Advanced Bioengineering" and "Multidisciplinary Practices for Applied Bioscience" are also recommended. Safety first.

activityGoals.body: To able to understand and explained the basic principles of food technology.
To able to understand the qualities of food and changes caused by processing.
To able to understand numerically and discussed logically changes caused by processing and storage.
To able to create presentations and reports based on logical considerations.

advice: This course mainly aims at students who wish to be science teachers at secondary school. requiredKnowledge: In order to teach Science at secondary school, it is necessary to understand knowledge of physics in senior high school.     担当教員名
 TANIGUCHI Masahiro, OKADA Go, KUSANO Eiji, HIGUCHI Masanori, TSUYUMOTO Isao
    授業科目の学習・教育目標   キーワード 学習・教育目標     1.Mechanics 2.Electromagnetism 3.Wave 4.Demonstration of physics experiment  ●To understand basic knowledge and skills for physics experiments, which include the basic operation of laboratory equipment and safety precautions. ●To understand the methods of data processing using computer. ●To design and conduct physics experiments, and to analyze and report the results of them. ●To plan, conduct, and teach physics experiments in the subject "Science" in secondary school.
    授業の概要および学習上の助言   This course mainly aims at students who wish to be science teachers at secondary school. Through learning basic physics experiments, students will acquire knowledge on how to operate laboratory equipment and safety necessary for conducting experiments in the subject "Science" of secondary school. Students will experience how to conduct experimental lessons in the subject "Science".
    教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック
    履修に必要な予備知識や技能   In order to teach Science at secondary school, it is necessary to understand knowledge of physics in senior high school. Therefore, students should review high school physics thoroughly before this course. This course does not only cover the contents specified in the Course of Study of Science, but also the laws of conservation of angular momentum in mechanics and Maxwell's equations in electromagnetism, which are useful for the subject "Science".

title: 地学基礎実験
subtitle: Basic Experiments in Geoscience
keywords: Geology 2.Minerals 3.Weather map 4.Atmosphere and humidity 5.Water analysis
educationalGoal: Learn the use of basic experimental tools correctly and what is necessary for safety throughout basic experiments in geoscience. Learn data analysis of the experimental results using a computer. Plan and conduct geological experiments, and Prepare a report describing the experimental method and results. Learn how to achieve high educational effects in geological experiments when geological experiments conduct.
advice: This course is intended for applicants for teachers of science in junior high school or high school. Learn the safety training, the use of experimental tools and instruments correctly, and the knowledge of data analysis using a computer throughout basic experiments in geoscience for junior high school and high school. Conduct field works such as minerals sampling and stratum observation in addition to indoor experiments. Fieldwork will be conduct on Saturday in April. The order of the experiments may change due to the weather or schedule, check the Student Portal carefully.
books: Textbook: Chigaku Kiso Jikkenn (Kanazawa Institute of Technology Publishing) Reference book: Mizu no Bunseki (Kagaku Dojin Publishing), Chishitsu Chousa to Chishichizu (Asakura Shoten Publishing), Tenkizu no Mikata Tebiki (Kuraimu Publishing), Ganseki Kaseki no Kenbikyou Kansatsu (Chijin Shokan Publishing), Tenkizu no Kakikata Tebiki Saihan (Kuraimu Kishou Tosho Shuppan Publising)
requiredKnowledge: It is necessary to a deeper understanding than what you teach in order to teach geological experiments in Junior high school and High school. In order to require knowledge of geoscience in the high school field, review the geoscience field of high school. In this class, learn useful knowledge for teaching geoscience through the experiments.

activityGoals.body: Read the textbook, and conduct the experiment using the equipments and experimental tools properly.
Analyze the data using computer.
Discuss and evaluate the results properly.
Prepare the experiments useful for understanding in geoscience field, and teach the experiments.

lessons.assignments: Readings: Chapter 3 Complete a Lab report.

lessons.content: Water analysis - Pretreatment of natural water samples - Determination of fluoride in spring water and groundwater samples
lessons.assignments: Readings: Chapter 5 Complete a Lab report.

lessons.content: Overall review -necessity of geological experiments, and safety training- Self-evaluation Day
lessons.assignments: Check your mistakes and review your weakness.

This course consists of three parts. One is Pre-guidance for final preparation of the experience of nursing care, second is experience of nursing care, and the last is Post-guidance for reflection on the experience of nursing care. In Pre-guidance, students will acquire.
advice: 1. title: 地球環境学
subtitle: Environmental Science of Earth
keywords: Biogeochemical cycle 2.Chemical composiiton of the earth's crust 3.Basic chemical equilibria 4.Environmental issues
educationalGoal: The earth can be divided into the atmosphere, the lithosphere, and the hydrosphere, but elements such as carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus circulate among all of these spheres. This course will cover the behavior of substances in the global environment and the chemical reactions related to the behavior of the substances. The goal of this course is to raise awareness of the factors affecting the global environment.
advice: 1. Chemical composition of the earth's crust. 2. The evolution of the earth and changes in the atmosphere. 3. Basics of analytical chemistry. 4. Basics of aquatic environment. 5. Chemical equilibria in environmental water. 6. Environmental problems.
books: (Textbook) An Introduction to Environmental Chemistry, Julian E. Andrews, et al., Wiley-Blackwell, ISBN: 9780632059058
requiredKnowledge: A knowledge of high school level chemistry and biology is required to understand the lectures.

activityGoals.body: Understand the origins of the earth and changes in the global environment.
Understand atmospheric changes of the earth from the beginning to the present.
Describe the greenhouse effect caused by carbon dioxide..
Understand major chemical equilibria in environmental water.
Understand the mecanisms of seasonal variations in the water quality of lakes.
Understand global environmental problems.

title: 環境計測学
subtitle: Environmental Analysis
keywords: Global environment 2.Environmental analyses 3.Environmental issues 4.Water quality measurements
educationalGoal: To fully understand environmental issues, such as pollution, that have multiple effects on the global environment, you will learn about the natural environment (air, water, soil) and the circulation of matter in the environment. In addition, you will be able to explain the role of environmental analysis in environmental issues and understand the principles of environmental measurement technology.
advice: To understand environmental issues, such as pollution, that significantly affect the global environment, an understanding of the natural environment (air, water, soil) and the circulation of substances through it are necessary. In this course, you will learn about the natural environment, material circulation, and environmental issues. You will also learn the principles and application of measurement methods used for environmental analyses, especially water quality measurements.
books: Textbooks: Chikyu no Kagaku to Kankyou (Sankyo Shuppan Publishing) Reference books: Kankyo Kagaku (Shokabou Publishing), Mizu no Bunseki (Kagaku Dojin Publishing), Kankyo Kagaku Gairon (Maruzen Publishing) Reserved books: Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of analytical chemistry is necessary. In addition, knowledge of instrumental analytical chemistry is helpful to understand the principles and applications of environmental analysis methods. Bring a scientific calculator to class.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain material circulation in the natural environment (air, water, soil).
Be able to explain the significance of environmental analysis in relation to environmental issues.
Be able to describe water analysis methods.
Be able to understand the principles and characteristics of dating methods.

lessons.content: Material circulation in the atmosphere
lessons.assignments: Preview: Study the composition of the atmosphere. Review: Material circulation in the atmosphere.

lessons.content: Material circulation in soil and the hydrosphere
lessons.assignments: Preview: Study the structure and function of soil, and the circulation of water. Review: Representative composition in the hydrosphere.

lessons.content: Air pollution, soil pollution, and water pollution
lessons.assignments: Preview: Understand the content in chapters 1 to 4. Review: Each type of pollution.

lessons.content: Outline of water analysis methods and the significance of water quality measurements
lessons.assignments: Preview: Study various analytical methods. Review: Water analysis methods and the significance of water quality measurements.

lessons.content: Analysis of water (1): Volumetric analysis (neutralization titration and chelate titration)
lessons.assignments: Preview: Understand acid-base reactions and chelate formation. Review: Volumetric analysis based on acid-base reactions and chelate formation.

lessons.content: Analysis of water (1): Volumetric analysis (redox titration)
lessons.assignments: Preview: Understand redox reactions. Review: Volumetric analysis based on redox reactions.

lessons.content: Analysis of water (2): Spectrophotometry
lessons.assignments: Preview: Understand the content in chapters 5 to 8. Review: The principles and characteristics of spectrophotometry.

lessons.content: Analysis of water (3): Electrochemical analysis
lessons.assignments: Preview: Understand redox potential. Review: The principles and characteristics of electrochemical analysis.

lessons.content: Analysis of water (4): Chromatography
lessons.assignments: Preview: Study chromatography. Review: Various chromatographic methods.

lessons.content: Dating method (1): Radionuclides and decay
lessons.assignments: Preview: Understand the content in chapters 9 to 11. Review: Radionuclides and their decay.

lessons.content: Dating method (2): Dating methods using disintegration of primary natural radionuclides and 14C.
lessons.assignments: Preview: Understand primary natural radionuclides. Review: The carbon-14 dating method.

lessons.content: Overall review Final examination
lessons.assignments: Preview: Study for examination

lessons.assignments: Identify your mistakes and review your weaknesses.

title: 教育相談(夏期集中講義)
subtitle: School Counseling
courseType:
Teacher Certification Program
Teacher Certification Courses
keywords: Counseling 2.Truant and Bullying 3.Developmental Disorder 4.Developmental Counseling 5.Cooperation between School and Community
educationalGoal: This course covers psychological problems in secondary school(relationship between students and parents, truant, bullying, school maladjustment, developmental disorder, and so on). Students will discuss psychological features in adolescence, relationship between teachers and students, and relationship between teachers and parents, and aim to acquire the correct view and skill for students with school maladjustment.
advice: This course includes the following materials: (1) To consider the current issues of school maladjustment in secondary education(truant, bullying, and school maladjustment) (2) To understand psychological features and psychological problems in adolescence, and the support system for students with school maladjustment (3) To understand basic theories of school counseling and psychological support for students with school maladjustment. Students are expected to consider what is necessary for secondary school students.
books: Toshiyuki Kasugai & Minako Itoh(2011) Yoku Wakaru Kyouiku-Soudan, Mineruva-Shobou.
requiredKnowledge: To understand basic knowledge of educational psychology.

activityGoals.body: Be able to answer the space filling and descriptive questions about truant, bullying, and school maladjustment.
Be able to explain how to understand secondary school students with psychological problems.
Be able to explain the correct psychological support for secondary school students.
Be able to engage in this course and self-evaluate objectives of this course to be achieved.

keywords: Survey of training school 2.Objectives of Teaching Practice 3.Teacher Responsibility 4.Aptitude as a Teacher 5.Ideal Teacher Image
educationalGoal: The objectives of Teacher Practice are working at a school experientially, determining own aptitude as a teacher, and clarifying the ideal teacher .  一般に、授業あるいは課外での学習では:「知識などを取り込む」→「知識などをいろいろな角度から、場合によってはチーム活動として、考え、推論し、創造する」→「修得した内容を表現、発表、伝達する」→「総合的に評価を受ける、GoodWork!」:のようなプロセス(一部あるいは全体)を繰り返し行いながら、応用力のある知識やスキルを身につけていくことが重要です。このような学習プロセスを大事に行動してください。
